author: mecaloza
body:
## Resumen

Primer PR del refactor (B1). Reorganiza el backend sin cambiar la API: mismos endpoints y respuestas (lo comprobé con 66 requests contra la versión anterior; solo cambian el nombre/versión en `/`, el redirect https detrás del proxy y que el 500 ahora es JSON con CORS).

Va apilado sobre #1 (hotfix HeyGen): mergear #1 primero.

## Cambios

- **Estructura `app/`**: `core/` (config, logs, seguridad), `api/` (deps + routers bajo `/api/v1`), `db/` (modelos separados por dominio, sesión, arranque), `services/`. `main.py` queda como alias: `uvicorn main:app` y `python main.py` siguen funcionando.
- **Configuración por entorno** (`pydantic-settings`):
  - Ya no hay password de BD ni secreto JWT por defecto en el código.
  - En Railway o producción, la app **no arranca** sin `DATABASE_URL` de Postgres y `JWT_SECRET` (o `SECRET_KEY`) de 32 caracteres o más.
  - Los errores de validación no muestran los valores de las variables.
- **Seguridad**:
  - `python-jose` (con CVEs) y `passlib` se reemplazan por PyJWT + bcrypt. Los hashes y tokens actuales siguen sirviendo; hay tests con hashes reales de la versión anterior.
  - Los refresh tokens se guardan como sha256 y se rotan con compare-and-set: dos refresh simultáneos con el mismo token ya no ganan ambos.
  - El login tarda lo mismo si el correo no existe, así no se puede averiguar qué cuentas existen.
- **Logs estructurados**: JSON por stdout con `x-request-id`, sin `print()`. Los errores SQL ocultan sus parámetros.
- **Deploy**: Dockerfile con usuario no root y `exec` (apagado limpio en redeploys). `railway.json` agrega un healthcheck en `/health`: si falta una variable, el deploy nuevo no recibe tráfico y el anterior sigue activo.
- **Limpieza**: se borran scripts, SQL y documentos obsoletos. README nuevo en español y `scripts/seed_dev.py`, que solo corre contra SQLite local.

## Sin cambios de comportamiento a propósito

- El access token sigue durando **7 días** (`ACCESS_TOKEN_MINUTES`): el frontend desplegado hace `fetch` directo y nunca refresca. Se reducirá cuando todas las pantallas usen el cliente nuevo.
- Otros ajustes menores: la sesión de SQLAlchemy usa `expire_on_commit=False` y el pool pasa a 5+5 (antes 5+10).

## Antes de mergear (Railway)

1. Confirmar que existen `DATABASE_URL` (Postgres) y `JWT_SECRET` de 32+ caracteres. Generar el secreto con `python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"`. Cambiarlo invalida las sesiones actuales, que es lo buscado.
2. Si el servicio tiene un *Start Command* propio, puede quedarse (`uvicorn main:app` y `python main.py` funcionan), pero lo ideal es quitarlo y dejar el del Dockerfile.

## Pruebas

- `pytest`: 73 tests pasan (config, seguridad, auth, seed, persistencia HeyGen).
- Arranque probado con `python main.py`: `/health` responde y los logs salen en JSON.

author: glomargadaffi
body:
Part of #379.

This PR covers one half of what is left of #379: a 3CX leg whose Telephony->device GET stream never opens is now dropped at 3CX, once. It leaves out PR 2, reconciling orphaned legs after a reboot.

## The defect

`TelephonyAnchorClient::runRxLoop()` retries the GET stream open up to 240 times, about 2 minutes. When 3CX refused every attempt (the #518 403s), the loop logged `stream never opened`, closed its client and returned. Nothing dropped the leg. On .244 one such leg was still showing on the 3CX route point about 25 minutes later, after the board had rebooted with no sessions.

## The fix

- **`runRxLoop()`** (`TelephonyAnchorClient.cpp`): when the whole budget was spent (`attempt >= kMaxAttempts`) and no teardown is under way (`keepRunning()`), it reports the leg as a new `CallEvent::MediaNeverOpened`. It does not drop the leg itself, for two reasons. `dropCall()` would join this very rx task: its `stopMediaStreams()` waits 2 s, then detaches the task and counts it toward the #65 restart. And the anchor client cannot see whether the call is a 911.
- **`RequestsHandler::anchorMediaNeverOpenedLocked()`**, called from the anchor event callback:
  - If a 911/933 session (`Session::isEmergency()`, #604) owns the leg, the leg is kept and one line is logged. With no inbound audio the PSAP may still hear the caller, and no automated teardown hangs up an emergency call.
  - Any other leg, whether its session is live or already gone (the .244 case), has its bridge stopped and its session marked `setAnchorLegReleased()`, and is dropped through `asyncDropCall()`. 3CX's Remove then BYEs the handset through the existing Dropped branch. The stopped bridge and the released flag keep `endCall()` from dropping the leg a second time.

### Why the decision is in RequestsHandler (scope note)

The brief for this PR was to touch only `runRxLoop` and its drop path, so that it stays clear of #688's `tick()`/maint work. Posting the drop straight from `runRxLoop()` would hang up 911 calls: emergency calls go out through the anchor (`emergencyRouteLocked()`), and only `RequestsHandler` can see `isEmergency()`. So the anchor side only reports the leg, and the handler decides. I announced this on #379 before building it. `tick()` and the maint task are untouched. I checked the hunks of every open PR that touches these files (#688, #517, #589, #449, #487), and none of them touches the anchor event callback or `runRxLoop()`.

### What is deliberately not covered

- **Transport give-ups:** 3 consecutive transport failures, or `could not rebuild client`. They end in seconds rather than minutes, a later upsert can restart rx on that leg (#554), and dropping on a TLS blip mid-ring would hang up a live call. Only a spent budget counts. `runRxLoop()` also does not tombstone the leg, so a 911 leg that was kept can still be restarted.
- **403 fail-fast (#518):** unchanged. The only re-scope proposed on #518 (2026-09-27 05:23) is an unaccepted suggestion, and it does not ask for 403 to fail fast.
- **Two remaining edges of "once":**
  - A SIP-side `dropCall()` can land between the rx task's `keepRunning()` check and the handler's drop. In that race two drop POSTs go out, and 3CX answers the second with a 4xx.
  - If the drop POST fails, or the 12 KB drop worker cannot be spawned, the leg is already marked released and its bridge stopped. A later handset hangup will not retry the drop. That makes this path at most once by design, and PR 2's reconcile is the backstop.

## Tests

- **`tests/AnchorRouting_test.cpp`**, three new tests that drive the handler through `anchorMediaNeverOpenedForTest()`. The callback is wired only for a real anchor, never the host suite's Loopback.
  - `LegWhoseStreamNeverOpenedIsDroppedOnce`: exactly one `dropCall()`, and none more after the handset's BYE.
  - `OrphanLegWhoseStreamNeverOpenedIsDropped`: a leg with no session is dropped.
  - `EmergencyLegWhoseStreamNeverOpenedIsKept`: a 911 leg is not dropped or released, and its bridge keeps running. That part is absence-only; its positive control is the same leg with the flag cleared, which is dropped.
- **`tests/tools/test_anchor_rx_never_opened_drop.py`** pins the production side, which no host test reaches because the anchor client is ESP-only. `runRxLoop()` must report the event only on a spent budget with no teardown under way, and must never call `dropCall()` or `stopMediaStreams()`. The callback must route the event to the handler.
- **Floor:** `tests/min_tests.d/379-rx-never-opened-drop.txt` adds +3.
- **Red runs** are posted as a PR comment.

Full WSL host suite: 1582 tests, 1581 passed, 0 failed, 1 skipped (the expected FirmwareInfo git-stamp skip). Floor is 1582 (= 1280 + 302). Python tool tests: 101/101 pass.

## Constrained build (4 MB, `SIP_CONSTRAINED`)

Both `TelephonyAnchorClient.cpp` and `RequestsHandler.cpp` compile into the constrained build, and the change is not guarded out, because a billed orphan leg and the 911 rule apply there too. These sizes are estimates; there was no ESP build here:

| Change | Estimated growth |
|---|---|
| One enumerator | 0 B |
| The `runRxLoop()` report | about 60-80 B of code |
| The handler and its callback branch | about 250-350 B of code |
| Two short log strings | about 75 B |

That is roughly 0.4-0.5 KB of the ~1.5 KB left (#689). BigDog should confirm this with the size gate.

## Stack and heap

- **Stack:** the callback now also runs on the 6144 B `tel_media_rx` stack, under `runRxLoop()`'s frame. The precedent is the Dtmf event, which already runs the same callback on the 6144 B WS task. I have not measured it; a high-water read on the first hardware run would settle it.
- **Heap:** there are no new members and no new kind of allocation. The rx side reuses the existing `_eventCb` snapshot, whose `[this]` capture fits the SBO. The handler reuses `queueLog()`/`asyncDropCall()`, the same as the other callback branches.

## Hardware check after merge (BigDog)

Dial an unroutable far end (the #518 repro), so the GET stream is refused. About 2 minutes after ringing starts, expect this sequence:
1. `stream never opened`
2. `[Telephony] no rx audio, dropping leg N`
3. `Successfully dropped participant N`
4. 3CX Participant Remove
5. The handset gets a BYE, and the call is gone on 3CX.

body:
**Stacked on #42** (`fix/accordionref-conductor-deps` — Landlock sandbox #40 + egress check #41). Base branch is `fix/accordionref-conductor-deps`, not `main`; this diffs cleanly once #42 merges.

## Summary

Two independent hardenings, per owner decision on 2026-09-28 ("dont let them have internet"):

### 1. Bench agents get no internet by default

- `sandboxEgress` now defaults to `"blocked"` whenever the effective `sandbox` mode is `"landlock"` (previously always defaulted to `"unchecked"` regardless of sandbox mode). It still defaults to `"unchecked"` when sandbox is `"off"`.
- An **explicit** `sandboxEgress: "unchecked"` (from bench config or trial spec) is now a thrown error whenever the effective sandbox mode is `"landlock"` — not just defaulted away. This is a deliberate breaking change: a config that previously wrote `sandbox: "landlock", sandboxEgress: "unchecked"` explicitly will now fail loudly instead of running with the network open. That matches this codebase's existing "tighten-only, fail loudly rather than silently permissive" philosophy for sandbox config, and closes the actual gap found in production: on 2026-09-28 a Landlock-sandboxed agent cloned SlopCode's public repo (hidden tests + reference solutions) from GitHub mid-run, because Landlock only restricts the filesystem, not the network.
- Adds `scripts/egress-allowlist.sh`, generalized from the iptables owner-match allowlist used to patch the affected VM by hand. It:
  - scopes an iptables `BENCH_EGRESS` chain to one bench OS user via `-m owner --uid-owner`,
  - resolves and pins each `--allow host:port` entry into `/etc/hosts` (defeats CDN IP rotation while keeping an IP-based allowlist valid),
  - is idempotent on re-run,
  - blocks IPv6 entirely for that user,
  - has a `--check` mode that verifies (as the bench user, via `sudo -u`) that github.com/pypi.org are blocked and the allowed hosts are reachable.
  - Documented in TUTORIAL.md under a new "Sealing a bench host" section; README's Layout table and Setup section reference it too.
- This script was written and `bash -n` syntax-checked only. **It was never executed against any real host** (constraint from the requester — no GCP, no live VM changes in this task).

### 2. `caps.costUsd` now caps agent + conductor cost combined

- `caps.costUsd` previously only compared against the agent's own spend (`pi get_session_stats().cost`). An LLM conductor's own summary calls — logged via Accordion's completion-usage side log (bellows #38: `completions.jsonl` / `host.jsonl` `t:"complete"` rows) — run 29-43% of a conductor's total spend and were not capped, so an LLM conductor could run well past a deterministic conductor's effective ceiling for the same dollar cap.
- `driveUntilDone` now reads both telemetry files live on every cost poll (new `liveConductorCostUsd` in `collect.mjs`, shared with the post-run fold so the mid-run check and the final record agree) and aborts (`"aborted-cost"`) once **agent + conductor** cost reaches the cap. Both figures are already on the same $ basis (pi's own pricing for the agent; the Accordion extension logs conductor completions in the same $ terms), so no unit conversion was needed.
- The abort detail and the `[done]` summary line both now break out the total: `cost=$X (agent $A + conductor $C)`.
- No config/trial opt-out was added — the task explicitly favored a single combined default, and this isn't something a trial should be able to dial back down.

## Decisions to flag for review

1. **Breaking validation, not just a changed default** (Change 1): an explicit `sandboxEgress: "unchecked"` alongside `sandbox: "landlock"` now throws instead of being silently overridden. If any existing bench config or trial YAML does this today, it will need updating (drop the explicit `"unchecked"`, or set `sandbox: "off"`).
2. **No opt-out flag for the combined cost cap** (Change 2) — defaulted to combined, per the task's stated intent, rather than gated behind a config flag for backward compat.

## Testing

- `npm test`: **555 passed, 28 skipped, 0 failed** (full suite, including new tests for both changes).
- New tests: `src/runner/__tests__/sandbox.test.mjs` (mode-based `sandboxEgress` default + rejection cases), `src/runner/__tests__/config.test.mjs` (updated), `src/runner/__tests__/collect.test.mjs` (`liveConductorCostUsd`), `src/runner/__tests__/run.test.mjs` (`driveUntilDone` combined-cap abort/no-abort cases across host.jsonl, completions.jsonl, both, and neither).

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent stale fast-loot state and handlers from remaining active and ensure grouped/master-loot filtering and queueing match the intended loot policy.

### Description
- Add `Loot:ResetQueue()` to detach `OnUpdate`, clear `LootSlots` with `wipe`, and reset `Grouped` state. 
- Reset queue state at the start of `Loot:LOOT_READY()` so prior handlers/queues cannot remain active.
- Make grouped/master logic reachable and enforce that grouped loot only queues items below `GetLootThreshold()` while non-grouped loot queues all unlocked slots by changing the queue condition to `if (not self.Grouped or Quality < Threshold) then`.
- Only install the `OnUpdate` handler when `#self.LootSlots > 0`, and ensure `OnUpdate` calls `ResetQueue()` when the queue becomes empty or after looting completes.
- Remove the reverse `table.remove` cleanup loop in favor of `wipe(self.LootSlots)`, and ensure disabling the fast-loot setting also calls `ResetQueue()`.

### Testing
- Ran a `python3` static assertion script that verified `LOOT_READY`/`OnUpdate` invariants and handler/queue placement, which passed.
- Ran `git diff --check` to validate the working tree and formatting, which reported no issues.
- Confirmed repository changes show the updated `HydraUI/Elements/Loot.lua` and no outstanding diff errors.

body:
### Motivation
- Prevent internal/healthcheck telemetry from generating sessions and detections while preserving raw telemetry for forensic inspection.
- Establish a simple, stable schema (schema version 1) and a separate ingestion timestamp so normalized documents are typed and auditable.
- Replace fragile dynamic-mapping reliance with explicit Elasticsearch templates and add a safe operator workflow to remediate historical loopback-derived derived-data.

### Description
- Add a reusable telemetry rules module with loopback detection using Python's `ipaddress` and a `SCHEMA_VERSION = "1"` marker (`backend/app/services/telemetry.py`).
- Filter internal/loopback events (legacy loopback or `trapsig.internal == true`) before session reconstruction and attach `trapsig.schema_version` to derived sessions and detections (`backend/app/services/processor.py`).
- Update the Python reference normalizer to emit `event.ingested` (UTC ISO-8601), set `trapsig.schema_version`, mark `trapsig.internal`/`trapsig.internal_reason` for loopback sources, and coerce ports/MQTT packet types to integers (`backend/app/services/normalizer.py`).
- Add Logstash final validation (`elk/logstash/pipelines/90-validation.conf`) to enforce required fields, resolve `%{...}` interpolation failures, validate enumerations and integer bounds, and tag/route invalid records to dead-letter indices; adjust output routing so dead-letter indices receive parse/validation failures (`elk/logstash/pipelines/99-output.conf`).
- Provide composable Elasticsearch index templates for `trapsig-events-*`, `trapsig-dead-letter-*`, `trapsig-sessions`, `trapsig-detections`, and `trapsig-experiments` with explicit field mappings and single-node settings (`elk/elasticsearch/index-templates/*`), plus an idempotent install script and one-shot `elasticsearch-setup` Compose service (`elk/elasticsearch/setup/install-templates.sh`, `docker-compose.yml`).
- Align analytics aggregations to the explicit mappings (remove reliance on `.keyword` subfields) and exclude internal loopback events from analytics queries (`backend/app/api/analytics.py`).
- Surface dead-letter volume in `/system/status` and ensure missing dead-letter indices return zero instead of failing the endpoint (`backend/app/api/health.py`).
- Add a safe maintenance command that is dry-run by default and deletes only loopback-derived records from `trapsig-sessions` and `trapsig-detections` when `--confirm` is provided (`backend/app/tools/cleanup_internal_derived.py`).
- Document the schema version, `@timestamp` vs `event.ingested` semantics, internal classification, dead-letter behavior, templates, and cleanup procedure (`docs/EVENT_SCHEMA.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`).
- Add unit/integration-style tests covering loopback handling, normalization fields and types, template presence, Logstash routing expectations, analytics contract, dead-letter visibility, and cleanup dry-run/confirm behavior (`tests/ingestion/test_telemetry_integrity.py`).

### Testing
- Ran targeted tests with `python -m pytest -q tests/ingestion/test_telemetry_integrity.py tests/backend/test_processor.py tests/ingestion/test_normalization.py tests/ingestion/test_pipeline_contracts.py` which returned **19 passed**.
- Ran the repository test suite; the run shows the repository-wide suite passes except for a known unrelated test mocking mismatch: `tests/backend/test_api.py::test_collection_endpoints_use_stored_schema_sort_fields` (this mock does not accept the `missing_index_is_empty` kwarg) reported as a pre-existing failure during verification.
- Performed static checks including `git diff --check` and Python compilation of modified modules; Docker-based live integration (Logstash/Elasticsearch template PUT and mapping inspection) was not executed because Docker is not available in the execution environment.

body:
## Summary

`shipit` described `version-bump` as generic and deciding "from project context". In fact, `version-bump` decides from `.github/scripts/version-bump-required.sh` and stops when a project lacks that script. `shipit`'s description and land-sequence stop list now name `version-bump`'s actual outcomes and stop cases. `shipit`'s behavior is unchanged.

`version-bump` step 1 also hardcoded `origin/main`, while step 0 resolves `$DEFAULT` and forbids guessing `main`. Step 1 now uses `origin/$DEFAULT`.

This is one of 22 independent PRs from a prompt audit of the agent and skill files, which checked them against current Claude models and for drift between files. Each PR is built from `main`, and every pair merges without conflict (`git merge-tree`, 231 pairs, 0 conflicts), so they can land in any order.

**Versioning:** this changes the distributed runtime surface, so `/shipit` assigns a version at land time. On purpose, there is no `[Unreleased]` changelog bullet: the sibling PRs from the same audit would all insert at the same line and conflict. With `[Unreleased]` empty, `version-bump` derives the bullet when this lands.

## How to Verify

- `node --test tests/*.test.mjs` on this branch: 28 pass, 0 fail, 1 skipped. The skip is the paparazzi Playwright capture test, which needs a package this environment doesn't have. The suite includes the skill-path-reference check, which resolves every link and path this change touches.
- `git diff --check`: clean.
- Read the diff against the Summary. Each hunk maps to one stated fix.

**Not run:** `claude plugin validate .` and a live pipeline run.

## Merge risk

Two-way door. The change is limited to instruction text, with no data, deployment, or external effects. Recovery is `git revert` of the squash commit.

body:
## Summary
- Adds a Nix-native stand-in for FireConnect, which can't work here: it rewrites `~/.claude/settings.json` and `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json` in place, and both are read-only symlinks into the Nix store. The module writes the settings the CLI would instead. It ships inert — both harness flags default to `false`, so this commit changes no runtime behavior.
- Pins OpenCode to nixpkgs-unstable. The 1.18.30 in the weekly snapshot cannot run a single prompt, which blocked testing the gateway at all.
- Routine dependency refresh: `nix flake update` plus a Neovim plugin sync.

## Changes

### home-manager/programs/fireworks.nix (new)
- `enable` is a per-harness attrset (`claude`, `opencode`) so OpenCode can run on Fireworks while Claude Code stays on stock Anthropic. `anyEnabled` gates only the shared sops secret.
- Claude Code: `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` plus router assignments for the Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, Fable and subagent model slots, alongside the behavior tuning FireConnect applies (tool search re-enabled, Explore inherit cap disabled, server-side auto-mode off, telemetry off).
- OpenCode: a `fireworks-ai` provider block with context/output limits for the routers, which models.dev doesn't carry. Merges with the existing ollama provider.
- The API key is kept out of both generated configs, since they land world-readable in the Nix store and this repo is public. OpenCode reads the sops secret via `{file:...}` interpolation; Claude Code gets it from an `ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS` export in fish, as `settings.env` only holds literals.
- Declares no `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`: the gateway authenticates on `X-Fireworks-Api-Key` alone, and setting one makes Claude Code warn that a claude.ai session and an API key are both present.
- `sops.secrets` is declared only when enabled, so `nix flake check` still passes for anyone without the key in `secrets/secrets.yaml`.

### home-manager/programs/opencode.nix
- Pin `package` to `pkgs-unstable.opencode` (1.18.31), following the same pattern as `neovim.nix` and `codex`. 1.18.30 is built with a bun 1.4.2 that mis-splits the bundle, so `SystemPrompt.environment` dereferences an undefined node and every prompt fails with `undefined is not an object (evaluating 'a.name')` — surfacing in the TUI as "Failed to send prompt / Unexpected server error". It fails before any provider is contacted, so it reads as a credential problem and isn't one. Fixed upstream in 1.18.31 (anomalyco/opencode#48397). Drop the pin once nixpkgs-weekly catches up.

### home-manager/home.nix
- Import `./programs/fireworks.nix`.

### secrets/secrets.yaml
- Add the encrypted `fireworks_api_key` entry; re-encrypted with sops 3.13.3.

author: devnacho
body:
## Behavior

Add project-level `locator: { ambiguity: reject | first }`, enforced in the shared core resolver for click, fill, and remembered-element resolution.

- **Omitted** preserves published main behavior, including legacy repeated-control model picks. It is deliberately not an alias for `reject`.
- **Explicit reject** disables permissive duplicate-selection options and requires a uniquely justified target.
- **Explicit first** allows deterministic candidate-collection-order selection only within a conservative literal matching set. Complete control names/kinds and exact section, landmark, or complete peer-label constraints must consume the entire request. Unsupported qualifiers are not discarded.

First selection requires a validated non-none provider choice within the matching set, combined comparable probability >= 0.75, and confidence >= 0.3 when supplied. General low confidence, provider failures, incomplete observations, and stale targets are not permissions to act. Ordinal/contextual resolution remains intact. All first matches pass fresh-target validation; any candidate-surface change rejects the selection. Normal executor actionability checks remain unchanged.

Explicit policies bypass identity-only locator-cache entries, which cannot establish uniqueness or first-match order. Diagnostics expose `ambiguity_policy` cache bypass and `ambiguity_first` through the existing locator gate, now also projected into canonical JSON results. A gate records selection, not proof that an action executed.

## Verification

- `env -u TYPESAFE_API_KEY -u TYPESAFE_BASE_URL -u TYPESAFE_DEFAULT_MODEL pnpm test`: 667 passed, 86 skipped (optional browser/live suites).
- `SEDUM_BROWSER_INTEGRATION=1 pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/src/flow-runner.cache.integration.test.ts packages/core/src/step-executor.integration.test.ts`: 12 passed, provider credentials unset.
- `pnpm fixtures:verify`: 4 passed, recorded provider replies, no live API calls.
- `pnpm build`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, and `git diff --check`: passed.

Coverage includes omitted/reject/first distinctions, constrained duplicate subsets, explicit ordinals, kind/disabled filtering, split probability and confidence boundaries, fill/read, multi-batch collection order, malformed/failed providers, incomplete/stale observations, cache bypass, actual browser clicks, blocked actions, and canonical diagnostic projection. Chrome was installed locally because the existing default browser path did not recognize the missing-Chrome error as a Chromium-fallback condition.

## Integration notes

Independently based on published main at [1b957e4](https://github.com/sedum-dev/sedum/commit/1b957e4f5c80b7226cc3d61254e0a6bddfe1f3c2), not older local-main or uncommitted vision work. That published base already defaults repeatedMember to modelPick, hence the explicit compatibility distinction above.

Future vision-fallback integration overlaps locator.ts, flow-runner.ts, CLI config/run wiring, and docs/configuration.md. The new `ambiguity_rejected` gate can return before older repeated-member gates; a fallback attached only to those older gates will not see every explicit-policy rejection. Decide vision-versus-first precedence explicitly and preserve the shared refresh/actionability checks. No vision code, merge, or deployment is included.

author: disnet
body:
Adds `apple/`, a native SwiftUI reader for macOS 14+ and iOS 17+. It also includes a small backend change so the app can sign in natively.

## Backend: native sign-in handoff

The web app gets its session as an HttpOnly cookie, and the CLI gets it on a loopback port. A native app can only be reached on its custom URL scheme, and any other app on the device can register that same scheme. So the session never goes over the scheme; instead there is a PKCE-style handoff:

1. The app starts `GET /api/auth/login` with `native_challenge = base64url(SHA-256(verifier))`. The response carries `native: true` to confirm the server understood the challenge. The app won't open the auth sheet without it, because an older server ignores the challenge and would finish in the web app inside the sheet.
2. The callback stores a one-time code bound to that challenge. It redirects to `skyreader://auth/callback?code=…` with no cookie.
3. The app sends `{ code, verifier }` to `POST /api/auth/native/exchange` and gets back `{ sessionId }`.

The code:
- lives for 2 minutes;
- is deleted on the first exchange attempt, whether or not the verifier is right;
- is swept by the hourly cron along with expired `oauth_state` rows.

If the auth server returns an error during a native flow, the redirect goes back to the app scheme.

- **Needs migration `0088_native_auth_handoff.sql`**. It adds `oauth_state.native_challenge` and the `native_auth_handoff` table.
- The code is in `backend/src/routes/native-auth.ts`. The tests are in `backend/test/native-auth.spec.ts` and `auth-login.spec.ts`. The full backend suite passes.

## SkyreaderKit (Swift package, Foundation-only, tests run on Linux)

**Client:** covers auth, timeline, reading, bodies, subscriptions and saves.
- 503 `session_refresh_pending` responses are retried with the web client's backoff.
- A 401 signs the user out.
- Subscription records are decoded one at a time, so a single odd record, such as one with a null `feedUrl`, can't hide the rest.

**`Library`:** an observable store that follows the web client's model.
- Timeline:
  - one global `since_seq` + `generation` cursor;
  - the first load is paged, and its cursor is saved only after the last page arrives;
  - each feed keeps its newest 100 items, matching `ARTICLE_WINDOW_PER_FEED`, and saved items are never trimmed.
- Backfill: a followed feed with no local items gets a one-off `feeds/fetch`.
  - This covers feeds followed on another device, which sit below the cursor, and feeds the server hasn't crawled yet.
  - It fetches 10 feeds per sync, rotating the starting feed.
  - An empty success is remembered; a failure is retried on the next sync.
  - This is a port of the web client's `backfillMissingSubscriptions`.
- Read state:
  - local reads go into a saved queue and are sent to `mark-read-bulk` / `mark-unread` after a short debounce;
  - each change carries the time the reader acted as `updatedAt`;
  - changes from other devices arrive through `GET /api/reading/positions`, and a local change that hasn't been sent yet wins.
- Bodies: the item's own content, else `items/body`, else `extract`.
- Offline cache: everything is stored in `Application Support/Skyreader/library.json`.

**Tests:** 26 tests cover:
- paging and cursor commit;
- the read-state delta versus unsent local changes;
- persistence and trimming;
- backfill: the empty-versus-failed cases, and the per-sync cap and rotation;
- lossy subscription decoding;
- 503 retry and PATCH encoding;
- native login and callback handling.

## App

- **Sign-in:** native sign-in through `WebAuthenticationSession`, with the session stored in the keychain.
- **Debug builds:**
  - a **Server** picker: Production, Staging, or Local (`127.0.0.1:8787` for `./scripts/dev-local.sh`);
  - a sidebar label when the app isn't on production;
  - pasting a CLI session ID to sign in.
  - `NSAllowsLocalNetworking` permits plain HTTP to loopback.
- **Layout:** three columns.
  - Sidebar: folders (from `category`), feeds, unread badges and a failing-feed marker. standard.site publications are shown as not yet supported.
  - Article list: unread filter, mark all/older as read, and swipe actions.
  - Reader: serif body using DESIGN.md tokens.
- **Reader safety:** the `WKWebView` runs with **JavaScript off**. Clicked links open in the browser, and main-frame navigations other than the page's own are refused.
- **Saves:** save and unsave from the list or reader, a Saved list, and save-a-link.
- **Feeds:** add a feed from a site address (discovery), rename, move to a folder, unsubscribe.
- **Also:** settings for account and sync, and macOS menu commands with shortcuts (⌘R, ⇧⌘U, ⌘D, ⌘↩).

## Build and CI

- `project.yml` is an XcodeGen spec. The `.xcodeproj` and the Info.plists are generated and gitignored.
- `.github/workflows/apple-ci.yml` runs the kit tests on Linux and unsigned `xcodebuild` builds of both targets on `macos-15`, only for PRs that touch `apple/`.
- Docs: `apple/CLAUDE.md` (including testing against a local backend), and the sign-in modes in `backend/CLAUDE.md`.

## Testing notes

- The macOS app has been run against a local backend, and native sign-in round-trips there. After the first sync only one feed appeared; that was the local backend's empty database, not the app. Its bugs are fixed in this PR: the missing backfill, and a list decode that one odd record could fail.
- Native sign-in against staging or production needs this backend change deployed. Until then, debug builds can sign in to production with a CLI session ID.

## Not yet

standard.site documents, highlights and notes, linkblog sharing, channels, OPML import, a share extension, an app icon, and signing/TestFlight.

author: jakejackson1
body:
## Summary

Backport of #1754 for 6.17.3.

The background PDF queue is built on Gravity Forms' `GF_Background_Process`, and its constructor registers AJAX, cron, multisite and uninstall hooks. Gravity PDF built three separate queues on every request: in the installer, the uninstaller and the background-processing setup. After each dispatch it built another, so those hooks were registered three or four times over.

The plugin now builds one queue in `Router::init()` and shares it. After a dispatch the queue is emptied rather than replaced, because Gravity Forms before 2.9 doesn't empty it when saving.

Unlike #1754, `Model_Install`'s constructor keeps its queue parameter, so its public signature doesn't change in a patch release. It now receives the shared queue.

## Try it

From the plugin directory inside the wp-env tests container:

```bash
vendor/bin/phpunit -c phpunit.xml.dist --filter '/Test_Bootstrap|Test_Controller_Pdf_Queue|Test_Installer|Test_Uninstaller/'
```

## Test plan

- [ ] The tests above pass
- [ ] Turn on Background Processing, submit a form whose notification attaches a PDF: the email arrives with the PDF
- [ ] Resend that notification from the entry list: it arrives with the PDF again

<details>
<summary>More info</summary>

**Differences from #1754.**
- `Model_Install::__construct()` still takes `Helper_Pdf_Queue $queue`. On `development` the parameter is dropped because the model never used it, which is a signature change for 7.0. Here `Router::installer()` passes the queue from the singleton instead, so no extra queue is built and nothing that constructs `Model_Install` breaks. `test-installer.php` and `test-uninstaller.php` are untouched as a result.
- The tests go in this branch's `tests/phpunit/unit-tests/` files and are tagged `@since 6.17.3`.

**Where the queues came from.**
- `Router::installer()`: passed to `Model_Install`, which never used it
- `Controller_Uninstaller::get_instance()`: passed to `Model_Uninstall`
- `Router::async_pdfs()`: passed to `Controller_Pdf_Queue` and registered in the singleton
- `Controller_Pdf_Queue::reset_queue()`: a new one after every dispatch

**Now.**
- `Router::init()` builds the queue straight after the singleton and registers it there.
- `installer()` and `async_pdfs()` read it from the singleton, and `Controller_Uninstaller::get_instance()` reads it through `GPDFAPI::get_mvc_class()`, like its other dependencies.
- The queue still has to be built on every request, because its AJAX and cron healthcheck hooks must exist when the async request comes in.

**`reset_queue()`.** It calls `$this->queue->data( [] )`. GF 2.9's `save()` clears `$this->data` itself, but GF 2.6's doesn't, and Gravity PDF supports GF 2.5+. `data()` has been public on `WP_Async_Request` all along.

**Verification.**
- `test_pdf_queue_is_built_once` counts the AJAX handlers one `Router` registers, and `test_dispatch_queue_empties_the_queue` checks the queue is emptied after a dispatch. Both fail on `hot-patch-6.17.3` without the fix.
- The mocked `save()` in `Test_Controller_Pdf_Queue` now records the tasks it was given. The resend test used to read the mock after dispatch, which only worked because `reset_queue()` swapped the queue out.
- Full PHPUnit suite locally: 1273 tests. The only failures are 3 errors and 2 failures in `Helper\Mpdf\Test_Request`, which fail the same way on an untouched `hot-patch-6.17.3` checkout (a local `vendor_prefixed/` build artifact). The touched classes also pass on multisite.

</details>

body:
Build 041 calibration showed the win-rate p-value leaked: with clustered events most scrambled runs produced a false survivor, and with every edge set exactly at cost (worthless) ~80 hypotheses per run survived.

- src/science/bootstrap.ts: studentized circular moving-block bootstrap of the net-of-cost mean, max over horizons (accounts for horizon choice), blocks of 20 with shared draws across horizons, 4,999 resamples with safe early stopping, and a 160-event minimum per horizon.
- Discovery Test stores the bootstrap result; a positive mean without enough independent events is INCONCLUSIVE (existing retry cooldown). Price series are cached per asset within a run.
- FDR uses the bootstrap p-value. Pre-042 PASS results are not judged on the old rule; their hypotheses return to PROPOSED for retest.
- Calibration: adds the new rule, an at-cost null, heavier clustering, merges exact-duplicate hypotheses (mirror-image pairs), and lists the strongest real-data candidates.

Synthetic calibration: worthless-edge runs with any final survivor fall from 100% to 2.5-7.5%; power is lower for marginal edges (documented).

No trading authority is added or changed.

body:
Mario: *"Are all images for all features in the website up to date?"* and *"There are more games now."*

**No, and the gap was an app rather than a game.** Of the 33 items on the shelf, 32 had a card and a screenshot. **NOTES had neither** — it is the ninth app, it shipped in 1.13.26, and it came from a real person's request (card #508).

The three games that landed in the last nine days, **Hearts, Hex and Underhand**, already have cards and 1x images.

## The check that exists to catch this passed anyway

`host-tests/site/shelf_coverage.py` was written after Sudoku and Get Books shipped through eleven releases with nothing on the site. Its own docstring says so. It passed on trunk with Notes missing.

It asked whether the title appears anywhere in `index.html`. The page contains the word "Notes" exactly once — inside the **Instapaper card's alt text**, describing an invented saved article called *"Notes on building a compiler"*. A screenshot's own caption answered for a missing app.

It now asks for the shape the site actually promises: an `<article>` whose `<h3>` is the title, carrying a shot. A card with no image reports separately from no card at all. The README half is unchanged — it is a prose table and naming the thing is all it owes.

    $ python3 host-tests/site/shelf_coverage.py <trunk>
    the app NOTES is on the shelf and has no card on the site
    $ python3 host-tests/site/shelf_coverage.py <this branch>
    $

## The card

The shot is a packing list open mid-use: two items ticked, struck through and counted (`4 LEFT OF 6`), four still to go, `ADD` and `CLEAR DONE` below. Seeded by writing three Markdown files into the agent card's `/notes`, which is the app's own storage format — nothing staged, nothing drawn.

The prose claims only what was on screen. The phone route exists in the firmware (`CrossPointWebServer`, `WAITING FOR YOUR PHONE`) but I did not exercise it, so the card does not mention it. Worth adding once somebody confirms the flow.

## Nothing else replaced

**Wallpapers** was spot-checked, because I reshot it on 2026-09-20 and its app has taken 15 commits since — more than any other app in that window. Its entry screen is the same offer it was then, so the gallery shot behind it stands.

## Verified

- `CHECKSH-VERDICT: host-green-device-skipped`
- 289 of 289 site checks pass
- The Notes card looked at rendered on the page beside Wikipedia and Calculator

**Not verified:** whether the other 31 shots still match their apps. That is a mid-use reshoot of each, not an audit, and it is not in this PR.

author: camshaft
body:
## What

Fleet TOML-config mandate (**seq-1377**, tracker #159, board #166): daemons take their config from `--config`, never env vars. capmeshd already used `--config` for everything **except log verbosity**, which came from the `RUST_LOG` env var (injected by the NixOS module as `environment.RUST_LOG`).

## Change (capmeshd only)

- `Config` gains a `log` field — a `tracing` env-filter directive (`info`, `capmeshd=debug,info`, …), default `"info"`.
- `main` reads `--config` for the directive and inits tracing from it (`EnvFilter::new(cfg.log)`) instead of `try_from_default_env()`; a missing/unparseable config still brings logging up at `info`.
- The NixOS module renders `logLevel` into the TOML `log` key and **no longer sets `environment.RUST_LOG`**.
- The `nixos-module-render` gate now asserts the rendered TOML carries `log = "info"` **and** that no `RUST_LOG` env var is set — locking the no-env-var invariant.

## Scope / coordination

capmeshd only. The `nmidid` and `surfaced` conversions under the same mandate are coordinated with **v-nmidid** / **v-surfaced** on board #166.

## Gate

`cargo test -p capmeshd` + `cargo clippy -p capmeshd --all-targets -D warnings` + real `nix flake check` (module-render rebuilt with the new assertions) all green.

body:
## 改动类型

- [x] 新功能（新页面 / 新选项 / 新能力）
- [x] Bug 修复（有用户可见行为修正）
- [x] 文档改动

- [ ] CI 流程改动
- [ ] 杂项（脚本 / 工程化 / 版本号）
- [ ] 其他

## 🔗 关联 Issue / PR

None

## 💡 背景与方案

新建、历史恢复与多 Tab 共用会话启动链路，异步准备和建联期间的页面切换容易使提交归属、订阅时机与图片清理脱节。本次最终采用前端预分配正式 SessionID 的方案，用明确的新建／恢复意图区分流程，并将会话身份与连接身份分开管理。

- 输入框使用 `uuidv4` 预分配正式 SessionID，新建请求直接携带 `TimelineSessionID`；历史恢复使用已有 ID。每次连接另用独立 `streamToken`，避免旧连接回调影响重试后的连接。
- 新建提交立即呈现首问和目标会话；握手完成后登记正式 store、接入桥接订阅并处理缓冲事件，再发送一次首问。历史恢复等待首批历史完成后继续发送，失败不误发首问。
- AI Agent 多 Tab 下，切换欢迎页或历史不会取消原 Tab 的建联；凭预分配 ID 直接定位已打开或建联中的 Tab，避免重复打开及后台连接完成后抢占当前视图。移除等待后端分配 ID 的页面导航流程。
- 图片从上传起保存到正式 SessionID 对应目录，不再复制采纳或替换目录。图片转换／写盘未完成时拦截按钮和回车提交，完成后重新读取编辑器正文及附件；取消未完成的新会话时等待在途写盘结束再清理，失败重试保留所需图片。
- 历史列表仅订阅已注册 store，不为读取运行状态创建占位。未绑定会话切换运行模式只更新本地设置，不发送空 SessionID 热补丁。
- 共享嵌入式 Provider 的新会话在注册完成后订阅桥接事件，修复提前 `ensureSession` 占用 ID 导致启动失败的问题；历史订阅由当前选中会话维护，仅新建触发绑定订阅回调，避免旧历史恢复完成后覆盖新选择的会话订阅。补齐 Fuzzer、YakRunner、知识库等入口的真实启动链路回归测试。
- 补齐连接提示国际化，以及并发、取消、重试、历史补载、图片生命周期和页面导航测试；更新中文多行提交信息规范。

## 影响范围

影响 AI Agent 的新建、历史恢复、重试、取消、图片附件及多 Tab 操作，以及共享聊天 Provider 的 History、Fuzzer、YakRunner、知识库等嵌入式入口。保留一级菜单多开 Tab 和历史会话复用已有 Tab 的行为。

会话 ID 由前端生成并传给后端，不要求后端重新分配 ID。兼容 pong 未携带 SessionId 的响应；若返回非空且与请求不一致的 ID，则拒绝错误绑定。

本分支已 rebase 到最新 origin/master；保留 master 的删除当前会话后返回欢迎页，以及切回 Tab 刷新历史的行为。

本轮验证（HEAD：`c2d36461eec33aa91295e5c1e28f6bff17e48b97`；基线：`origin/master`，`4fb8f3f89a7a31a3afce5273871759d453338d2d`）：

- 主渲染端 `yarn type-check` 通过。
- 按 CI 规则选择相关测试，仓库根执行 `yarn test:vitest <相关测试文件> --run`：84 个文件、706 个用例全部通过。
- `git diff --check origin/master...HEAD` 通过。
- 页面导航用例覆盖已有／建联中 Tab 定位、读取最新缓存、关闭后重开及连续导航；嵌入式回归保留 Provider → 启动 Hook → IPC Hook → Controller 的真实调用链，用模拟 IPC 回包控制时序。
- 新增回归覆盖普通历史切换、断连后发送问题恢复并切换会话、恢复返回错误和恢复响应缺少游标；确保当前 B 会话继续接收事件，迟到的 A 会话不会改写工具页，恢复失败不会发送问题。
- 修复验证时执行过三种定向变异：恢复无条件绑定回调、跳过新建订阅、跳过历史选择订阅，均被测试检出；变异代码已还原。
- 本轮未重新启动应用进行 UI 或跨平台性能测试。

## 代码评审结论

**结论：可以合并**（正确 6 项 / 问题 0 项（P0 0 项 / P1 0 项）/ 警告 2 项）

审查本分支相对 origin/master 的全部 13 个提交、61 个变更文件，重点检查源码、类型、调用链与测试，样式和文案抽检；无依赖或运行、构建配置改动。旧 P1 页面导航测试缺口、嵌入式新会话提前订阅导致的启动失败，以及历史恢复迟到回调覆盖当前桥接订阅的问题均已修复并有回归覆盖。

## 建议合并前修复的问题

author: larsbx
body:
Three commits:

1. **Tooling.** `experiments/scripts/spectral.py` collects the Fourier and Ramanujan-sum helpers, parameterised by `q` and by the singularity profile. `bridges_spike.py` now imports them, and its JSON output is byte-identical. `kappa_sweep.py` gains `--jobs`. `jump_law.py` is the next-move-2 analysis.
2. **Results.** New data `kappa_q2003.json` (1001 bulbs, FFT route) and `jump_law.json`, and register entry **V33** in both registers. The finite register uses forms T + S and passes `audit_limits`.
3. **A review fix.** The `|δ| log|δ|` profile is now tested jointly with its `1/m²` companion. As a result it is disfavoured, not refuted, and the log amplitude is recorded as model-dependent.

## V33: what `q = 2003` shows, compared with `q = 1009`
| | Finding |
|---|---|
| (a) | The coefficient tail **halves** when `q` doubles. Sampling noise would shrink by only √2, so this is a deterministic `1/q` term |
| (b) | **Jump law.** In the lowest window, `J·q'²` agrees with `q = 1009` within 0.01. The best-conditioned slope over `q' = 3…10` is **−1.97**, but other windows give −2.7 to −1.5, and the slope moves with `q`. So `q'^{-2}` holds within a factor 1.5, and the exponent is not settled |
| (c) | **`Re κ` has log-type singularities, with a V part.** At equal parameter counts, log + V beats `|δ| log|δ|` + V in 7 of 8 window × `q` fits; the exception is the tail-dominated top window at `q = 1009`. The log amplitude depends on the model: `≈ 0.006/q'` in the log-only fit, `0.001–0.006/q'` with the V companion. It agrees between the two `q` within 0.0015 in both fits, but is not identified |
| (d) | **Not a one-sided holomorphic boundary value.** That would force `D/(J/π) = 1`. The measured ratio is 0.03–0.70 in every fit, nearly the same at both `q`, and rises with `q'` |
| (e) | **Brjuno-type organisation.** A truncated Brjuno sum `B_T(x*)` is the best singular regressor. Beyond 8, 16 and 32 smooth modes it removes 31, 19–20 and 12–16% of the residual sd, against at most 14, 7 and 10% for fixed-weight log sums over all rationals. Its amplitude is not identified |

## Corrections
- **V31c** (added in #24) called `|δ| log|δ|` "the conjugate profile of a jump". The harmonic conjugate of a jump is `log|δ|`. The wording is struck and corrected, and so is the same claim in `docs/bridges-spike.md`.
- **C14″** now reads: log type with a V part, a model-dependent amplitude, Brjuno-type organisation; `|δ| log|δ|` disfavoured.
- **Next move 2** is marked done at `q = 2003`. Next: `q = 4001`, a spectral basis with Brjuno weights, and pinning down the Brjuno amplitude.
- A bug in my first draft of `jump_law.py` is fixed before this PR. It evaluated the Brjuno sum at `p̄/q` instead of `x* = |x̃|`.

## Checks
- `pytest tests/`: **14925 passed**, with `tests/test_spectral.py` (+33). It covers Ramanujan-sum identities, the Brjuno sum at the golden mean, and recovery of two-family amplitudes by the joint fit.
- `tools/audit_limits.py`: passed
- `tools/audit_estate_layout.py`: passed
- Every V33 figure was re-checked against `jump_law.json`

body:
## Summary
One skill per commit, tuned only on the tuning (non-holdout) queries, holdout checked once per candidate; before/after numbers are in each commit message.

| skill | tune P/R before → after | holdout P/R before → after |
|---|---|---|
| router | 1.00/0.60 → 1.00/0.70 | 1.00/0.00 → 1.00/0.00 |
| standards | 1.00/0.70 → 1.00/0.80 | 0.00/0.00 → 0.00/0.00 |
| learn | 1.00/0.70 → 1.00/0.90 | 0.50/0.17 → 1.00/0.17 |
| intel | unchanged (0.80/0.40) | unchanged (1.00/0.00) |

- **router**: picks the best skills *and their order*; applies to work with several steps where no skill is named, to "which sequence of skills / where to start", and to projects where more than one installed workflow could fit. Shorter (594 chars).
- **standards**: imperative lead (use before calling work done or ready to merge, and when reviewing); names the general items (one purpose per change, commit messages, tests, security, architecture decision records) apart from the per-role principles.
- **learn**: one note per lesson/preference/convention/term/fact, scoped to a role, project or skill (how the CLI applies them).
- **intel**: five rewrites (imperative, shorter, deduplicated phrases) all scored lower on tuning queries, so it stays as is.

Why holdout recall barely moves: the proxy ranks the core skills against ~150 registry descriptions that average ~68 characters, while the core descriptions are ~550-650; BM25 length normalization plus the top-3 cutoff put most held-out phrasings at rank 5-10. I did not shorten descriptions past the point of clarity to chase that. A real-agent run (`--agent claude`) against the edited skills is the better check.

## Test plan
- [x] pytest (floors on tuning queries), validate, lint, build --check (dist regenerated), check_versions, privacy_guard
- [x] all descriptions < 1024 chars, model-neutral

author: kixelated
body:
## Problem

IETF peers without the MoQ Hidden setup option could not discover dot-prefixed namespaces. Rust also measured hiddenness from authorization scope heads, exposing `.stats/node` to an empty-prefix request when the publish grant was `.stats/**`.

## Approach

Negotiate filtering in both publishers, for solicited and unsolicited discovery. Rust keeps a private request-relative visibility prefix through scoped and mounted origin cursors. Supplemental subscriptions avoid duplicating namespaces already advertised unsolicited. Update the feature draft and reader docs, and remove the completed quest.

## Impact

- Public API: none.
- Wire: IETF peers without Hidden receive all authorized namespaces; declared peers retain per-subscription filtering. No encoding changes. MoQ Lite is unchanged.

## Alternatives

Filtering emitted paths alone would lose the original path of covering routes. Keeping visibility inside the origin cursor preserves scope and mount behavior.

## Validation

`just check` passed, including 4,616 affected Rust tests, capture/play feature tests, JavaScript builds/types, and common checks. `just drafts check`, `quest check`, and all 32 `just test interop --all` publisher/subscriber combinations passed. Focused JavaScript tests passed, including all 16 legacy/inline negotiation cases. The new Rust matrix reproduced the undeclared-peer failure before the fix and passes across drafts 14, 15, 16, 19, and 22. JavaScript covers legacy and inline discovery, unsolicited advertisements, scoped grants, and local readers filtering unexpected hidden paths.

## Follow-ups

None.

- Cliente nuevo sin vendedor con ID de Operam (sin `operam_id` o fuera del registro): `darDeAlta` devuelve `{ tipo: 'bloqueo', motivo: 'sin-vendedor-operam' }` en dos capas (`mensaje` con el nombre y la salida, `detalle` tecnico), sin `clienteId` y con cero escrituras.
- Subida de cotizacion: 422 con codigo `VENDEDOR_SIN_ID_OPERAM`, el documento sale como PRE con motivo propio `sin-vendedor` (mismo trato que `sin-lista-precios`, nunca el 503 de "fallo Operam"); chip "PRE: vendedor sin ID de Operam" en el Historial.
- Alta completa: 422 con el mensaje en dos capas.
- Domicilio nuevo de un Cliente Operam existente (#414): con persona unica en la cartera no se bloquea; sin ella y sin vendedor resuelto, se bloquea antes del POST de sucursal.
- Registro de vendedores ilegible (`listar()` lanza): bloqueo por falla con su propio texto ("No se pudo revisar el registro de vendedores: intenta de nuevo"), sin escribir nada y sin afirmar que falte el ID; toma el camino por defecto (503, PRE operam, Reintentar).
- Reutilizar un cliente sin domicilio nuevo y el upgrade fiscal: sin cambios.
- `/admin`: el texto junto a "ID Operam" ya no promete "el vendedor por defecto de Operam".
- `docs/arquitectura.md`: los dos quirks del `PUT /branches` medidos el 2026-09-25 (contacto `person_id` 0 y `br_post_address`) y la regla del bloqueo; una linea en CLAUDE.md.

## Tests

16 nuevos (11 en `test/alta-cliente.test.js`, 2 en `test/alta-sin-vendedor-api.test.js`, 2 en `test/admin-id-operam-texto.test.js`, 1 en `pipeline-logica.test.cjs`). Cinco pruebas existentes daban de alta con un usuario fuera del registro: se arreglaron dando `salesman: 2` al fixture, sin excepciones en la condicion. Suite: 4759 pass en main, 4774 pass en la rama, 0 fallas.

## Revision (Standards y Spec): aprobada, sin violaciones duras

## Por que requiere ojos humanos (no se fusiono AFK)

Cambia la secuencia de escrituras hacia Operam:
1. Guardas nuevas antes de `crearClienteDirecto` y `crearBranchCliente`.
2. El PUT de configuracion comercial (`sales_type`) del cliente reutilizado se movio DESPUES del POST del domicilio nuevo (necesario para que el bloqueo no deje nada escrito). Efecto: si el POST de sucursal falla, la configuracion comercial ya no queda aplicada antes del fallo; el reintento la aplica.
3. El POST de sucursal ahora siempre lleva `salesman` (el de la cartera o el de la solicitud).
Ademas, el camino "registro ilegible" solo se prueba a nivel modulo: sin `DATABASE_URL` no se puede hacer fallar `listar()` en una prueba HTTP.

## Hallazgos de la revision que no se atendieron

| Hallazgo | Que pasa si se ignora | Por que se deja |
|---|---|---|
| Reorden de la configuracion comercial despues del domicilio nuevo | Si el POST de sucursal falla, la lista de precios no queda aplicada hasta el reintento; cambia el orden de pasos en el panel | Lo exige "cero escrituras antes del bloqueo" |
| `registro-vendedores-ilegible` cae al 503 / PRE operam | El Historial lo etiqueta como fallo de Operam aunque la falla es de Neon | La fe de erratas pide texto propio y cero escrituras, no codigo HTTP propio; es pasajera y Reintentar si sirve |
| El 422 `VENDEDOR_SIN_ID_OPERAM` sigue ofreciendo Reintentar en el panel | El reintento no sirve hasta que un admin asigne el ID | Igual que `CLIENTE_SIN_LISTA_PRECIOS`; el issue no lo pide |
| El paso del bloqueo de cliente nuevo se llama `POST customer` sin haber POST | La fila "Crear cliente" del panel sale en error | Deliberado para que el panel lo muestre; el detalle dice que no se escribio nada |
| Tres motivos con nombre casi igual (`sin-vendedor` x2, `sin-vendedor-operam`) | Confusion al leer el codigo | Juicio de estilo |

author: jungjaehoon-lifegamez
body:
## What changes for the owner

The owner agent stops starting every turn with everything. It works one step at a time: it decides what the next step needs, fetches only that, looks, then decides the step after.

- **Index up front, the rest on demand.** A turn starts with each action's name and purpose (4,092 chars, was 6,477) and a standing prompt of 5,080 chars (was 8,611). The procedures (full report, recording, corrections, sources, files, wiki) are `help({topic})` texts, as Kagemusha's `help("full-report")`. An action's arguments come from `help({actions: [name]})` before its first call.
- **The full report is a delta on the ledger.** The procedure no longer prescribes 24 h of sources, the whole pipeline and 14 days of calendar.
- **Finding tools.** `source.recent` lists changed channels (key, count, latest line) and returns lines only for requested channels. `work.list` gains `due` (overdue / today / upcoming / unscheduled) and `changedBefore`.
- **Many items: settle and record one at a time.**
- **`judge` (Jev) is the owner's choice.** Registered only when `jev.enabled: true`; the standing prompt mentions it only then. Everything works without it.

## Evidence (2026-09-29, live)

- 14:42 full report: context 25.7k → 112k tokens in one turn; tool results 33,077 (`source.recent`), 19,258 (pipeline), 11,373 (help) chars; 218 s.
- 14:36 full report: timed out at 300 s after 26 tool calls.
- 14:53 cleanup: started at 119k tokens, hit CLI compaction (~57 s), 28 model calls, 15 empty name-guess searches, 0 writes before the 298 s timeout.

## Deleted / moved

- Standing prompt sections `## Runtime` procedures, `## Continuity and memory` corrections, `## Full report` → help topics (relocated verbatim, tests assert each procedure is in a topic and not in the prompt).
- Argument signatures removed from catalog lines (`actionSignature` stays for `help`).

## Checks

- standalone: 117 files / 1169 tests pass; typecheck, lint, prettier clean.
- Live check after deploy: one full report and one bulk cleanup with Jev **off**, reading steps, context growth and duration from the session transcript.

**Reviewed head:** `13f2082c30787e36d729b541d4648153784733a2` on baseline `c7514761db165458eb8faf91cb6a7ba8ea84f9ce`.

The specification and implementation now connect through stable rule IDs, real test IDs, fresh execution results, and explicit remaining assessment procedures.

### Inventory and mappings

`conformance/spec-v0.1.json` catalogs **46 mandatory statements** from Specification v0.1, preserving their exact text and normative strength. Each record includes ownership, mapped assertion scope, and the procedure/evidence still needed for a full assessment.

| Coverage | Statements |
|---|---:|
| Partially covered by automated tests | 25 |
| Explicit product/manual review | 8 |
| Concrete test or integration gap | 13 |

The partial mappings reference **35 distinct existing Vitest tests** across five files. These are reused tests, not 35 newly added application tests.

Example: `SPEC-8-003` binds approval to proposal identity/version/material parameters. Its mappings include `tests/components.test.tsx::blocks same-version changes to the target` and `tests/review-components.test.tsx::blocks changed content under the same proposal version`, with server-side canonical binding retained as required integration evidence.

### Machine-checkable behavior

- `python scripts/check_conformance.py` checks complete mandatory inventory, source text/strength drift, unique IDs, exact literal test declarations, required assessment fields and generated matrix consistency.
- `--write-matrix` regenerates `conformance/TRACEABILITY.md` from reviewed mappings. Counts are generated here rather than duplicated in the guide.
- `--run` executes mapped files with the installed Vitest JSON reporter, joins fresh file/title outcomes to requirement IDs, and writes `artifacts/conformance-results.json`.
- Missing, skipped, failed, ambiguous or unrecognized mapped results fail the run. A failed attempt cannot reuse a previous success report. Evaluated inputs are hashed before/after; changes during a run invalidate the evidence.
- Reports identify source commit, input hashes, run times, Node/Vitest versions, CI run, individual test results and remaining assessments. `automated_checks` and `product_conformance` are separate fields.
- Documentation CI checks traceability and Python regressions on every push/PR. React CI collects mapped evidence and now triggers on conformance/specification changes. Existing artifact upload includes the report.

### Final-head validation — passed

- [Documentation CI 36532847226](https://github.com/kochrisdev/TUN-Systemic-Design/actions/runs/36532847226): **success**. Inspected job `109290185380`: **32 Markdown files, 444 local link occurrences, 14 component exports, zero errors; all 50 existing documentation-checker tests and 49 new conformance-checker tests passed**. Traceability checked all 46 mandatory statements and 35 mapped IDs.
- [React CI 36532847263](https://github.com/kochrisdev/TUN-Systemic-Design/actions/runs/36532847263): **success**. All existing install/audit/token/typecheck/test/build/package/consumer/browser steps and the new mapped-evidence step passed.
- CI evaluated merge candidate `1ea85c73c29175c953ce9060a5bd6496a8410b99` against unchanged baseline.
- Downloaded final artifact `11017591781` and verified ZIP SHA-256 `5d70a426cfc37dfc059fbc4ccb2315e850c478a39fc97880a246ac2d75b5adb7`.
- Inspected `artifacts/conformance-results.json`: **35/35 mapped tests passed**, all 25 partially mapped statements have passing automated checks, and the other 21 remain explicitly unassessed by automation. Node `22.23.2`, Vitest `4.1.11`, CI run `36532847263`; no collection errors.
- Report SHA-256: `20e9f58e80285e09ca88e5b7575678705b1fe945640edc1b41b21bd0f27383c3`. Its input hashes match the reviewed specification, manifest and locally tested Python files.
- Local Python 3.13.5: 49 regression tests passed; Python 3.10 grammar parsing passed. Script blob `fb250ab616764b3c76844494b65725ec3a47fefb` and test blob `1d5105b29ce309bed7e941e9b6e01242b02dedd0` match the tested files.

### Review and documentation

Reviewed the complete eleven-file diff and all mapped assertions against the test sources. Added malformed enum/result tests so invalid inputs cannot leave an earlier successful report in place. Kept current coverage totals generated to avoid the documentation drift addressed in PR #10.

The conformance guide includes a scoped assessment worksheet: product scope/revision, requirement outcome, reviewer/date, evidence and justified non-applicability. Documentation index, scope, roadmap and changelog link to the working layer. The roadmap now calls for extending traceability and attaching pilot evidence rather than building an unspecified future mechanism.

### Scope

This initial profile covers mandatory sentences in numbered specification sections, retaining compound obligations. The RFC vocabulary section and two exact terminology-only sentences are excluded; standalone SHOULD/MAY recommendations and component-catalog requirements are future traceability expansion. The source locator supports unique literal Vitest titles; additional runners/dynamic titles need an adapter. Mapping relevance is reviewed, not inferred from names.

No full product assessment was performed: each partial rule states its residual review and each gap states concrete evidence to add. This is an assessable baseline, not an aggregate badge inferred from test presence.

The value-first root README, normative specification text, all canonical component/application code, existing application tests, dependencies, tokens, deployment configuration, CI permission levels and historical validation reports remain unchanged. The workflows add checks and triggers, not credentials or broader privileges.

author: cameronsjo
body:
This fixes two items from #596. **1. A stray or unclosed tag no longer breaks the reader layout.** On main, a stray `` in a doc (`"\n\nx"`) makes it through bluemonday. It closes the shell's `.doc-body` early, so the rest of the doc renders outside it (checked in Chromium). - **Parsing.** The new `balanceFragment` (`balance.go`) parses the sanitized body with `parseBody`. That runs `x/net/html`'s full-document `html.Parse` on a `…
` wrapper and takes the wrapper's children, plus anything a stray closer pushed out after it. - This is not `ParseFragment`, which turns off svg/math foreign-content breakout. With that off, `` would pass as well-nested while Chromium breaks out of it. - **Balancing.** If the source's tag stream already matches the tree, the body is returned byte-identical. - Otherwise it re-renders the tree, which is balanced by construction, and runs it back through the sanitizer. It repeats until the output stops changing, at most 4 passes. Escaped text is the last resort. - **Deep nesting.** A body nested deeper than x/net's 512-element limit is served sanitized but unbalanced, as on main, never as escaped text. That gap is #623. - **Void elements.** `hoistVoidChildren` works around an `x/net/html` quirk: `
` inside SVG produces a `
` with children, which `html.Render` refuses. - **Order.** Balancing runs after bluemonday and before `transformCallouts`. Callouts preserve balance, and balancing after them would re-sanitize away the icon's `aria-hidden`. A test pins this. - **Dependencies.** `x/net` moves from indirect to direct at v0.55.0, the version already in use. go.sum is unchanged. **2. Heading ids are generated in linear time.** goldmark's default `IDs.Generate` rescans suffixes from `-1` on every call, so it's quadratic. 8k duplicate headings took 5.4s to render, and scanning took as long again. - The new `headingIDs` keeps a set of the ids in use plus a suffix cursor per base slug. The base slug still comes from goldmark itself. - Both parse contexts, render and scan, use `newParseContext()`. - 32k duplicate headings now take about 0.18s for render plus scan. Refs #596. goldmark's internal quadratic cases stay open there. **Tests.** Each goes red under its mutation: - ids match goldmark's default over 10k random sequences; - linear time with 32k duplicates; - balance: stray, nested, unclosed and misnested tags, callouts, lists, and svg breakout (self-closed table, open table, `

`); - deep nesting renders as markup, not escaped text: a 300-deep list, 520 nested blockquotes and 600 ``; - a well-nested body is byte-identical; - 20k random tag soups; - a server test that parses the served page and checks that content stays inside `.doc-body`, with the nav and status bar outside it. **Verification** - `go build`, `go vet` and `go test ./...` pass, and `-race` passes on the new tests. CI is green. - Gate 2 (Opus security and code review) found two Important issues: the svg breakout and deep-nesting escape. Both are fixed. The delta review is clean. - The delta review compared this against Chromium: 305 targeted breakout shapes and 5,000 random sanitized docs gave 0 containment escapes and 0 served-stream mismatches. - Every return path serves sanitizer output or escaped text. - No polish marker was recorded because cadence-hooks isn't available here. Filed from review: #622 (an unclosed skip-content element hides the rest of the page; pre-existing) and #623 (deep-nesting residual). ## Release notes BEGIN_COMMIT_OVERRIDE fix(docs): keep a document's HTML inside the reader's content pane, as a browser parses it, even with stray or unclosed tags or HTML tags inside SVG; render duplicate headings in linear time END_COMMIT_OVERRIDE 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_01MHsB2SCt26cWBr6Ws9LiEH

author: roboclaw-bot
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes: Telegram E2E credential readiness fails on hosts that reject token-bearing local HTTP, even when the leased QA user and Telegram’s HTTPS Test Server are available.

## User Impact

Developers can run the canonical Telegram Test Server doctor without starting a local Bot API adapter. This changes QA tooling only, not production Telegram configuration. Full Gateway scenarios still require their local adapter, Gateway health checks, and (when selected) mock model server; this is not proof that those scenarios can run without local networking.

## Why This Change Was Made

The doctor now uses the runner’s existing lease-scoped JSON request over official Telegram HTTPS. Both the direct client and the retained SUT adapter use the existing Test Server path transformation. The unchanged leased-fetch lifecycle lives with its run scope and is shared by readiness, Gateway probes, and published-upgrade scenarios. User/bot identity checks, group readiness and repair, cancellation, and lease cleanup remain enforced. The adapter stays available for SUT routing and hold/reject fault controls.

Requested by and co-authored with Ayaan (@obviyus).

## Work sessions

- [Original discussion with @obviyus](https://team.openclaw.ai/chat/roboclaw/dashboard/cb21229b-a6be-42fa-be10-dbf778051bfe)

author: cameronsjo
body:
- **#1087:** a `tool_input` that failed its typed shape used to deserialize to `None`, so every guard allowed it. Two examples: `{"command":"git reset --hard","file_path":5}` and an array `command`.
  - `salvage_tool_input` now reads the object one field at a time, keeps the fields that parse, and records the dropped ones by fixed field name only.
  - When the dropped field is one a security-critical hook needs, dispatch fails closed with exit 2. For Bash that is `command`/`cmd`; for Write, Edit, MultiEdit and NotebookEdit it is the path, content and edit fields, or a `tool_input` that isn't an object.
  - The block message names the field, never its value. Non-critical hooks and `mcp__*` tools run on the salvaged input.
  - Nothing is coerced: an array `command` is not joined into a string.
- **#1076:** `verify-pr-autoclose` now picks its flow from parsed `gh pr` segments rather than a substring match.
  - The bare-merge `CurrentBranch` path was dead: gh refuses `-R` with no argument. It is replaced by `gh pr view --json number,url` in the session cwd, used only when the PR is in origin's repo.
- **#986:**
  - `warn-unreviewed-ready-flip` uses `BoundedGhRunner`, so a 2–5 s gh answer now leaves the nudge silent.
  - `verify-pr-autoclose` gets a new `DeadlineGhRunner`: up to 8 s per call and 25 s per flow, which fits its deliberate 10 s wait under the 30 s hook timeout.
- **#990:** panic stderr is now sanitized and capped at 400 characters, and keeps `(at file:line)`.
- **#939:** on Unix, `run_bounded_capped` starts each child in its own process group and SIGKILLs the whole group on timeout, overflow or a pipe that never drains. The reader retries on EINTR, and an abandoned flag stops a leaked reader. Every production `GitSpawn` match was already exhaustive, so the enum gains a doc rule instead.

`make ci` is green.

Closes #1087
Closes #1076
Closes #986
Closes #990
Closes #939

author: janwelker
body:
## Why

Kured cannot drain `freya`: `authentik-db-2` is the primary, and CloudNativePG's `authentik-db-primary` PodDisruptionBudget (`minAvailable: 1`) refuses the eviction regardless of the two replicas. Every attempt runs into the 15-minute drain timeout, the node is released and retried every half hour, and each attempt evicts the Ceph OSD on freya for the duration. Same shape as homelab-apps#67 for the single-instance clusters.

## What

`enablePDB: false` on `authentik-db`. With three instances the eviction takes the primary down and the operator fails over to a replica within seconds; `docs/platform/authentik.md` says so instead of claiming the primary switches over on its own.

## Verification

yamllint, markdownlint and `zensical build --strict` pass. After sync `kubectl get pdb -n authentik` is empty and Kured's next attempt on `freya` drains.

body:
Fixes from a review of the backend and frontend. Seat capacity, pool/ride consistency and fares were checked and found correct; these are the issues that turned up.

## Security
- **Open redirect:** `/login?next=/\evil.com` sent users off-site after sign-in. `next` is now parsed as a URL and must be same-origin.

## Correctness
- **Cancel vs. accept race:** a passenger cancelling as a driver accepted could lock ride → pool (deadlock risk) and record the wrong previous status. Cancel now locks pool then ride, re-checks the membership, and retries if the ride moved.
- **Accept after a pool empties:** a driver was told "Your trip is under way" when their last rider had just cancelled. A pool found cancelled under the lock no longer counts as their trip.
- **Co-riders by first name only,** as `docs/assumptions.md` says.

## Frontend
- `/passenger/rides/<not-an-id>` crashed; it now shows "Ride not found", and ride-detail queries have their own key space
- The waiting message no longer promises an automatic join

- Behind the Next.js rewrite, rate limits see the frontend's address, so they are effectively per email. Added to the known limitations in `docs/architecture.md`.

author: tas50
body:
## Description

`chocolatey_installer` with `action :uninstall` fails on every Chef 19 run with:

```
NoMethodError: undefined method 'exists?' for class Chef::Resource::File
```

### Why it breaks

The uninstall action checked for the Chocolatey bin directory with a bare `File.exists?(path)`. That's wrong in two ways:

1. **Constant lookup.** The action block is evaluated inside the `Chef::Resource` namespace, so a bare `File` resolves to `Chef::Resource::File` (the `file` resource), not Ruby's `::File`. Switching to `File.exist?` would *still* fail for the same reason.
2. **Removed method.** `File.exists?` was removed in Ruby 3.2, and Chef 19 ships Ruby 3.4.

The fix is `::File.exist?(path)`, which is how the rest of this resource already does it (e.g. `is_choco_installed?` on line 86). `chef-18` is not affected; this line doesn't exist there.

### Why the existing test missed it

The existing "Uninstalling chocolatey" spec calls `resource.action :uninstall`, which only *sets* the action and never runs it. It's also `:windows_only`, so it doesn't run on Linux/macOS CI at all.

The new specs run the action through the provider via `resource.run_action(:uninstall)` (the same path a recipe takes), with `powershell_exec` stubbed so they run on every platform:

- Chocolatey installed: the action converges, runs the removal PowerShell, and marks the resource updated.
- Chocolatey not installed: the action runs no PowerShell and does not mark the resource updated.

Both new specs fail on `main` with the `NoMethodError` above and pass with this change (verified on Ruby 3.4).

## Related Issue

None filed. Found while auditing test stubs against real method signatures.

## Types of changes

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## Checklist

- [x] I have run the pre-merge tests locally and they pass.
- [x] I have updated the documentation accordingly. (n/a)
- [x] I have added tests to cover my changes.
- [x] All new and existing tests passed.
- [x] All commits have been signed-off for the Developer Certificate of Origin.

author: kevinraymond
body:
Board #3324, phase 1: the live depth map from `XR_META_environment_depth` as a depth occluder, so things the scan does not know (an unscanned chair, a person, the wearer's own body, a moved object) hide the particles. Phase 2 (the map as a collision source for the sim) is not in this PR.

## What it does

- `crates/fosfora-xr/src/env_depth.rs` (new): the depth provider and its swapchain through the `openxr` raw function table, each two-layer D16 image wrapped as a wgpu texture, one acquire per frame at the predicted display time in the stage space.
- The eye pass draws one full-screen triangle first, right after the clear (compare Always, depth write on, color off). Each fragment looks the map up at the point 2 m along its eye ray, scales the depth camera's ray to the stored distance and writes that point's eye depth. No-data texels, distances under 0.2 m and points outside the depth fov are discarded.
- A gray diagnostic of the same pass (`envdepthshow`), and a numeric self-check (`envdepthcheck`) that reads a 40x40 grid of each layer back asynchronously and compares it with the room's boxes and the floor along the same rays, as read, rows flipped and columns mirrored.
- Provider creation that fails is retried every 5 s from the frame loop, up to 12 times.
- Hooks: `xr.rs` (extension, acquire), `gfx.rs` (image wrap, draw first in the pass), `app.rs` (knobs). No core change.

## Runtime facts (Quest 3, v207)

- The first launches failed at `xrCreateEnvironmentDepthProviderMETA` with `ERROR_RUNTIME_FAILURE`: the MR service (up 42 h) failed to create the 320x320 D16 depth swapchain for every client, the OS shell included. A reboot fixed it.
- Then: 4 images, 320x320 x 2 layers, hand removal supported and on, first frame 3138 ms after creation, near 0.1 m / far inf, layer 0 fov -54.0 / 40.0 / 44.0 / -55.0 deg, 720 acquires per 10 s, 0 errors.

## Cost (mode world, 72 Hz, room loaded, 60 s runs, App GPU ms median)

- Flux XR Room 400K: 9.25 baseline, 9.36 / 9.39 occluder, 9.20 diagnostic; 73 fps, 0 long frames throughout.
- Murmur XR World 40K: 10.11 baseline, 10.39 occluder; 72-73 fps.
- The reprojection costs 0.1-0.3 ms, inside run-to-run noise, so the occluder is on by default in `mr` and `world`. Full table in `docs/xr/MEASURED.md`.

## Check verdict

Texture row 0 is the bottom of the view (GL order from the runtime's own renderer). Read that way the map agrees with the scanned room to a median of +0.006 / +0.017 m (42 % of texels within 10 cm against 4 cm slabs and unscanned objects); read top-down the median was -0.12 to -0.17 m, columns mirrored worse still. `envdepthflipv` defaults to 0 accordingly.

## Worn gate: pending

An unscanned object, a person and the wearer's own body hiding the cloud; no halo on head turns; hands with removal on versus off.

## Knobs (read at startup)

```
debug.fosfora.envdepth 0|1        occluder (default on in mr/world, off elsewhere)
debug.fosfora.envdepthshow 0|1    gray diagnostic, 0 m black to 4 m white
debug.fosfora.envdepthhands 0|1   hand removal in the map (default 1)
debug.fosfora.envdepthnear 0.2    discard distance, m
debug.fosfora.envdepthflipv 0|1   texture row order (default 0: row 0 at the bottom)
debug.fosfora.envdepthcheck 0|1   the numeric self-check against the room's boxes
```

With `envdepth`, `envdepthshow` and `envdepthcheck` all 0 no provider is created.

author: hottahd
body:
## 変更理由

Closes #176。

`project()` の後に置かれた `set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING ...)` は、`project()` が既に空のキャッシュ項目を作っているため無効でした。その結果、**これまで全てのビルドが最適化なし・assert 有効**で走っていました。

- CMakeLists (miso と demo 7 つ): 未指定のときだけ `FORCE` で Release にする定型に変更 (#171 と同種の順序問題)
- Release では `assert` が消えるため、消えては困る検査を `std::runtime_error` に変更しました。
  - ファイル入出力の失敗 (`grid.hpp`, `time.hpp`, `mhd_checkpoint.hpp`, `rt_host.hpp`, `config.hpp`)。開けたかどうかに加え、読み出しが成功したか (空や途中で切れたファイルを受け入れない)、書き出しが成功したか (`close()` の flush まで含めて確かめ、途中までのファイルを黙って作らない) も検査します。`Time::save` は時刻ファイルの書き出しを確かめてから `n_output.txt` を進めます
  - config.yaml 由来の値 (`time.tend`, `time.dt_output` が正であること、`mhd.artificial_viscosity.ep`, `fh` が非負であること)。例えば `dt_output: 0` は `save_if_needed()` の条件を常に真にして毎ステップ出力し続けるため、Release で素通りさせたくないものです
  - インデックス範囲などの内部的な不変条件の `assert` はそのまま残しています
- `test_cpu.yml`: ユニットテストとデモのビルドを `Debug` と `Release` の matrix で走らせます。加えて、`-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` を渡さない既定の構成で `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE` が `Release` になることを検査するジョブ (`default-build-type`) を追加しました (#176 で壊れていたのがこの経路のため)

## 検証

| 項目 | 結果 |
| --- | --- |
| 既定の構成 | `CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release`、`-O3 -DNDEBUG` (変更前はフラグが `-std=gnu++17` のみ) |
| `-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug` の明示 | 尊重される (`-g`) |
| ctest (既定 = Release) | 12/12 pass |
| ctest (Debug) | 12/12 pass |
| clang-format | 違反なし |
| 磁気圏デモ 32³ CPU 2 ランク | 0.53 s/step → 0.10 s/step |

GPU は nvcc がビルドタイプによらずデバイスコードを最適化するため、ほとんど変わりません (磁気圏 32³ 2×RTX4090 で 3.6 s → 3.7 s、128³ で 3.7 s → 3.4 s。ホスト側のみの差)。

## 数値結果への影響

丸め誤差程度。`-O3` による浮動小数点演算の順序 (FMA の contraction を含む) が変わるため、ビット単位では一致しません。main を Release でビルドした結果と本ブランチの既定ビルドの結果は一致します。

## 別に見つかった問題 (この PR では直していません)

検証中に、**磁気圏デモが最適化なしのビルドで非決定的な結果を出す**ことが分かりました。同じ実行ファイル・同じ設定で 10 回走らせた結果です (32³, 2 ランク, CPU, t=30 まで)。

| ビルド | 正常 | 異常 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Release | 10 | 0 |
| Debug (最適化なし) | 4 | 6 |

異常時は 4 ステップで t=47.8〜48.9 に飛びます (正常は 96 ステップで t=30.17)。dt が 30 倍過大になっています。同じバイナリで結果が変わるので、未初期化メモリの読み出しが疑われます。main (この PR の前) を Release でビルドすると正常、本ブランチを Debug でビルドすると異常が出るので、**原因はビルドタイプであってこの PR の変更ではありません**。

この PR は既定を Release にするため、この問題を覆い隠す方向に働きます。別の問題として issue を立てて追う必要があります。容疑は `qq_argm` / `qq_rslt` の未初期化領域と、辺・角のゴーストセル (#184 が埋めようとしているもの) です。GPU 2 ランクで稀に解が壊れる現象とも関係しているかもしれません。

## この PR に含めなかったもの

- チェックポイントの目印 (`n_output.txt`) を全ランクの書き出し成功後に進める件は #192 に切り出しました。main に元からある挙動で、直すには集団通信を含む設計判断が要るためです。
- 磁気圏デモが最適化なしのビルドで非決定的な結果を出す件 (下記) も、この PR では直していません。

## レビュアーに特に見てほしい箇所

- どこまでを例外にするかの線引き (ファイル入出力の失敗と config.yaml の値まで。内部的な不変条件は `assert` のまま)
- CI で Debug と Release の両方を走らせる方針でよいか (これまで実質 Debug 相当で走っていたので、assert による検査も残す意図)
