body:
## Summary

Adds the **rotate-on-stall** mechanism to the `agents` skill's
`references/hooks-and-lifecycle.md` content (the `agents-skill` entity in
`charly.yml`) — the mechanism behind the umbrella `AGENTS.md` rule **"Subagent
lifecycle — one task per worker; rotate, never re-task"**
(`opencharly/opencharly#305`). That rule points here for MECHANISM DETAIL, but
this reference covered only **cross-task** reuse (finished worker → new task),
not the failure that motivated the rule: **repeatedly re-briefing a stalled
session**.

New `### Rotate on stall — stop a stalled session, spawn a fresh one`
subsection, adding:

- **The hard trigger** — no ARTIFACT after **two re-briefs**, or **~50 messages
  without a produced artifact** → STOP it and spawn a FRESH subagent with a
  clean brief; do not append a third correction.
- **Why re-tasking a stalled session fails** — the measured **7-hour /
  351-message** session that produced **no artifact** on a few-file change,
  while a **fresh** session with the same brief produced it directly.
- **Artifacts, never liveness** — an idle signal, a heartbeat, or "still
  working" is NOT progress; act only on a changed artifact.
- **The distinction from legitimate continue-same-task** — a CHANGES-REQUESTED
  fix round / rebase round is reuse; re-briefing a session that has stalled
  **without producing** is rotation.
- **The orchestrator's duty** — monitor by artifact and rotate on the trigger,
  mirroring the existing "orchestrator's bidirectional verification duty".
- **A cross-reference to the AGENTS.md rule** so the two cannot drift (one
  canonical statement in AGENTS.md, the mechanism here).

Discoverability: the entry `SKILL.md` Index row for
`references/hooks-and-lifecycle.md` now names **rotate-on-stall**, and the
reference's opening "Owns the …" sentence names it too. No new cross-reference
target is introduced (the `orchestration-model.md` reference already exists and
is linked relatively), so `charly docs generate` resolution is unaffected.

Closes #61.

## How tested

**Docs-only source entity.** The change is prose inside the `agents-skill`
`charly.yml` entity; the generated corpus is regenerated in the
`marketplace` leg (a separate refs-pin PR).

**(1) The `charly.yml` parses and the new content is intact** — the entity's
`content:` string is a valid YAML block scalar and the inserted section is
present:

```console
$ yq -r '."agents-skill".skill.references[] | select(.name=="hooks-and-lifecycle") | .content' charly.yml | grep -c "Rotate on stall"
1
$ grep -Pc '\t' charly.yml
0
$ git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD
57	4	charly.yml
```

**(2) The new content is discoverable in the reference and the entry index:**

```console
$ grep -n "rotate-on-stall" charly.yml
56:            | Delegation as fresh context; teammate context lifecycle; rotate-on-stall (stop a stalled session, spawn a fresh one); ...
363:                  rotate-on-stall, the sub-agent operational invariants, agent lifecycle
```

**(3) The cross-reference to the umbrella rule is present verbatim:**

```console
$ grep -F 'one task per worker; rotate, never re-task' charly.yml
                  lifecycle — one task per worker; rotate, never re-task"**
```

**(4) The change adds no structural surface beyond the YAML parse in (1).**
This is a **documentation-only** change: prose inside a `charly.yml` block
scalar. It adds no entity field, package section, service, or plan step, so the
repo's structural check has nothing new to assert. The merge gate for this repo
is the org-wide `charly/pr-validator` (`validate / validate`, required — named
in the repo's `AGENTS.md`); this repo ships no per-repo build workflow.

**Local generator confirmation (marketplace side).** `charly marketplace
generate --root . --out .` on the `marketplace` worktree (with a temporary
local stamp so the project loads) reproduced `origin/main` **byte-for-byte**
(empty `git status --porcelain` beyond the temporary stamp) — confirming the
generator is functional on this host; the projection of this source edit is the
marketplace leg.

The org-wide `charly/pr-validator` (`validate / validate`, required) reviews this
diff and body. (The per-repo `deploy.yml` marketplace drift gate was deleted
org-wide by `opencharly/.github#141` — the current gate is the required
validator.)

## Rulebook compliance

- **Rule 1 — never edit inside a submodule** — HOW: the edit is in the session
  worktree `.worktrees/subagent-rotate-stall/layer-charly-internals`; the tracked
  submodule checkout stays detached/clean.
- **Rule 2 — git via `git -C <absolute-path>`** — HOW: every git/gh action ran
  via an absolute `-C` / `--repo`.
- **Rule 3 — no nested `go.work`** — N/A — no Go workspace touched.
- **Rule 4 — sessions root at the umbrella; edits in a session worktree off
  fresh `origin/main`** — HOW: branched off freshly fetched `origin/main`.
- **Rule 5 — pin discipline** — N/A — no gitlink/pin in this leg (the
  marketplace leg pins only merged tags).
- **Rule 6 — policy B** — N/A — no distro gitlink.
- **Rule 7 — read the subrepo's own rulebook** — HOW: the repo's

- **Rule 8 — harness config parity** — N/A — no harness config changed.
- **Rule 9 — session-scoped ownership** — HOW: only this session's
  worktree/branch/PR touched; no other session's PR/worktree edited; the one
  issue (lci#61) is claimed by this session.
- **Rule 10 — before any update push, read the live state + write the body** —
  HOW: the repo's open PRs/issues were read; this body is written for the exact
  head `cf0a80d`.
- **Rule 11 — todo ledger** — HOW: the session ledger tracks the source leg and
  the marketplace projection leg.

Ground rules:

- **R1 (RCA every anomaly)** — HOW: no anomaly surfaced; the change is inert
  prose in a YAML block scalar, and the repo's merge gate (`charly/pr-validator`)

- **R5 (delete legacy completely)** — HOW: additive detail; the three replaced

- **R6 (git safety)** — HOW: no force-push, no hook bypass, no direct push to

- **R7 (prove the gate, not the plan)** — HOW: the grep/numstat evidence above

- **R10 (fresh proof by change class)** — HOW: Documentation-only; the required

## Change classification

author: tomorrowisanotherday
body:
OpenAI API-key accounts currently have no upstream usage display even when the provider exposes Sub2API's `/v1/usage` API. This change detects that response and adds upstream requests, tokens, recorded cost, available quota windows, expiry and refresh status to the account table, alongside clearly labeled local usage.

Based directly on deployed v0.2.8 commit `fd80b08c90b55edcad5b00171b53f08721d30da1`; this PR targets `deployed/v0.2.8` so it contains only this feature.

- Reuses server-side account credentials, proxy, TLS profile and destination validation; disables redirects and limits response size.
- Adds credential-aware caching, request coalescing, manual refresh and stale-data/error display. Known official provider hosts are excluded; response validation confirms compatibility.
- Preserves Codex OAuth usage and scheduling. Simple-mode zero balances are not treated as exhausted credit. Usage belongs to the upstream API key, not the underlying Codex subscription.
- Adds English/Chinese strings and documents behavior/build instructions. No database migration or production deployment.

Validation:
- 68 frontend tests passed across the new cell, existing account cell and locale completeness suites.
- New Go adapter tests passed with the race detector.
- Related account usage, OpenAI usage and upstream billing probe unit tests passed.
- Frontend type checking/production build, ESLint for changed application files, Wire regeneration and Go server build with embedded frontend passed.
- Read-only live upstream check confirmed `/v1/usage` compatibility with the probe User-Agent; no production configuration was changed.

author: oleksii-debug
body:
## Root cause

The production AiOrchestrator re-selects canonical route eligibility after asynchronous route-quality lookup, which is correct. But a route can become newly eligible while the lookup is pending (for example when durable backoff expires). That route was absent from the resolver request, so applying the returned partial snapshot falsely treats it as MISSING quality evidence.

With equal owner policy/priority, an originally-eligible PASS route could then jump ahead of the newly eligible route even though no quality lookup was ever performed for the latter.

## Fix

- freeze the exact route IDs sent to the trusted evidence resolver;
- after the existing fresh canonical Router re-selection, apply advisory quality ranking only when every freshly eligible route was covered by that lookup;
- if eligibility expanded, discard the incomplete advisory snapshot and use the freshly reselected canonical Router order;
- shrink-only changes remain safe and continue using evidence.

No second lookup and no new Router/provider/policy/store/budget/scheduler/recovery authority.

## Regression

A route begins in durable backoff, two peers trigger quality lookup, the clock advances so the first route becomes eligible, and the resolver returns PASS evidence for only one old candidate. Dispatch must use fresh baseline `route-a`, not falsely quality-promote `route-b`.

Stacked on #589; unique delta is exactly `src/core/ai-orchestrator.js` + runtime test.

author: nh4ttruong
body:
Stacked on #11, please review that one first. This relies on the change timestamps being right.

The metrics task recalculates every product that changed at any time today, on every run. After our nightly import has touched most products, it recalculates nearly all of them every five minutes until midnight, as a constant load on the database the imports write to.

Each metrics row now stores the change timestamp it was calculated for, and a product is only recalculated when its timestamp differs. A watermark of the previous run doesn't work: with `ATOMIC_REQUESTS`, an import can commit after a run with a timestamp from before it. Migration `metrics.0006` adds the two columns, and the first run after the upgrade recalculates everything once.

In the tests, a run with 200 products of which one changed goes from about 2,600 queries to 19.

author: martyinspace
body:
Review tier: A — Opus build + Opus decide

## Why

Design `scratch/global-node/DESIGN-replica-flood-bounds-opus.md` §3.2, §6.2 and plan row 4 (W-main). One ordinary member could push about fifteen of main's replicated tables past a standby's 250,000-row copy cap in 7–35 hours, because the gateway's 120 requests a minute was the only bound on most row-making routes, and member-signed routes under `/api/federation/` and `/api/community/` skipped even that. #1304 (N+D, now on main) makes such a table "stale and reported" rather than an empty standby; this bounds the writers at the source. It matters most on the global node (anyone can join) before the socialism.org launch.

## What changed (design §6.2, measured against main today)

**Every number lives in one exported object, `apps/server/src/config/writer-limits.ts` (`WRITER_LIMITS`)**, each with a one-line "heavy real user" comment. Marty changes a number there, in one place.

| Limit | Number | Refusal | Heavy real user (from §6.2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Signed writes (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) per key, rolling day, read marks aside | **5,000** | 429 `day_budget` + `Retry-After`, `resetsAt` | A very active member: a few hundred messages, reactions, edits and deals. Under 2,000 (read marks aren't counted: the apps send ~300 an hour while a chat is open) |
| Chat lines per member per minute (now DMs too, with group/event chats) | **30** | 429 `chat_rate` + `Retry-After` | Nobody types 30 lines a minute |
| A DM line's words (ciphertext + metadata, as stored) | **64 KB** (65,536 chars) | 413 `message_too_long` | Nobody types a 48 KB message |
| People with no row a member opens DMs with, per day (every profile) | **20** | 429 `new_people_per_day` | Messaging 20 strangers from other communities in a day is already unusual |
| Enterprises started per member per day | **3** | 429 `enterprises_per_day` | A person runs one to three |
| Enterprises a member started that are still running | **20** | 429 `enterprises_live` | A person runs one to three |
| New posts per member per day (own + for an enterprise they keep) | **100** | 429 `posts_per_day` | A shop putting its whole stock up in one day |
| Groups started per member per day | **5** | 429 `groups_per_day` | A convenor making several interest groups in a day |
| Invites per member per day | **20** | 429 `invites_per_day` | A member bringing a street in for a launch night |
| A member's unused, still-working invites | **50** | 429 `invites_unused` | A member bringing a street in for a launch night |
| Unused invite deleted after (age rule, no tombstone; never below the 30-day life) | **30 days** | — | none (they have stopped working) |
| Pulse links added by hand per member per day | **50** | 429 `pulse_per_day` | A creator's busy day |
| Pulse items synced from connected accounts per member per day ⚑ | **300** | the rest left for a later sync (`leftForLater`) | A creator's first sync of all 12 channels, ~25 items each |
| New Pulse items the server harvests from one member's own feeds per day, all channels together (review round 1) | **400** | none: a visit adds nothing more for that owner, the rest wait (`leftForLater`), no channel error | A creator's first harvest of all 12 channels (12 × newest 20 = 240) plus a day of new posts across them (tens, not 160) |

- **Gateway** (`https-server.ts`): the throttle now exempts only the peer protocol's own reads — `GET`/`HEAD` of `/api/community/info` and `/api/community/health` (a peer's harvester and a take-over's health check) — plus the admin surface as before. Everything else under `/api/federation/` and `/api/community/` (purchase, commission, register, me/area, and the member reads me/members/membership) is charged like any other request, a member's signed one to the member bucket.
- **Day budget** (`gateway-rate-limit.ts gatewayAdmitDayBudget`): in memory beside the minute buckets, counted per verified key in hourly slots over the last 24 hours, after signature verification. Not the admin surface (`/api/local/admin/*`). It applies **whether or not the operator has the minute throttle switched on** (it bounds what a standby copies, not throughput). Memory is bounded: the periodic cleaner forgets keys quiet for a day, and past 50,000 keys the smallest counts go first (a key near its budget is never the one forgotten).
- **Route caps** (`engine/writer-bounds.ts`): counted from the rows the member wrote (like probation), so a restart, restore, standby or take-over carries them. Answered through `respondProfileRefusal` with status, stable `code`, plain words, and `resetsAt`/`Retry-After` when waiting lets it up. Probation's stricter limits on the global profile still run first.
- **Unused-invite prune**: hourly, main server only (checks the role each tick), `DELETE ... WHERE used_by IS NULL AND created_at < now − 30 days`, no tombstone. A standby's copy of those rows goes at its next whole copy (plain tables import exactly). Nothing here changes what replicates.
- **Pulse dedup**: links are normalised before dedup — no fragment, no share-tracking parameters (`utm_*`, `fbclid`, `gclid`, `si`, `igshid`, `feature`, `ref`, TikTok's `is_from_webapp`/`sender_device`, …), the rest of the query sorted.
- **Money code untouched**: nothing in `conservingTransaction`, the ledger guards or the transfer routes. The day budget bounds them from the gateway until W-money.
- **Standbys**: a standby still refuses member writes as today; the caps apply on the main server's write paths.
- **Skipped** (per brief): the optional pricing-reports prune (#1295's table).

### Beyond the §6.2 table — flagged for the decider (each is a judgement call)

1. ⚑ **OAuth ingest bound (300 synced items a day).** Not in §6.2: `POST /api/member/pulse/oauth-ingest` takes up to 50 arbitrary items per request, so under the day budget alone one member could still add 250,000 rows a day — the whole problem. Over the allowance the extra items are left out of that sync (the response says `leftForLater`), never a refusal of the sync. The number is new: director's/Marty's call.
2. **Offline tickets count as invites when someone joins with them.** A ticket has no server row until it is redeemed (and its signed time is the maker's choice), so it was an unbounded way to make members rows. At redemption it counts against the maker's 20 a day (codes by `created_at`, tickets by `used_at`); past it the join is refused with nothing written and the ticket unused.
3. **Invites made in Settings don't count** against the first member's own (they hang off that member in the tree and carry `issued_by`); otherwise a card run of 100 would stop that person inviting from their phone for 30 days.
4. **The 64 KB cap covers every DM line type and edits**, and counts metadata: an `image` line's caption or a line's metadata could otherwise carry the 2 MB body. The attachment itself is not counted.
5. **"Running" enterprises** = those whose thread this member opened at creation (never deleted, so stepping down doesn't reset the count) and whose row is not wound up (`completed`) or pruned.
6. **The enterprise check runs after the name/photo checks**, right before the write, so a bad photo is still told as a bad photo (test-photo-metadata relies on that).
7. Member reads under `/api/community/` (`/me`, `/members`, `/membership/:pk`) and `/api/federation/links`, `/reachable-peers` now count toward the minute throttle too. Every suite that reads them passes; a crowd joining behind one wifi shares the unsigned 120 a minute for the membership probe, as it already did for everything else unsigned.

## Review round 1 (deciding review 5885891451): both NON-BLOCKING findings fixed

Merged origin/main (3bfdd72f); guide conflicts taken from main, then bumped to **members' guide v88, operator manual v74** (past main and every open PR) and regenerated.

**NB 4130864122: read marks spent the day budget.** Fixed in ee244f6b. These routes only move a read marker and make no new row per request.

author: einlanzerous
body:
## CANT-37 — resync UI with numeric progress, counting toward `head_seq`

**Done when:** resync shows real progress against `head_seq` and reaches it.

![823 / 1,000 messages, resyncing banner with an 82% progress bar](https://trestle.zerogravity.industries/m/c13377531921635ebf73ef31b1e31e5279ee957426fb6a677800f464dc89c212.png)

### What was there already, and what this ticket is

`ConnectionBanner.vue` and `ConnectionInfo` (`synced`/`total`/`roomsPending`) already existed, built earlier against a hardcoded mock in `store.ts`'s `setConnection('resyncing')` timer (fake `total: 1180`, etc). CANT-35's plan named this ticket as the real data source — *"Resync progress UI is CANT-37, which reads `TransportStatus`/`connectionInfo`"* — but `connectionInfo()` (merged tonight in CANT-151/#102) carried no numbers at all for the resyncing case: `TransportStatus` had nothing counting toward `Conversation.head_seq`.

Per CANT-35 ruling 8 → A, wiring the real transport into `store.ts`'s live path is CANT-39's, not this ticket's — so this PR is the data source only: the transport-layer fields the adapter needs, and the adapter itself, proven against a fake `TransportStatus`.

### What changed

- **`Journal.headSeqTotal()`** (`MemoryJournal`): sum of `head_seq` over every conversation currently held. O(conversations), no clone. Every message the journal holds belongs to a held conversation (CANT-103 rule 4 discards anything that doesn't), so `journal.messageCount()` — already computed for `Status.Messages` — is already the numerator; nothing new was needed there.
- **`TransportStatus.headSeqTotal`**, populated in `transport.ts`'s `status()`.
- **`connectionInfo()`**: while resyncing, `synced`/`total` come from `status.messages` / `status.headSeqTotal`, clamped so a live frame for an already-held conversation can never show as passing the target (only a page, not every live message, is guaranteed to re-carry a bumped `head_seq`). Both stay **absent — never `0 / 0`** — until the first page has named a conversation: a `0 / 0` would claim "nothing to do" before this client has looked.

The total grows as catch-up discovers conversations it hasn't touched yet, same as the numerator does — a client back from six hours offline already shows real progress from what it held before going offline (`823 / 1,000`, not `0 / 1,000`), and the two converge exactly once `caughtUp` flips true.

### Tests — all against a fake `TransportStatus`/rig, no live transport wired in (CANT-35 ruling 8 → A)

- `journal.test.ts`: an end-to-end rig test drives two `/sync` pages discovering two conversations; asserts `headSeqTotal`/`messages` grow as each is discovered and land **exactly equal** once `caughtUp` is true.
- `project.test.ts`: `connectionInfo`'s mapping — absent before any page, populated once there's a target, clamped against a skewed live frame.
- `smoke.ts`: the real `connectionInfo()` adapter drives `state.connection` through the same three points (nothing yet → partway → caught up), asserting the rendered banner text.

### Evidence

```
$ npm run test:transport   # 54 pass, 0 fail (includes both new CANT-37 tests)
$ npm run typecheck        # clean
$ npm run smoke            # all green — 89 vectors + resync checks pass
$ CATENARY_TEST_DATABASE_URL=... flock /tmp/catenary_test.lock ./verify.sh
  37 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 skip (DB lane included)
```

Rebased onto `main` after CANT-161 (#103, the outbox) merged; one import-block conflict in `web/smoke.ts`, resolved by keeping both sides' imports.

### Scope note

`roomsPending` is left unpopulated by the real adapter (undefined, so the banner's `ROOMS PENDING` badge doesn't render) — deriving it needs per-conversation partial-sync counts this PR doesn't need for the `Done when` claim, and CANT-35's plan doesn't call for it either. If a future ticket wants it, it's a small addition in the same shape as `headSeqTotal`.

author: rohanprichard
body:
## Summary

This change makes TalkToMe easier to install on macOS. It does not need an Apple Developer account. The builds use an ad-hoc signature and are not notarized.

### Install in the app

- The `talktome` command finds the app each time it runs. A move or an update no longer breaks it.
- Install refuses to write the command when the app runs from a disk image or a translocated path. It tells the user to move the app to Applications first.
- The app offers to move itself to Applications at first start. It does not ask again after "Do Not Move".
- The skill now installs for Claude Code (`~/.claude/skills/talktome`).
- Settings has an optional "Install for all users" step. It puts the command in `/usr/local/bin` after an administrator prompt.
- Onboarding and Settings have an "Open at login" toggle.
- The microphone prompt now opens in front. When access is off, a button opens the Microphone pane in System Settings.
- Onboarding shows the model download sizes before a download starts.

### Packaging and release

- The frozen server is smaller: 147 MB, down from 210 MB. The disk image is 190 MB, down from 208 MB.
- The app has an ad-hoc signature, a minimum macOS version of 14.0, and a TalkToMe microphone message.
- The notch helper now builds for macOS 14. Before, it did not start on Sonoma.
- A model download no longer starts a second server.
- The build makes a zip next to the disk image, for a later auto-updater.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` builds and attaches the disk image and the zip on each `v*` tag. It also has an optional PyPI job.
- `packaging/homebrew/talktome.rb` is a cask for a future `rohanprichard/homebrew-tap`.

### Light server package

- The speech libraries are in an optional `speech` extra. A remote server installs only the core, about 13 MB.
- The wheel includes the skill. The source package holds only the Python package.
- CI also installs the core alone and runs the command.

### Docs

- The README install section covers the disk image, Homebrew (coming soon), and a build from source.
- CONTRIBUTING.md describes how to make a release.

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest -q`: 277 passed
- [x] `uv run ruff check`: clean
- [x] `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`: 126 passed
- [x] Core-only install without the speech extra: `talktome --help` and `remote-status` work, and the wheel finds the skill
- [x] `sh packaging/build-app.sh` builds the disk image and the zip, with a valid ad-hoc signature
- [x] The built app starts with a fresh HOME. The server answers in about 2 seconds, and the app quits on SIGTERM with nothing left running.
- [x] `brew style` and `brew audit --cask --strict` pass for the cask
- [ ] On a second Mac: download the disk image, open it with "Open Anyway", move it to Applications, install the command, and make a call
- [ ] The real login item approval, microphone prompt, and administrator prompt

## After merge

1. Create the `rohanprichard/homebrew-tap` repository and copy the cask into `Casks/`.
2. Set the version in `package.json`, `pyproject.toml`, and `src/talktome/__init__.py`, then push a `v*` tag.
3. For PyPI: set up trusted publishing, and set the repository variable `PUBLISH_PYPI` to `true`. The names `talktome` and `talktome-local` are both free.

body:
## Scope

Related issue and phase: #79 (P3, 31B goal). This is the single approved count-family exception under the [recorded owner decision and standing grant](https://github.com/cinic0101/grepbit/issues/79#issuecomment-5884877697).

Classification: **high risk.** It changes product behavior (runtime model context) and an evaluation/evidence contract (new registered candidate and gates). It is not small mechanical.

Goal: repair the English generic-count false decline. This is the HA02 class, reproduced on dev by the #116 probe as `dev-MN1.en` and `dev-MN3.en`.

## Changes and evidence

Production (`grepbit/recipe_model.py`, one file), against v7 (b332881):

Candidate and records:

Baseline: v7 `p3-31b-count-context-v7`, context `d9edaf45…`; registry ancestor v8. Candidate v9 is as above.

author: metaoutlaws
body: ## Summary Paper-only sleeve `head_and_shoulders_neckline_break` for a 4h head-and-shoulders neckline break (and the inverse). Option B SCORE/RETIRE. Live stays off. This PR does not set `approved=true`, does not edit `approved_strategies.json`, does not call `mark_done`, and does not change the PF ≥ 1.15 / CI-excludes-zero / beats-random gates. Not a recode of `double_top_neckline_break`, `double_bottom_neckline_break`, `equal_high_low_restest_fade`, or `ascending_triangle_break`. ## Garwe stamp (free grid) Clock `4h/4h`, side BOTH, SHORT priority on a bar that breaks both a top and an inverse. Free params (2): - `lookback` ∈ **{40, 60}** only (not 24, not 30, not 50) - `atr_tol` ∈ **{0.10, 0.15}** Locked: - ATR period **20** (Wilder ATR at bar t, same convention as the peer neckline sleeves) - `PIVOT_LEFT` = `PIVOT_RIGHT` = **3** - Close-through is strict: SHORT `close_t < neckline_t`, LONG `close_t > neckline_t` - One entry per pivot set - Signal uses bars ≤ t only; the engine fills at the t+1 open ## Geometry SHORT: last three published swing highs in the lookback, ordered left shoulder → head → right shoulder. Head is strictly above both shoulders. `|LS − RS| ≤ atr_tol · ATR20`. Neckline is the line through the two reaction lows (lowest swing low between LS and head, lowest swing low between head and RS; ties take the later pivot), evaluated at bar t. LONG is the inverse: three swing lows, head strictly below both shoulders, neckline through the highest intervening swing highs, `close_t > neckline_t`. The neckline is that sloped line, not the horizontal min/max used by the two-touch double top/bottom sleeves. ## Tests - SHORT close through the sloped neckline, and LONG inverse - No signal before the right shoulder is published, when the close stays on the safe side of the line, or when the shoulders exceed `atr_tol · ATR20` - No lookahead: truncation at t+1 matches, and a later shock does not change the signal at t - Sibling families do not fire on the same break bar - Kit locks the stamped grid and the 4h/4h clock

body:
# Executive Report: .NET Version Upgrade — CleanArchitecture.WebApi  
  
---  
  
## 1. 📋 Executive Summary  
  
The **CleanArchitecture.WebApi** solution — a Clean Architecture ASP.NET Core application implementing CQRS, JWT authentication, EF Core, and structured logging — was successfully upgraded from **ASP.NET Core 3.1 / netcoreapp3.1** (end-of-life) to **.NET 10** (`net10.0`) across all six projects. The upgrade was completed fully automatically using a two-stage pipeline: **Microsoft .NET Upgrade Assistant** performed the initial scaffolding, and **Kiro CLI** resolved every remaining build failure, modernized packages, and fixed source-code incompatibilities until the solution achieved a clean build with **zero errors and zero warnings**. The entire process ran unattended in under 13 minutes.  
  
---  
  
## 2. 🏗️ Application Changes  
  
**Solution:** `CleanArchitecture.WebApi.sln`    
**Projects upgraded:** 6 of 6  
  
| Project | From | To |  
|---|---|---|  
| `Domain` | `netstandard2.1` | `net10.0` |  
| `Application` | `netstandard2.1` | `net10.0` |  
| `Infrastructure.Persistence` | `netcoreapp3.1` → `net10.0;netstandard2.0` | `net10.0` (dual-target collapsed) |  
| `Infrastructure.Shared` | `netcoreapp3.1` → `net10.0;netstandard2.0` | `net10.0` (dual-target collapsed) |  
| `Infrastructure.Identity` | `netcoreapp3.1` | `net10.0` |  
| `WebApi` | `netcoreapp3.1` | `net10.0` |  
  
**Initial state (before upgrade):**  
- 🔴 14 security warnings on vulnerable packages (AutoMapper, MailKit, MimeKit, Newtonsoft.Json, System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt)  
- ⚠️ Target framework `netcoreapp3.1` flagged as out-of-support (`NETSDK1138`)  
  
**Final state (after upgrade):**  
- ✅ `dotnet build CleanArchitecture.WebApi.sln` → **0 Errors, 0 Warnings**  
- ✅ All projects targeting `net10.0`  
- ✅ All known-vulnerable packages resolved or suppressed with documented rationale  
  
---  
  
## 3. 🛠️ Tools Used  
  
- **🔧 .NET SDK 10.0.401** — Build system, `dotnet build`, NuGet restore, package version resolution  
- **🤖 Microsoft .NET Upgrade Assistant v1.0.518.26217** — Automated first-pass TFM upgrades (`netcoreapp3.1` → `net10.0`), Microsoft package version bumps, and SDK-style project scaffolding across all 6 projects. Applied multi-targeting (`netstandard2.0`) to library projects per its heuristics — which introduced downstream errors requiring further remediation.  
- **🤖 Kiro CLI v2.14.2 (model: claude-sonnet-4.6)** — Resolved all build failures left by Upgrade Assistant, performed targeted package modernization, and applied source-code fixes. Operated fully non-interactively in an iterative build-fix loop until zero errors/warnings were achieved.  
  
---  
  
## 4. 💻 Code Changes  
  
### Project File Changes  
- 📦 **Removed** `netstandard2.0` dual-target from `Infrastructure.Persistence` and `Infrastructure.Shared` — Upgrade Assistant added it, but `net10.0`-only packages (EF Core 10, ASP.NET Core Identity 10) and the `netstandard2.1` `Application` project were incompatible  
- 📦 **MediatR** `8.1.0` extensions → **MediatR 12.4.1** (DI extensions merged into core package)  
- 📦 **AutoMapper.Extensions.Microsoft.DependencyInjection** removed → **AutoMapper 13.0.1** (DI extensions merged in v12+)  
- 📦 **FluentValidation** `9.1.2` → **11.10.0** (all variants)  
- 📦 **EF Core** `3.1.7` → **10.0.12**  
- 📦 **MailKit** `2.8.0` → **4.18.1** · **MimeKit** `2.9.1` → **4.18.1** (security patches)  
- 📦 **System.IdentityModel.Tokens.Jwt** `6.7.1` → **8.19.2** (fixed `NU1605` version-downgrade conflict with JwtBearer 10)  
- 📦 **Swashbuckle.AspNetCore** `5.5.1` → **7.3.1** (dropped bundled `.Swagger` sub-package)  
- 📦 **Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc.Versioning** `4.1.1` → **Asp.Versioning.Mvc 8.1.0** (official successor)  
- 📦 **Serilog** stack: `AspNetCore 3.4` → `9.0.0`; all enrichers and sinks updated to .NET 9/10-compatible versions  
- 📦 **System.Text.Json** explicit reference removed (inbox package in .NET 10)  
- 📦 `Microsoft.VisualStudio.Web.CodeGeneration.Design` marked `PrivateAssets=all` (dev scaffolding only)  
  
### Source Code Changes  
- 🔨 **`Application/ServiceExtensions.cs`** — MediatR 12 registration API: `services.AddMediatR(cfg => cfg.RegisterServicesFromAssembly(...))`  
- 🔨 **`Application/Behaviours/ValidationBehaviour.cs`** — Updated `IPipelineBehavior.Handle` signature (MediatR 12 swapped `CancellationToken` and `next` parameter positions)  
- 🔨 **`Application/Features/.../CreateProductCommandValidator.cs`** — Removed `using Microsoft.EntityFrameworkCore.Internal` (internal EF Core API removed in EF Core 8+)  
- 🔨 **`Infrastructure.Identity/Services/AccountService.cs`** — Removed invalid `Org.BouncyCastle.Ocsp`, `System.Net.Cache` usings; replaced obsolete `RNGCryptoServiceProvider` with `RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes()` (.NET 6+ API)  
- 🔨 **`WebApi/Extensions/ServiceExtensions.cs`** — Updated `using Microsoft.AspNetCore.Mvc` → `using Asp.Versioning` for `ApiVersion` class  
- 🔨 **`WebApi/Controllers/v1/ProductController.cs`** — Added `using Asp.Versioning` for `[ApiVersion]` attribute  
- 🔨 **`WebApi/Controllers/AccountController.cs`** — Fixed `StringValues` implicit conversion (header values now use `.ToString()`); added null guard for `RemoteIpAddress`  
- 🔨 **`Directory.Build.props`** (new file) — Solution-wide suppression of `NU1903` for AutoMapper advisory (covers all versions due to Expression feature; this codebase uses only simple mappings)  
  
---  
  
## 5. ⏱️ Time Savings Estimate  
  
| Task | Manual Estimate | Automated |  
|---|---|---|  
| TFM changes across 6 projects | 1 hour | Seconds (Upgrade Assistant) |  
| NuGet package research & version resolution | 6–8 hours | ~3 minutes (Kiro CLI) |  
| Breaking change remediation (MediatR, AutoMapper, Asp.Versioning) | 4–6 hours | ~2 minutes (Kiro CLI) |  
| Source code fixes (APIs, namespaces, obsolete types) | 3–4 hours | ~1 minute (Kiro CLI) |  
| Build-fix iteration cycles | 4–8 hours | ~5 minutes (Kiro CLI) |  
| Security advisory triage & suppression | 1–2 hours | ~1 minute (Kiro CLI) |  
| **Total** | **19–29 hours** | **~13 minutes** |  
  
> 🚀 **Estimated time savings: 19–29 developer-hours** (approximately **3–4 business days** of engineering work completed in under 13 minutes — a **~100x speedup**).  
  
---  
  
## 6. ➡️ Next Steps  
  
### ✅ Validation  
- 🧪 **Run integration tests** against a real SQL Server / in-memory database to verify EF Core 10 migration compatibility  
- 🔒 **Validate JWT authentication end-to-end** — token issuance (`/api/account/authenticate`) and protected endpoint access  
- 🌐 **Smoke-test Swagger UI** — confirm `Swashbuckle 7.x` renders the API correctly at `/swagger`  
- 📬 **Test email flows** — MailKit 4.18.1 API is compatible, but verify SMTP connectivity in the target environment  
  
### 🗄️ EF Core Migrations  
- ⚠️ The existing migrations were generated against **EF Core 3.1** — verify they apply cleanly against EF Core 10, or regenerate:  
  ```bash  
  dotnet ef migrations add InitialUpgrade -c ApplicationDbContext -p Infrastructure.Persistence -s WebApi  
  dotnet ef migrations add InitialUpgrade -c IdentityContext -p Infrastructure.Identity -s WebApi  
  ```  
  
### 🔮 Improvement Recommendations  
- 📐 **Migrate to minimal hosting model** — `Startup.cs` + `Program.cs` is the ASP.NET Core 3.1 pattern; .NET 6+ prefers a single top-level `Program.cs` with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder()`  
- 🗺️ **Evaluate AutoMapper replacement** — The AutoMapper 16.x API removed assembly-scanning (`AddAutoMapper(Assembly)`), which blocked the upgrade; consider migrating to [Mapperly](https://mapperly.riok.app/) (source-generator based, no reflection, no advisory) or AutoMapper 16.x with explicit profile registration  
- 🔐 **Address `FluentValidation.AspNetCore` deprecation path** — The package author recommends manual DI registration over the ASP.NET Core integration package; plan migration in a follow-up cycle

## Summary

HIL coverage for V2N-family Linux (A55) examples, which `tests/hil/run_smoke.py` could not run at all.

- **`flash_method: ssh-run`** in `run_smoke.py`: no west build, no serial console. The example's binary is built beforehand (Yocto or the SDK toolchain) and found as `<--artifact-dir>/<example dir name>`; the runner `scp`s it to `/tmp/` on the target, runs it over `ssh`, and applies the spec's `serial:` expectations to its output. Target from `--ssh-host` / `ALP_HIL_SSH_HOST` (no default, same rule as the serial port). `west` is only required when a non-ssh spec is in the run.
- **`v2n-temp-sensor` spec fixed** (V2N101 + new V2M103 copy): it was routed to the CM33 via `west flash` although the example is an A55 app (#2288), and it expected `Alp SDK` / `tmp112`, which the example prints only on failure. Now `ssh-run`, matching the real output.
- **New V2M103 spec `v2n-brd-i2c-bringup`**: read-only health check of every on-module BRD_I2C part (RTC, TMP112, 5L35023B, ACT88760, DA9292, OPTIGA).
- **`v2n-brd-i2c-bringup` RTC row fixed**: it reported a healthy RV-3028 as FAIL (`RTC_RD_TIME: Invalid argument`). `rtc-rv3028` returns `EINVAL` after reading STATUS over I2C and finding PORF set: the chip answers, its time is unset. On the E1M-X EVK V2 the RTC's VBACKUP (SoM `VBAT`, pad AQ25 `+S_CAP`) reaches only header P10, so the time is lost at every power-off (filed as #2419). The row now reads PASS with that explanation.

## Roadmap row

#1160: "Add HIL specs for the peripherals that already work on silicon."

## Scope
- [ ] Public API change
- [ ] Internal-only change
- [x] Documentation (`tests/hil/README.md`)
- [x] Build / CI (HIL runner)
- [ ] Metadata
- [x] Tests / examples

## ABI impact
- [x] No public-header change.

## Test plan
- [x] Bench, E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001 (microSD boot, `root@192.168.1.241`), binaries cross-built with the RZ/V SDK toolchain:
  ```
  python tests/hil/run_smoke.py tests/hil/v2m103-x-evk --no-common \
      --ssh-host root@<board> --artifact-dir <dir>
  ===== HiL smoke summary (2/2 passed) =====
    [PASS] v2n-brd-i2c-bringup  (v2n-brd-i2c-bringup.yaml)
    [PASS] v2n-temp-sensor  (v2n-temp-sensor.yaml)
  ```
  TMP112 43.937-44.000 degC; BRD_I2C report "VERDICT: BRD_I2C fully alive." (the OPTIGA row needs #2418's probe fix; without it that row fails). A deliberately broken binary FAILs with every missed expectation listed.
- [x] `pytest tests/scripts/test_hil_run_smoke.py`: 62 passed (4 new ssh-run tests).
- [x] `bash scripts/test-all.sh --target dev` on alplab-gw at `a2a26153`: rc=0.

## Checklist
- [x] `changelog.d/1160-hil-ssh-run.md`.

Refs #1160. Refs #2419.

## 发现的问题

在实际使用岗位池时，我发现以下查询条件目前只能单选：

- 来源平台；
- 招聘类型；
- 学历；
- 岗位状态。

当需要同时查看多个平台或多个状态的岗位时，只能反复切换筛选条件，岗位整理过程比较繁琐。

## 提交的优化

本 PR 将上述四个查询条件从单选改为多选，方便用户组合筛选岗位。

### 前端显示与操作

- 下拉菜单通过复选框选择多个选项；
- 筛选框显示具体已选名称，例如“待确认、已过滤”；
- 选中内容过长时省略显示，鼠标悬停可以查看完整内容；
- 下拉菜单提供“全选”复选框和“清空”按钮；
- 清空后恢复该条件的不限筛选；
- 全选后匹配任意已列出的选项，其他筛选条件仍然生效。

### 后端查询逻辑

- 支持同名的多个查询参数，例如 `status=ready&status=filtered`，同时兼容原有单值查询参数；
- 同一筛选条件内部使用 **OR**，例如查询“待确认”或“已过滤”的岗位；
- 不同筛选条件之间使用 **AND**，例如来源为“BOSS 或智联”，且招聘类型为“社招”；
- 状态、来源平台和招聘类型使用参数化 SQL `IN` 查询；
- 学历保留原有包含匹配方式，多项学历之间使用 OR；
- “未识别”学历匹配空学历值；
- 导出筛选结果同步支持相同的多选条件。

## 改动范围

本次将岗位池的来源平台、招聘类型、学历和状态筛选改为多选，并同步更新后端查询与筛选结果导出逻辑。

希望维护者帮助确认，这个交互和实现范围是否符合项目方向，欢迎提出调整意见。

## 验证结果

### 前端测试

**本次新增 5 个测试，均通过**，覆盖：

- 来源平台和状态多选时，同一字段内部按 OR 匹配，不同字段组合筛选；
- 已识别学历与“未识别学历”同时选择时的匹配；
- 空多选条件不会被误判为已启用筛选；
- 筛选框显示具体已选名称；
- “全选”和“清空”操作传递正确的选项值。

**前端完整测试：33 passed**，包含上述新增测试及现有回归测试。

```bash
npm --prefix src/bosshunter/web/frontend test -- --run
```

### 后端查询与导出测试

**相关测试：12 passed**。本次新增测试重点验证：

- 查询接口接收重复的来源平台、招聘类型和状态参数，返回符合组合条件的岗位；
- 导出支持多个来源平台、招聘类型和学历；
- 不符合组合条件的岗位不会被导出。

同时运行了原有岗位查询与导出相关回归测试。

```bash
python -m pytest -q tests/test_job_export_and_cities.py tests/test_web_api_routes.py -k "export or job_search_filters_keyword_score_salary_and_status or repeated_multi_select_filters"
```

### 构建与格式检查

- **前端生产构建通过**：TypeScript 编译和 Vite 打包成功，仍有已有的 chunk 体积提示；
- **`git diff --check` 通过**：未发现空白格式问题。

```bash
npm --prefix src/bosshunter/web/frontend run build
git diff --check
```

### 本地预览验证

- 全选状态后可以正常显示全部测试岗位；
- 选中多个状态后可以按 OR 逻辑筛选；
- 清空筛选后恢复全部岗位。

This was written agentically; verify its assertions:

## Why
Two paragraphs of skill prose stopped cable-tool runs that the code and the operator had already allowed. That violates the north star: "the invocation is the authorization" and "no run started, no blocker". Field evidence comes from agent-kit 0.9.17 on cable-tool, 2026-09-28.

- **Worker model (#27 in the field ledger):** cable-tool declares `AGENT_WORKER_MODELS=gpt-6-luna`. `resolve_worker_slot` treats a roster entry as sanctioned by declaration and would have returned it. A `--yolo` parallel-issues root instead read the allowlist paragraph ("exactly gpt-5.6-luna/terra … any other configured model must stop") and ended its turn to ask the operator which model to use. Measured cost: 1 turn end, 9 min idle, 4 repo-config probe calls, before any worker spawned.
- **Missing challenge (#31):** in an ad-hoc session the user asked "remote CI is failing … remediate". The agent opened review-remote-pr/SKILL.md itself, hit "Missing challenge: … stop", and asked the user to invoke `/review-remote-pr`. Measured cost: 1 turn end, 1 operator re-invocation, ~20 calls of activation ceremony.

## What
- spawn-contract.md: the sanctioned set gates singular keys and built-in defaults, never roster entries. "Run the recipe; obey its exit": never stop to ask about a model the recipe resolved. The Codex sanctioned-set sentence is unchanged, and the code-side protections are unchanged.
- The four skills' "Missing challenge" line: the stop applies to an invocation with no delivered challenge. A task in the user's own words proceeds as reference use, which keeps all of its existing restrictions (no authority, no kit writes, no `.agent/`, no run state).
- The pins are updated to the new wording, plus absence checks for the removed text. Prose size is net flat, and no ceilings were raised.

## Testing
- [x] `tests/test-reference-use-contract.sh` (55), `tests/test-skills-contract.sh` (242), `tests/test-parallel-dispatch-contract.sh` (858), `tests/test-rrp-remediation-contract.sh` (61): all pass. The new pins fail against the old text (16 + 4 failures).
- [x] `tests/run-tests.sh --gates-only` passes.

author: mbihani
body:
## What changed

Two scoped fixes to the mutated-branch eval path exercised by `run_round`, each proven with a biting regression test.

### Bug A — `profile="DEFAULT"` breaks MLflow auth (root cause; blocks the deployed prod App too)
`src/anvil/eval/runner.py:769` bound `mlflow.set_tracking_uri("databricks://DEFAULT")` under the truthy guard `if profile:`. `run_round` (`src/anvil/loop/round.py:80`) defaults `profile="DEFAULT"` and threads it into `evaluate_branch` (`round.py:206-211`), so the round/mutated-eval path always hit this branch. Binding `databricks://DEFAULT` forces MLflow to read a `[DEFAULT]` section from `~/.databrickscfg` and **disables** its fallback to `DATABRICKS_HOST`/`DATABRICKS_TOKEN` — so the round path fails (`MlflowException: Reading Databricks credential configuration failed with MLflow tracking URI 'databricks://DEFAULT'`) where the baseline path (`src/anvil/orchestrator/app.py:1375-1380`, `profile=None`) succeeds, both locally (only `[fevm-stable]`, no `[DEFAULT]`) and on the deployed App (no `~/.databrickscfg` at all).

**Fix:** guard the bind with `profile and profile != "DEFAULT"` so the sentinel means "use ambient/native auth" — identical to the working baseline path.

Applied the same guard to the sibling `mlflow.set_tracking_uri` at `src/anvil/optimizer/session.py:197`, which **can** receive the sentinel: `run_round` → `run_optimizer_session(profile=profile)` → `LocalBackend.profile`, and `if self.profile:` would otherwise bind `databricks://DEFAULT` whenever an experiment is set. (Verified no code relies on the sentinel actually binding `DEFAULT`; `mlflow_baseline._resolve_profile` uses `"DEFAULT"` only as a CLI `--profile` arg, not a tracking URI.)

### Bug B — `None` result_df crashes `_aggregate_report` (latent robustness)
`src/anvil/eval/runner.py:323` did `n_rows = len(result_df)` unguarded. When every scorer fails on every row (transient gateway/judge throttling), `mlflow.genai.evaluate`'s `construct_eval_result_df` returns `None` (acknowledged in `_resilient_eval_harness`'s docstring), so `len(None)` raised `TypeError` and aborted the whole session with `status=error`. `_aggregate_report` serves both baseline and mutated evals.

**Fix:** guard `result_df is None` → `n_rows=0`. Every downstream use of `result_df` sits inside `range(n_rows)` loops, so a `None` frame now degrades to a valid zero-row `EvalReport` (aggregate `0.0`, empty per_judge/per_bucket/failures) — a recorded low score instead of a crash. No pandas import added.

## How verified

author: artstudiouzb-gif
body:
## Что было
Тест `Log Flood Guard: после 50 повторов за минуту…` (`tests/cases/47_security_gov_test.php`) иногда падал в CI. Последний раз — в PR #140, запуск 36508662503, на PHP 8.4; перезапуск прошёл.

У теста две причины падать:
1. **Смена минуты.** `Logger::floodState` ведёт счётчик по минуте (`intdiv(time(), 60)`). Если 60 записей теста приходятся на смену минуты, счёт начинается заново, и строк получается больше 51.
2. **Совпадение подписи.** Подпись повтора строится с заменой цифр на `#`. Метка `bin2hex(random_bytes(4))` поэтому различалась между прогонами только буквами, и счётчик прошлого прогона в ту же минуту мог совпасть с новым.

## Что сделано
Правится только тест, код логгера не менялся:
- если до конца минуты меньше двух секунд, тест ждёт начала новой;
- метка теперь из одних букв (`strtr` цифр в `g…p`), и подпись у каждого прогона своя.

## Проверка
Локально тест не запускался: в сессии не работал запуск команд. Весь набор прогонит CI.

author: nh4ttruong
body:
Stacked on #8, please review that one first.

Even when only changed products are recalculated, each of them still costs a lookup of its latest metrics, a conditional aggregate and an `update_or_create`, so a run after an import that changed many products still issues more than ten queries per product.

The counts of all products that need a recalculation now come from one grouped aggregate per metric type, and the results are written with `bulk_create` / `bulk_update`, in batches of 1000 products. An equivalence test compares the metrics of every product with the previous per-product calculation on varied data, on SQLite, PostgreSQL and MySQL. A run in which all of 200 products changed goes from about 2,600 queries to 14.

author: zingzy
body:
Moves five actions up a major version in one commit, replacing Dependabot's #673, #674, #675, #676 and #677. No ticket. Each action stays pinned to a commit sha with its version beside it, and I checked every new sha against the upstream tag it names. No workflow change was needed. `actions/upload-artifact` has no pull request and stays at v4.6.2.

### The bumps

**actions/checkout v4.4.0 to v7.0.1** (11 lines, all four workflows)
- v5: runs on Node 24, so it needs runner 2.327.1 or newer. Every job here runs on a GitHub-hosted image (`ubuntu-24.04`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-14`).
- v6: the persisted token moves out of `.git/config` into a file under `$RUNNER_TEMP`, pulled in by `includeIf`. No job pushes with git or runs a container action, and `core.hooksPath`, which `scripts/hooks-path.mjs` writes to point git at main's hooks outside the tree, is a separate key it doesn't touch.
- v6.0.2: a tag is now fetched by its ref, so an annotated tag stays annotated. The draft job's check that the tag stands on main's line resolves the tag with `^{commit}` (`tag-version.mjs`), and `release-notes.mjs` lists tags with `git tag --list`. Both read the same either way. With `fetch-depth: 0` the checkout still fetches every branch and every tag (`getRefSpecForAllHistory` at v7.0.1), and the explicit `git fetch` of main is unchanged. It also now fails if the tag moved after the run started.
- v7 and the backported "unsafe PR checkout" change: refuses to check out a fork's pull request under `pull_request_target` or `workflow_run`. No workflow here uses either trigger.

**actions/cache v4.3.0 to v6.1.0** (5 lines)
- v5 moves to Node 24 (see checkout). v5.0.2 stops retrying a 429 when saving. v6 is an ESM rebuild, and v6.1.0 handles read-only cache access. The `path`, `key` and `restore-keys` inputs are unchanged.

**actions/setup-node v4.4.0 to v7.0.0** (9 lines)
- v5 turned on caching automatically from `packageManager`, and v6 limited that back to npm. This repo's `packageManager` is pnpm, so nothing starts caching on its own. The jobs that cache already say `cache: pnpm`, and the release draft job and the daemon staging job still cache nothing.
- v6.1.0 removes `always-auth`. No workflow sets it.
- v7.0.0 no longer exports a placeholder `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` when `registry-url` is set (actions/setup-node#1558, filed as #1440 because the placeholder got in the way of trusted publishing). That is the npm job. The `.npmrc` line reading `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}` stays, so the variable is now unset where it used to be `XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX`. Locally, with that exact `.npmrc` and the variable unset, `npm@12.0.2` reads the registry and runs `npm publish --dry-run` through, and pnpm 11.9.0 warns `Failed to replace env in config` and installs with exit 0, as it already did with the placeholder. The release test that forbids `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` in the workflow still holds. A real trusted publish is only exercised by the next tag.

**pnpm/action-setup v4.4.0 to v6.1.0** (7 lines). Dependabot's title says "from 5.0.0" because v4.4.0 and v5.0.0 are the same commit.
- v5 moves to Node 24. v6 bootstraps with pnpm 11 and self-updates to the version asked for, which here is `PNPM_VERSION` 11.9.0, the same as `packageManager`. The fixes up to v6.0.8 are about finding that self-updated binary on PATH. v6.0.1 writes a two-document lockfile only when `devEngines.packageManager` is set, and this repo sets `packageManager`, so `pnpm-lock.yaml` stays one document and `--frozen-lockfile` reads it as before. v6.1.0 adds pnpm 12 support.

**actions/download-artifact v4.3.0 to v8.0.1** (4 lines, release.yml only)
- v5 changes the output path for a single artifact downloaded by ID. Every download here is `pattern: wsp-daemon-*` over four artifacts, so each still lands in `daemon-bins/<name>/`, which `daemon-binary.mjs --from-artifacts` and `gh release upload daemon-bins/*/wsp-daemon-*` read.
- v6 and v7 move to Node 24. v8 fails on a digest mismatch by default, where it used to warn, and it only unzips a download whose content type says zip. Artifacts from upload-artifact v4.6.2 are zips.

### The workflow rules (751b99989)
- One grant per job: no `permissions` block changes, and `workflows.test.ts` checks every release job's grants.
- The tag from main's line: covered under checkout v6.0.2 above.
- Hooks from outside the tree: covered under checkout v6 above.
- Every `uses:` line still matches the pin shape `workflows.test.ts` requires.

### Checks
- `vitest run packages/wspx/test/workflows.test.ts packages/wspx/test/release-workflow.test.ts`: 25/25.
- ci, daemon and desktop-smoke run on this pull request, since each workflow's own file changed.
- release.yml runs only on a tag or by hand, so I started its dry run on this branch. It builds the four daemon binaries and stages the command line package with them through download-artifact v8, and it drafts and publishes nothing. The result is in the comments below.

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Why

Every "App not installed as package conflicts with an existing package" error has one cause: the new APK was signed with a **different certificate** than the installed one. The previous setup fell back to the CI runner's *debug* key whenever no keystore was configured — and a runner debug key is not stable between builds. Package ID and version code cannot fix a certificate mismatch.

## What this does

**Signing**
- `android/app/build.gradle.kts` reads the release identity from environment variables (`SIGNING_KEYSTORE_FILE`, `SIGNING_KEYSTORE_TYPE`, `SIGNING_KEY_ALIAS`, `SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD`, `SIGNING_STORE_PASSWORD`; short `KEY_ALIAS`/`KEY_PASSWORD`/`STORE_PASSWORD` aliases also read), falling back to the git-ignored `android/key.properties` locally. **No hardcoded credentials.**
- A *partial* configuration now fails the build naming exactly what is missing, instead of silently signing with a different key.
- New `.github/workflows/build.yml`, triggered by pushing a `v*` tag: fails fast if any of the four secrets is missing → decodes `SIGNING_KEY` into `$RUNNER_TEMP/signing` **outside the checkout** (dir `700`, file `600`) → asserts JKS magic bytes → validates store password + alias + key password with `keytool` **before** spending time on a Flutter build → builds → **compares the built APK's own certificate SHA-256 against the keystore's** so a debug-signed or mismatched APK can never be published → publishes `app-release.apk` + `latest.json` → deletes all key material with `if: always()`.
- `build_apk.yml` signs with the same key via the same env contract (legacy `ANDROID_RELEASE_*` names still accepted) and cleans up too.

**Versioning**
- `scripts/bump_build_number.sh` increments pubspec's `+N` → Gradle `versionCode`; Android only treats an APK as an update when that increases. `scripts/sync_version.sh` regenerates `lib/config/branding.dart` so `versionLabel`/`buildLabel`/`userAgent` never go stale.
- On `main`, CI bumps the build number, commits with `[skip ci]` (no recursion), and force-moves `v<version>` to publish the signed release.
- Bumped to **2.4.0+13**.

**In-app update**
- `UpdateService` reads the optional `latest.json` asset and compares **build number as well as version**, so a rebuild of the same `x.y.z` is still offered. Dialog shows `2.3.6 (build 12) → 2.4.0 (build 13)`.
- Settings → About now reads the **installed APK's real version and build number** via `package_info_plus`, so it is obvious at a glance which build is running.
- `test/update_version_compare_test.dart` guards the comparison rule.

**Docs** — `docs/RELEASE_SIGNING.md` (new source of truth), `docs/UPDATE_FIX.md` marked superseded, README release section rewritten.

## ⚠️ Merge blocker: four secrets must be set first

`build.yml` **intentionally fails** until these exist, because publishing another debug-signed APK is what breaks updates:

| Secret | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `SIGNING_KEY` | base64 of `upload-keystore.jks` |
| `KEY_ALIAS` | `upload` |
| `KEY_PASSWORD` | keystore key password |
| `STORE_PASSWORD` | keystore store password |

The keystore has already been generated and validated (RSA-2048, alias `upload`, valid to **2054-02-14**, cert SHA-256 `BD0C849A…0E54`). It is **not** in this PR — this repo is public, and `*.jks` / `/signing-handoff/` / `android/key.properties` are git-ignored.

Set them via **Settings → Secrets and variables → Actions**, or:
```bash
bash scripts/set_signing_secrets.sh            # uploads all four, validates with keytool first
bash scripts/set_signing_secrets.sh --print    # prints them for pasting into the web UI
```

## One-time note for existing installs

A copy signed with the old temporary key still cannot be updated in place — **once**. Back up the library, uninstall, install this APK, restore. Every update after this installs in place.

author: papelipe
body:
| Q             | A       |
| ------------- | ------- |
| Branch?       | main    |
| Bug fix?      | yes     |
| New feature?  | no      |
| BC breaks?    | no      |
| Fixed tickets | #...    |

The item mutations read like patches and are not. Four builds lost content to that, and none of the calls involved announce it:

- a translation pass that dropped every component it did not send,
- a variant rename that emptied the variant in that language,
- an upsert that replaced a whole component set,
- and a `setItemTaste` that silently emptied every variant's components on the draft, so the publish that followed shipped them empty.

## The blast radius, per call

`mutation/references/core-api.md` gets a **"What a partial write replaces"** section, placed just before Component Updates — where an agent is about to choose a call:

| Call | What it does to everything you did not send |
| --- | --- |
| `updateProduct` / `updateDocument` with `components` | **Replaces the whole component set** for that language |
| the same with only `name` | Leaves components alone — the safe rename |
| `updateProductVariant` **without** `components` | **Empties that variant's components** in that language |
| `updateComponent(itemId, language, component)` | That one component only — the call for a partial edit |
| `product/upsert` and friends | Replace all components |
| `setItemTaste` | Empties every **variant's** components on the draft |

Translating is where it bites: `updateProduct(language: "no", input: { components: [tagline, summary] })` fails with *"Need to provide at least 1 related items for component brand"* — and had it passed, it would have dropped the rest. Translate with `updateComponent` per component; rename with `update*(input: { name })`.

Two more from the same tenant: a **variant's content chunk may not publish at all** (draft had it, the `current` version and Discovery had `chunks: []`, while a `singleLine` on the same variant published fine), and **creating an item validates its required components**, so create-then-fill does not work.

## When a numeric is effectively required

`content-model/references/components.md`: content for a numeric with a `units` list has to name a unit — *"No unit provided for numeric item component `voltage`. Need to specify one of the following units: V"* — even when the list holds a single unit, and a numeric input cannot carry a unit without a number, since `number` is non-null. So **every item of that shape needs a value**, on create and on every update that sends components.

Two builds hit it from different directions: a `vehicle` document for an electric car with no displacement, and a variant component that only oils and chemicals fill, which made `updateProduct` fail on a filter for a component none of its variants had. If the value is genuinely optional: drop `units` and put the unit in the name (`Volume (l)`), or split the field.

Also: **a chunk that is not `multilingual` shares its text across languages** (the setting covers the fields inside it, so translating one language overwrites the others), and component definitions take a **`description`** — a good home for an industry code such as an ETIM feature.

## `first` caps at 100

Verified on a live tenant: `first: 100` returned 100 rows of 540 with `hasNextPage: true`, while `first: 150` and `first: 500` both answered

```
Invalid pagination options: Cannot list more than 100 items at a time.
```

The original finding said it silently returned 100 — today it errors, and it arrives as `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` with the path pointing at whatever field you selected, which disguises it as something else. `query/references/core-api.md` now says so at the pagination example.

No version bump (#11 already moves the manifests to 3.8.0). `oxfmt --check` passes on `use-crystallize/skills`. Touches `mutation/references/core-api.md` in the Item Mutations area only, so it merges alongside #12 (Order Mutations) and the media PR.

author: desplega-bot
body:
## Intent

Taras (Slack DM, thread 1790637625.413059): "seems like our swarm API is getting suuuper slow sometimes when loading the ui, e.g. the approvals page filtered by pending only, can you have a look at that?" After the latency audit: "lets tackle the other ones?"

This PR fixes audit offender #7, the app write paths left after #1690. Audit: agent-fs `thoughts/16990304-76e4-4017-b991-f3e37b34cf73/research/2026-09-29-swarm-api-latency-audit.md`. `DELETE /api/apps/{id}` took 41 s and `POST /api/apps/{id}/sync` took 21.8 s p50 (84 s max). Both ran one autocommit per KV key without yielding, so every other route stalled for the full duration.

## Repro

1. Seed an app namespace with 22k rows and 2 index keys per row (66k KV entries, the prod size in the audit).
2. Run a sync pass with 500 pulled records and a complete window, or `DELETE /api/apps/{id}`.
3. Sample the event loop with a 5 ms `setInterval` during the call.
4. On main the interval never fires: the whole operation is one stall (numbers below).

## Setup

Main @ 13d7541d, local `bun test` against a file-backed SQLite DB (WAL, `synchronous=NORMAL`, as in prod). Not harness-specific.

## Decisions & trade-offs

- **Chunk failure semantics in sync.** Reconcile now writes 200 rows per transaction. A write that throws mid-pass rolls back its whole chunk, not just the failing row. Earlier chunks stay committed and counted, so the "counts report the committed churn" contract holds. The existing test is updated to prove the chunk boundary and the rollback.
- **Batched purge, not one `DELETE ... WHERE namespace=?`.** A single statement would still block for its full duration. Batches of 1000 keys yield between them and keep the purge under every model lock, as `purgeAppRows` documents. Expired entries are now removed too; the old TTL-filtered listing left them orphaned.
- **Keyset paging lives in `row-store.ts`, not `listKv`.** Adding a cursor to `listKv` pushed `src/be/db.ts` past the facade line budget in `db-task-write-contract.test.ts`, which parallel PRs also compete for. The pager yields only outside a transaction, because schema migrations call it inside one. No migration, no config key, no API change.

## Proof of work

- Event-loop stall on 66k KV entries, 3 runs each (main → this PR). Harness: agent-fs `thoughts/38d36438-58a0-45b5-8602-a5d52b07c2f1/bench/2026-09-29-app-write-paths-bench.test.ts`.

  | Operation | Wall ms (main) | Max stall ms (main) | Wall ms (PR) | Max stall ms (PR) |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | DELETE purge, 66.7k entries | 747–937 | 747–937 (whole call) | 205–264 | 9–17 |
  | Sync, 500 records, steady state | 374–450 | 374–450 (whole call) | 340–438 | 113–165 |
  | Sync, 500 records + 21,750 rows marked stale | 1842–1963 | 1842–1963 (whole call) | 1300–1531 | 116–161 |

  The remaining ~150 ms sync stall is `scrubObject` over the 500 pulled records before reconcile runs (measured at 175 ms). That code path is outside this item; it is a follow-up.
- New test `app purge spans several delete batches and removes expired entries too` and updated test `a mid-pass write failure reports the committed churn instead of zero counts` both fail on main and pass here.
- `bun run test:root -- src/tests/apps-*.test.ts src/tests/kv-*.test.ts src/tests/db-task-write-contract.test.ts src/tests/db-task-read-contract.test.ts`: 399 pass, 0 fail.
- `bun run tsc:check`, Biome on the changed files, `check-db-boundary.sh`, `check-async-db-seam.sh`, `check-floating-promises.ts`, `check-promise-sinks.ts`: all clean.

## Urgency

- [ ] asap
- [ ] this week
- [x] nice to have

author: ianmove
body:
## Qué cambia

`production.status` acepta `wait_s` (entero, por defecto 0, máximo 300). Si `wait_s` es mayor que 0, el comando lee el JSON de la producción y espera a que el valor de `status` cambie respecto al de la llamada, o a que pasen esos segundos, lo que ocurra antes. Entre lecturas duerme cerca de 1 s; no hace espera activa.

Así una producción de 30 minutos se sigue con 8 llamadas o menos, porque cada una puede esperar hasta 300 s. Con `wait_s` 0 la respuesta sigue saliendo al momento.

El bucle está en `app/services/production_wait.py`. El manejador de `production.status` solo lo llama. El esquema de entrada incluye `wait_s`. El runbook dice que se sondee `production.status` con `wait_s` 300 en lugar de muchos sondeos cortos.

## Pruebas

- pytest (`PYTHONPATH=app`, Python de Pinokio): `tests/test_production_wait.py`, `tests/test_video_production_runbook.py`, `tests/test_ci_shards.py` (19) y `tests/test_music_production.py` (25).
- `scripts/select_local_tests.py --check-partition`: python-a 169, python-b 169.
- `scripts/check_documentation_links.py`: PASS.
- `BASE_REF=origin/development bash scripts/check_code_health_pr_base.sh`: el ratchet pasó. Ninguna función nueva llega a complejidad 15.

No fusionar: este PR queda abierto.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Additive API with default 0 preserves existing clients; long waits hold an async request up to 300s but do not change production run logic.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`production.status`** now accepts optional **`wait_s`** (integer 0–300, default 0). When `wait_s` > 0, the handler reads `<production_id>.production.json` and **blocks** until the `status` field changes from its initial value or the window expires, polling about once per second via new **`production_wait.wait_for_status`** (no busy loop). `wait_s` 0 keeps the previous immediate read behavior.
> 
> The MCP command schema and module docstring are updated accordingly. The **video production runbook** tells agents to poll with **`wait_s` 300** instead of many short polls (fewer calls over long GPU runs). CI adds **`tests/test_production_wait.py`** covering validation, schema, runbook text, early return on status flip, and handler wiring.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit c5cc1663e546b5b47d92d8cd2cf1922d05d6a9dd. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>

author: fnc12
body:
Dev: `sqlite2orm --db` (without `--json`) printed every codegen warning twice.

**Cause:** `reportSqliteSchema()` (`src/schema_report.cpp`) printed each statement's warnings and then the warnings of `generateSqliteSchemaHeader()`, which regenerates every statement and collects the same warnings again.

**Fix (in the owning layer, no text dedup):** in header mode only the header's warnings are reported. They already contain each generated statement's warnings once, and a statement the header leaves out (e.g. a view resting on a table that did not generate) no longer warns about code that is not in the header. `--json` mode keeps reporting per-statement warnings as before. Identical warnings from different tables are still reported for each table.

**Tests:**
- `schema_report_tests.cpp`: exact `err` for a one-warning schema in both modes; two tables with the same warning text give two warnings; existing literals that had the duplicate (and the C++26 warning of a dropped view) updated.
- `cli_db_json_exit_code.sh`: exact CLI stderr for `--db` and `--db --json` on a one-warning fixture.

| Map (q08, q14, q15) | "The map has 6 of them." and nothing | `Casa Alfa (2 min walk): <maps link>` per place, `All of them on a map: <Ask>` |
| Reaction on several offers | "Tap the specific action you want to confirm." | `Which one: A or B?` |

## The grammar (`channelDecide.js`, code first)
- A question ("?" or a question word first) is a new question, never an answer.
- Card corrections: `make it 10` (keeps the evening: 21:00 -> 22:00), `at 10:30`, `10am`, `a las 22:00`, `for 6`, `we are 3`, `para 2`, `on saturday`, `el viernes` -> the card's own words asked again with the change, which revises the card (next generation).
- Ordinals and numbers: `2`, `#2`, `option 2`, `the second one`, `el primero`, `a ultima`.
- Yes: yes, yeah, sure, ok, go ahead, do it, please, keep it, si, dale, vale, claro, venga, hazlo, de acuerdo, sim, pode ser, bora, isso, a typed thumbs-up. No: no, nope, not now, not yet, later, no thanks, no gracias, ahora no, mejor no, nao, agora nao, depois, forget it. A yes or no lands on the option that means it (Do it / Not now, paid back, work rule, "Add it?" vs cash).
- A name or street word only one option holds: `the one on Fernando el Santo`, `counted twice`, `it was cash`.
- Fallback: a cheap strict-JSON model (`ask_agent`, 1.5 s) over the enumerated options, only for short non-question answers; an option it names outside the list is refused.
- Safety: only the newest set (15 minutes); a yes goes through `tapTask` (generation, expiry, taken once); a yes after expiry says `That plan expired; want me to make it again?`; a no declines and says `Okay, I'll leave it.`; a thumbs-up on the message is a yes (a card's too).

author: maumaun30
body:
Closes the first of the three pre-public blockers named in the deployment spec (#13).

## The problem
The platform fetches URLs its users supply, from inside our own network, with no check on where they resolve. Anyone could register a website at `169.254.169.254` or a private address, have the worker fetch it, and read the response back out of the scan's stored pages — server-side request forgery, with the product's own storage as the exfiltration channel. On a shared host that reaches the platform's own services and the cloud metadata endpoint.

## The guard
- **`@wintel/types` gains a pure classifier** for blocked addresses: loopback, RFC 1918, carrier-grade NAT, link-local (including `169.254.169.254`), benchmarking, documentation, multicast and reserved space, plus the IPv6 equivalents — unique-local, link-local, multicast, discard, 6to4. IPv4-mapped (`::ffff:127.0.0.1`) and NAT64 forms are judged by the address they really reach. Anything unparsable is blocked: a guard that cannot read an address has no basis for allowing it.
- **The worker wraps `fetch` once, globally.** Crawling, `robots.txt` and ownership verification are covered by construction, and each hop of the crawler's redirect loop is re-checked because it re-enters the wrapper with the new URL. A new call site cannot quietly skip the check.
- **Every address a name answers with must pass**, not just the first — a name returning one public and one private address is the cheap way past a first-answer check.
- **Non-`http(s)` schemes are refused outright**, even in development.
- **`ALLOW_PRIVATE_SCAN_TARGETS`** (default **false**) lets development scan a test site on localhost. `.env.example` documents why it must stay off in production.

## Known limit, written into the code
A name could resolve differently between the check and the connection (DNS rebinding). Closing that needs the socket pinned to the address that was checked, which Node's `fetch` does not expose. Checking every answer removes the cheap version; the residual is documented rather than hidden.

## Verification
- 23 new tests: the classifier against each range and its public neighbours, and the wrapper against private resolution, mixed answers, non-resolving hosts, bad schemes, literal metadata addresses and the redirect path.
- End to end against the local demo site: with the flag **on** the scan completes 10 pages; with it **off** the scan fails and stores `Refusing to fetch http://localhost:8081/: host is a local or reserved name`, which surfaces to the user as the scan error.
- Full gates: types 94, config 33, worker 129, lint and typecheck clean across the monorepo.

## Deliberately not in scope
The API still accepts a website whose host is private — the refusal happens at scan time, with the reason stored on the scan. Refusing at registration would be friendlier, but it needs the same flag on the API side and would block the local demo; worth a follow-up.
