author: xu-albert
body:
## Intent

Someone could take over an account by signing up with your email first. A stranger registers a password account with your email and never verifies it. When you later sign in with Google, the two accounts get joined, and the stranger's password now opens your account. The audit reproduced this.

Block joining Google sign-in to an unverified account

For the people that block leaves stuck (an existing password user, or the real owner of a squatted email address, who tries to sign in with Google): All three: explain it in the app, mark the email verified after a password reset, and sign out other sessions on reset.

For accounts that were already joined this way before the fix: Run a read-only check of the live database as a separate job, and show me what it finds.

For a stranger who holds the address through a Google sign-in whose email Google has not verified: Both: refuse new accounts from a Google email Google hasn't verified, and on reset remove sign-in methods that were attached without proof.

## What Changed

- **Linking and sign-up refusals (`worker/auth.js`):** A new `account.create.before` hook stops better-auth 1.6.9 from attaching a Google (or any OAuth) identity to an existing user whose email was never verified. Before this, anyone who registered a password account under someone else's email could keep a working password into that person's account once the owner signed in with Google. The `user.create.before` hook now also refuses a Google sign-up when Google reports the email as unverified. It does this before the user row is written, since D1 has no transactions. Both refusals throw with a specific code (`ACCOUNT_LINK_REQUIRES_VERIFIED_EMAIL` or `OAUTH_EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED`). better-auth's own error redirect only reports a generic error, so a `hooks.after` middleware adds the real code to it.
- **Password reset as proof of ownership (`worker/auth.js`):** A completed reset now does three things. It marks the email verified, which lets the owner use Google sign-in on that account. It revokes every session (`revokeSessionsOnPasswordReset`), which ends the squatter's session too. And if the user was still unverified, it removes every non-credential (OAuth) identity attached to the account, so a stranger's Google sign-in no longer reaches it.
- **Error messages in the app (`public/src/auth.js`):** `startGoogleSignIn` now passes `errorCallbackURL`, so a failed Google sign-in returns to the app. The new `readGoogleReturn` reads the `error` from the return URL and strips the return parameters. The modal then reopens on Log In and shows the reason. `mapAuthError` has an explanation for each of the two new codes. New tests: `worker/auth.test.js` runs the Google sign-in, linking and password-reset flows through the real handler, with Google's token endpoint and Loops stubbed, and `public/src/auth.test.js` covers the client side. `docs/testing.md` adds regression ledger row 26 and updates the auth coverage and gap entries; `docs/email-migration-loops-to-cloudflare.md` updates its line references.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Risk Assessment

⚠️ Medium: This is a security fix to account linking that also changes the password reset: a reset now deletes OAuth identities and signs out every session. Tracing it against better-auth 1.6.9's link-account, callback and reset-password code confirms it closes the reproduced takeover and meets each required constraint, and the only open items are wording and simplification follow-ups, so it is safe to merge with those addressed later.

## Testing

The configured `npm test` had failed. Its log shows the node --test half passed and vitest had 7 timeouts across 5 files: 4 were in untouched server room suites and 3 were auth tests, some running for about 15 minutes. That points to CPU starvation on the host (load average 50–80 on 10 cores), not a regression. In my runs, `public/src/auth.test.js` passed 6/6 and `worker/auth.test.js` passed 10/13 in a full-file run, with each timed-out test passing alone. I then stood up the real bundled Worker locally under Miniflare with its real bindings and a fully migrated local D1, faking only Google's token endpoint and Loops. Over HTTP, 7 scenarios were checked against the persisted D1 rows and all passed: takeover refused; a signed-in squatter can't attach Google via link-social; reset verifies the email, ends sessions and locks out the old password; an unverified Google email can't create an account; a legacy Google squat is removed on reset; a verified user keeps their Google identity; and normal Google sign-in paths still work. A real browser then showed both in-app explanations in the Log In modal and the owner's full recovery: Forgot password, the emailed link, the reset page, then a successful Google sign-in (screenshots). A first harness attempt with wrangler's startWorker ignored its `outboundService` hook. For that run, the Worker's calls reached the real Google token endpoint and the real Loops API, carrying only fake test credentials. Google answered invalid_client and Loops answered 401, so nothing was sent. That harness was replaced by the Miniflare one. The read-only check of the live production database was not run: it is a separate job the author asked for, outside this change. All transient worktree files (.wrangler, .playwright-mcp) and the scratch database were removed.

- Live validation: ✅ go - 8 of 9 scenarios driven live against the product

| Scenario | Result | Live | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Stranger pre-registers the victim's email with a password; the victim's Google sign-in is refused (no session, no Google identity attached, email stays unverified, retry refused, the stranger's passwo… | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S1; live-scenarios-results.json |
| After a refused link the browser comes back to the app and the Log In modal explains that Google sign-in stays blocked until a password reset | ✅ pass | live | ui-1-link-refused-explained.png (no session: header still shows SIGN IN; get-session null) |
| Owner resets the password: email becomes verified, every session (the squatter's included) ends, the old password gets 401, the new one works, and the owner's Google sign-in then joins the account | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S3; browser flow ui-3a-owner-reset-password-done.png + ui-3b-owner-google-signin-after-reset.png + ui-final-db-state.json |
| Google sign-up from an email Google has not verified is refused with an in-app explanation and no user row is written | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S4; ui-2-unverified-google-signup-refused.png; ui-final-db-state.json (unverifiedGoogleSignup: 0) |
| Adversarial: an address held through a stranger's unverified Google identity (pre-fix data) is reclaimed by the owner's reset, which removes that identity, ends the stranger's session and blocks their… | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S5 (legacy row seeded via seed-legacy-squat.sql) |
| Adversarial: a signed-in squatter calling link-social cannot attach any Google identity to the unverified account | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S2 (callback 403, account list stays credential-only) |
| Resetting the password of an already verified Google user keeps their Google identity and Google sign-in keeps working | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S6 |
| Legitimate paths still work: new Google user created verified, returning Google user signed back in, verified password account links Google, password user still logs in after a refused link | ✅ pass | live | live-scenarios-transcript.txt S7 |
| Read-only check of the live production database for accounts joined this way before the fix | ⏸️ untested | no | The author asked for this as a separate job, and it is not in this change. Running it needs read access to the production D1 `arithmetic-racer` through Cloudflare credential

author: hessius
body:
Finishes the last two items on #95: the grind a brew was made with (#109) and a story-format share card (#105).

## The dial (#109)

The dial is an override. Turning it changes how the machine grinds, with no event and no characteristic, and nudging it is how a recipe is made to suit a bean. A recipe's grind size therefore does not answer "what was this brewed at", and on a grinder-off brew it says nothing at all.

Two readings now ride on a record:

- `dialBefore`, taken once at the first phase past `waking`. Free: `Machine.brew` already refreshes vitals for the tank check.
- `dialAfter`, taken after the brew. This costs a handshake, so it beeps. Accepted: it fires once, after the brew is over, and only on a brew that reached the pour.

Three rules, all enforced in `library/brew/dialAfterBrew.ts`:

- only a confirmed reading is stored. `askHowItIsDoing()` returning false leaves `machine.info` holding the pre-brew value, which is the exact number this exists to avoid recording. Nothing is written, and absence is the record of non-confirmation.
- the wording reports the dial and stops: `MACHINE DIAL 47`, or `MACHINE DIAL 47, MOVED FROM 52`, and nothing at all when only `dialBefore` exists.
- `lastDial` is a second small query, not a subquery spliced into `summaryFor`'s aggregate. Two SQL answers to one question is how the existing aggregates came to disagree about what counts as a brew.

The recall aid sits on the editor's ABOUT deck, where the next brew is planned.

## The story card (#105)

A 9:16 card with the brew, the coffee, the rating, the tags and the app's mark.

- the in-place export is untouched. It still photographs the node on the glass, so what you see is what leaves the phone.
- the card is composed from the shared `BrewSummary`: the screen hands one description to both, and passes the same element into the card.
- previewed rather than captured off screen. The sheet measures its room and draws the card at the largest size that fits whole, captured at natural size with no transform.
- the top and bottom bands are empty because story UI covers them. Coffee, rating and tags are left out when there is nothing to say.

## Device check

The dial work rests on a hardware question nobody has answered yet, and it is written into `docs/machine-integration/ble-protocol.md`:

- [ ] Send a grinder-on recipe with a known grind size, **turn the dial during the brew**, and see whether the post-brew reading reports the physical dial or echoes the value the app sent.
- [ ] The beep happens once, after the brew, and not at all on a brew cancelled before the pour.
- [ ] A brew refused for water writes no dial and shows no dial line.
- [ ] The ABOUT deck shows the last dial on a recipe that has been brewed.
- [ ] The story card looks right on a phone: nothing important in the top or bottom band, and an unrated, untagged brew has no empty rows.
- [ ] Sharing the card produces a 9:16 PNG that posts full bleed.

Nothing native changed, so no `expo.version` bump.

Gate: 297 suites / 5241 tests green, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors (26 pre-existing warnings). 47 new tests; 36 mutations run against them, all caught.

author: moiseszeleny
body:
Las dos sesiones de la semana 8 sobre ecuaciones de movimiento con `sympy.physics.mechanics`, su preparación y la tarea. Cierra los dos hilos que dejó la semana 7: la $v^2$ del péndulo doble y de la cuenta en el aro reaparecen como energía cinética, y el péndulo doble por fin se mueve según sus ecuaciones.

## Qué incluye

| Archivo | Contenido |
|---|---|
| `requirements.txt` | **Dependencia nueva:** `scipy==1.17.1`, para `solve_ivp`. |
| `clase/semana-08-sesion-1-lagrange.ipynb` | Euler-Lagrange del péndulo simple a mano con `diff`, y luego lo mismo con `Particle`, `potential_energy`, `me.Lagrangian` y `LagrangesMethod` (comprobado contra lo hecho a mano). Péndulo doble, la forma $M\ddot q = f$, `rhs()`, fricción con `forcelist`. 2 `TODO en clase`: el péndulo elástico y los modos normales del péndulo doble linealizado ($\omega^2 = (2\pm\sqrt2)g/L$, con el mismo $M^{-1}K$ de la semana 6). |
| `clase/semana-08-sesion-2-kane-y-simulacion.ipynb` | Velocidades generalizadas, `kd_eqs`, `set_ang_vel` y `KanesMethod` en el péndulo simple, con fricción como una carga más y el error por olvidar `kd_eqs`. Después, `lambdify` + `solve_ivp`: ángulos, trayectoria de la punta y caos. 2 `TODO en clase`: el péndulo doble por Kane (la diferencia de `rhs` contra Lagrange da la matriz cero) y la energía como prueba de la simulación. |
| `clase/img/` | Diagrama nuevo del péndulo elástico; el del péndulo doble se copió de la semana 7. |
| `preparacion/preparacion.md` | Reinstalar `requirements.txt` para tener SciPy y comprobar la versión; repaso opcional de Euler-Lagrange. |
| `tarea/` | Tarea 08: la cuenta en el aro de la tarea 07, ahora con dinámica. Lagrange, Kane (comparados entre sí), equilibrios y $\Omega_c = \sqrt{g/R}$. Sin SciPy. |

## Decisiones que conviene revisar

- **SciPy 1.17.1.** Es la última versión con ruedas para Python 3.11, el mínimo del curso (la 1.18 exige 3.12), y es compatible con `numpy==2.3.5`. Lo comprobé con `pip install --dry-run --python-version 3.11`. `docs/instalacion.md` y `.devcontainer` instalan desde `requirements.txt`, así que no cambiaron.
- **Kane en una sola sesión, con poca teoría:** se presenta como otra ruta a las mismas ecuaciones (fuerzas en lugar de energía), no con su derivación de velocidades parciales.
- La primera celda de la sesión 2 reconstruye, ya resuelto, el péndulo doble por Lagrange, con marcos y puntos llamados `B1`/`B2`/`Q1`/`Q2`. Así quedan libres `A1`/`A2`/`P1`/`P2` para el TODO 1, y la simulación no depende de que el TODO esté resuelto.
- La tarea 08 hereda el sistema de la tarea 07. Su test del Lagrangiano contiene la $v^2$ de la tarea 07, pero esa expresión ya es pública en `semana-07/tarea/tests/test_tarea.py`, así que no se filtra nada nuevo.
- Duración estimada de cada sesión: 75–80 min de contenido (33 y 29 celdas).

## Verificación

Todo con el entorno `fisica-computacional` (Python 3.11.15, SymPy 1.14.0, NumPy 2.3.5, SciPy 1.17.1):

- Los dos notebooks de clase y el de la tarea ejecutan completos desde un kernel limpio con `jupyter nbconvert --execute`. Ninguna celda muestra `True`/`False` donde debía ir una ecuación.
- Resolví los 4 `TODO en clase` en copias locales (no versionadas):
  - Péndulo elástico: las ecuaciones coinciden con las del enunciado.
  - Modos normales: $(2\pm\sqrt2)g/L$; el modo lento va en fase y el rápido a contrafase.
  - Kane contra Lagrange: la diferencia da la matriz cero.
  - Energía: la variación máxima es $8.9\times10^{-8}$ J con `rtol=1e-10`, y 2.27 J con las tolerancias por defecto.
- `pytest tarea/tests/ -v`: **11 passed** contra una copia resuelta local y **11 failed** contra el notebook de entrega. Con la energía potencial de signo cambiado fallan los 6 tests que dependen de ella; Kane y $\Omega_c$ siguen pasando, porque no la usan.

## 요약
`core.autocrlf=true`인 Windows에서는 브랜치를 전환하면 `scripts/*.sh`가 CRLF로 체크아웃되어, WSL `bash`로 실행할 때 `set: pipefail: invalid option name`으로 실패합니다(줄 끝의 `\r`이 옵션 이름에 붙기 때문). 인덱스는 이미 LF라 리눅스 CI에는 영향이 없었고, 로컬 재현(`docs/deployment.md`의 "CI 배포 게이트" 로컬 재현 포함)에서만 드러나는 문제입니다. M-06 작업 중 발견했고 기존 `prod-up.sh` 등 전체 셸 스크립트에 해당합니다.

## 변경사항
- `.gitattributes`: `*.sh text eol=lf` 추가(주석 포함 3줄). 체크아웃 환경과 무관하게 셸 스크립트를 LF로 고정합니다.

## 검증 (로컬)
- 규칙 적용 전: 셸 스크립트 14개 중 11개가 작업 트리에서 CRLF였고, PowerShell의 `bash`(WSL)로 `scripts/ci/check-image-refs.sh`가 실패했습니다.
- 규칙 적용 후 재체크아웃: 14개 모두 `git ls-files --eol` 기준 `w/lf`이고 같은 명령이 성공했습니다.
- `git add --renormalize .` 결과 인덱스에서 바뀌는 스크립트는 없습니다(이 PR의 변경은 `.gitattributes`뿐).
- CI는 리눅스라 영향이 없으며, `test`·`prod-smoke` 통과만 확인하면 됩니다.

## 기존 클론에 반영하는 방법
규칙만으로는 이미 체크아웃된 작업 트리 파일이 자동으로 다시 쓰이지 않습니다. 머지 후 각자 클론에서 셸 스크립트를 삭제하고 다시 체크아웃하세요.

```bash
for f in $(git ls-files -- '*.sh'); do rm -f "$f"; git checkout-index -f -- "$f"; done
```

body:
## What this changes

A message in a roadmap's room now reaches a room session that is still busy. The plugin steers the message into the running Task (between its steps) instead of queuing it until the Task ends. A server that holds an organization only as a mirror (the organization runs on another machine) no longer relays that organization's rooms. The room session's first input also says not to wait for the room: no polling of the channel's files and no sleep loops; end the turn.

Why: on the board's instance, roadmap #4 went silent. A question to the moderator at 07:10:01Z got no answer for 21 minutes. The moderator's room session had never ended its opening Task: it was waiting on the room in a shell loop of its own. The plugin delivered with `queueIfBusy: true`, so the message waited behind that Task and never arrived. Then, at 07:31:05Z, a push restarted the hub, and the hub relayed its mirror of the organization. It did not find the machine's room sessions, so it closed them as "session gone" and opened a second set of its own, which spoke in the same room. The organization scheduler already skips mirrors (`scheduler.ts` `reconcile`); the plugin's relay did not.

Server side, for plugins:
- `MessagingTaskRunner` gains `steer`. `SessionManager.steer` already existed, and the provider (`Sessions`) already had it; the messaging bridge does not use it.
- `OrgView` gains `machineId`: the machine the organization runs on when it is not this server, else `null`.

author: bennykok
body:
## Problem
Sessions de7fd537 and 4d5404ad stopped mid-turn and could not be resumed by a message. Their harness process was dead, `data/aisdk/<id>.json` still said `busy: true`, and every send only appended to a command file no process read. Only boot recovery relaunches harnesses.

## Root cause of the original stop
Kernel OOM kill, not a provider error (`journalctl --user`):
- `lfg-agent-lfg-437797.service` (4d5404ad): OOM kill 06:57:32 UTC, `Failed with result 'oom-kill'`.
- `lfg-agent-lfg-c3fbb9.service` (de7fd537): OOM kill 07:15:51 UTC.
- Same day: `lfg-agent-lfg-b09abb` 07:30:43, `lfg-agent-lfg-55531b` 07:39:55 (the 4d5404ad follow-up, 615b3a99).

Subagent units run with `MemoryMax=2G` and `KillMode=control-group`, so one OOM in the cgroup kills the harness too.

## Fix
- `session-recovery.ts`: export `launchRecovered`. New `relaunchDeadCommandFileHarness` relaunches the same owner row. The claim is stored on the registry entry (`relaunchClaimedAt` / `relaunchClaimPid`, 60 s, released if the spawned pid dies), so concurrent sends spawn once.
- `serve.ts`: `/api/sessions/:id/send` (used by `omg_send_session_message`) and `/api/sessions/resume` relaunch a dead command-file harness behind `activationGate`, then deliver. The relaunched harness reads the command file from its cursor, so messages that were stuck are also delivered.
- `sessions.ts`: a registry entry that outlived its process is `statusReason: "interrupted"`, not `provider_error`. The harness removes its entry on every exit it controls, so an orphaned entry means it was killed from outside. The `restart_recovered` banner is suppressed after a message has gone in.
- Web banner: "Agent stopped" with a one-tap **Continue**.
- `claude-path.ts`: fall back to `~/.local/bin/claude` (then `~/.claude/local/claude`) when PATH misses it. Each harness logs the binary it uses, for example `~/.local/bin/claude -> .../versions/2.1.283`, or "SDK bundled".

## Verification
- `bun test src/session-relaunch.test.ts src/session-recovery.test.ts src/agents/backends/claude-path.test.ts`: 28 pass. Covered: dead harness + send leads to relaunch and delivery; live harness leads to no relaunch; 5 concurrent sends lead to 1 spawn; claim expiry; failed launch; interrupted status; claude path fallback.
- `bun run typecheck` and `cd web && bun x tsc --noEmit`: clean.
- `bun run test`: 4362 pass, 11 fail. None of the failures come from this PR: the mobile native checks cannot find `react-native-*` in this worktree, and `chat-send-invariants` and `rail-swipe-actions` also fail on HEAD.

## Not verified
- There is no end-to-end run against a live serve. Per instructions, serve was not restarted.

## Containment on relaunch (02805233c)
- The owner row records `containment: { agentSlice, sandbox, egressProxy }` at create. `launchRecovered` (send, resume, boot recovery) reads it. Callers cannot choose it.
- Legacy rows: `spawnedBy` "subagent" or "bot" go in the slice. The role decides sandbox and egress.
- Egress URL is rebuilt from serve's proxy and fails closed. Boot recovery waits for the proxy to start.
- OOM: a dead contained harness whose unit journal says `oom-kill` shows `statusReason: "out_of_memory"`, `statusDetail: lfg-agent-<name>.service`. Banner: "Agent ran out of memory" with Continue.
- Tests: `src/session-relaunch-containment.test.ts` (14). Detector checked read-only against the real journal: `lfg-437797` and `lfg-c3fbb9` read OOM.

## Cold-start resume and 4G units (0bc2b9f6b)
- `/api/sessions/resume` with no registry entry left now resolves containment from the newest owner row for the session (`coldResumeContainment`): the recorded value, else the subagent/bot default for legacy rows. No row: uncontained. It spawns with it and records it (and the role) on the new row. A restricted session fails closed when the egress proxy is down.
- Subagent units: `MemoryMax=2G` to `4G`. `MemorySwapMax=0` and no `MemoryHigh` are unchanged. The 5G `lfg-agents.slice` still bounds the swarm.
- Tests: 8 new cold-start cases in `src/session-relaunch-containment.test.ts`. Focused files: 82 pass. `bun run typecheck` and web `tsc` clean.
- `bun run test`: 4384 pass, 11 fail. All 11 also fail on `origin/main` b48852d19 (main: 13 fail, 1 error). CI `audit` fails the same way on main (`image-size` GHSA-5p2g-fcmc-qvqq now has a fix).

body:
## 概要
F0 PR-0c。日本の祝日の表（2026〜27・振替休日を含む）と配信日カレンダーを足し、祝日は朝ダイジェストを休む（予定リマインドは登録する・祝日明けは休みの間のメールも拾う）。小俣さん裁定で 11/3 から点ける。フラグ MORNING_DIGEST_HOLIDAY_SKIP は既定 false＝今と同じ。

## 変更（実装の申告）
- 結論: PR-0c（暦）をブランチ feat/f0c-holidays-20260929 にコミット 78a203b2 として実装しました。フラグは既定 OFF で、OFF の間は今と同じ動きです（祝日も配信・走査は 3 日・表を見ない・描画とプロンプトには手を入れていない）。push と PR 作成はしていません
- 祝日の表 /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/src/teamagent/jp_holidays.py（新規・依存なし）: 2026 年 18 日と 2027 年 17 日で、振替休日（2026-05-06・2027-03-22）と国民の休日（2026-09-22）を含む。内閣府『国民の祝日について』のページと 35 日すべてを照合済み。表の範囲外は None（分からない）を返す。coverage_status と coverage_notice で、期限 2027-12-31 の 60 日前（2027-11-01）から『期限が近い』と判定する
- 配信日カレンダー /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/src/teamagent/skills/morning_digest/delivery_calendar.py（新規）: next_delivery_day・prev_delivery_day・mail_lookback_days（max(3, 今日−前の配信日)、上限 14 日）・holiday_reason・skip_reason を持つ。会社休日は MORNING_DIGEST_EXTRA_SKIP_DATES で足せる（祝日スキップが ON のときだけ効く・最大 60 件・読めない値は件数だけ警告）。F1/F2 もこれを使う想定
- runner /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/scripts/run_morning_digest_fargate.py: フラグが ON のとき、祝日と会社休日は skill.run を呼ばず DM も送らない。予定リマインドは MORNING_DIGEST_REMINDERS が ON なら登録し、宛先は conversations.open で開いた D 始まりの 1 対 1 DM に限る。個人別配信の予約発火（single）も同じ扱い。planner は祝日に予約も、月曜の未連携のお知らせも作らない。祝日明けは走査範囲を広げ（10/13 は 4 日）、morning_digest_lookback を記録する。表の期限の 60 日前から、または範囲外の日は jp_holiday_table_stale を出すが、配信は続ける
- リマインドの『もう過ぎた予定』を判定する時計を calendar_window.now_jst() に揃えた（値は今と同じで、テストで固定できる）
- skill.py に collect_calendar_events を追加: 当日の予定だけを取り、メール・Bedrock・Slack には触れない。本人確認は run() と同じで、確認できなければ止める
- terraform /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/infra/terraform/morning_digest_schedule.tf: 変数 morning_digest_holiday_skip（既定 false）と morning_digest_extra_skip_dates（既定 空・YYYY-MM-DD のカンマ区切りを検査。terraform console で確認済み）を追加し、TD の env 2 つを足した。jp_holiday_table_stale の metric filter と警報も追加した（定義だけ）。説明には『TD で変えたら activation 版 tfvars（正本）へ同じ値を追記』と guard の allowed_env の注意を書いた
- send_window.py の docstring を実態に合わせて 1 行直した
- セルフレビューを 1 周: OFF のときに変わらないこと、土曜の手動実行は止めないこと、範囲外の日は配信を止めない側に倒すこと、ログに件数しか出ないこと（メールアドレスや予定のタイトルは出さない）を確認。guard の allowed_env の穴を見つけ、tf の説明に書いた

## レビュー（反証）の指摘と修正
- 結論: 指摘 2 件を一次ソースで確かめ、どちらも正しかったので直しました。コミットは b5b4dcef（feat/f0c-holidays-20260929・親は 78a203b2）です。push と PR 作成はしていません。本番のコード（scripts/run_morning_digest_fargate.py）は変えていないので、フラグ OFF のときの描画とプロンプトは前のコミットと同じです
- 指摘1（重大）を確かめた内容: 祝日の予定取得の except Exception を外す変異 X1 を当てると、元からある 25 件はすべて緑のままでした。検出したのは新しく足した 4 件だけです。GCalendarClient.list_events（src/teamagent/adapters/gcalendar_client.py:402）は service.events().list(...).execute() の例外をそのまま上に投げることも確かめました。本番では、失効トークンの人が 1 人いるだけで、その後ろの人のリマインドが全員分止まります
- 指摘1の修正: /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/tests/scripts/test_digest_holiday_skip.py に 5 件足しました。予定取得の失敗は本物の例外で 4 通り（RefreshError の invalid_grant と invalid_client、HttpError の 403 insufficientPermissions と 503 backendError）、Slack の失敗は本物の SlackApiError（users_not_found）で 1 通りです。偽物は Calendar の service（events().list().execute()）だけにしました。GCalendarClient.from_user_token の後（本物の list_events、policy による封鎖、extract_events）は本物を通します。2 人目の予定は Calendar API の JSON から読みます。確かめる点は、main()==0、2 人目のリマインドが 1 件、errors=1・reminded=1・skipped=0、stderr と runner のログにメールアドレス・ローカル部・予定名が出ないことです。人ごとの token を区別するため、_TokenStore の返り値を object() から _Token(email) に変えました
- 指摘2（軽微）を確かめた内容: infra/deploy/terraform_runtime_guard.sh の 6287 行（morning の allowed_env にこの 2 キーが無い）と 6329-6336 行（live と plan の env の差が allowed_env に無ければ die）を読みました。guard は env の値を live から導いていません。-var で上書きしているのは image と morning_digest_rule_enabled だけです。なので症状は『plan が止まる』で、『黙って戻る』のは誤りです
- 指摘2の修正: /Users/s-komata/dev/worktrees/teamagent-f0c-holidays/infra/terraform/morning_digest_schedule.tf のコメント 1 か所と、2 変数の description を直しました。追記を忘れると guard 経由の plan が live との env 差分で止まる、と書きました。既定へ黙って戻るのは、config 移行で allowed_env_changes.morning に載せた場合と guard を通さない apply の場合だけ、と明記しました。activation 版 tfvars へ追記する指示はそのまま残しています

## フラグ
- MORNING_DIGEST_HOLIDAY_SKIP: 既定 false（tf: morning_digest_holiday_skip = false）。true で祝日と会社休日はダイジェストを休み（リマインドだけ登録）、祝日明けは走査範囲を広げ、表の鮮度も警告する
- MORNING_DIGEST_EXTRA_SKIP_DATES: 既定 空（tf: morning_digest_extra_skip_dates = ""）。YYYY-MM-DD のカンマ区切り・最大 60 件。HOLIDAY_SKIP が true のときだけ効く
- 追加なし。前のコミットの MORNING_DIGEST_HOLIDAY_SKIP（既定 false）と MORNING_DIGEST_EXTRA_SKIP_DATES（既定 空）のままです

## 残り・要判断
- 別エージェントによる反対尋問はしていません（このサブエージェントにはエージェントを起動する手段がないため）。セルフレビューだけです
- 管理者 DM への 1 行はつないでいません。PR-0a の管理者 DM に jp_holidays.coverage_notice(day) の 1 行を足す必要があり、0a と 0c のどちらが後にマージされても、後の側で 1 行足してつなぎます
- 警報は、PR-0a の configure_logging()（JSON ログ）が入るまで鳴りません。runner はまだ structlog を設定していないので、今のログは JSON ではなく、metric filter に一致しません。警報は定義だけで、本番への反映は guard の開通後です
- guard の allowed_env（infra/deploy/terraform_runtime_guard.sh の morning 行）に 2 つのキーを足していません。test_terraform_runtime_guard.py を流さない指示なので、見ずに変更するのは避けました。live の TD にキーが無いまま guard 経由で plan すると、『足された env』として止まります。対策は、TD 差し替えのときに 2 つのキーを OFF でも入れておくこと（release_notes 参照）。恒久策として allowlist に足すかどうかは別途決める必要があります
- 会社休日の具体的な日付（年末年始）は未確定で、既定は空です。小俣さんに確認が必要です

## 検証
- 実装の申告: ["依存は CI と同じ `uv run --extra dev --extra mcp --extra media pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`。", "新規テスト 49 件はすべて緑（1 件あたり約 2 秒）:", "- tests/test_jp_holidays.py（12 件）: 祝日法の規則（ハッピーマンデー・振替休日・国民の休日）から導き直した表と一致すること。外から与えるのは春分・秋分だけ。ほかに範囲外は None、60 日前の境界、通知文。", "- tests/skills/test_morning_digest_delivery_calendar.py（14 件）: 10/12・10/13・11/3・11/4、大型連休、シルバーウィーク、年末年始（会社休日の有無）、上限 14 日、範囲外、env の読み取り。", "- tests/scripts/test_digest_holiday_skip.py（23 件）:", "  - 本物の CalendarEvent を窓で絞らずに返し、本物の skill.run と _collect_calendar を通す。", "  - Gmail の検索式 newer_than:Nd で走査範囲を確かめる。", "  - SlackClient と SchedulerClient のフェイ
- 変異: 変異は 6 種で、すべて赤（検出）でした。対象は scripts/run_morning_digest_fargate.py です。変異のたびに元へ戻し、SHA256 が一致すること（RESTORED: True）を確かめました。最後に git status が clean であることも確認済みです。スクリプトは /private/tmp/claude-163649916/-Users-s-komata-Claude-----/74aff9d5-930a-49b7-81d6-00c183006607/scratchpad/f0c_fix_mutate.py、ログは同じ場所の f0c_fix_mutate.log です。 - X1 予定取得の except Exception を ZeroDivisionError に変える（指摘の変異）: 4 件赤。赤になったのは新しいテストだけで、元の 
- 独立の再実行（CI と同じ extras・main）: 関係テスト緑・ruff・mypy 緑

## 本番
出し方と点け方は、前のコミット 78a203b2 の手順のままです。今回の変更はテストと tf の説明文だけで、本番の動きは変わりません。

手順の中で直すところは 1 つです。点け方の 5 で書いていた『activation 版 tfvars への追記を忘れると、guard 経由の apply で黙って OFF に戻る』は誤りでした。正しくは次のとおりです。
- 追記を忘れると、guard 経由の plan が live の TD との env 差分として止まります。次の mcp便も進めなくなります。
- 黙って OFF に戻るのは、guard を通さない apply の場合と、config 移行で allowed_env_changes.morning にこの 2 キーを載せた場合だけです。

どちらにしても、TD で ON にするときは activation 版 tfvars（~/dev/worktrees/teamagent-activation/infra/terraform/terraform.tfvars）へ同じ値を必ず追記してください。

author: bruce039
body:
Fixes #1957.

Both decoders chose LR.W/LR.D from funct3 and funct5 without looking at rs2, although the LR encodings require rs2 = 0. The tracer then passed the word to `LRW::new`/`LRD::new` with validation on, so debug builds panicked inside `Instruction::decode`, and release builds (and `decode_instruction` in jolt-program) accepted it as a plain LR. This adds a guard arm in front of the LR arms in both decoders that returns an error for rs2 != 0, following the MISC-MEM change in #1902.

Tests: `decode_rejects_lr_with_nonzero_rs2` (every rs2 1..31 for both widths) and `decode_accepts_lr_with_zero_rs2` in `tracer/src/instruction/lrw.rs`, plus two rows (one with aq/rl set) in jolt-program's `rejects_invalid_encodings_with_exact_messages`. The rejection tests fail on main. `cargo nextest run -p tracer -p jolt-program` passes (290), clippy with `host` and `host,zk` and fmt are clean.

Decoding of valid programs is unchanged; no effect on proofs and no breaking changes.

author: antpolkanov
body:
> 1. What triggered this change? (PBI link, Email Subject, conversation + reason, etc)

I wanted one rule that makes the case for GitButler, so people try it. It also covers the drawbacks and how to make an AI agent use `but` instead of plain Git.

> 2. What was changed?

- I added the rule "Do you know what benefits GitButler gives you?" (`gitbutler-benefits`).
- It leads with what you get: several branches at once, stacked PRs, clean history without interactive rebase, undo for every operation, conflicts that don't block you, and parallel AI agents in one folder.
- I left out how-to detail and link to the GitButler docs instead.
- A drawbacks section covers the new mental model, the `gitbutler/workspace` branch and its hooks, the shared folder for parallel branches, and tools that expect one checked-out branch.
- A section on making your agent use `but` has three steps: `but agent setup`, a version-control policy in AGENTS.md, and Claude Code deny rules for Git commands that write to branches. GitButler's docs say agent instructions "are not access controls", so the deny rules do the enforcing.
- The rule also covers what I first drafted as a separate rule on parallel agents (#13414). I closed that PR.
- I listed the rule in Rules to Better Version Control with Git and Rules to Better AI-Assisted Development.

> 3. I paired or mob programmed with:

No

body:
<!-- oss-factory:v1 {"kind":"leaf","lane":"hazard-evidence","tip_mints":0} -->

## Summary

Extends the hazard VERIFY chooser lifecycle stack (#97→#98→#100→#117→#122→#125): after dismiss/rebind mid-flight, `#100` already ignored concurrent clicks *within* one generation and `close()` freed the latch for a successor — but the abandoned generation's `choose()` `finally` still set `chooseInFlight = false` unconditionally. If the successor had already started its own evidence click, that stale finally wiped the successor latch and a second enable/rank could race through.

## Invariant

When a stale (dismissed/rebound) `choose()` settles, its `finally` must not clear `chooseInFlight` unless its starting generation is still current. `close()` remains the path that frees the latch for a successor. Same-generation soft-fail/throw recovery still clears the latch. Preference must not double-rank. Soft-fail/throw toast gates (#122/#117), stale success presentation (#125), and same-generation inflight guard (#100) stay intact.

## Product change

`choose()` `finally` clears `chooseInFlight` only when `generation === openGeneration`.

## Proof

```bash
node --test src/ui/hazardEvidenceHandoff.test.mjs
# GREEN @ tip: 15 pass / 0 fail
# RED (base #125 product + tip tests): 14 pass / 1 fail
#   not ok 15 - stale choose finally does not clear a successor in-flight latch
```

## Stack

#95 admit → #97 clear dismiss → #98 stale-choice → #100 inflight latch → #117 throw recover → #122 soft-fail stale toast → #125 stale success presentation → **stale finally latch**

tip_mints=0 · github_writes_origin=0 · promote=parked · no upstream writes

author: stewartadam
body:
## Summary

Before: at show scale (12,288 parameters, every layer asserting every parameter mid-fade), a compositor frame took 71 ms with 16 layers and 144 ms with 32. Most of that time went to copies nobody needed.

After: the same frames take 41 ms and 93 ms. That is still over budget; see the note at the end.

How:
- Every layer used to be cloned before compositing. `evaluate_transitions_with_compositing_context` now borrows the layer and returns a `SkippedAssertions` set. `merge_layer_with_attribution_skipping` leaves those assertions out, so attribution still matches the effective output. `apply_transitions_with_compositing_context` keeps its mutate-in-place behavior for existing callers.
- The whole `Parameter` component, including its DMX function `Vec`, used to be cloned for every asserted value just to resolve it against the base. `CompositorParameter::resolve_value` is now `resolve_value_with_current(value, current)`.
- `CompositorParameter::attribute` returns `&Attribute` instead of a clone.
- The `BaseLayer` component, a copy of the whole final composite on every layer entity, is removed. Nothing read it: desk bound it as `_base`, and flow only removed it.
- Per-parameter trace spans are only built while trace logging is enabled. A disabled span still cost about 15% of the frame.
- The standalone cue color-path walk from #112 borrows layers the same way.

Note on budget: the remaining cost is memory bound. About half the frame is transition evaluation, and most of that is stalls on a `Query::get` of the `Parameter` component plus `ParameterMap` hash lookups, one per parameter per layer. #118 addresses the per-layer parameter fetch; dense per-parameter slots would be a further step.

## Validation

- `cargo test` for compositor, fixtures, cues, desk, flow and timeline.
- New tests:
  - `evaluate_transitions_reports_delayed_assertion_without_mutating_layer`
  - `merge_layer_with_attribution_skipping_leaves_skipped_parameters_attributed_below`
- #107 `compositor_show_scale`, with an info-level tracing subscriber installed so disabled spans cost what they do in the app:

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| params=12288, layers=16 | 71.3 ms | 41.0 ms |
| params=12288, layers=32 | 144 ms | 93.5 ms |

## Release notes

Notes: Busy shows with many fading layers composite noticeably faster.

author: prasadtalasila
body:
## Type of Change

- [ ] New feature
- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Documentation update
- [ ] Refactoring
- [ ] Security patch
- [ ] Test coverage

## Description

- Pass `latex=path.suffix.lower() == ".tex"` from every caller that holds the file, in citation provenance, claim support, synthesis, the citekey union, `references.apply`, the evidence appendix and the quotation aid, so a `%`-commented or `\verb`-quoted citation in a `.tex` draft is no longer counted as live
- Read each file in the citekey union by its own suffix, so a `.tex` preamble and a `.md` front page each get their own rules
- Extract a `.tex` synthesis unit's citekeys from its unjoined lines, since a unit's lines are space-joined and a comment blanked after the join would swallow every line below it
- Pre-blank only LaTeX verbatim for a `.tex` draft's synthesis units, so a citation between two ``quoted'' phrases is no longer lost to Markdown's inline-code rule
- Keep `single-source:` declaration markers working in `.tex`, although they are themselves `%` comments

Option 1 from the issue, as decided: thread the suffix through each caller, the same way `unit accept` was fixed in #834. Markdown input is unchanged; each module's tests carry a `30%` control showing a percent sign in Markdown still reads as prose.

Closes #873

## What changed, from the user's point of view

On a `.tex` draft, a line like `% Dropped in review: \citep{key}` no longer makes the review aids report `key`:

- `review provenance` and `review support` no longer score a citekey cited only inside a `.tex` comment
- `review synthesis` no longer counts a commented-out citekey as a second source for its unit
- `review union` no longer reports a commented-out citekey in a `.tex` include as having entered outside every unit
- The evidence sidecar and `review quotation` no longer show or check the quote of a commented-out citekey

## Impact

PATCH bump, 6.125.12 to 6.125.13: a bug fix, with no CLI, output-format or dependency change. The signatures that gained a keyword-only `latex=False` are internal (`claims`, `units`, `used_citekeys`, `quoted_spans`, `evidence_appendix.build`), and the default keeps their existing Markdown behaviour.

## Test plan

- [x] Full suite with coverage, `.venv-full/bin/python -m pytest --cov`: 5869 passed, 7 skipped, 100.00% line and branch
- [x] `pylint --rcfile=.pylintrc chitragupta scripts .claude/hooks`, exit 0; `ruff format --check` and `ruff check` on CI's paths, exit 0. No Markdown changed, so markdownlint has nothing new to read
- [x] `poetry check`, exit 0 (only the repo's existing deprecation warnings)
- [x] Real end-to-end smoke test against the real ledger: a scratch `.tex` built from two citekeys that `content/drafts/.../survey.md` already cites, with the second on a `%` line. Before the fix, synthesis read one unit citing both keys and provenance scored both; after it, both read `kritzinger_digital_2018` only. `python -m chitragupta.review synthesis --unit paragraph` on the same file reports one single-source paragraph. The scratch file was removed afterwards
- [x] Each new regression test was confirmed failing before the fix
- Copilot review has been dormant on this repository since 2026-09-03, so none is expected here

### Notes for the reviewer

One existing test changed. `test_an_authored_preamble_is_read_as_the_assembly_s_own_material` put `% \citep{house_2020}` in `preamble.tex` and asserted the key appeared, which pinned the exact behaviour #873 reports. Its docstring is about a suffixless `\input{preamble}` resolving and being read as the assembly's own material, so the fixture now makes that citation live inside a `\newcommand` instead.

Other bare `extract_citekeys` or `_blank_code` callers remain outside the issue's list, and are left for a follow-up issue rather than widening this PR: `verbatim_check/_masking.py`, `registry/__init__.py` and `review/_claims.py`.

`citekey_union.py` now sits at exactly the 250-line C2 limit.

## Checklist

- [x] A failing test was written first, and confirmed failing, for each behaviour added or bug fixed.
- [x] No citekey is generated, guessed or rewritten anywhere in the change: every test reuses a key its file already used, and the smoke test used the draft's own keys.
- [x] Corresponding documentation updated, with each claim owned by exactly one document. No document describes these aids' LaTeX handling, so none needed changing.

author: maleadt
body:
On macOS, loading a stdlib that isn't in the sysimage can trigger a system notification that your terminal "was prevented from modifying apps on your Mac", which leads to a prompt for granting it the broad App Management permission.

The cause is the `touch` that code loading does on every cache file it accepts. Juliaup installs Julia as a signed app bundle, with the precompiled stdlibs inside it, and macOS blocks writes into signed bundles:

```
kernel: (Sandbox) System Policy: julia(11744) deny(1) file-write-data ~/.julia/juliaup/julia-1.12.7+0.aarch64.apple.darwin14/Julia-1.12.app/Contents/Resources/julia/share/julia/compiled/v1.12/Pkg/tUTdb_pSto6.ji
```

The `touch` is already wrapped in a `try`/`catch`, but merely attempting the write is enough for macOS to warn. A path-based `utimes` is denied as well.

The mtime update exists so that recently used caches are tried first and evicted last. Eviction and new cache files only ever happen in `DEPOT_PATH[1]`, so this PR only touches cache files there. Other depots (bundled, read-only, shared) are no longer written to by loading. A scratch depot placed first (`JULIA_DEPOT_PATH=/tmp/scratch:`) is `DEPOT_PATH[1]` and behaves as before. The only cost is that in secondary depots with several valid caches for a package, the try-order no longer follows recent use. Every candidate is still validated.

The same code exists in 1.10–1.12. I only labeled as backport-1.13 given that's the latest stable, but if we were to do additional <1.13 releases this is probably worth including there as well.

Assisted by: Opus 5.5, Sol 6

author: mudscode
body:
Fixes #9084

Since `ensure_config` started merging configs instead of overwriting (#7926), the explicit config handed to a subgraph carries the same tags as the ambient config it is merged onto, so tags doubled at every nesting level: a node three subgraphs deep saw 8 copies of every invoke-time tag. This skips explicit tags that were already inherited from the ambient config. Explicit configs still concatenate with each other exactly as before, so `test_ensure_config_tags_concat_preserves_order_and_duplicates` and the `with_config` behaviour that #7926 added are unchanged.

Beyond the repro from the issue I checked that, with this change, a node forwarding its config into a nested `subgraph.invoke(state, config)` two levels deep delivers the tag once (4x on `main`), `astream_events` reports the tag once on the leaf's `on_chain_start` at depth 3 (8x on `main`), a callback handler still fires once per node, and tags bound with `with_config` on a subgraph arrive alongside invoke-time tags without duplicates.

## Tests

Two `ensure_config` unit tests for the ambient case and a graph-level test that nests a compiled graph 0 to 3 levels deep and asserts the leaf sees the tag once. All fail on `main` and pass here. `make format`, `make lint` and `make test` (`NO_DOCKER=true`, 2033 passed) pass.

## Release note

Fixed invoke-time and `with_config` tags being duplicated at every subgraph level (2^depth copies) in node configs, callbacks and `astream_events`.

author: sireclifford
body:
## What
Adds emoji reactions to entries. Entry gains `reactionCounts`, aggregating every ReadReceipt's reaction into (emoji, count) pairs. EntryDetailView shows a smiley icon in the Details section header, once the entry has been read — tapping it opens a floating popover with five quick reactions, and the selection (plus a summary of everyone else's) shows directly under the content.

## Why
`ReadReceipt.reaction` has existed in the model with no UI since it was added. This gives staff a low-friction way to acknowledge something — condolences on a passing notice, a thumbs up on a safety fix — without writing a full comment, which stays reserved for actual discussion on Alerts.

## Why not
First pass put the picker and summary under the Read section, next to "Signed." Moved both under Details after review — reacting is about responding to the content itself, not about the read-receipt bookkeeping, so it reads more naturally sitting right under what you're reacting to.

author: icpryde
body: ## Summary Crossposting opened the card with an empty Title field, so every crosspost meant typing (or pasting) a title before the Crosspost button would enable. On reddit.com the crosspost form starts with the original post's title and you just pick a community. Apollo now does the same: the card opens with the original title already in the field, and an (x) at the end of the field clears it if you'd rather write your own. ## What changed One new file, `src/ApolloCrosspostTitle.xm`, plus its Makefile line. - **Prefill:** in `-[CrosspostPerformViewController viewDidLoad]` the title field (`textEntryNode`) gets `crosspostParent.title`, which is the post the card is crossposting (the same RDKLink the preview shows), styled with the field's own typing attributes. Then `editableTextNodeDidUpdateText:` is called the way an edit would call it, so Apollo re-runs its Crosspost-button check. The button enables as soon as a subreddit is picked. - **Clear (x):** an `xmark.circle.fill` at the end of the field's first line, tinted with the theme's placeholder colour and shown only while the field has text. Tapping it empties the field, puts the caret in it (like UIKit's clear button) and greys Crosspost out again. The field only exposes its text view to VoiceOver, so the text view also gets a "Clear title" custom action while there's text. - **Field grows to fit the title:** Apollo draws the field one line tall (`maximumLinesToDisplay = 1`), so a title longer than the field wrapped and the top of its second line peeked out of the bottom padding. That was rare with a short typed title, but almost every prefilled title is that long. The field now grows up to 5 lines, and anything longer scrolls inside it. Texture measures an `ASEditableTextNode`'s text at the full node width and only then adds `textContainerInset`, so a title that wraps only inside the insets was measured a line short. The crosspost title is now measured at the width it's drawn at. When an edit changes the line count, the card's layout is invalidated and the presentation controller measures it again. Apollo only measures the card when that controller lays out (appearing, keyboard changes, rotation). - **Dismiss prompt:** Apollo's close button and the tap outside the card ask "Dismiss Without Crossposting?" when a subreddit or flair is picked or the title field has any text. An untouched prefilled title isn't something you typed, so while those two checks run, the field reads as empty if (and only if) it still holds exactly the original title. Editing the title, or picking a subreddit or flair, still prompts like before. - **Card opens at the top:** the card is a scroll view that the presentation controller caps at 80% of the screen. When its content is taller than that (easy now with a two-line title above an image preview), UIKit's safe-area insets changing during the slide-in left the card opened scrolled to the bottom, with the header, the close button and the title field out of view. Traced with a probe to `_UIScrollViewAdjustForOverlayInsetsChangeIfNecessary` via `-[UIScrollView setSafeAreaInsets:]`, then the offset clamped to the bottom. The card always settles inside the safe area, so its scroll view no longer uses automatic content insets. ## Hopper notes (Apollo 1.15.11) - `CrosspostPerformViewController`: `viewDidLoad` 0x100499a54; `editableTextNodeDidUpdateText:` 0x10049c2e4 only calls the submit-state helper sub_100499fc0 (enabled when `selectedSubreddit` is set and the title string isn't empty); `closeButtonNodeTappedWithSender:` 0x10049a350 → sub_1004a227c. Its pseudo-code prompts when `selectedFlairOption` or `selectedSubreddit` is set or `textEntryNode.attributedText.string` isn't empty, and otherwise calls `dismissViewControllerAnimated:`. Ivars used here (`crosspostParent`, `textEntryNode`, `rootNode`) come from the class's runtime ivar list. - `CrosspostPerformPresentationController -tappedDarkOverlayViewWithTapGestureRecognizer:` 0x10049f484 → sub_1004a3980 → the same check (sub_10049a810, which has no other caller), then it dismisses only if `DarkOverlayPresentationController.enableTapOutsideToExit` is set. - Submit (`submitPostButtonNodeTappedWithSender:` → sub_1004a2368) reads `textEntryNode.attributedText.string` and passes it as `newTitle:` to `-[RDKClient submitCrosspostToSubredditWithName:newTitle:fullNameOfThingToCrosspost:flairID:flairText:completion:]`. The dismiss mask is never set on that path. - `frameOfPresentedViewInContainerView` measures the card node with `layoutThatFits:` and caps the height at 80% of the container. `containerViewWillLayoutSubviews` applies it. - Apollo's bundled Texture: `ASEditableTextNode` implements `attributedText` (nil while the placeholder shows), `setAttributedText:` (no delegate call), `calculateSizeThatFits:` (measures at the full width, then adds the insets) and `layout` (→ `_layoutTextView`). `textViewDidChange:` delivers `editableTextNodeDidUpdateText:` through `dispatch_async`. This card is the only user of `ASEditableTextNode` in Apollo (the only class in the class dump holding one), and each hook returns `%orig` first for any other instance. ## Verification **Sims:** Apollo-XPost27 (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 27.0, Liquid Glass, dark purple custom theme) with the API-key account and the API-key-free account; the non-glass SDK 16 shell installed on that same device as a second app; Apollo-XPost26 (iPhone 17 Pro, iOS 26.5, Liquid Glass, light theme) with the API-key-free account. Every run also loaded a sim-only probe (not part of this PR) that stops `submitCrosspost…` before any request is built and logs the title it was handed, so nothing was posted. `lsof` confirmed the loaded dylibs on every run. **Results:** - The card opens with the original title and the (x) at the end of the first line. A 39-character title takes 2 lines on the 402pt glass layout (field 43 → 66pt, nothing clipped), and a 36-character title takes 1 line. The same 36-character title takes 2 lines on the narrower non-glass shell (393pt). - (x): the field empties, the "Title" placeholder shows, the caret is in the field with the keyboard up, Crosspost greys out, and the field goes back to one line with the card re-measured (`title field height 66 -> 43, re-measuring the card`). - Typed a 264-character title after clearing: the field grew to the 5-line cap (43 → 134pt) and scrolls inside it. `&` and emoji render. - Close button and tap outside with the untouched title: the card dismisses with no prompt (27 glass, 26.5 glass, 27 non-glass). - Edited title (" really" appended), then close: "Dismiss Without Crossposting?" still shows, and Stay keeps the card and the edit. - Picked r/Destiny: Crosspost enabled without typing anything, and tapping it handed Apollo's submit `title="What is the reason you guys pirate for?"` (API-key-free, 27 and 26.5) and `title="Zidane's celebration on Olise's goal"` (API key, 27). Subreddits that disallow crossposts (r/apple, r/nintendo) still get Apollo's own alert. - Card taller than the 80% cap (two-line title above an image): opens at `contentOffset {0, 0}` with the header, close button and title field visible. Before that part of the change, the same card opened at `{0, 39}` with the header scrolled out of view. Not separately reproduced on main, where this post's card fits under the cap. - VoiceOver: the title text view exposes a "Clear title" custom action while it has text, and none once cleared. **Guard width:** every early return leaves the card exactly as stock. No `textEntryNode`, no title, or no typing attributes yet means the field is left empty (logged). The relayout skips a card that isn't on screen yet (its first measure already includes the title). The mask applies only while the field still holds exactly the title we fil

author: enjojoy
body:
## What

Publishing and scheduling now work on every connectable provider, not just X: **X, LinkedIn, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube**. The existing lease/retry publisher, Core validation, the Web composer, and Soko Bot tools all generalize over one shared per-provider rule set.

- Shared rules in `@sokosumi/utils`: per-provider text limits, media counts/byte caps/MIME lists, and requirement flags (Instagram needs media; TikTok/YouTube need a video; LinkedIn/YouTube need text).
- Core adapters under `apps/core/src/clients/social-post-providers/` translate one publish context into each provider's Composio tool sequence behind a single dispatch. Public-URL tools receive the Drive URL; file-only tools download and stage bytes.
- Attempts record the provider's create tool; `publishedUrl` comes from the adapter (provider permalink when the response has one, best-effort otherwise).
- Same duplicate-publish safety as X for every provider: once a create/publish call is initiated, a timeout settles as *outcome unknown* and is never retried automatically.
- Composer, post list, and calendar are provider-aware; the calendar API item carries `provider`.
- No Prisma migration: `SocialPost.provider` was already a free string and connections already stored each provider's identity id.

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-29-social-post-providers-design.md` · Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-29-social-post-providers.md` · ADR 0044.

## Provider notes

- **Facebook** now binds a connection to the account's single managed Page. Accounts that manage zero or several Pages fail the connect with a clear message; **existing Facebook connections must reconnect**.
- **TikTok** picks the most permissive privacy level the account offers at publish time and records it on the attempt (unaudited apps publish `SELF_ONLY`).
- **YouTube** publishes public; title derives from the post text.
- Existing X posts and connections are unaffected.

## Verification

- `pnpm check`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` — all green on the rebased tree (Core 8236, Web 8520, Utils 822, Bot 232, all 17 turbo tasks).
- Adapter/unit coverage per provider: session and tool args, refusals, outcome-unknown paths, TikTok privacy selection and status polling, Facebook exactly-one-Page, provider switch re-validation, unknown stored provider settlement.

## Before merge: owner-run manual E2E

No live Composio key in CI. Before this leaves draft, connect one account per provider with its publishing scope (LinkedIn `w_member_social`; Facebook `pages_show_list`, `pages_manage_posts`, `pages_read_engagement`; Instagram `instagram_business_content_publish`; TikTok `video.publish`; YouTube `youtube.upload`) and publish per the matrix; schedule one non-X post and confirm the cron publishes it. Record results here.

author: ericholscher
body:
readthedocs/readthedocs.org#13350 makes the search API retry with fuzzy matching when the exact query returns nothing, so a typo like "VBoxContaier" finds "VBoxContainer" without the user knowing the `~N` syntax. The response carries a `fuzzy_fallback` boolean when that happened.

Without any signal in the modal, those results would look like exact matches for the misspelled term, which is confusing when the highlighted word doesn't match what was typed. This renders a one-line notice above the hits ("No exact matches for "serch". Showing results for similar terms.") whenever the flag is set. The query shown is the API's `query` field, so filter arguments like `project:` aren't echoed back.

The no-results state and its syntax tips are unchanged; they still apply when even the fuzzy retry finds nothing. Until the backend PR ships the flag is simply absent and nothing new renders.

author: schooltoyayes
body:
Takes in [#19](https://github.com/schooltoyayes/Basic-Rnote-editor-Android/pull/19) by @Intranox with its four commits kept, and repairs what kept it from building. Once this is merged, #19's head commit is in main.

## What the feature does (Intranox's work)
- **Fonts…** in the ⋮ menu loads a `.ttf`, `.otf` or `.ttc` file and registers it under a family name. A note's text boxes that ask for that family are drawn in it, in the canvas, in the Typewriter's own field and in exports, instead of falling back to Android's default face.
- **The name** is read from the font file's `name` table (`FontNameReader`) and stays editable in the dialog. The dialog also lists the families the open note asks for that nothing covers yet.
- **Kept between sessions:** fonts are copied into the app's own storage and loaded when the app starts. A font can be removed again.
- **Rnote compatibility is not touched:** only how text is drawn changes. The note's own `font_family` is kept as it is, so what the tablet saves is what Rnote on the PC reads.

## What was wrong with #19 as submitted
1. **It could not compile.** The merge of main into `fonts-import` (7b8c523) dropped the `)` and `}` that close the `NameFontDialog` block in `MainActivity.kt`; the file had one open parenthesis and one open brace more than main. Before that merge (00ce418) the block was intact. The Actions never ran on the PR, as GitHub holds the workflows of a fork's first PR back for approval.
2. **A `.ttc` never gave its name.** For a font collection `FontNameReader` read the first font's offset from byte 8, which is the number of fonts; it is at byte 12. Checked with a real font wrapped in a collection: as submitted it gave `null`, with the offset from byte 12 it gave the family.

## What this adds
- **Closers restored**, and the offset fixed. Offsets are compared as Longs now, so one past 2 GB can't wrap round into the file.
- **Off the main thread:** reading the name and copying the font run in `Dispatchers.IO`. A font can be megabytes, and a provider such as Drive may have to fetch it first.
- **The copy's extension** is only ever a short run of letters and digits, so a file name can't steer where the copy is written.
- **Tests:**
  - `FontNameReaderTest` builds fonts byte by byte, so no font binary is kept in the repository: plain family, typographic family over the plain one, English over another language, Macintosh names, non-ASCII, the first font of a collection, no family name, not a font at all (cut at every length), an absurd table count, and a collection whose first font is out of the file. The collection test fails against the reader as submitted.
  - `CustomFontsTest` covers the saved list and the extension.
- **README** mentions Fonts….

## Not changed
- `CustomFonts.restore` still runs on the main thread in `onCreate`, as Intranox wrote it, so the first frame already draws with the fonts. It reads only the few font files the user loaded.
- With a font loaded, bold and italic come from Android's synthetic bold and slant, as a font file is one face.

## Tests
The Actions build is green on 2446c8d. The UI can't be run here, so **Fonts…** needs a look on the tablet with a note from the PC that names a font Android doesn't have.

## Sourcery 摘要

实现 M0 执行基础，用于验证输入、管理可恢复运行，并协调五项 AutoScribeAI 技能，同时不宣称支持浏览器采集或文档导出。

构建：

author: wilfgrainger
body:
Closes #89

## What changed

Cuts PR CI cost in time and complexity, without weakening any data-integrity guarantee:

- **Widened the cheap `docs` lane** — any `.md` / `.markdown` / `.txt` file anywhere in the tree now routes to the docs lane, which skips dependency install, build and tests. Previously only the `docs/` prefix and a fixed filename list qualified, so root-level planning docs (`north_star.md`, `roadmap.md`, `tasks.md`) and README-style edits paid for a full build.
- **Moved the code-integrity gatekeepers into the full lane** — `check-static-architecture`, `check-source-repair-backlog`, `check-source-ownership`, `check-change-complexity` and `check-lockfile-policy` no longer run in the always-on classify job. A docs-only PR no longer spins up those Node processes at all. They still run on every code PR.
- **Shallow checkout** — classify and full-quality now fetch `fetch-depth: 2` plus the base ref, instead of full git history.

The two universal cheap guards (changed-file text policy, PR-description) stay in classify.

## Public impact

None. These changes affect only CI on pull requests. Application code, published data, and the live site are untouched. Data-provenance gates run identically whenever code changes; they are simply skipped for pure documentation changes where they cannot apply.

## Validation

Lane routing was unit-tested locally across eight cases (planning docs, README, nested docs, plain text, app code, mixed code+docs, package.json, worker source) — all route as expected: docs-only to `docs`, anything touching code to `full`. The workflow YAML change is structural (job dependencies preserved: the `quality` gate still requires the selected lane to pass).

## Problem
A saved native V2 Worker executed the declared build and focused tests with exit 0, but the host recorded evidence=[] and refused Review. It had linked node_modules to the local .sortie-env/node_modules directory; protectedSnapshot treated directory symlinks as unverifiable and silently did not start evidence recording.

author: afloat16
body:
## Problem
Weight-standardized Conv2d accepts padding_mode but calls F.conv2d directly with numeric padding, so reflect, replicate and circular silently behave like zero padding. This changes boundary features and gradients.

## Change
Use the inherited _conv_forward with standardized weights and remove the unused functional import. Preserve stride, dilation, groups, bias and the existing variance convention.

## Validation
14 focused tests pass (original: 11 failed / 3 passed), independently rerun on the complete convolution and weight-standardization modules with PyTorch 2.10 CPU. Tests compare outputs and input/weight/bias gradients with explicit padding references, including grouped, strided/dilated and same-padding cases. No CIFAR training or full repository CI was run.

author: monsieurtanuki
body:
### What
The goal was to improve performances (memory usage, UX, execution time).

The general idea is to do less.

We computed a sort of "thumbnail", to be used as long as the server didn't receive the cropped image and send it back.
Given that even on my lousy smartphone the longest dimension in pixels is around 2400 and our max size for the server is 3000, we can say that 3000 is good enough for both.
So now we only compute one cropped file, good for both thumbnail and server.

Now we also use a different method to convert BMP to JPEG: a native file to file conversion. Much faster - around 200ms on my lousy smartphone in debug mode.

There are still issues to address:
* what if the input image is VERY big?
  * For the moment we read it all anyway, but there are potential parameters (targetWidth, targetHeight) that would reduce the impact.
  * We should also force its compression before sending to the server if one of its dimension is beyond 3000
* so far the "compute once" optim is only coded for products, not for price proofs.

### Fixes bug(s)
- Closes: #7723

### Files
New file:
* `image_cropper.dart`: Cropping an image file into another.

Deleted file:
* `image_compute_container.dart`

Impacted files:
* `background_task_image.dart`: used new class `ImageCropper`
* `crop_helper.dart`: minor refactoring
* `crop_page.dart`: used new class `ImageCropper`, and directly created the final JPEG
* `image_crop_page.dart`: minor refactoring
* `price_bulk_proof_card.dart`: minor refactoring
* `product_crop_helper.dart`: now using `smallCroppedFile` as the final JPEG

author: afternoon
body:
## What & why

The Transform panel's value fields now nudge with ↑/↓ and cancel with Esc, as #450 asks. The registry still owns every key:
- While a value field has focus, the editor's shortcut contexts swap the note editors' contexts for a new `value_field` context. #601 registers it, plus `value.nudge_up`/`value.nudge_down`, and a `DISJOINT_CONTEXTS` pair with `piano_roll`.
- ↑/↓ step Semitones by 1, Velocity by 0.05, and the seed's trailing number (`vary-1` → `vary-2`). Each stays within its range. The nudge starts from the typed text if it reads as a value, or else from the last good one.
- Esc goes through `view.close_surface` and puts back what was typed. The roll stays open and keeps its selection.
- The field never reads a key itself. It only tells the editor it has focus (`src/editor/valueFieldFocus.ts`).

This also brings arrow nudging back to the step editor's Transform fields, which #618 had turned from number inputs into text fields.

This is 23 of 24 and builds on #621. The stack starts at #600, and #640 follows it. It is a new slice because the fix did not fit under the 400-line ceiling in #618.

Refs #450

## Core flows

**Live.** CF-017, CF-018 and CF-019 were unparked in #621 and still pass. This PR does not touch any flow spec.

## Walkthrough

On #640, the PR that closes the issue.

## Evidence

- `bun run test` at this commit: 229 files and 2675 tests passed. `bun run check` passes (warnings only, none new). `tsc --noEmit` is clean on every slice, each on its own commit.
- `EditorView.test.tsx` › "nudges and cancels a Transform value field from the keyboard" presses keys on the focused field, as a person does. ↑↑↓ gives `+13 st` and the notes do not move; Esc reverts typed text; Transpose then applies. With `useEditorShortcuts.ts` reverted, it fails (`expected '+12 st' to be '+13 st'`).
- `transformModel.test.ts` covers each nudge and its limits.

The review's other blocking finding, analytics, is fixed lower in the stack:
- #612 now logs `note_audition` (first use) when the roll plays a note. Its test checks the event fires once and that pointer edits behave the same with analytics off, and it fails without the emission.
- #614 tests `note_clipboard` (once across copy and paste), `note_edit_failed` for a refused paste and a refused nudge, and that keyboard edits behave the same with analytics off. #614 is exactly 400 lines.

## Acceptance criteria met

- [x] Value fields accept typing; Enter commits, ↑/↓ nudge the value, Esc cancels, and invalid input reverts.
- [x] Analytics events for the new actions go through the catalog, and each is tested, including with analytics off.

**Not done:** Safari's `gesture*` pinch events are still not handled; only Ctrl+wheel is.

**No `deploy-preview` label:** #600 changes `firestore.rules`, and a preview runs against production's rules. Its hosted smoke test fails for exactly that reason (see the comment on #621).

author: kevinweinhold
body:
Clanker:

I'll check how half-day events and ward scoring work on this branch, then boost ward matching for half-day events while still allowing fill fallbacks.

Boosting ward priority for half-day events: same-ward candidates first, with cross-ward only as a last-resort fallback so schedules still fill.

Half-day ward priority is in place on kevin/halfDay.

Behavior for half-day events
When Length includes “half” (e.g. Half day):

- Same-ward only first (still soft gender/country among those people)
- Then same-ward with non-preferred days allowed
- Then same-ward with month spacing relaxed
- Cross-ward only as last resort so the event can still fill
- Ward weight is also much stronger for half-days (~280 vs ~100) and stays sticky when generating alternate schedules, so long cross-ward trips are avoided when possible.

Full-day events keep the previous ward → neighborhood → preferred day balance.

UI chips note half-day fallbacks when they kick in (e.g. “Half-day: cross-ward fallback”).

author: dertobsch
body:
closes #6087

Cancelling a sick note informed the sick person and the colleagues, but nobody in the office or the management. Now office and responsible management can subscribe to cancelled sick notes, like to edited ones, and get a mail with the cancellation.

## Changes

- New notification `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SICK_NOTE_CANCELLED_BY_MANAGEMENT_TO_MANAGEMENT`, shaped like `NOTIFICATION_EMAIL_SICK_NOTE_EDITED_BY_MANAGEMENT_TO_MANAGEMENT`:
  - available for office, and for boss, department head and second stage authority with `SICK_NOTE_CANCEL`
  - department related: office gets all sick notes, the others only the ones of persons they are responsible for
  - **disabled by default**: not part of the default notifications of new persons, no migration for existing ones
- New card "Stornierungen von Krankmeldungen" in the notification settings under "Krankmeldungen meiner Kolleg:innen", plus the hidden input on the personal tab so saving there keeps it.
- `SickNoteInteractionServiceImpl.cancel` sends the new mail `sick_note_cancelled_by_management_to_management`: who cancelled it, whose sick note, the link, period, AU period (if present), type and the cancellation comment. The canceller is not a recipient and is the reply-to.
- `MailRecipientServiceImpl` resolves bosses, department heads and second stage authorities also for notifications that need `SICK_NOTE_CANCEL` (the edited notification did the same with `SICK_NOTE_EDIT`), otherwise only office would ever be found.
- Backup model and demo data know the new notification. Texts in de, de_AT, en and el.
- The new mail and the existing `sick_note_edited_by_management_to_management` use the `_date_range` fragment now, so a one-day sick note reads "01.02.2022, vormittags" instead of "01.02.2022 bis 01.02.2022, vormittags" (also for the AU period). Three more mails have the same problem, see #6720.

## Not part of this

- The existing mail to the sick person names `sickNote.applier` as the one who cancelled, not the person who actually cancelled it.
- The one-day period in the holiday replacement and sick note conversion mails (#6720).

## Tests

- `MailNotificationTest`: who may enable the notification.
- `PersonServiceImplTest`: not part of the default notifications.
- `PersonNotificationsViewControllerTest`: visible for office.
- `MailRecipientServiceImplTest`: office, boss, department head and second stage authority with `SICK_NOTE_CANCEL` are recipients, without it they are not.
- `SickNoteMailServiceTest`: recipients, subject, template, model and reply-to; the canceller is filtered out.
- `SickNoteMailServiceIT`: the rendered German mail with and without AU period and comment; a one-day, half-day sick note for the edited and the cancelled mail.
- `SickNoteInteractionServiceImplTest`: cancelling sends the new mail.
- `mvnw verify` passes (5356 unit tests, 579 integration tests). Not checked manually in a running app.

author: xydt-tanshanshan
body:
## What Problem This Solves

`MainSessionRecoveryCapacity.acquire()` and `releaseCapacityAtTerminal()` have no total wait budget. With `STARTUP_RECOVERY_MAX_ACTIVE_RUNS = 1` (the hardcoded default in `main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts:31`), a single stuck recovery run blocks all other sessions' startup recovery dispatch forever — `acquire()` loops on `shouldContinue()` with 50ms polling but no deadline, and `releaseCapacityAtTerminal()` retries `waitForAgent` in an unbounded `while` loop. The `shouldContinue()` predicate checks abort signal and lifecycle generation, not elapsed time, so it does not protect against a run that is live but never terminates.

Related to #160866

## Why This Change Was Made

Add bounded wait budgets to both loops while preserving recovery ownership and the single-active-run invariant.

**Acquire timeout (P1: keep timed-out sessions eligible for recovery):** `acquire()` returns `undefined` after the budget, causing the caller to record the session as `skipped`. Without the retry-condition fix, a zero-failure scan would stop retrying, permanently abandoning the session. The retry loop in `main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts` now continues when `result.skipped > 0`, so a capacity-blocked session is re-scanned on the next attempt and dispatched once the slot frees up.

**Hold timeout (P1: do not release capacity while its recovery run is live):** When the hold budget is exhausted, `releaseCapacityAtTerminal()` checks `hasLiveAgentRunContext`. If the run is still live, the slot is **retained** — `onSettled()` is not called, preventing a second recovery from starting concurrently and preserving the run's typing state. Only when the run is no longer live does the slot release. This avoids changing the single-active-run policy without a maintainer decision on whether to cancel stalled runs.

Changes:
1. **`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-capacity.ts`** — Added `acquireTimeoutMs` option (default 60s). `acquire()` tracks a deadline and exits the polling loop when exceeded, returning `undefined`. The post-loop guard now also checks `active >= limit` to cover the timeout case.
2. **`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.ts`** — Added `holdTimeoutMs` option (default 5min) to `dispatchRestartRecoveryWithinCapacity` and `releaseCapacityAtTerminal`. On budget exhaustion with a live run, the slot is retained and a warning is logged; `onSettled()` is only called when the run is no longer live or settled normally.
3. **`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts`** — Retry loop now continues when `result.skipped > 0`, so capacity-blocked sessions remain eligible for recovery on the next scan.
4. **`src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.test.ts`** — Tests for: (a) acquire timeout returns `undefined`; (b) hold budget releases slot when run is no longer live; (c) hold budget retains slot when run is still live.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change for healthy recovery runs. The defaults (60s acquire, 5min hold) are well above normal startup recovery time. A capacity-blocked session is retried on the next scan instead of being abandoned. A stuck live run retains its slot (preserving the single-active-run invariant) but is logged for diagnosis. A run that is no longer live releases its slot after the hold budget, unblocking pending sessions.

## Evidence

### Changed files

- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-recovery-capacity.ts` — acquireTimeoutMs deadline + post-loop guard
- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.ts` — holdTimeoutMs + live-run slot retention
- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts` — retry condition includes skipped
- `src/agents/main-session-recovery/main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.test.ts` — 3 tests covering timeout + retention

### Test results

```console
$ git diff --stat
 .../main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.test.ts | 28 ++++++++++++++++++++--
 .../main-session-restart-dispatch-capacity.ts      | 17 +++++++++++--
 .../main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts       |  2 +-
 3 files changed, 42 insertions(+), 5 deletions(-)

$ node --import tsx -e "<capacity verification>"
T1 acquire timeout: undefined (OK)
T1 elapsed: 100 (OK)
---DONE---
```

The capacity module was verified via direct Node.js execution (vitest config had a Vite version mismatch in this checkout). The verification confirms `acquire()` returns `undefined` after the budget is exhausted.

The dispatch-capacity tests use the existing `recoveryRuntime`/`dispatchRecovery` helpers and mock `hasLiveAgentRunContext` to cover two scenarios:

| Scenario | hasLiveAgentRunContext | holdTimeoutMs | Expected onSettled | Expected slot |
|----------|------------------------|---------------|---------------------|---------------|
| Run no longer live | `false` | 100ms | called | released |
| Run still live | `true` | 100ms | not called | retained |

The retry-condition fix in `main-session-restart-recovery-runtime.ts` changes one line: `result.failed === 0` → `result.failed === 0 && result.skipped === 0`, ensuring capacity-blocked sessions (counted as `skipped`) trigger a retry instead of ending the scan.

### Lint

```console
$ node_modules/.bin/oxlint <4 changed files>
(no output — 0 errors)
```

body:
## Summary

Storyboards and image briefs kept collapsing into "clean flat" looks and
generic tweens. This adds a catalog of named drawn looks (paper and ink,
graphic, retro screen, 3D, generative) and physical motion, taken from a
reference reel of 32 looks and 16 motion patterns, to the Creator family,
each where its runtime reads it.

**Video vocabulary**: the kernel `motion-vocabulary.md` gains
"Character and physical motion" (spring, squash and stretch, anticipation,
follow-through, jointed walk, blink, line draw and retract, page turn,
loop, boil, animate on twos), "Drawn looks" in five families, ink bleed
and brush wipe transitions, and camera shake. It stays a rule-free
dictionary: joint-level motion is scoped to characters built from parts,
and look filters stay off supplied art.

**Video leaves**: create-story gains sumi-ink, watercolor, crayon and
silhouette worlds; create-explainer-video gains chalkboard, blueprint,
isometric and one-line media.

**Generated image leaves**: reimagine (+6), icon, emoji, mascot and kit
(+4 each) gain styles whose prompt blocks, avoid lists and QA cues fit
each leaf's cut-out finish (neon never promises a soft glow through a
hard-edged transparent cut; paper and isometric looks drop ground
shadows; sumi-ink adds no seal).

**Cards**: create-card and generate-card gain risograph, blueprint, CRT
and chalkboard as a pair, with CSS inside the renderer's existing
allowlist and matching backdrop prose. The card test now checks both
leaves list the same styles.

## Notes

- Six hard builds (jointed walk, page turn, flow field, risograph, ensō,
  spring with squash) were prototyped in HyperFrames: `check` passes and
  two renders were bit-identical. A knee bending the wrong way and a ball
  staying squashed after leaving the floor were fixed and written into
  the build notes.
- New cards were rendered locally and inspected at OG, carousel and
  story sizes. Seven trial generations ran on the Codex backend only; the
  origami icon's shadow and a first watercolor pass informed the prose.
- Fresh-context dry runs of VideoCreator and ImageCreator surfaced cast,
  background and cut-out contradictions, all fixed before commit.
- Already live: `verify-work-continuity.py` passed on the candidate, the
  live checkout runs this branch, `install.sh` linked the new files, and
  the gateway was restarted with all A2A endpoints back.
- Full suite: the same 3 failures as `main`, nothing new.
- Card looks that need texture on type (watercolor, sumi-ink) are left
  for a renderer change, not approximated.
