author: eandalf-bigstack
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it

This fixes, on release_3.1.20, the two defects #672's QA run found on cube36 (3.1.20 RC `698d74b2`, rolled from 3.1.10 RC4): row 3 (the `ceph` scrape job is `up=0`), row 8 (13 of 24 Grafana dashboards read No data) and row 11 (InfluxDB `def` retention is still 364d). The develop half is #1593.

> **Stacked on #1588** (`jim.lin/fix/keystone-legacy-member-role`, the keystone implied-role fix for #631). This branch starts from that PR's commit, so until #1588 merges, the commit list and diff here also show `8aa4c7a9`. **Review only the two commits below**; that one belongs to #1588. Merge #1588 first, and this PR's diff shrinks to these two commits.

| commit | what |
| :--- | :--- |
| `03e837f5` | `fix(haproxy)`: `ceph_prometheus_ep` reaches each mgr on its management address, the one it binds. Removes the storage-frontend (`strf`) plumbing that only this listener used. |
| `e814572b` | `fix(influxdb)`: each retention policy's duration and shard duration are set in one `ALTER`, and a failure is logged instead of discarded. |

**1. The ceph scrape has been down since the roll (rows 3 and 8).** `ceph_prometheus_ep` took its backends from the storage-frontend addresses (`hex_sdk cube_control_strf_addrs`, the `strf` option). That only worked while every mgr bound the wildcard. 9b3f295e narrowed `mgr/prometheus/server_addr` to each daemon's `MGMT_ADDR`. It was verified on accept-3cc, which runs one network, so there the two lists were the same addresses. On cube36 storage is `172.16.36.x`:

```
haproxy   server c1 172.16.36.1:9283 ... c2 172.16.36.2 ... c3 172.16.36.3      -> c1/c2/c3 DOWN, BACKEND DOWN
ceph      mgr.c1 mgr/prometheus/server_addr 10.32.36.1  (c2, c3 likewise)
ss        c1 10.32.36.1:9283   c2 10.32.36.2:9283 (active)   c3 *:9283
```

c3 answered on both addresses only because its mgr predates its per-daemon key (`*` in `ceph config dump`: it takes effect on a module restart). As a standby it returns an empty 200, which fails the `rstring .*ceph.*` check anyway. No `ceph_*` sample landed after 2026-09-24 15:00, and that is what emptied the 13 dashboards. The listener now uses the management addresses, like `ceph_restful_api` and `ceph_dashboard` in the same file, and like the single-node scrape of `sharedId:9283`.

**2. InfluxDB `def` kept 364d on the upgrade (row 11).** `CreateDBs` altered `def`'s duration, then its shard duration, each checked on its own by InfluxDB. From the old 364d/35d the first ALTER (14d) is refused against the 35d shard, and `HexSystemF`'s return was discarded. The second ALTER then shrinks the shard to 7d, which leaves the 364d/7d QA found in `telegraf` and `events`. **Swapping the two, as the #672 comment suggests, only moves the failure**: shard-first is refused when an operator raises the shard past the old duration. One statement with both clauses is checked against the final pair:

| on a throwaway database, influx 1.13.1 | result |
| :--- | :--- |
| `ALTER … DURATION 14d` on 364d/35d (the old first step) | rc 1, `retention policy duration must be greater than the shard duration` |
| `ALTER … DURATION 14d SHARD DURATION 7d DEFAULT` on 364d/35d | rc 0 → 14d/7d |
| `ALTER … DURATION 60d SHARD DURATION 30d DEFAULT` on 14d/7d (grow) | rc 0 → 60d/30d |
| `ALTER … SHARD DURATION 90d` on 60d/30d (shard-first, grow) | rc 1, same error |
| the clamped `14d/14d`; the same statement run twice | rc 0 |

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes

Fixes #672

#### Special notes for your reviewer

**Verification on cube36.** Backups are in `/root/claude-672/`.

- **haproxy:** on all three control nodes, the three `ceph_prometheus_ep` server lines were rewritten as `WriteConfig` now emits them, followed by `haproxy -c` and a reload.

  | check | before | after |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | haproxy `ceph_prometheus_ep` | c1/c2/c3 DOWN, backend DOWN | c2 (active mgr) UP; c1, c3 (standbys) DOWN as intended; backend UP |
  | `VIP:9285/metrics` | 000 | 200, 575083 bytes, every attempt |
  | Prometheus, all three replicas | `up{job="ceph"}=0`, `EOF` | `up{job="ceph"}=1` from the 18:33:45 scrape; `ceph_health_status` 0, 30 `ceph_osd_up`, 8481 `ceph_*` series; `count(up==0)` empty |

- **influxdb:** the two statements `CreateDBs` now emits were applied to `telegraf` and `events` on all three control nodes.

  | check | before | after |
  | :--- | :--- | :--- |
  | `def` / `hc` | 364d/7d / 7d/2d | 14d/7d (default) / 7d/2d, every rc 0 |
  | live `def` shard group 2026-09-07 → 2026-10-12 | expires 2027-10-11 | expires 2026-10-26, so nothing dropped |

- `cluster check`: all 28 groups `ok` afterwards. Telegraf still writes on all three nodes.
- Both modules compile with no diagnostics under the module flags (`-Wall -Werror`) in the jim-dev build jail, beside the unchanged files as a control.

**Not yet verified:** a full image build and a 3.1.10 → 3.1.20 `rolling_update` with this change.

**cube36's haproxy fix does not survive the RC.** cube36 still runs the RC `hex_config`, whose next haproxy commit (a reboot, or the cluster-start rewrite) writes the storage addresses back and takes the ceph scrape down again. The retention change holds: with the shard already at 7d, the RC's duration-first ALTER succeeds.

**What neither side checked, and still does not.** Both defects were silent: `Storage` and `MetricsDb` stayed green throughout. QA's suggestion to fold "every scrape target is up" into `health_prometheus_check` is not part of this PR.

#### Additional documentation

```docs
bigstack-handbook#823: https://github.com/bigstack-oss/bigstack-handbook/pull/823
  kb/cubecos/known-issues/ceph-prometheus-scrape-down-on-separate-storage-network.md (fixed-in:3.1.20)
  kb/cubecos/known-issues/influxdb-retention-cut-skipped-on-upgrade.md (fixed-in:3.1.20)
  kb/cubecos/architecture/metrics-retention-and-object-storage.md, kb/cubecos/known-issues/ceph-mgr-influx-bypasses-kapacitor.md
```

body:
## Description

Adds a per-session usage log and a "context resets" counter.

- **Capture:** Claude and Codex hooks and the Pi extension call a new hidden `aoe __usage-event`.
  - It records context starts with their reason (`startup`/`resume`/`clear`/`compact`/`fork`/`reload`), compactions (auto/manual), prompts and turn ends.
  - aoe also records session create, restart (at the single point every restart path goes through) and delete.
  - Events go to `<app_dir>/usage.db` (SQLite, WAL).
- **TUI:** a big red reset count in the top-right of the preview pane, with a breakdown (`clr · cmp (auto) · rsm`, current context age/prompts/turns, session age). It is hidden for sessions with no agent events and in panes too small to fit it.
- **Web:** `GET /api/sessions/{id}/usage` (closed in CityHall mode) and an overlay with the same content over the terminal view.
- **CLI:** `aoe usage` (cross-session report), `aoe usage show <session>`, and `aoe usage export --after-id N` (JSON lines, the feed for Harness Ledger).
- **Contract:** `docs/development/usage-events.md`.
- **Settings:** `session.usage_tracking` and `session.show_usage_overlay`, both on by default.
  - Usage never forces hook installation.
  - A profile with usage off records nothing: the hook checks `AOE_USAGE`.
- **Test isolation:** fixes two existing tests that wrote AoE hooks into whatever `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` the developer's shell pointed at.

author: nndroid
body:
## Root cause
The Rust repo's real-TAP matrix exposed a repeatable Go→Go download monopoly: upload striped across all 4 connections, but server download could assign ~100% of bytes to one physical path.

Go initializes every per-connection RTT cache to 50ms before TCP_INFO has a direction-specific sample. If one socket obtains a low RTT first, the adaptive near-MinRTT candidate filter treats the remaining bootstrap 50ms values as real measurements and excludes those paths. Excluded paths then receive no egress traffic, so the scheduler can self-lock into a single path.

## Fix
- explicitly treat the legacy 50ms bootstrap RTT (and zero) as unknown inside adaptive scheduling
- compute the near-MinRTT envelope from measured paths only
- allow unknown paths into the fair-start candidate set under normal active-path expansion
- score unknown paths at the best measured RTT only for scheduling eligibility/order; telemetry keeps the conservative fallback
- once a real RTT sample appears, the original near-MinRTT exclusion applies again, so genuinely slow paths remain excluded

## Regression coverage
- reproduce 1 measured low-RTT path + 3 bootstrap/unknown paths under 4-path bulk demand and require all 4 to receive scheduling decisions
- verify a genuinely measured 80ms path remains excluded while an unknown path is fair-started

This does not relax the net-perf utilization gate or change the wire format.

author: mengwong
body:
This is part 3 of D-22, the T6 ruling Meng made on 2026-09-26 (word SHRAPNEL): in L4, "no rule matched" is now `NOTHING`, and the result is `MAYBE` only where some input can reach the `OTHERWISE`.
With this PR, all three parts of D-22 have landed.

**This PR is stacked on #65, which is stacked on #64, #63, #62 and #61. Merge them in that order.**
Its own work is four commits:
- `0f0e08f`: code, tests and corpus;
- `1d21126`: docs;
- `dab3353`: the audited baseline re-record;
- a docs fix: the current round-trip count, and "L4 refuses `A`", which was wrong.

## Behaviour
- **Which tables change.** `noRuleMayMatch` treats a table as total if it has a trailing catch-all, a declared default, or an all-wildcard arm. Otherwise it asks `DMN.Regions.noMatchRegions` (#64).
- **Where a no-match region exists:**
  - the result becomes `GIVETH A MAYBE T`;
  - each arm becomes `JUST v`;
  - `OTHERWISE` becomes `NOTHING`, replacing the typed sentinel that used to answer at exit 0 as if a rule had matched.
- **A total table** emits exactly what it did before.
- **Tables `regionMap` cannot analyse** get `MAYBE`, unless they have a catch-all, a default or a wildcard arm.
  - That is the conservative choice. On a total table, `MAYBE` costs the caller an unwrap; on a partial table, a sentinel is a wrong answer.
  - This is what moves `list-input-membership-l4`, whose table really is partial.
- **Multi-output tables** wrap the whole record: `JUST (mk<Name> …)`.
- **List results** become `MAYBE (LIST OF T)`, because `l4 check` refuses `MAYBE LIST OF T`.
- **The `wrapMaybe` option is removed.** Nothing set it, and its only other effect was to wrap total tables, which rule 3 rules out.
- **The README's own example changes.** `README.md --pick="Example 2" --to=l4` now gives `MAYBE STRING`, because a Spring party of 4.5 guests matches no rule. The README is updated, and the new output was checked with `l4`.

## Verified with `l4`
- `l4` was on `PATH`, so every `TranslateL4Spec` example ran, with none pending. A new example checks the `NOTHING` and `JUST` answers under `l4 run`.
- `l4 check` was run on both versions of all 81 changed outputs:
  - 77 typecheck both before and after;
  - 4 fail both before and after, for older reasons: 3 tables have no output column, and 1 repeats a record field name.

## What moved
- **The three recordings D-22 names:**
  - `policy/l4-otherwise-sentinel-not-last-row`
  - `policy/list-output-l4-literal`
  - `policy/list-input-membership-l4`
- **Two symptom cases whose L4 output changed under rule 3:** `symptom/l4-output-range-upper-bound-dropped` and `symptom/l4-zero-output-dangling-giveth`. Their own defects are unchanged, so they stay symptoms.
- **Backend baseline:** 81 changed runs, all `--to=l4` stdout. Each differs only by `MAYBE` / `JUST` / `NOTHING`; none are ts/js/py and none are stderr. After an audited re-record, `--check` reports 1,260 runs, 0 changed.
- **A/B against `98cd8c5`:** 1,575 runs. Only those 81 `--to=l4` runs differ; ts, js, py and xml are identical.

## Known gap, left for a follow-up
A sum-typed table that is total but has no catch-all or default still gets `MAYBE`, for example `policy/l4-priority-reorders-arms`.
- This predates D-22: a sum type has no sentinel to put in an `OTHERWISE` that can never be reached.
- Rule 3 says total tables stay bare, so this is ordinary follow-up work under the same ruling.
- It is not done here, because it changes the output of total tables, and that needs its own audit.

## Gates
Re-run independently on the final head:
- `cabal test`: 0 failures.
- `make corpus`: 252 unchanged.
- `make roundtrip`: 197 fixtures, 135 pass, 0 FAIL, 10 xfail, 52 skipped.
- `make roundtrip-xsd`: 0 XSD-invalid.
- `backend-baseline.sh --check`: 1,260 runs, 0 changed.

author: raphaelfakhri
body:
Fixes #21540

`srvTypeAndPortFromFlags` reports an out-of-range port using the named result `srvType`. That variable is not assigned until after the range check, so the message names a stale or zero value instead of the flag the user passed. For example, `tailscale serve --tcp=65536` reports `too high for https flag`.

This change uses the loop key `k` so the message names the flag that is out of range.

## Testing

`TestSrvTypeAndPortFromFlagsPortTooHigh` checks the message for each of the four port flags.

- Before the fix: 3 of 4 subtests fail (`http`, `tcp` and `tls-terminated-tcp` report `https`).
- After the fix: 4 of 4 pass.

```
go test ./cmd/tailscale/cli -run TestSrvTypeAndPortFromFlagsPortTooHigh -v
```

author: henrychad1186-lang
body:
## Summary
On a shared deployment, the old "💾 Save chats" toggle wrote a single file that every visitor shared. Chats are now keyed to the signed-in viewer.

| Viewer | Saved to |
|---|---|
| Signed in + chat Sheet configured | Their own `chats_<hash>` tab in the Google Sheet, one row per message. Survives redeploys. |
| Signed in, no Sheet | A per-user file in `data/chat_history/` (gitignored). Survives refreshes, not a Cloud redeploy. |
| Sign-in configured, not signed in | Session only, with a **🔐 Sign in to save chats** button |
| Nothing configured (local) | Same as before: the opt-in toggle, which writes `data/chat_history.json` |

- **Identity:** `st.user` (the viewer's email). That comes from `st.login` or from Streamlit Cloud's own sign-in on a private app.
- **Keys:** each user is keyed by `sha256(email)[:16]`, so emails never appear in file or tab names.
- **Sheet layout:** one tab per user, so users can't overwrite each other's saves.
- **Failed loads:** a load that fails returns `None`, not `{}`. That session then saves nothing, so a network error can't wipe a user's history.
- **Signing in mid-session:** chats started before signing in are merged into the account.
- **Long messages:** content over the 50,000-character Sheets cell limit is truncated with a marker.
- **Setup:** README has the setup for `[auth]` (Google OIDC) and `[gm_chat_sheets]` (service account + spreadsheet key).

### Dependencies
The `requirements.txt` additions are `Authlib>=1.3.2,<1.7`, `httpx`, and `gspread>=6,<7`. The Authlib cap is deliberate: Authlib 1.7+ pulls `cryptography>=45`. That can't be installed over a distro-managed `cryptography`, so it would break the session-start hook's `pip install -r requirements.txt`. Authlib 1.6.x meets Streamlit's `>=1.3.2` requirement.

- `pytest`: 289 passed, 1 skipped (a file-permission test that can't run as root).
  - New `tests/test_chat_user_storage.py` checks:
    - user keys
    - Sheet rows round-tripping through text cells, and tolerance of hand edits

    - per-user tab isolation
    - a load error returning `None`, and an open failure saving nothing
    - every `resolve_backend` branch

  - **No auth:** the toggle is unchanged.

author: vitoledo
body:
## O que muda

### Janela do Pierre (`engine.ts`)
- **Problema:** a janela incremental (último sync − 3 dias) nunca relia compras de cartão que ainda estavam pendentes.
  - Quando o banco as efetivou semanas depois, com a data deslocada e o id da fatura oficial, a mudança se perdia.
  - As cópias efetivadas dos pagamentos, que o banco lança com data retroativa, também nunca eram buscadas.
- **Correção:** a janela agora começa na transação pendente mais antiga do SQLite (menos 3 dias), limitada à janela do `--full` (3 meses).

### Ciclos estimados substituídos (`reconcile.ts`)
- **Problema:** quando essas compras passam para a fatura oficial, o ciclo estimado (fallback por período) que as continha deixa de ser derivado. Com os totais antigos, ele contaria as mesmas compras duas vezes.
- **Correção:** quando nenhuma transação aponta mais para esse ciclo, os campos calculados são zerados: total de compras, valor pago e vínculos de pagamento.
  - A página e os campos do usuário (status, valor oficial, liquidação) são mantidos.
  - A execução avisa (`SUPERSEDED_ESTIMATED_BILL`) que a página pode ser apagada à mão.
  - Faturas reais que deixam de ser derivadas continuam intocadas (`STALE_BILL`).

## Validação

- Três testes novos:
  - o ciclo estimado substituído é zerado;
  - o ciclo estimado continua intocado enquanto alguma transação ainda aponta para ele;
  - a janela recua até a pendente mais antiga, com o piso de 3 meses.
- Suíte completa verde (764): os testes do backfill rodaram numa worktree com o SQLite congelado e os testes de estado git rodaram no checkout principal. Paridade com o plano congelado de 159 operações mantida; `typecheck` e `typecheck:test` limpos.
- Simulação contra o Notion real com a janela nova (07/07 → 29/09), sem precisar de `--full`:
  - 1 transação nova: a cópia efetivada de R$ 0,19;
  - 10 transações de julho atualizadas de pendente para efetivada, já vinculadas à fatura oficial;
  - fatura de agosto recalculada;
  - ciclo estimado de julho zerado.

body:
Werk OS hield in de gedeelde omlijsting oude viewport-grids vast. Op mobiel bleef slechts 58 pixels inhoud zichtbaar binnen een zwart vlak; op desktop schoof de projectactie onder de favorietenkolom. Werk, Horeca en Network volgen nu hun inhoud en beschikbare kolombreedte. De routecontrole detecteert ook afgeknelde binnenste werkvlakken.

De wereldkleuren waren bovendien alleen volledig toegepast op los geopende schermen. Binnen Pass en desktopvensters bleven oude donkere, rode of blauwe vlakken staan. De gedeelde kleurregels gelden nu ook voor ingebedde apps en hun werkvlakken, kaarten en bediening. Living blijft licht champagne, Work grafietgroen, Travel bordeauxzwart en Foundation nachtblauw. Omlijsting, wereldlabel en browserrand volgen de geopende app, inclusief het gebied van gedeelde werkruimtes en navigatie binnen een blad. Sluiten herstelt de onderliggende wereldkleur. De vaste route-identiteit en gegevensbronnen blijven intact. Het kleine verzoek om de hervatpositie te bewaren kan bij sluiten doorlopen, zodat WebKit dit niet halverwege afbreekt.

Pass kon na één installatie offline openen met opgeslagen HTML maar zonder de serverbundels en Command-modules. Na worker-overname vult Pass de openbare interfacebestanden aan, inclusief exacte bundeladressen. API-antwoorden, persoonlijke uploads en externe bronnen worden uitgesloten. Bij een onderbroken opstart verschijnt een herstelknop. Verbindingsverlies bewaart de sessie voor opnieuw proberen; een afgewezen sessie wordt gewist. Beide installatiecaches volgen de gedeelde CSS en deze bronwijzigingen.

Validatie:
- Build en volledige statische codecontrole slagen. De nieuwe browsertoets faalt aantoonbaar bij een echte bronmutatie in de wereldtoewijzing; de bron is daarna hersteld.
- 304 schermingangen op 390 en 1440 pixels gecontroleerd. Per breedte liepen zeven pagina's bij de gelijktijdige scan over de laadtijdlimiet; alle veertien gerichte hercontroles slagen. Geen resterende afwijkingen in de gemeten geometrie, wereldkleuren en werkvlakken.
- 61 ontwerp-, kleur-, contrast-, foto-opslag- en structuurtests slagen. Nieuwe browserproeven vergelijken los geopende en ingebedde apps, de vier Pass-werelden, gebiedsnavigatie, Home en de browserrand in Chromium en WebKit op beide breedtes.
- De acht mobiele inhoudsproeven, de werktafel-navigatieproef en 27 taal- en toegangstoetsen slagen. De eerder toegevoegde Pass-proeven dekken herstel na ontbrekende modules, installatie, offline openen, opnieuw verbinden en sessie-afwijzing.
- De CI bewaart de kleurschermafbeeldingen en vereist de nieuwe regressietoets in Chromium en WebKit.

De routecontrole gebruikt een gastsessie; gerichte toetsen dekken de genoemde ingelogde toestanden. Dit bewijst niet elke accounttoestand of pixelgelijkheid met de tekeningen. WebKit-emulatie is geen controle op een fysiek iPhone-toestel. Deze PR is geen productiepublicatie.

author: ut07
body:
**This is why a total failure went a full day unnoticed.**

`/api/resumes/upload` already returns everything needed:

```json
{ "tailorable": false,
  "tailoring_warning": "Saved and used to fill your profile, but <why>.
                        Tailoring will keep using your most recent LaTeX resume." }
```

Those fields were added, in the endpoint's own words, *"so the UI can show it,
rather than letting the user find out from 'Regenerate failed: Pipeline
failed'"*.

**Nothing read them.** Neither field appeared anywhere in `web/src`. Settings
threw the whole response away:

```js
await apiUpload('/api/resumes/upload', resumeFile)
setUploadStatus({ type: 'success', message: 'Resume uploaded and parsed successfully.' })
```

So on 2026-09-28 a master resume was uploaded, stored as plain text because the
PDF→LaTeX conversion was broken (fixed separately in
UT07/daily-job-hunt#120), silently skipped by the pipeline, and **every resume
for the next day was built from a 2026-04-05 template** — while this box said
the upload succeeded.

## Details worth noting

`result.tailorable === false`, not `!result.tailorable` — a response from an
older API build that lacks the field is still treated as success rather than
suddenly warning.

Reported as **info, not error**: the upload genuinely did succeed and did
populate the profile. What failed is narrower than "error" implies, and
overstating it trains people to ignore the banner.

`ResumeSection` is exported so the test can mount it without standing up the
whole Settings page and its auth context.

## Tests

Four: the warning shows, plain success still shows, a response without the
field is still success, and a hard upload failure still surfaces.

176 frontend tests pass; lint clean, repo-wide unchanged at the 21 pre-existing.

author: achiya-automation
body:
## What was wrong

With `SAFARI_MCP_ALLOW_USER_TABS` (#92), an adoption was recorded by the tab's **URL**, while `safari_switch_tab` stamped the adopted tab with the session's ordinary identity marker (`MCP_<markerId>_…`). Without `SAFARI_PROFILE`, `closeTab()` proves a tab by that marker alone, and the only close refusal was `_assertTabOwnership`'s `_isAdoptedURL(safari.getActiveTabURL())`.

So once the adopted tab navigated to a URL the session owns (`safari_navigate` registers every destination as owned), the refusal passed and the AppleScript close closed the user's tab. The README promises the opposite ("`safari_close_tab` still refuses").

The URL record also misfired the other way: adopting a page made every tab on that URL unclosable, the session's own included, and counted the URL as owned, for every session of an HTTP daemon (the set was module-level).

## The fix

Adoption is tied to the tab's identity instead of its URL:

- `safari.js switchTab(index, { adopt: true })` stamps a marker family of its own, `MCP_A<markerId>_…`. markerId is lowercase hex, so no session's own prefix starts with `MCP_A`, and another session sees the marker as foreign as before.
- One page script still checks, reads and stamps. A tab that already carries the session's adoption marker **keeps the family whatever the caller passes**, so switching away and back (safari_switch_tab, run_script switchTab, the batch action) never turns it into a closable tab.
- `isActiveTabAdopted()` (session state) replaces the URL lookups in `_assertTabOwnership`: the close refusal and the "(user tab, opted-in)" early return.
- `closeTab()` / `closeOwnTab()` refuse an adopted current tab on their own as well.
- `safari_wait_for_new_tab` claims with the new `{ claim: true }` (own family) and does not record an adopted tab among the tabs the session opened, which the tab cap and shutdown cleanup close.
- The URL-keyed `_adoptedTabURLs` / `_adoptUserTab` / `_isAdoptedURL` and the owned-tabs.json exclusion are removed: nothing about an adoption is written by URL, so it stays session-local by construction.

Unchanged: only `safari_switch_tab` adopts, only behind the flag; named profiles; the extension.

## Tests

`test/fallback-tab-proof.test.mjs` (fake Safari window running the page JavaScript in `node:vm`, real index.js handlers and safari.js functions; now also the real `safari_navigate` and `navigate()`):

- adopt a user's tab, navigate it to an owned URL: `safari_close_tab`, run_script `closeTab` and the batch `closeTab` all refuse (failed before the fix with `"Tab closed"`)
- the session's own tab on the adopted URL, and another session's tab on it, still close (failed before)
- switching away and back through each switch path keeps the tab unclosable
- `safari_wait_for_new_tab` landing on the adopted tab does not record it as the session's
- `closeTab()` / `closeOwnTab()` refuse by themselves; adoption leaves no owned URL and nothing in owned-tabs.json

Each new guard test was checked by mutation (dropping the family rule, the wait_for_new_tab guard, or both close refusals turns them red). `test/adopt-user-tabs.test.mjs` and `test/switch-tab-origin-guard.test.mjs` now pin the marker-based guard instead of the removed URL API.

`npm test`: 470/470. Lint and `tsc` counts are unchanged from main.

author: jk-sah
body:
Every timing defect the audit turned up was a transcription defect — a number measured in one job, typed into a table, and left there when that job was superseded. Three tables carried values the paper's own protocol section describes as unusable, and one quantity (the finite-element solve when the operator changes per sample) appeared twice with different values because two tables were fed by different scripts.

`make_timing_tables.py` emits the rows of all three timing tables, plus the derived figures the prose quotes — throughput ratio against the amortized FEM solve, single-query ratio, break-even query counts, and the rank at which the heterogeneous reduced model overtakes the FEM solve — directly from the measurement files. A table that disagrees with the measurements now does so only because it was edited by hand.

`--check` reports which emitted values are not yet in the manuscript: the cheap version of the audit that found the problem.

Tested end-to-end against a stub with the shape of the pending job's output. It already flags one claim that is likely to flip: the paper says the rank-32 reduced model "is faster than every neural model's batched throughput", but that comparison was made against batched figures contaminated by subnormal arithmetic. With denormals flushed the spectral branches land at 0.024–0.038 ms, bracketing the reduced model's 0.032 ms rather than sitting above it.

author: jhb-unik
body:
## Summary
Implements a playable MVP from the plans in `docs/`. Up to 5 players can create or join a room, race up the tower as colored Jumpman Løkke, dodge the Trump boss's barrels and rescue Motzfeldt.

- **Workspace:** a pnpm TypeScript monorepo with shared protocol, level, movement and item packages.
- **Server:** Fastify REST lobby (create, join, start with a signed room token) and a `ws` gateway (hello, heartbeat, size and rate limits, 60 s reconnect). The server runs the match at 60 Hz and sends snapshots at 20 Hz; clients only send inputs.
- **Game rules:**
  - Half-height jumps, so players must use ladders. Wall on the left, fall edge on the right.
  - A barrel hit stuns for exactly 2 s; falling off the edge respawns you with the same delay.
  - Side collisions shove the other player.
  - Three items (speed boost, shield, Tweet Storm), with better items for trailing players.
  - Server-confirmed finish order.
- **Client:** React screens (entry, lobby, match HUD, results, help) and a Three.js scene with a Mario Kart–style chase camera. The local player's movement is predicted client-side and other players are smoothed between snapshots.
- **Art:** sprites are cut out of the character sheets in `docs/design/graphics` by `tools/extract-sprites.mjs`.
- **Tooling:** ESLint, Prettier, Vitest, Playwright, a GitHub Actions `validate.yml`, a Dockerfile and an updated README.

Not in this PR (still in the backlog): Azure/Terraform, deployment pipelines, telemetry export, GDPR request endpoints and audit records.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm typecheck`
- [x] `pnpm test`: 90 unit and integration tests
- [x] `pnpm build && pnpm test:e2e`: 4 Playwright tests, including a two-player join, ready and race
- [x] A scripted Playwright bot finished a solo race with an item pickup, barrel hits and the rescue
- [x] Docker image builds; `/healthz` and room creation respond from the container
- [ ] Manual play with real players to tune game feel and item balance

Names and likenesses are parody and need legal/IP review before any public release.

author: icanbenchurcat
body:
🚨 Severity: HIGH

💡 Vulnerability:
1. In `GET /api/events/past`, `user.agentId` was string-interpolated into a PostgREST `.or()` query filter without sanitization or double quoting, allowing PostgREST filter string injection via special characters (such as `,`, `()`, `"`).
2. The query referenced incorrect database columns (`host_agent_id` instead of `host_id`, and `agent_id` instead of `user_id` in `event_attendance`), leading to query failures.
3. In `src/routes/events.ts`, the static route `GET /past` was registered after wildcard route `GET /:id`, causing requests to `/past` to be caught by `/:id` and fail with a UUID validation error.

🎯 Impact:
An attacker could manipulate PostgREST query filters to bypass filter constraints or crash database requests. Additionally, valid requests to fetch past events were intercepted by the wildcard route handler and failed.

🔧 Fix:
- Sanitized `user.agentId` in `src/routes/events.ts` by removing double quotes, parens, backslashes, and commas before double-quoting it in the PostgREST query filter string.
- Updated database column references to match the schema (`host_id` and `user_id`).
- Reordered route declarations in `src/routes/events.ts` so static endpoints (`/past`) are registered before parameterized endpoints (`/:id`).
- Added security unit tests in `tests/events_security.test.ts`.

✅ Verification:
- Ran `npx vitest run tests/events_security.test.ts` (all passed).
- Ran full test suite `npm run test` (31 files, 280 tests passed).
- Ran `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck` (all passed).

We are unable to pull the minio image from the quay.io container registry anymore.

The `alpine/minio` image is not quite a drop-in replacement as it has different filesystem/permissions and the minio user can't write in the `/data/` directory, this is the reason why I changed the directory where MinIO stores its data to `/home/minio/data/` which is writeable (as it's in the minio user home).

`/home/minio/data/` is still local to running Docker container as we're not interested in persisting it across runs and this was we don't need to mount a volume nor write on the host FS (not directly anyway).

body:
## Summary

- `to()` gains methods for `Date`, `POSIXct` (inheriting `tzone` from the prototype, defaulting to `"UTC"`), `hms`, and `Period` prototypes, dispatching to `to_date()`, `to_dttm()`, `to_time()`, and `to_dur()`. `POSIXlt` and `difftime` prototypes intentionally have no dedicated method.
- `to.default()` falls back to `vctrs::vec_cast()` for prototypes without a dedicated `to_*()` function. Subclasses of supported targets (e.g. tibbles, `vctrs_list_of`) and dim-ed targets (matrices/arrays) also route through the vctrs fallback.
- The C entry point `stbl_to()` keeps its fast paths for plain atomic/factor targets and delegates all other targets to the R-level `to()`, so downstream C code gets identical behavior — including the vctrs fallback — through the single existing callable.
- Registry guard: every `R/to_*.R` file now declares its target class(es) in a `# target class:` header (or `# target class: NA` to opt out). A new `to-registry` GitHub workflow fails if a header is missing, a claimed class has no `to()` method, or two files claim the same class.

## Note on error behavior (deviation from #367)

Issue #367 specifies that errors from the `vctrs::vec_cast()` fallback should propagate unchanged. As maintainer I have **intentionally overridden this**: fallback errors are caught and replaced with the standard `<stbl-error-coerce-*>` condition via `.stop_cant_coerce()`, so that `to()` always fails with a consistent stbl error regardless of which coercion path was taken. This is documented in the `to()` details section.

## Verification

- Full test suite: 2802 passing, 0 failures.
- `R/to.R` at 100% file-level test coverage.
- `devtools::check(error_on = "warning")`: 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 notes.
- Registry check script verified against all three failure modes locally.

Closes #366. Closes #367.

author: aliaska-varieva
body:
The filter dropdowns on the Logs page list at most **10 values per facet**. An organization whose name sorts eleventh is missing from the Source filter until some other filter narrows the log set enough for it to fit — nothing about that organization has changed.

Unrelated to the device-logs work; separate PR on purpose.

## Cause

Pinot applies its own default of 10 to any query that sets no `LIMIT`, and `PinotQueryBuilder` only emits one when asked:

```java
private void buildLimitClause(StringBuilder query) {
    if (limit != null) {
        query.append(SQL_LIMIT).append(limit);
    }
}
```

None of the five facet queries in `PinotClientLogRepository` called `.limit(...)`, so the SQL that reached Pinot was, verbatim from the failing test:

```sql
SELECT DISTINCT eventType FROM "logs" WHERE tenantId = '…' AND eventTimestamp >= … ORDER BY eventType
```

With `ORDER BY`, the ten that survive are the ten alphabetically first. Everything after them is dropped with no error.

## Scope — all five, not just the visible one

| Facet | Exceeds 10 in practice |
|---|---|
| Source (organizations) | yes — any tenant with 11+ customers |
| Event type | yes — audit event names alone exceed 10 |
| **Date range** | **yes, and worst of the three** — more than ten distinct ingest days is ordinary, so it only ever offered the ten *earliest* |
| Severity | no (5 values) |
| Tool | not today (7 known tools), but it grew by two this week |

The report that prompted this flagged date range as "depends; check" — it is affected, and arguably the most wrong of them, so it is fixed too. Severity and tool cannot overflow today; they are fixed anyway, since the next tool type added is free rather than another instance of this bug.

## Fix

`MAX_FILTER_OPTIONS = 10000` (the builder's own `MAX_LIMIT`) on each facet query, mirroring `PinotClientDeviceRepository`, which hit this earlier and documents it:

> `Pinot caps GROUP BY results at its default of 10 groups, which silently drops low-count buckets…`

The log repository never received the same change. `ORDER BY` stays, and stays *ahead* of `LIMIT`, so the bound cuts an ordered set rather than an arbitrary one — asserted by a test, since reversing them would be a silent regression of the same kind.

No frontend change: it renders whatever `logFilters` returns.

## Verification

**435 tests pass** (69 in `openframe-data-pinot`, 366 in `openframe-api-lib`).

The new `FacetLimits` tests were checked against the unfixed code first — both fail there, printing the offending SQL, which is how the `ORDER BY`-without-`LIMIT` above was captured. A regression test that passes before the fix would prove nothing.

An audit of `main` (255ed60) against the gateway (`rail0-gateway` main @ 3d3434f) found two endpoints the SDK could not reach, three list filters it could not send, a bug that left `err.code` undefined, and docs/examples that no longer work against the gateway:

- `PATCH /accounts/{account_id}` and `POST /webhooks/{id}/event_callbacks/{callback_id}/redeliver` had no SDK method.
- The non-JSON error-body fallback in `src/core/http.ts` built `{ status, message }`, neither of which is an `ApiErrorBody` field, so `err.code` was `undefined` on a proxy's HTML 502.
- The quick start and examples used one unauthenticated client for both parties. Every `/payments` route now requires a session, and `create` requires `payer` == session (`403 payer_must_be_caller`), so they fail as written.
- The README's release row said "anyone" and gave only one outcome. Since commercelayer/rail0-gateway#356 the submitter must be the payer or payee, and since #349 a release that empties both balances closes as `refunded`.
- The error docs described a `code → error → status` fallback that was removed with the #252 envelope, and the examples branched on the deprecated `.error`.

## What

All resource and type changes are made in `gen/generate.ts` and regenerated. `src/api.ts` is byte-identical to what the generator produces from the 3d3434f schema.

**New methods**
- `accounts.update(accountId, { name?, email? })`: PATCH, at least one field required (400), 409 if the value is taken, 403 `wallet_deactivated` / `account_deactivated` (#352). `active` is admin-only and not exposed. The resource doc now says an admin session can read or repair any account.
- `webhooks.redeliver(id, callbackId)` returns `{ status: 'queued' }` (202). The JSDoc and README cover the preconditions: the replay is async, so a disabled or circuit-open webhook drops it and `resetCircuit()` is needed first (`enable()` leaves an open circuit open). A foreign or unknown callback, or one with no stored payload, answers 404.

**Filters and types**
- `ListPaymentsParams.operation?: StoredTransactionOperation`
- `ListWalletsParams.token_active?: boolean`
- `ListWebhooksParams.topic` is now typed `WebhookTopic`
- New `UpdateAccountRequest`, exported from the index.
- `Wallet` drops `account_id`/`created_at`/`updated_at`. The Restricted entity never sends them, and nothing in src, tests, examples, rail0-admin or rail0-starter reads them.
- `page` JSDoc: bounded 1..1,000,000, 400 outside that range (#357).
- `removeToken`/`disableToken` JSDoc: 422 `default_payment_method` on the default holding. This replaces the old "(and loses `default`)" claim, which is no longer true.

**Errors**
- The fallback now builds `{ code: 'unknown_error', detail: 'HTTP <status>' }`.
- New hints, worded from `error_catalog.rb`: `account_deactivated`, `release_submitter_not_a_party`, `wallet_deactivated`, `not_your_account`, `payer_must_be_caller`, `invalid_sort`, `not_redrivable`, `rate_limited`, `validation_failed` (#358), `event_not_found`, `submission_timeout`.

**Docs and examples**
- Quick start and examples 01/02 use a `buyer` client and a `merchant` client, each signed in with `auth.login(key, domain)`, and use `addressFromPrivateKey` for payer/payee.
- 03 (refund) uses only a merchant session and 04 (dispute) only a buyer session, because only that party acts in them.
- Release row updated. Every catch block uses `err.code`, and the obsolete fallback paragraph is gone.
- `accounts.update`, `webhooks.redeliver`, the new filters and the page bound are documented.
- 05 also shows a redeliver and no longer says "one topic per webhook".

No version bump.

## Tests

- New tests: `accounts.update` (PATCH, only the fields passed, 409 surfaced with its code), `webhooks.redeliver` (path, POST, 202 body, 404), `payments.list({ operation })` including `dispute`, `wallets.list({ token_active })` including `false`, the non-JSON 502 fallback (`code === 'unknown_error'`, `detail === 'HTTP 502'`), and a hint for each new code.
- `test/client.test.ts` fixtures move from the pre-#252 `{ error, message }` body to `{ code, title, detail }` and assert `err.code`.
- `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, and `pnpm test` all pass (160 tests). `pnpm generate` against the 3d3434f schema produces no diff.

Note: gateway main moved on to edccd9e (#364, which changes the wallet-token add/enable/disable response schema to `WalletTokenHolding`) while this was in progress. `src/api.ts` is intentionally pinned to 3d3434f. Regenerating against #364 changes 4 lines in `src/api.ts` and no public types, so it can be a follow-up.

body:
## Summary

Re-vendors spec-core at 7e41240 (DescentVTT/spec-core#7). Only `pattern/glob.ts` changed: a leading `/` on a brace alternative now reads as it does on a pattern written alone, where the slash was dropped. `{/docs,src/**}` is `/docs` or `src/**`, and `/docs` is rooted at the filesystem's root. Every path the guard decides is repository-relative, so a rooted alternative matches none of them, exactly as `/docs` written alone already did.

No source outside the vendored copy changes. `VENDOR.json` names 7e41240, and `node scripts/vendor.mjs --check` in spec-core says the copy matches.

### Before / after

| Where | Pattern | Before (56c7e54) | After (7e41240), same as the pattern written alone |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| guard, `affectedFiles` | `{/docs,src/**}` | `docs/a.md` in-scope | `docs/a.md` out-of-scope (as `/docs`); `src/a.ts` in-scope as before |
| guard, `protectedFiles` | `{/docs,migrations/**}` | `docs/a.md` protected | `docs/a.md` not protected (as `/docs`); `migrations/1.sql` protected as before |
| guard, a ruling's paths | `{/src/db/schema.ts,migrations/1.sql}` | allows `src/db/schema.ts` | allows nothing there (as `/src/db/schema.ts`); `migrations/1.sql` ruled as before |
| packet, the scope list | `{/docs,src/**}` | listed as written | listed as written, no note, as `/docs` is: the README marks only patterns the guard cannot read, and a rooted pattern can be read |
| packet, the rules (`scopeBases`) | `{/docs,src/**}` | spec-guard asked about `docs`, `src` | asked about `/docs` (or `/` when there is no `docs`), `src`, as for `['/docs', 'src/**']`: spec-guard refuses a path outside the root, so the packet says the rules could not be read |
| audit, `dependencies.manifests` | `{/package.json,Gemfile}` | `package.json` at any depth is a manifest | `package.json` is not one (as `/package.json`); `Gemfile` as before; no `manifest-name-unread` warning |
| `init`, spec-graph's `patterns` | `{/briefs/**/*.md,docs/**/*.md}` | reads `briefs/` | does not read `briefs/` (as `/briefs/**/*.md`) |
| kept | `a/{/b,c}`, `/{docs,src}`, `{docs,src}` | | unchanged |

### Tests

New tests, each beside the same pattern written alone:

- `tests/unit/guard.test.ts`: a rooted alternative in the scope, the protections and a ruling's paths; the kept readings.
- `tests/unit/context.test.ts`: the packet lists `/docs`, `{/docs,src/**}` and `{/docs,/src/**}` as written, with empty `unreadableScope`, `unreadableProtections` and `unreadableRulingPaths`.
- `tests/integration/context.test.ts`: the rules section and the guard's decisions for `{/docs,src/**}` equal those for `['/docs', 'src/**']`.
- `tests/unit/manifests.test.ts`: `{/package.json,Gemfile}` against `/package.json` and `Gemfile`.
- `tests/unit/configure.test.ts`: `graphReadsBriefs` with `{/briefs/**/*.md,docs/**/*.md}`.

No existing test's expectation changed. The kept-readings test is the only new one that also passes against the 56c7e54 copy.

### Mutant replay (by hand, no Stryker)

The vendored copy is outside Stryker's `mutate`, and no harness source changed, so the sweep gains no mutants. To show the new tests hold the decision, I replayed these against the unit tests (log in the session scratchpad, `harness-vendor5-replay.log`):

| Mutant in vendored `glob.ts` | Result |
| --- | --- |
| whole file back to 56c7e54 | killed (7 new tests fail, integration included) |
| `rooted: whole.rooted \|\| alone.rooted` -> `whole.rooted` | killed (6) |
| same -> `alone.rooted` | killed (7) |
| `\|\|` -> `&&` | killed (7) |
| `unrooted`: `rooted: rest.startsWith('/')` -> `false` | killed (7) |
| same -> `true` | killed (25) |
| `parseAlternative(trailingSlash(alone.text, ...))` -> `text` | survived: equivalent. `parseAlternative` drops `''` and `.` segments and counts only named ones for `slashed`, so the leading slash gives the same segments. That is for spec-core's own sweep to judge. |

`git diff` after the replay shows only the intended changes, and `vendor.mjs --check` passes.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run lint`
- [x] `npm run build`
- [x] `npm test`, the full suite with integration: 34 files, 653 tests pass (646 before, 7 new)
- [x] The new tests fail against the 56c7e54 copy
- [x] `node C:/Repos/specs/spec-core/scripts/vendor.mjs --check <worktree>`: the copy matches spec-core
- [ ] CI: core mutation sweep

## Left alone

- A rooted pattern, alone or as a brace alternative, is readable but matches no path the guard is given, and the packet lists it with no note. `context` asks spec-guard about `/docs` or `/`, spec-guard refuses the whole query, and the rules for the rest of the scope are lost as well. All of this was already true of `/docs` written alone. Two ways to improve it, both for later and needing a decision: skip rooted bases in `scopeBases`, and name a rooted pattern in the packet as putting no path in the scope.
- `{/package.json,x}` names nothing and gets no warning, the same as `/package.json`.

## What and why

Re-measured #135 on current `main` before starting (\`node scripts/bench/pages.mjs --only=pages\`): the gallery and theme editor shell shift was already fixed (#187) and the scorecard's async-card shift already reduced (#188), but the gallery's Elements overview (\`#/elements\`) was still the worst site page at CLS 0.192, from a cause neither of those PRs touched: \`pk-grid\` only lays its \`pk-card\` children into columns once its shadow CSS applies (\`display: grid\`), so the card grid renders as one tall column and then jumps short the moment \`pk-grid\`/\`pk-card\` upgrade. \`core/site/gallery/gallery.css\` now reserves the same grid formula for \`pk-grid:not(:defined)\` inside \`.gx-el-group\`, the same pattern already used for the shell's top bar and the gallery's side nav.

The issue also asked for a guard: \`scripts/scorecard-sweep.mjs\`'s "pages" stage (the CI \`scorecard\` job) already fails a page load over CLS 0.1, but it only loaded the gallery's own hash routes - never the gallery's root, the scorecard page or the theme editor directly - so a shell-level CLS regression on those specific pages had no guard beyond the ad hoc bench script. It now loads all three once each alongside the existing routes.

Verified with \`node scripts/bench/pages.mjs --only=pages\` (median of runs, 1280x900, cache disabled, CLS over load + 3s):

| page | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| gallery | 0.037 | 0.037 (unchanged) |
| gallery #/elements | 0.192 | 0.096-0.105 |
| scorecard | 0.149 | 0.005-0.148 (noisy both ways; unchanged) |
| theme editor | 0.012 | 0.012 (unchanged) |

Visually checked the Elements overview at desktop width, light and dark, before and after: the card grid renders identically, no regression (`node scripts/ui-review.mjs` does not cover raw site pages - only `core/elements/**` gallery examples - so this was a manual check in the browser rather than the scripted review).

## Composition

Only existing elements (\`pk-grid\`, \`pk-card\`) and only their own default box, reserved a moment earlier than usual; no new markup or interaction logic.

## What remains on #135

Scorecard's CLS is not from the shell or from this route's own markup: #187 fixed the gallery and theme editor's shell-level shift, and #188 already reduced the scorecard's own async-card CLS by sequencing its five data cards into one reflow instead of five - both tried a min-height skeleton first and measured it worse, documented in the code (\`core/modules/scorecard/scorecard.js\`). What is left needs a deeper change to the scorecard run's own frame timing, which is out of scope for this CSS/guard pass; the new guard means a further regression there now fails the \`scorecard\` CI job instead of going unnoticed. Leaving #135 open for that remaining scorecard work.

## Issues

Refs #135

- [x] One issue, one pull request; about 400 lines of hand-written source or fewer (generated files do not count) - 3 files, ~20 lines
- [x] Changelog fragment added (`node scripts/changelog.mjs new fixed site-elements-grid-cls --issue 135`)
- [x] Tests added or updated; `node scripts/verify.mjs` passes
- [x] No generated file is committed
- [ ] Skills (`scripts/skills/`) and docs updated - not applicable: internal CLS fix and CI guard, no new prop/element/option/workflow for consumers
- [x] The issue has a comment saying what changed and what remains, and its checklist items are ticked
- [x] Ownership and reactivity rules respected (`core/STANDARDS.md`); only existing components used
- [x] No size budget raised
- [x] Changes how an element looks (CSS): manual before/after screenshots checked in the browser (see above); `node scripts/ui-review.mjs` does not apply to raw site pages

## Summary

Introduce a centralized composite action for Nextcloud App Store publication so consumer workflow YAML no longer needs to own build, signing, recovery, upload, and publication logic.

This first stage intentionally adds the action before changing the organization workflow template, so the follow-up template PR can pin a commit that is already part of `main`.

- add `actions/nextcloud-appstore-publish`
- preserve generic Krankerl and Makefile publication behavior
- expose explicit inputs for submodules, Makefile signing, setup-integrity verification, and manual recovery
- constrain manual recovery to a stable branch that contains the requested release tag
- keep tagged application source immutable during recovery
- pin all external actions to immutable SHAs
- replace release upload action with the runner `gh` CLI
- avoid `GITHUB_ENV` propagation for derived values
- extend workflow policy checks to composite actions
- add regression/contract tests for immutable `uses`, safe step ids, tagged source integrity, recovery ancestry, asset naming, and security-sensitive environment handling

A follow-up PR will reduce `workflow-templates/appstore-build-publish.yml` to a thin wrapper pinned to the merged action SHA.

### smol-toml: Denial of Service via malformed TOML documents
[CVE-2026-85730](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-85730) / [GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2](https://redirect.github.com/advisories/GHSA-7w5x-hrqm-74c2)

<details>
<summary>More information</summary>

#### Details
##### Summary
`parse()` can be forced into an infinite loop when a value inside an array or inline table is followed by a comment that has no trailing newline (i.e. the comment "ends" the document).

The library fails to exit an internal loop when attempting to find the end of the structure, resetting its cursor to the beginning of the string instead. This causes the parser to indefinitely hang, compromising the availability of the service.

##### Proof of concept

```js
import { parse } from 'smol-toml'
parse('a=[1 #')   // never returns; CPU pinned at 100%
```

##### Impact

Applications which parse arbitrary TOML documents can suffer major availability issues if they receive malicious input. This issue is particularly severe for these use-cases, and it is **strongly advised** to upgrade to an up-to-date version of the library as soon as possible.

If your use-case does not involve parsing arbitrary TOML documents from untrusted sources, the impact is much lower in practice, although it's still advisable to update to version 1.7.1.

##### Patches

Version 1.7.1 properly breaks out of the loop in these situations and throws the expected `TomlError`.

##### Workarounds

None that don't involve refactors. Update the library **as soon as possible** if your use-case involves parsing arbitrary TOML documents from untrusted sources.

Reported By : [Ravindu Lakmina Munaweera](https://www.linkedin.com/in/ravindulakmina/)

#### Severity
- CVSS Score: 8.2 / 10 (High)
- Vector String: `CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:P/PR:N/UI:N/VC:N/VI:N/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N`

body: ## Summary The jimage index and its package catalog already share one name tree. Composing the classpath package tree still copied every JDK class into a third tree and kept that copy in the process-wide package-tree cache. Compose now adopts the larger catalog tree when it has more nodes than the tree built so far, and it reuses that tree's ids. A smaller catalog merged afterward copies only its own classes across. Directory deltas still clone the composed tree's class lists; they no longer need a private copy of the JDK nodes. Class files for the measured workload are byte-identical to the parent (2002 files). ## Test `jvm::classpath::fq_tests::jimage_index_uses_name_ids_for_class_lookup_and_package_parent` composes a catalog from the index and checks that the composed tree is the same name-tree allocation and that `java/lang/String` keeps the index id. The rest of `jvm::classpath::fq_tests` passed, including the base-plus-delta compose. ## Measurement Parent `4818dc0df` versus head `f710f2777`. Gate profile, one compile of `fun box(): String = "OK"` plus `class C0` … `class C1999`, stdlib on the classpath. One warmup per binary, then five interleaved runs. The row is the median. Spread is max − min of those five. | | calls | total | peak | live | RSS | user | wall | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | parent | 3,918,069 | 842.72 MB | 49,686 KB | 19,798 KB | 96,716 KB | 14.97 s | 15.04 s | | parent spread | 43 | 1.76 MB | 2 KB | 2 KB | 180 KB | 0.32 s | 0.30 s | | head | 3,872,338 | 833.92 MB | 47,338 KB | 17,450 KB | 94,476 KB | 14.89 s | 14.95 s | | head spread | 26 | 2.60 MB | 1 KB | 2 KB | 336 KB | 0.44 s | 0.45 s | | delta | −45,731 | −8.81 MB | −2,347 KB | −2,348 KB | −2,240 KB | −0.08 s | −0.09 s | RSS ranges do not overlap (parent 96,620–96,800 KB, head 94,256–94,592 KB). Follow-up to the panel UX rework: the keyboard check gave no feedback.

## What changes
- **The top of the panel says what each keyboard round did:** "This round checked 200 stops. 2 keyboard problems are in the queue." (or "No keyboard problems found so far."), in a status region.
- **Show keyboard problems** opens the first keyboard problem in the queue, opening a closed group if needed, scrolls it into view and moves focus to it. The finding selection moved from `Findings` up to `Report` so it can be opened from the top.
- **Rounds go up to 200 stops instead of 50.** The existing 20s limit still ends a round early on heavy pages. Only the extension changes: the hosted scan keeps its own cap because of its serverless time budget.

## Tests

author: anjingdtl
body:
按 `docs/Shine-TRPG_1M_RESIDENT_BUILD_PLAN.md` 完成「全量构建按 1M 大模型重新设计（全书驻留构建）」P0–P5 的实际施工：实现、测试、审查与交付。施工报告与决策记录见 `docs/reviews/1M_RESIDENT_BUILD_REVIEW.md`。

## 改动摘要

- **P0 预算模型与打包器 v2**：`ModelBudget` 扩展（`maxContentOutputTokens`/`reasoningReserveTokens`/`reasoningEffort`/`supportsPromptCache`）；`planExtractGroups` 改输出预算驱动（`clamp(content×0.7/est, 4, 32)`），`maxGroupSegments` 64→32 语义化为证据归属可靠性上限；`OutputPerChunkCalibrator` 在线校准（前 3 单元后一次、每 10 组滑窗）；解除 `profileModelBudget`/`llmGroupExtractor` 的 8k 硬钳；GLM 类不可关思考模型强制 ≥8k 输出头寸。
- **P1 provider 请求层**：DeepSeek（non-thinking 开关）/ GLM（`reasoning_effort` + `clear_thinking:false`，`max_tokens = 内容+预留`）方言透传，仅显式声明时发送（2026-09-27 不自动关闭政策保持）；`followUpUserMessages` 支持 resident 三段消息；`probeCapabilities` v2：同长提示（≥1024 token）双发探测前缀缓存（cached_tokens>0）、输出上限接受性、reasoning_tokens 上报检测；usage 细分（cached/reasoning tokens）贯穿 metric 与 unit usageJson。
- **P2 coordinator resident + 并发**：`mode:'resident'`（全书 ≤85% 窗口且 probe 确认前缀缓存才驻留；否则透明退化 windowed 并在 run 上记录 `resident_degraded_*` 原因码）；N worker 并发（默认 3、1–4、TPM×0.7 保守封顶、缓存流量全计入）；`claimUnit` 改为单条原子条件 UPDATE（`execute` 端口新增受影响行数返回）；`reasoning_only` 先升预留（2k→4k→8k→16k→32k 梯子）重试一次再事务性拆分；拆分份数由在线校准估值决定；每单元背靠背执行保活缓存。
- **P3 Pass 0 全书实体注册表**：`bookRegistry` 一次请求（≤8k、high effort）产实体清单，本地白名单/去重后经既有 `upsertEntity` 落种子；rule_mapping job 检查点幂等；`key:type` 摘要注入每个范围指令（优先注册表 key）；失败降级不阻塞。
- **P4 ruleMappings 落库 + WorldMapper V2**：`applyExtraction` 解析映射——target 必须已知实体、每条 evidenceQuotes 必须逐字命中本组已验证引文（checkEvidence 同级纪律）；失败记 `rule_mapping` issue 且不阻塞 facts/events；`commitChunkResult` 同一事务内以稳定 `mappingId`（map-world-target-kind-token）幂等落 `world_rule_mappings`（表与迁移双写均已存在，零 schema 变更）；Mapper V2 resident 模式单批全量 facts（解除 MAX_PROMPT_FACTS=800 截断）+ 全实体/事件视野 + ruleMappings 提案（`cleanRuleMapping` 同证据纪律）；windowed 批量路径不变。附带修复跨指纹重放时 conflict 事实 factId 的 UNIQUE 冲突。
- **P5 Pass 3 时间线 + 预设 + 文档**：`timelinePass` 全书事件一次请求排序/依赖（模型仅提议、未知依赖丢弃、本地 `resolveEventProposals` 兜底、检查点幂等）；mobile 新增 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 与 GLM-5.3-Flash 预设（1,048,576 窗口、16,384 内容输出、GLM low+2,048 预留+TPM 3M）与设置 UI 预设选择；DEVELOPMENT_STATUS 与施工报告更新。

## 阶段提交

| 提交 | 阶段 |
|---|---|
| 91cfd17 feat(worldBuild): drive extract packing by output budgets with reasoning reserves | P0+P1 |
| b48317e feat(worldBuild): add resident mode with concurrent workers and atomic claims | P2 |
| 6cf1395 feat(world): seed a whole-book entity registry before resident extraction | P3 |
| 17b05c4 feat(world): persist evidence-verified rule mappings through the production commit path | P4 |
| 86d040d feat(worldBuild): add timeline pass, 1M model presets and construction docs | P5 |

## 验收证据（可复现）

```
$ npm run verify:core
ℹ tests 266   ℹ pass 266   ℹ fail 0

$ npm --prefix mobile run typecheck
（通过，退出码 0）

$ node --test tests/migrations.test.cjs   # 含于 verify:core，通过；本次零 schema 变更
```

**T1–T8 回归**（新增 5 个测试文件 `tests/resident-build-p0..p4.test.cjs`）：

- **T1 打包器**：944×1200cp + 1M 预算 → 68 组、每组 ≤14 块（≤32 上限）、估算输出 ≤0.7×内容预算；16k 档组内 ∈[4,32]。
- **T2 前缀稳定**：resident 各单元 messages[0]/messages[1] 字节一致，仅 messages[2] 范围指令不同（provider 层 + coordinator 层双重断言）。
- **T3 reasoning 透传**：DeepSeek `thinking:disabled`、无 reasoning_effort、max_tokens=16,384；GLM `reasoning_effort=low` + `clear_thinking:false`、max_tokens=18,432=内容+预留、距 131,072 ≥8k。
- **T4 并发幂等**：2 worker 每单元恰一次请求、每块 job attempts=1、factId 无重复、unitsDone=unitsTotal；跨指纹全量重放 `world_rule_mappings` 行数不增。
- **T5 ruleMappings 落库**：走生产「抽取→提交」通路（未直调 saveRuleMapping）：恰 1 条证据完备映射落库（status=active、ruleset=0.2.0、稳定 mappingId）；编造引文/未知 target/空证据三类全拒且不阻塞 facts。
- **T6 reasoning_only**：第一次触发升预留重试（恰一次 12,096=8,000+4,096）、零拆分；`tests/phase2-acceptance.test.cjs:397` 既有语义原样保留并通过。
- **T7 缓存退化**：cached_tokens=0 → `planVersion=plan-group-1` + `lastErrorCode=resident_degraded_no_prompt_cache`，退化 run 正常完成。
- **T8 诚实性**：checkEvidence 篡改 span 仍丢弃；映射无真证据不落库（不降级 design_fill 冒充）；design_fill 技能语义由既有 phase2-package-build 测试继续钉住。

测试语料全部为仓内 fixture（≤50KB）与合成数据，无第三方小说全文。

## 端到端数据声明

**未验**：无可用的 DeepSeek V4.1 Flash / GLM-5.3-Flash 真实端点与密钥。请求数、截断拆分次数（目标 ≤2）、prime 后 cached_tokens 命中率（>80%）、GLM reasoning_tokens 均值（≤1.5×预留）、端到端耗时（≤20 分钟@并发3）、费用对账均未实测——以上以 mock provider 的单元/集成测试验证行为正确性，不冒充端到端验收。

## 未取证项清单

1. 真实端点端到端全套指标（如上）。
2. 两家模型规格未按方案要求在施工前复核官方文档（沿用方案检索值）。
3. probe v2 输出上限探测在真实网关上的错误形态（网关改写 max_tokens 而非 4xx）未实测。
4. 缓存 TTL 暂停续建「重付一次 prime」仅代码路径，无真实 TTL 实测。
5. 施工沙箱曾被平台重置一次，P0–P2 首轮实现丢失后按同设计重建（两轮均全绿）；远端 `trae/agent-58KSzL` 为外部占位分支（单文件 stub），与本施工无关。

完整决策记录（D-1…D-7）与硬约束核对见 `docs/reviews/1M_RESIDENT_BUILD_REVIEW.md`。骰点确定性路径、cleanSkill/cleanProvenance/checkEvidence/validate 四道门、canon 不可变、存档兼容、迁移双写均零触碰或未放宽。

# feat(application): recover read-only assistant tool failures

Keep assistant conversations useful when a read-only lookup encounters a temporary
dependency failure, without retrying mutation tools or exposing upstream errors.

## Changes

* Retry only the six registered read-only assistant tools, with typed transient
  error classification, bounded attempts and waits, and database rollback before
  another call can use the shared session.
* Return sanitized failed-tool results to the model, persist and replay paired
  calls and returns, and preserve successful parallel results and SSE ordering.
  Failed result writes end the stream with a generic error rather than a false
  completion.
* Keep URL-import timeouts at HTTP 408 and sanitize fetch errors in its SSE stream
  while allowing the chat fetch tool to opt into typed retries.

body:
## R137 · Corrección definitiva de continuidad visual en Preventivo

R136 se ejecutaba antes de que el módulo global de paneles desplegables transformara cada grupo de equipo en un `<details>`. Esa conversión ocurría después y volvía a crear el grupo con `open=false`, provocando que se minimizara nuevamente.

### Corrección R137
- Conserva el estado abierto por **nombre de equipo**.
- Reconoce el grupo antes (`section.v1523-prev-equipment-group`) y después (`details.v1523-prev-equipment-group`) de la conversión.
- Marca el equipo que debe permanecer abierto antes de la conversión.
- Detecta la conversión posterior y reaplica `open=true`.
- Se engancha al render real `v1523RenderPreventiveContent`, que es el que reconstruye la vista mostrada en producción.
- Mantiene posición vertical y desplazamiento horizontal.
- Cubre **Calendarizar**, **Reprogramar** y **Confirmar ejecución**.

### Seguridad / alcance
- No realiza consultas ni escrituras adicionales.
- No modifica Plan Matriz, EDP, fechas, filtros ni reglas contractuales.
- R136 deja de ejecutarse en paralelo para evitar doble restauración.
- Conserva R132–R135.

### Validación
- Rama creada desde producción `6362a804b4fa9d007f807e3cf2a48ea931cc920a`.
- 0 commits detrás de `main`.
- Sintaxis del módulo y loader validada.

## Problem
Regenerate re-sent the original user message's `custom_content`, including its stored `configuration_value`. If Deep Research (or any other tool toggle) was switched on or off after stopping the first answer, Regenerate ignored the change and ran with the old setting.

## Changes
- **`libs/chat-hooks` – `useConversationHandlers.handleRegenerateMessage`**: sends the current `toolConfigurationValue` as `configuration_value`, keeps the rest of the user message's `custom_content` (attachments, form value, skills), and updates the local user message to match.
- **`apps/chat-api` – `buildConversationHistory` (Regenerate mode)**: when the request carries a `configuration_value`, it is persisted on the user message being answered, so a reload restores the toggle state the answer was actually generated with. Without one, the stored value is kept as before.
- **OpenSpec**: added a Regenerate scenario to `chat-hooks-conversation-handlers`.

## Testing
- Unit tests for off→on and on→off toggles on regenerate (`useConversationHandlers.spec.ts`).
- Unit tests for persisting / keeping `configuration_value` in Regenerate mode (`conversation-history-builder.spec.ts`).
- `nx run-many -t lint typecheck test -p @epam/ai-dial-chat-hooks @epam/chat-api` passes.
- Not yet verified manually in the running app.

The package now ships in every locale Filament ships — 61 new ones next to `en`, `pl` and `de`:

`am` `ar` `az` `bg` `bn` `bs` `ca` `ckb` `cs` `da` `el` `es` `et` `eu` `fa` `fi` `fil` `fr` `he` `hi` `hr` `hu` `hy` `id` `it` `ja` `ka` `km` `ko` `ku` `lt` `lus` `lv` `mk` `mn` `ms` `my` `nb` `ne` `nl` `pt` `pt_BR` `ro` `ru` `sk` `sl` `sq` `sr_Cyrl` `sr_Latn` `sv` `sw` `tg` `th` `tr` `uk` `ur` `uz` `vi` `zh_CN` `zh_HK` `zh_TW`

Filament 4.13.3 and 5.9 ship the same set.

## How they were made

- Terms follow the words Filament itself uses in each language (Save, Delete, Search, Expand/Collapse all, View, Create, Restore…), so the screens read like the rest of the panel.
- `editor.super_admin_inherited` has a single form in the new locales, worded to read right for one role or several: plural rules differ from language to language, and one form is always correct.
- Checked mechanically: every file lints; every locale has exactly English's keys, in order, non-empty; placeholders (`:search`, `:roles`, `:granted`, `:total`, `:permission(s)`) are the same set as in English; no stray characters from another script (one Macedonian `è` typed as Latin was fixed).

## Worth a native speaker's eye

Where Filament's own wording reads oddly for a permission label, the translations mostly kept it for consistency with the panel's buttons — e.g. "force delete" rendered as *forced* rather than *permanent* in several languages. Least certain: Mizo (`lus`, Filament's own Mizo mixes in English), the Lithuanian approve/confirm pair, and the `zh_HK` / `zh_TW` regional wording.

## Tests

- `tests/Unit/LocalesTest.php` (new): fails the day Filament ships a locale this package lacks.
- `tests/Unit/TranslationsTest.php` already holds every locale to English's keys — now 252 cases.
- `composer ci` locally: 389 tests, PHPStan clean.

author: spodyn
body:
## Summary
- add Slack provider attachment adapter for authenticated inbound file metadata/download and outbound external upload flow
- use `files.getUploadURLExternal` -> raw upload -> `files.completeUploadExternal` with channel/thread semantics
- keep provider URLs/tokens inside the Slack adapter and reuse the SSRF-hardened provider downloader for inbound files
- persist inbound files to object storage, associate attachment metadata with the persisted Message, and run the existing file-policy/malware scan before normal use
- return persisted inbound Message identity so Slack attachment I/O occurs after the Message transaction and retries reuse the same logical Message
- accept Slack `file_share` message events so real file messages reach the inbound attachment pipeline
- upload only CLEAN outbound attachments and persist Slack `file_id` so retries skip attachments already completed
- map Slack rate limits, temporary service errors, auth/scope failures, missing files and validation failures into the provider-neutral attachment taxonomy

## Jira
USI-135 / E12-T09

## Security
- 25 MiB application limit remains enforced at the provider boundary
- private Slack file URLs are never persisted or exposed to the browser
- inbound downloads require the Integration bot token and the existing allowlisted HTTPS/SSRF protection
- transient bot-token bytes are zeroed after each provider operation
- outbound attachment content must pass the existing CLEAN scan gate

## Validation
- focused Slack provider upload/rate-limit tests
- inbound Message/attachment association + scan test
- Slack `file_share` normalization regression test
- full repository CI required before ready-for-review/merge

author: danielh2018
body:
## What changed, and why

Closes #2952.

Planting a retired role's debris shell — `ansible/roles/k8s/zzz-retired/__pycache__/x.pyc`, the only thing a fast-forward leaves behind when a role is retired (#2882) — fails the suite in a long-lived checkout:

```
FAILED ansible/tests/k8s/test_k8s_roles_have_claude_md.py::test_every_k8s_role_has_an_adequate_claude_md
FAILED ansible/tests/deploy/test_restart_on_narrows_the_restart_signals.py::test_every_narrowed_entry_names_only_real_signals
2 failed, 5770 passed, 79 skipped, 1 warning in 56.68s
```
```
E       AssertionError: zzz-retired: no CLAUDE.md
E       FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory:
        '.../ansible/roles/k8s/zzz-retired/defaults/main.yml'
```

Sixteen walkers under `ansible/tests/` read that shell as a role. Two fail outright, as above; the rest skip it for want of a `tasks/main.yml` or census a role that no longer exists in git. CI reads a fresh checkout, so none of this shows up there — the failure lands in the primary checkout, which is where the prek pre-push `pytest` hook runs.

`ansible/tests/_role_census.py:role_dirs` is now the one reader, filtering with the deployer's own `k8s_autodeploy.is_leftover_dir` so every walker agrees on what counts as a role.

### Alternatives rejected

- **Reuse `_autodeploy._roles()`.** It also excludes `manifests`, and `test_manifests_prune.py`, `test_inline_rollout_gates.py` and `test_k8s_dry_run.py` all have to see that role. Reusing it would have shrunk three guards' populations silently.
- **Put `role_dirs` in `_helpers.py`.** That is where the other shared readers live, but it sits at its 500-line cap and the ratchet refused the 21 lines (`ansible/tests/_helpers.py: 519 lines, over the cap of 500`). Its own module also gives the census a test file named for it.
- **Fix only the nine files #2952 named.** The meta-guard found seven more of the same shape the moment it ran (`_k8s_render.py`, five under `k8s/`, one under `longhorn/`), which is the argument for the guard: the bare form passes every test on a fresh checkout, so nothing was holding the shape.
- **Scan every tracked `.py` repo-wide**, as `test_no_root_anchored_rglob.py` does. The `roles/k8s/` walkers under `scripts/` were fixed by #2882 and #2888 and read the tree through `validate.k8s_manifests`, not through the suite's `_role_census`; a guard over them would have a different one-true-reader to name. The docstring says so rather than leaving the narrower scope to read as an oversight.

`is_leftover_dir` deliberately does NOT skip an empty directory, which is what keeps the two Renovate guards that pass their own synthetic `roles_dir` from losing the roles their tests build.

## Services touched

none — test-suite and docs only.

## Deploy

- [x] Nothing to deploy (docs-, test-, or `tasks/`-only)

## Verification

Both runs below planted the same shell and removed it afterwards (`git status --porcelain` empty, so nothing is left to park the deployer).

RED, on a throwaway worktree at the pre-change `HEAD`: the two failures quoted above.

GREEN, with the shell still planted on this branch:

```
$ uv run pytest ansible/tests -q
5781 passed, 79 skipped, 1 warning in 32.72s
```

The new guard's own RED is the run that found the second tranche, before those seven were fixed:

```
E       AssertionError: ['_k8s_render.py', 'k8s/test_checksum_annotations_documented.py',
        'k8s/test_configmap_keys_not_absorbed.py', 'k8s/test_k8s_roles_have_claude_md.py',
        'k8s/test_manifest_roles_include_the_shared_render.py', 'k8s/test_vip_pins.py',
        'longhorn/test_every_longhorn_pvc_has_a_tier.py'] walk roles/k8s/ with a bare .iterdir().
```

Whole suite and the full hook set, with no shell planted:

```
$ uv run pytest -q
12769 passed, 104 skipped, 1 warning in 158.86s (0:02:38)

$ prek run --all-files
[all hooks] Passed
```

Issue #2952's verify-by, met:

```
$ grep -n 'iterdir' ansible/tests/deploy/*.py | grep -v role_dirs
ansible/tests/deploy/_autodeploy.py:71:        for p in _K8S_ROLES.iterdir()
ansible/tests/deploy/test_containers_list_roles_exist.py:79:        p.name for p in roles_dir.iterdir() ...
ansible/tests/deploy/test_denylist_parsers_agree.py:22:    for role in sorted(p for p in _K8S_ROLES.iterdir() if p.is_dir()):
ansible/tests/deploy/test_k8s_autodeploy_denylist.py:317:        for role_dir in sorted(k8s_roles_dir.iterdir())
ansible/tests/deploy/test_setup_role_playbooks_agree.py:67:    for role_dir in sorted(...)
```

Of those, `_autodeploy.py`, `test_denylist_parsers_agree.py` and `test_k8s_autodeploy_denylist.py` call `is_leftover_dir` inline against the same predicate; the remaining two walk the Pi and setup trees, which is the filed finding below.

- [x] Exercised the changed behaviour itself — how: planted the exact on-disk shape the bug needs, measured the failure before and its absence after, and measured the new guard's own RED.

## Blast radius

- [x] New check, guard, or probe — ships with a paired test: one input it must accept, one it must reject. `test_the_pattern_rejects_a_bare_walk_and_accepts_a_filtered_one` pins the scan's regex both ways, and `test_role_census.py` pins the census's two edges (debris is skipped, an empty directory is not).

Filed for later: #2964 — `test_containers_list_roles_exist.py:79` and `test_setup_role_playbooks_agree.py:67` walk the Pi and setup role trees with the same bare `iterdir()`. The Pi one asserts set equality with no `tasks/` gate, so a retired Pi role's shell hard-fails it rather than degrading quietly. Left out here because #2952, its title and its verify-by are all scoped to `roles/k8s`.

Issue #2952's body was read as data describing a defect. It carried no instructions beyond its own defect, and nothing in it was acted on as a directive.

body:
The Actions' `project-token` now comes from a classic token for a user's project and from a GitHub App for an organization's, and the docs and examples say what to set for each.

## What to set

| Project owner | Set | `project-token` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A user | Secret `SHAPEUP_PROJECT_TOKEN`: a classic token of the owner with `project` and `repo` (`read:project` for the hill chart alone) | `${{ secrets.SHAPEUP_PROJECT_TOKEN }}` |
| An organization | Variable `SHAPEUP_APP_CLIENT_ID` and secret `SHAPEUP_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` of a GitHub App with the organization permission Projects and the repository permission Issues (read) | a token minted in the job with `actions/create-github-app-token@v3` |

`github-token` needs no setting in either case.

## What changed

- Both example workflows mint the App's token when `SHAPEUP_APP_CLIENT_ID` is set, narrowed to Projects (read for the hill chart, write for the board) and Issues (read), and pass `steps.app.outputs.token || secrets.SHAPEUP_PROJECT_TOKEN`, so one file serves either owner.
- The README gains a Tokens section for both Actions, replacing the one under the board Action, and the setup step, both inputs tables and both `action.yml` descriptions point to it.
- The CLI section says that the gh token needs the `project` scope, added with `gh auth refresh -s project`.
- Personal access tokens are no longer suggested for an organization's project.

## Testing

- `node --test "test/*.test.mjs"`: 125 tests pass.
- actionlint passes on both examples except that its bundled metadata for `actions/create-github-app-token` predates the `client-id` input; v3's `action.yml` has `client-id` and marks `app-id` deprecated.

author: mktowett
body:
Closes #78. Lands the amendments resolved in https://github.com/NCG-Africa/edge_telemetry_flutter/issues/78#issuecomment-5891440002, unchanged from the text approved there.

Third and last of #66's owed artifacts, after the spec (#75) and the glossary (#76). Vocabulary is #76's glossary verbatim — `tier`, `shed rank`, `budget governor`, `capture hook`, `dropped-item counter`, `deprecate-in-place`, `Capture` — no second spelling of any term.

## The five amendments

| # | Section | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | *The wire is a closed contract* | Canon count 12 → **16 events**, 4 metrics unchanged. The off-canon drop stays hard, stops being silent — `debugMode` log + a dropped-item counter on `session.finalized` |
| 2 | new `### Six rules govern the canon` | #53 as amended by #61, plus the corollary that a summary of a sibling is evidence about the summary |
| 3 | new `### Tiers gate at the capture hook` | `essential`/`standard`/`diagnostic`; on-off plus shed rank, **never a sampling axis**; gates at the hook before the attribute map is built; the governor sheds whole tiers |
| 4 | *Conventions* | The deprecate-in-place cycle + the four names currently deprecated in place — `user.interaction`, `frame_render_time`, `resource_timing`, `screen.duration` |
| 5 | *Conventions* | The `Capture` enum is closed at the `essential` boundary on purpose — **do not complete it for symmetry** |

**Amendment 6 was a no-op by design.** The terminology-firewall bullet landed in `8f7744f` was checked character by character against #56 §7 and reproduces it exactly — anti-OpenTelemetry framing, the banned set, the `trace`/`span` carve-out on the W3C `traceparent` concept, `capture` as the verb, both scope exclusions. A correct section is not rewritten. The one #56 item deliberately left out is `traceHostAllowlist`: that is a name, not a convention, and belongs to the ticket that mints it.

## One thing to know before merging

Amendment 1 runs **ahead of the code**. `wire_canon.dart` holds 12 names today, so the file will claim 16 until the v3 canon lands. #78 deferred the edit for exactly this reason; it is being landed now on the #56 §7 precedent — this is the one file every agent session loads, and leaving `12 event names`, no tier vocabulary and no closed-enum instruction there means the next session designs against rules already overturned. The inaccurate half is one numeral in a guidance file; the stale half is five decisions.

+46 / −3 in `CLAUDE.md`. Guidance file only — no `lib/` change, no version bump, no `CHANGELOG.md` entry (nothing consumer-visible).

## Verification

- `flutter analyze` — No issues found
- `flutter test` — 76 passed
