body:
**Stack (epic #112, merge bottom-up):**
1. #297 (#144)
2. #298 (#145)
3. #299 (#146)
4. #302 (#147)
5. #300 (#148)
6. #301 (#149)

Part of epic #112 (branch 04, stacked on #146 / #299).

## Summary
georeader GeoTensors have dims `("time","band","y","x")[-ndim:]`, so the band axis is always -3. Many operators assumed it was axis 0, so on a `(T, C, H, W)` stack they treated time as the spectral axis or crashed inside a library.

**New `geotoolz._src.shape`:**
- `band_axis`, `require_ndim`
- `keep_band_axis`: turns a band-collapsed `(T, H, W)` into `(T, 1, H, W)`
- `map_frames` / `@over_frames`: run a per-scene operator on each frame of a stack

**Changes by family** (all except `learn` and `einx`, which are in #300 and #301):
- **Band-axis defaults:** now -3 in indices, spectral, qa, radiometry, viz, plume.SBMP, matched_filter and restore. Band-collapsing outputs on a stack are `(T, 1, H, W)`.
- **augment:** one draw per band, shared across frames. `BandDropout` and `BandJitter` act on bands, not frames. `AtmosphericHaze` counts bands correctly.
- **normalize:** per-band statistics are pooled over frames. CLAHE works per slice. `reshape_stat` raises on a shape mismatch; before, it silently broadcast along x.
- **matched_filter, restore (DenoisePCA, MNF):** 2-D maps are rejected rather than having rows read as bands. MNF keeps the stack layout.
- **compositing:** `MedianComposite` and `MaxNDVIComposite` accept a 4-D GeoTensor stack.
- **geom:** OpticalFlow rejects 4-D by name; before, it failed with a scipy `RuntimeError`.
- **io:** `WriteCOG` on 4-D raises `GeoToolzIOError`.
- **Per-scene families** (qa, segment, viz colormaps and hillshade, SRF and reflectance, plume carrier ops): run per frame.
- **Already fixed on main by #110:** `WriteZarr` 4-D and `SensorReader.dims`.

**Contract test:** new `test_time_stack_contract` covers every operator. Each must either reproduce its per-frame results on a 2-frame stack or reject the rank with an error that names the operator. `learn` and `einx` are strict xfails until #300 and #301. There is also a new `time_stack()` fixture (2, 3, 4, 4) and a `test_4d_time_stack` in 17 families.

## Behaviour changes
- `get_config()` now emits `"axis": -3`. Output on `(C, H, W)` input is identical.
- 2-D input to MatchedFilter-family operators, `DenoisePCA` and `MNF` now raises.
- `reshape_stat` raises on a mismatched statistic.
- Composites reject a 2-D or 3-D GeoTensor.
- Fitted statistics on a stack are pooled across frames: normalize, matched-filter background and PCA/MNF.

## Test plan
- [x] Fast suite: 3073 passed, 513 skipped, 28 xfailed (all learn/einx, owned by #300 and #301)
- [x] 14 of the per-family `test_4d_time_stack` tests fail on the base branch. The mask, feature and measure tests already passed there; they only document existing behaviour.
- [x] `ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .` and `ty check src/geotoolz` are clean

Closes #147

body:
## Existing behaviour

The `main protection` ruleset requires a PR but no status checks and no code-owner review. The only CI job is `validate`, and it is not required. There is no AI review caller and no CODEOWNERS file, so a bot PR with auto-merge can merge with no gate at all.

## Intent

- `validate-skills.yml` gets a `ci-aggregate` job (`always()`, `needs: [validate]`, passes only on `success`). This is the stable context the ruleset will require. The existing `validate` job is unchanged.
- New `.github/workflows/review.yml` calls `LeePepe/shared-ci/.github/workflows/codex-review.yml@6e354f476bc53d68f0f09fc231d5cd938466af9c` with `codex-bin: /opt/homebrew/bin/codex`, `owner-user-id: "13819054"` and `rules-file: docs/review-rules.md`. It runs only when `vars.SHARED_CI_REVIEW_RUNNER == 'true'`. A hosted `codex-review-gate` job follows shared-ci's pattern: skipped, failed or cancelled review fails closed. Kimi is not included.
- New `docs/review-rules.md` holds the trusted rules the reviewer reads from the base commit. The repo has no AGENTS.md, and the reviewer fails closed if the rules file is missing.
- New `.github/CODEOWNERS` covers `/.github/`, `/scripts/`, `/AGENTS.md`, `/CLAUDE.md` and `/docs/review-rules.md`. There is no `*` catch-all.

## Compatibility

`review.yml` uses `pull_request_target`, so it takes effect only after merge. It does nothing until the repo runner is online and `SHARED_CI_REVIEW_RUNNER` is set. Ruleset changes (require `ci-aggregate` + `codex-review-gate`, code-owner review) are a separate step after live positive and negative probes. Roll back by reverting this commit.

## Removed or weakened tests or policy

none

## Test evidence

- Command: `python3 scripts/validate_skills.py`; `python3 scripts/gen_registry.py --check`; YAML parse of both workflows; `git diff --check`.
- Result: all pass (exit 0; one existing unrelated warning in my-designer). The gate `case` logic passed local success and non-success checks.

body:
## เป้าหมาย
งาน desktop redesign ที่ค้าง (`design_handoff_labstock` / Prototype v4): เปลี่ยนโทนทั้งแอปและโครงหน้าหลักตามต้นแบบ โดยไม่เปลี่ยน logic/API/สิทธิ์เดิม

## ภาพรวมการเปลี่ยนแปลง
**ธีม (ทั้งแอปพร้อมกัน)**
- โทเค็น ink/ground + สีเน้นฟ้าหม่น `#5980a6`; นิยามสเกล Tailwind `gray/slate` (เทากลาง), `blue/indigo/teal/purple/violet/pink` (สีเน้น) ใหม่ด้วย `@theme` สีสถานะ (แดง/เหลือง/เขียว) ไม่เปลี่ยน
- มุมโค้งการ์ด 20px, เงาบาง, ปุ่มหลักสีดำ, หัวเรื่องหน้า 32px น้ำหนักปานกลางทุกหน้า
- รหัส hex เขียวน้ำเงิน/กรมท่า 311 จุด แปลงเป็นโทเค็น
- กฎสีลิงก์ย้ายเข้า `@layer base` (คลาส `text-white` บนลิงก์ชนะได้)

**โครง shell**
- ไซด์บาร์สว่าง 260px โลโก้ SPR LAB; แถบหัว: breadcrumb + ปุ่มซ่อนเมนู + **ช่องค้นหาน้ำยา** (ส่งคำไปที่ Inventory Overview: `/dashboard?q=` หรืออีเวนต์เมื่ออยู่หน้าเดียวกัน; ซ่อนสำหรับ Vendor)
- แถบหัวแสดงเฉพาะผู้ล็อกอิน; LIFF และหน้าลงทะเบียนคงระยะเดิม (แก้ที่ว่างซ้าย 288px ของ `/register` ที่มีมาก่อน)

**หน้าต่าง ๆ**
- Login: hero ตามดีไซน์ (LabStock · SPR LAB, การ์ด FEFO/GS1/RBAC)
- ใบสั่งน้ำยา: บอร์ด 3 คอลัมน์ (รอดำเนินการ / กำลังดำเนินการ / ปิดแล้ว) การกระทำเดิมครบ (ตรวจสอบก่อนส่ง, แก้ไข, ยืนยัน/ปฏิเสธ, ดูรายละเอียด)
- Logs: ชิปกรองประเภทรายการ
- นับสต็อก: ตาราง + แถบสรุปติดขอบล่าง + แผง "ใบงานนับสต็อกของฉัน" (ใช้ API เดิม `listCountWorkOrders`)
- เบิก / รับเข้า: 2 คอลัมน์ (สแกน/ค้นหา | รายการ)
- ยืม / ให้ยืม: 2 คอลัมน์ (ฟอร์ม | รายการค้าง + ตะกร้า)
- หน้าอื่น (Analysis, Master, Users, RBAC, Settings, Notifications, Vendor, ใบสั่งซื้อ): ได้ธีม หัวเรื่อง ปุ่ม และมุมโค้งใหม่ โครงเดิม

**ไม่แตะฝั่งมือถือ** (`/mobile`, LIFF, ตัวสแกนกล้อง)

## ยังไม่ได้ทำ (ตั้งใจ)
- ตัวเลข badge ข้างเมนู (Inventory Overview / ใบสั่งน้ำยา) ต้องดึงข้อมูลเพิ่มทุกหน้า
- ตัวสลับ role แบบเดโมและบัญชีทดลองบนหน้า login (เป็นของต้นแบบ ไม่ใช่ฟังก์ชันจริง)
- กราฟหน้า Analysis ยังเป็นของเดิม (สีตามธีม)

body:
## Problema

`warmUp()` y `WARM_EVENTS` siguen definidos en `src/lib/lazyEmbed.ts`, y el limpiador del embed los desmonta (`removeEventListener`), pero **el registro desapareció**: `warm()` es código muerto desde el refactor de `7cc71ab` (Sprint 3), que reemplazó el bloque por los listeners de clic.

Evidencia (diff de `7cc71ab`):

```diff
-  WARM_EVENTS.forEach((event) =>
-    root.addEventListener(event, warm, { passive: true, once: true }),
-  );
+  const disparadores = root.querySelectorAll<HTMLElement>(...
```

Consecuencia: el precalentamiento (dns-prefetch + preconnect **solo ante intención real**) documentado en `AUDITORIA_RENDIMIENTO_Y_ROBUSTEZ.md` §3.1 no ocurría en el mapa, los reels ni el informe X431 embebido (Recepción se salva por el `preconnect` estático del HTML).

## Fix

Restaura el bloque original que ya funcionaba en la rama de carga diferida (PR #23 / `45cd423`):

```ts
WARM_EVENTS.forEach((event) =>
  root.addEventListener(event, warm, { passive: true, once: true }),
);
```

- Sin cambios de comportamiento visual: solo evita pagar DNS+TLS en el primer clic/tap.
- El limpiador existente sigue desmontando los listeners al reiniciar el embed (informe de otra visita).

## Verificación

- `npm run check` (astro check): **0 errores / 0 avisos / 0 hints** (58 archivos).
- Cambio acotado: +6 líneas en 1 archivo. Sin tocar HTML, estilos ni flujos.

## Notas

## 概要
放置したタブが止まる（メモリセーバー・スリープタブ・PC のスリープ）と、ブラウザはサーバーの心拍に返事できず、約 2 分で接続が切れる。サーバーは猶予（90 秒・固定）の後にホストへの接続をサインオフなしで閉じるため、戻ったタブは「セッションは既に終了しています」になり、ホストにはジョブが切断された形で残っていた。

## 変更点
- `--reconnect-grace <分>`（1〜1440）を追加。`SessionManager` の `reconnectGraceMs` へ渡す。指定が無ければ従来どおり 90 秒（既定は変えない）。
- 解釈と受け渡しを `parseReconnectGrace`・`sessionManagerOptions` に切り出して単体テストした。
- README の起動オプション表と寿命の注記を更新した。

## レビューガイド
- 猶予を長くすると、戻らないタブの装置とジョブをその間ホストで掴んだままにする。そのため既定は変えていない（decisions D1）。
- 心拍の死判定（約 2 分）は変えていない。猶予だけで足りることを実機で確認した（decisions D2）。
- 履歴上、猶予・心拍・TCP keepalive は 2026-09-08〜08-23 に入ったもので、ACS parity 対応の期間には変わっていない（research F4）。

## テスト
- server 1677 件は失敗 0、`npm run build` も通過。
- 実機（サーバー経由の /ws で `ping` に返事しない）: 260 秒後の再接続が、既定は `SESSION_NOT_FOUND`、`--reconnect-grace 10` は同じセッションの画面が返った。
- 単体 5 件、変異 3 通りはすべて検出。
- 未検証：ブラウザの実物でタブを眠らせての確認。

author: chennaji9
body:
## Problem

The public ref type of the shared `Select` in `packages/ui` declares `React.RefAttributes<HTMLUListElement>`, but the implementation forwards the ref to MUI Base `Select`'s root slot, which renders the trigger `<button>` element. Consumers typing their ref per the public contract operate on the wrong element kind (focus/scroll/click land on the trigger, not the listbox, or vice versa when following the type).

## Root Cause

The exported cast says `HTMLUListElement` (the popup listbox) while the inner `forwardRef` is correctly typed `React.ForwardedRef<HTMLButtonElement>` and MUI Base `Select` attaches the ref to its root `button` slot (see `node_modules/@mui/base/Select/Select.d.ts` / `useSelect` root rendering).

## Changes

- `packages/ui/src/components/Select/index.tsx`: one word — the public cast's `HTMLUListElement` becomes `HTMLButtonElement`, matching the implementation and the actual DOM element.

## Contract Impact

paired backend change: no. Type-level only; zero runtime change.
paired i18n change: no.
Consumer survey: no call site across `apps/web`/`packages` passes a ref to this `Select` today (grep-verified), so the corrected contract breaks no existing usage.

## Testing

- Type-only change: no runtime behavior to test; no test file added. `tsc --noEmit` output is identical before and after the change in both `packages/ui` and `apps/web` (apps/web baseline has pre-existing SVG-module diagnostics unrelated to this file).
- Runtime element kind cross-checked via a transient jsdom render through `apps/web`'s jest (`@oss-compass/ui` maps to `packages/ui` source): the element receiving the forwarded ref is a `BUTTON` node. Temporary file deleted, not committed.
- Prettier/ESLint on the changed file: clean.

## Risk

Minimal. No consumers pass refs today; future consumers get the truthful type.

body:
## Summary
This implements #191 §Known findings (standard 07): one register for golden and acceptance findings in `tests/support/known-findings.ts`, with the same map shape. There is a helper that declares expected failures from the register, and a guard test that catches stale or malformed entries and any hard-coded `it.fails`.

**Stacked on #188:** the base is `qa-engineer/103-golden-growth-s3`, because both PRs touch the golden runners. **Blocked by #191:** it implements that PR's standard text, so merge #191 first. Merge order: #191, then #188, then retarget this PR to `main` and merge it.

## Owner
qa-engineer · follow-up to #191 (tech-lead ruling on the findings register); no separate issue

## Requirements
none (test tooling). Supports the planning/13 release gates, which count open findings in one place.

## Changes
- `tests/golden/known-findings.ts` → `tests/support/known-findings.ts` (a git rename, same `KNOWN_FINDINGS: ReadonlyMap<string, number>` shape, still empty):
  - `FINDING_KEY`: the allowed key forms, a golden case ID (`GC-`/`GH-`) or `ACNN: <exact it title>`.
  - `findingMode(key, register?)`: an expected failure with its issue while the key is listed, otherwise a plain test. It's pure and takes an optional register for testing.
  - `itForFinding(key, title, test)`: runs `it.fails` (with the title suffix `(open finding #N)`) while the key is listed, and `it` otherwise.
  - `acceptanceIt(caseId, title, test)`: declares an acceptance test under the key `<caseId>: <title>`. Pass both arguments as string literals.
  - `declaredAcceptanceKeys(source)`: finds `acceptanceIt` declarations in source text, with single- or double-quoted titles and wrapped calls.
- `tests/golden/development-corpus.test.ts` and `tests/golden/holdout.golden.test.ts`: both use `itForFinding` instead of their own `it`/`it.fails` branches.
- `tests/golden/known-findings-guard.test.ts` (new): the guard.
  - Every key must be well formed.
  - Every entry must match a development or holdout golden case ID, or an `acceptanceIt` declaration found under `tests/acceptance/`.
  - No `*.test.ts` under `tests/` may hard-code `it.fails(`.
  - It lives in `tests/golden/`, like the holdout isolation test, because it reads holdout case IDs.

## Tests
- `tests/support/known-findings.test.ts`:
  - `findingMode` treats a listed golden key and a listed acceptance key as expected failures naming their issues, and an unlisted key as a plain test.
  - `declaredAcceptanceKeys` finds single-quoted, double-quoted (apostrophe) and wrapped declarations, and ignores plain `it`.
  - `FINDING_KEY` accepts and rejects the literal examples.
- `tests/golden/known-findings-guard.test.ts`: the register guard. It passes, since the register is empty, every key form is valid, and no test file hard-codes `it.fails`.
- The golden development and holdout suites run unchanged: 113 + 15 cases.
- `pnpm verify`: passed (186 test files passed, 14 skipped; 2060 tests passed, 95 skipped; build done).

## Academic safety and security impact
None to product behavior. The guard keeps expected failures honest: a finding can't linger after its test is renamed or deleted, and no test can be silently marked as failing outside the register.

## Risk and rollback
Low: test tooling only, and the register is empty. To roll back, revert the commit, which also restores `tests/golden/known-findings.ts`.

## Handoffs
- **tech-lead:** standard 08's `ownership-override` row "Known finding fixed" (in #191) already points at `tests/support/known-findings.ts`, so nothing more is needed once #191 merges. Until then, standard 07 on `main` still names the old path, which is why this PR waits for #191.

body:
Refs #1254

Agent: Claude Code — cc-39fac3

**Partial checkpoint** for PAPER-LE-LEHUNG-LEVIN-ETAL-23. It resolves the gap `kummer-tower-field-inputs` by decomposing the field theory behind the Kummer-tower restriction lemmas G68, G67 and G50 into three new items, all for p > 2:

- **Z143.** The Galois closure of K∞ is K∞(μ_{p^∞}), K∞ ∩ K(μ_{p^∞}) = K, and Gal(K̂/K) = G_0 ⋊ H_K with G_0 ≅ Z_p(1) under cyclotomic conjugation.
  - Source: Liu, *A note on lattices in semi-stable representations*, arXiv:0709.4523v1, PDF4, recalling his 2007 Lemma 5.1.2.
  - The proof steps derive surjectivity of the Kummer map and the semidirect product.
  - A checked p = 2 counterexample is recorded: π = −2 in Q_2, with √−2 = ζ₈ + ζ₈³.
- **Z144.** Gal(K(μ_{p^∞})/K(μ_p)) ≅ Z_p, via Mathlib's `cyclotomicCharacter`; EGS 7.4.3 uses it without proof.
- **Z145.** K∞ has no Galois subextension of degree p when ζ_p ∉ K. This is GLS 5.4.2's assertion (arXiv:1309.0527v2, PDF35), derived from Z143 by a commutator argument. The hypothesis is sharp.

A new source route sends them to `FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.4`, the Breuil–Kisin base-field owner. G68 imports them. The gap is removed, and its record is kept in validation.

Census: 779 items, 26 routes, 113 findings, 13 gaps.

Checks: `check_paper.py` is ok, `intake.py check-files` finds 0 problems, and the unit suite passes. No Lean file.

author: awgn
body:
This pull request removes the custom `arion-error` crate from the workspace and migrates all error handling in the `arion-configuration` package to use the community-standard `anyhow` and `thiserror` crate. This involves updating dependencies, refactoring error conversions and context additions, and cleaning up imports throughout the codebase. The changes simplify error handling and improve maintainability by relying on a widely-used, well-supported error library.

**Dependency and crate removal:**
- Removed the `arion-error` crate from the workspace, dependencies, and all relevant `Cargo.toml` files, and deleted the crate itself (`arion-error/Cargo.toml`). Its use has been replaced by `anyhow` for the application and `thiserror` for libraries.

**Error handling migration:**
- Replaced all imports and uses of `arion_error::{Context, Error}` with `anyhow::{Context, Error}` and updated code to use `anyhow::Result` as appropriate in the `arion-configuration` package and `arion-proxy`. 
- Introduced the `arion_lib::Error` type (using `thiserror`), a hierarchical `enum` which wraps all concrete errors in the crate, eliminating infer methods and limiting error downcasts to just a few places.
- Removed all `Box<dyn Error>` trait objects from the codebase, replacing them with concrete error types convertible to the main `crate::Error` type.

**Test and example updates:**
- Updated all tests and examples to use the new `arion_error::Error` and `anyhow` for error handling and context, ensuring consistency across the codebase. 

**Other unrelated improvements:**
- Improved TCP test client error handling to better handle connection resets in `arion-e2e-tests`.
- Enabled more verbose logging and debug output in a test setup for improved diagnostics.

author: flaviour-maker
body:
Three pieces of work on `feat/guided-capture-and-interface-pass` (101 files, +4,661 / −1,020).

### Serve the whole customer journey from the API

Quote submission, vehicle upsert, cover period, claim notification and the NCD endpoints. Payment is idempotent — replaying a key returns the first result, and double payment, an expired quote or a wrong amount are refused by name rather than by a 500. `common/contract.ts` is the single place database enums meet the wire vocabulary, with a test that fails when a schema member is left unmapped. Demo seeds are gated on mock mode, so an empty account against a real API shows an empty account. MinIO images pull again and the Keycloak realm export loads.

### Guide the inspection photos and check them before they are sent

Photos are judged where they are taken: focus (variance of the Laplacian), exposure, contrast and size, plus a foliage/sky check on the close-ups for the "photographed a tree instead of the mileage" case. One shot at a time against one instruction, and the phone hand-off closes itself on the last accepted photo.

Both confirmation steps are gone. Confirming a photo is clear is a judgement the person holding the phone is least equipped to make, and asking twice did not stop a blurred odometer reaching the insurer. The quote form grades uploads to the same standard, so both routes hold one bar.

Proving the *subject* needs a vision model, which belongs on the server; `withSubjectVerdict` is the seam where that verdict joins the local one.

### One interface, and a mobile shell that fits a phone

One form field (was six copies in two different treatments), one page-title size (was nine), one status badge (was pills, squares and three ad-hoc colour maps), one empty state (was five shapes). Status colour is a single accent again — blue, amber, purple, teal, indigo and orange are gone, including a dead status list in the domain layer that had been carrying Tailwind classes.

Vehicle inspections were still in the old visual language entirely and showed a fictional insurer against a real API; rebuilt on the shared pieces.

Fixed along the way:

author: yuuzulight
body:
Refs #36 (inline part, third step: https://github.com/Yuuzulight/Folio/issues/36#issuecomment-5892219684).

## What
- `vertical-align` (#32): baseline, sub, super, text-top, text-bottom, middle, top, bottom, and lengths or percentages of the element's own line height.
- Each line is built as a tree: the block's strut at the root, inline boxes nested inside it, and text and atomic inlines as leaves. Following CSS 2.2 §10.8.1:
  - each inline box and atomic inline is shifted relative to its parent box's baseline (text follows its box), so vertical-align inside a raised box adds up;
  - extents are gathered bottom-up and the line box fits them; `top`/`bottom` boxes are placed against the finished line box, which grows when they are taller;
  - `middle` uses the parent's x-height (from OS/2, half an em without one); `text-top`/`text-bottom` use the parent's font ascent and descent.
- Inline-blocks sit on their last in-flow line's baseline. With no line boxes, or when they clip their overflow, their bottom margin edge sits on it. One earlier case changes accordingly: an inline-block of text now lines up with the surrounding text.

## Not yet
- `sub` and `super` move by a fifth and a third of the parent's font size rather than the font's own offsets.
- Bidi reordering is the next step.

## Review passes
1. Correctness: 6 cases worked out by hand in the test box font (x-height 0.8em).
2. Cross-platform: plain arithmetic; the dump now prints -0 as 0.
3. Scope: `BuildLine` replaced by the tree version; no new file.
4. Naming and layering: `Folio.Layout` and `Folio.Style`.
5. Tests: lengths, sub, middle on a tall inline-block, top and bottom against a tall line, text-top with a larger parent font, inline-block baselines with padding and margins.

author: awesomekling
body:
An inline element has a committed box, but its layout node is not a `Layout::Box`, so using one as an explicit `IntersectionObserver` root crashed the rendering update when we cast it (cbl.gov.ly). No containing block chain passes through an inline element, so such a root stops no walk, and we now leave its box null.

A window whose document is no longer its navigable's active document (the previous document of a navigated iframe) can still construct an observer, for example from a promise job (vimeo.com). That hit the `VERIFY` e4ddb1908eb added for the implicit root. Such a window has no top-level browsing context, so its own document now stands in as the implicit root. The test attaches its iframe's load handler before the iframe can load, so it can't miss the load on a busy event loop.

## Problème

Le CDC §04 réserve `organisations_lieux` aux organisations `gestionnaire_lieux`. Côté serveur, rien ne l'imposait : seul le sélecteur de la modale admin filtrait. Or `f_collecte_visible` ouvre les collectes datées d'un lieu à **toute** organisation qui y est rattachée, sans garde de rôle.

Mesuré sur base locale : si un traiteur est rattaché par erreur à un lieu, il lit via PostgREST la collecte d'un autre traiteur sur ce lieu (`notes_internes` comprises).

`POST /admin/lieux` et `PATCH /admin/lieux/{id}` renvoient 422 (`champs_invalides: ['gestionnaire_organisation_id']`) si le gestionnaire est introuvable, n'est pas une chaîne ou n'est pas de type `gestionnaire_lieux`. Le refus intervient avant toute écriture. `''` et `null` restent un détachement.

Aucune migration.

À merger **avec ou avant** la PR du trigger P0047 (`fix/organisations-lieux-trigger-type`). Sans cette garde, le PATCH supprime l'ancien rattachement, puis son INSERT est refusé par le trigger : le lien légitime est perdu alors que la route répond 200.

Die Cluster laufen auf k3s `v1.36.4`, die Module pinnten `kcl-lang/k8s` noch auf `1.31` bzw. `1.32.4`. Anlass: Die ghcr-Sperre vom 2026-09-29 traf die älteren Tags besonders (#323, stuttgart-things/dagger#391).

## Stufe 1: sechs Module, direkt auf 1.36

| Modul | Version | vorher |
|---|---|---|
| `flux/flux-operator-instance` | 0.3.3 → 0.3.4 | 1.31 |
| `models/crossplane-provider-terraform` | 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 | 1.31 |
| `kubernetes/harvester-vm` | 0.3.0 → 0.3.1 | 1.32.4 |
| `kubernetes/resources` | 0.1.0 → 0.1.1 | 1.32.4 |
| `models/crossplane-provider-helm` | 0.1.4 → 0.1.5 | 1.32.4 |
| `models/crossplane-provider-kubernetes` | 0.1.1 → 0.1.2 | 1.32.4 |

Je `kcl.mod` plus die per `kcl mod update` neu geschriebene `kcl.mod.lock` (Version, Tag, Prüfsumme). Der Patch-Bump sorgt dafür, dass die Modul-CI veröffentlicht.

**Geprüft pro Modul:** `kcl run` (mit `test-settings.yaml`, wo vorhanden) liefert vorher und nachher **byte-gleiche** Ausgabe, ohne die Zeile `downloading …`. `kcl test` ist grün. Drei reine Schema-Bibliotheken ohne Einstiegspunkt scheitern bei `kcl run` schon vorher; für sie zählt `kcl test`.

## Noch nicht, mit Grund

- **`models/flux-helmrelease`, `models/flux-kustomization`** hängen an `crossplane-provider-helm` **0.1.4**, das `k8s 1.32.4` pinnt. `kcl mod update` schreibt ihre `kcl.mod` deshalb auf 1.32.4 zurück. Sie folgen, sobald 0.1.5 aus diesem PR veröffentlicht ist (**Stufe 2**), danach `tests/flux-app-kustomization-tekton`, das auf beiden aufsetzt.
- **`crossplane/xplane-harvester-vm`** hängt am Upstream-Paket `kcl-lang/crossplane-provider-kubernetes:0.18.0`, das `1.32.4` pinnt. Es bleibt, bis Upstream nachzieht.

Nebenbei aufgefallen: `flux-helmrelease` und das Test-Modul schreiben in `kcl.mod` `1.31`, ihre Lock-Datei löst aber längst 1.32.4 auf. Das wird in Stufe 2 mit bereinigt.

author: jon-bell
body:
## What happened

Grading a PR-mode submission (course 636, assignment 1226, submission 392629) hit three separate failures:

1. **The Files tab showed no code.** The file tree and the Monaco editor were invisible, so graders couldn't open or switch files. Only the PR diff showed.
2. **The diff was wrong.** It listed 1363 changed files, 1353 of them "removed". GitHub's compare for the same base and head shows 38 (15 added, 23 modified, 0 removed).
3. **The Checks tab failed** with `canceling statement due to statement timeout`.

## Causes and fixes

### Submission files truncated at 1000 (`hooks/useSubmission.tsx`)

The submission loader embedded `submission_files(*)` in the submissions select. PostgREST caps an embedded resource at `max_rows` (1000), with no error. This submission has 2379 files, so the page had 1000. The diff then compared the full base tree against a partial head and reported every base file outside those 1000 as removed.

Ingestion was fine: the stored rows match the head commit exactly. The files now load in their own paged query through the existing `fetchPostgrestAllPages`.

### Diff took the editor's height (`files/page.tsx`)

The inline diff rendered every file, with no height limit and no scrolling, above the tree and editor in a fixed-height column. At ~108,600px tall it left the tree and editor 0px and Monaco 5px.

The diff is now collapsed behind **Show changed files (N)**. When it's open on desktop, the diff and the navigator/editor share the height as a vertical resizable split. The editor panel stays mounted, so opening or closing the diff keeps the open tabs. On mobile the diff stays inline, capped at 50vh.

### Checks RPC seq-scanned `workflow_events` (migration)

Two causes:

- `20251006232741_reduce-db-ram-usage` dropped `idx_workflow_events_head_sha` before `get_submission_checks` started filtering on `head_sha`.
- With the index restored by hand on production, an RLS-bound caller *still* got a seq scan. The join clause `we.head_sha = coalesce(s.head_sha, s.sha)` stayed above the table's policy quals instead of becoming an index condition. That meant reading 1.13M rows to return 9.

The migration restores the index and resolves the SHA in a scalar subquery first. Authorization is unchanged: the subquery still reads `submissions` under the caller's RLS, so a submission the caller can't see yields NULL and matches nothing.

`EXPLAIN ANALYZE` on production, as an authenticated instructor:

| | plan | rows read | time |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | Seq Scan on workflow_events | 1,129,820 | 4072 ms |
| after | Index Scan using idx_workflow_events_head_sha | 9 | 0.6 ms |

The migration uses a plain `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS`, following `20260904120000_metrics_gap_remediation`: `migrate.sh` runs each file under `--single-transaction`, where `CONCURRENTLY` fails the deploy. The index already exists on production (built by hand), so there it's a no-op.

## Testing

Ran `npm run dev` locally against production data, on submission 392629:

- The Files tab loads 2379 files, matching the GitHub tree for `90de5eb`. "Show changed files" lists 38: 15 added, 23 changed.
- The file tree and Monaco render with the diff closed and open. Clicking files opens them in either state, the split drags, and closing the diff keeps the open tabs.
- The `get_submission_checks` fix was measured on production with `EXPLAIN ANALYZE` (table above), not through the page.
- ESLint is clean on the changed files. `tsc` reports the same errors before and after this change, none in these files.
- Not run: unit tests, E2E, or a production `next build`. The local build failed on an untracked script that isn't part of this branch.

## Not in this PR

- The instructor metadata export (`layout.tsx`, `FULL_SUBMISSION_SELECT`) embeds `submission_files` the same way, so exports of submissions with more than 1000 files are probably truncated too. It spans several submissions per query, so it needs its own change.
- The inline diff shows only `+`/`-` lines, with no hunk headers or line numbers.

Step 1 of the badges and challenges redesign. This is data only: no screen changes yet.

## What changes
- Each badge rule in `src/data/achievements.ts` now returns progress toward a goal instead of a yes or no. A badge is earned when its progress meets the goal, so a progress bar and an unlock can never disagree. `computeUnlocked` returns the same results as before.

- Progress follows the current found map, while the store keeps an unlock for good. An earned badge can show less than full after a find is unmarked, so screens should take "earned" from the store.

- Progress and unlocks agree across several found maps.

author: cheekyfellastef
body:
## Why

Live Battle Bridge evidence on 2026-09-29 showed:
- Completion Guardian had 39 `SCHEDULER_VISIBLE_READY` durable goals.
- The durable programme controller was nevertheless `HOLD`.
- Its blockers were `critical-backlog-did-not-authorize-idle-selection` and `critical-backlog-idle-selection-identity-mismatch`.
- The critical backlog was correctly `PARKED_BLOCKERS_ONLY`, so parked legacy/repair mission identities were still competing with elastic goal selection and deadlocking admission.
- The native capacity publisher was dark because its default `qwen:14b` failed the live deterministic source qualification.
- Live `qwen:32b` passed the exact qualification.

## Fix

- Exclude issue identities owned by strictly parked critical-backlog missions from elastic scheduler goal candidates while the parked backlog has released scheduler capacity.
- Preserve fail-closed behavior unless the parked projection is affirmative and has no remaining runnable legacy item or active mission.
- Make `qwen:32b` the single shared default for the native capacity certificate lane, with the runtime script consuming the shared constant.

## Proof

Battle Bridge focused tests:

```
node --test shared/agents/programmeAuthorityV1.test.mjs shared/agents/stephanosNativeCapacityPublisherV1.test.mjs
tests 33
pass 33
fail 0
```

The new scheduler regression proves parked #1284/#1286 identities release the scheduler to independent ready #1287 without weakening the critical-backlog gate.

## Por quê

Decisão do dono de 28/09 (D3 em `handoffs/COORDENACAO.md`): na Fase 1, **o painel da Render publica** (opção B), e com o gatilho **After CI Checks Pass** (regra C4), para continuar valendo a regra do projeto de só publicar o que passou na esteira.

Em 29/09, o merge do #29 foi ao ar **com o CI vermelho** (conferido sem token: `/v1/motivos/sign-upload` → 401). O `snakethai-api` hoje publica **por commit**, sem esperar os checks, e o `autoDeploy: false` do `render.yaml` não chega a ele.

## O que muda

- **`.github/workflows/ci.yml`:** sai o job "Publicar na Render" (deploy hook e verificação do `/health`). Com `checksPass`, a Render só publica se **todos** os checks do commit passarem (`success`, `neutral` ou `skipped`), então um job vermelho por falta do secret travaria toda publicação.
- **`render.yaml`:** `autoDeploy: false` (campo antigo) vira `autoDeployTrigger: checksPass` no `snakethai-api`, e o Cron Job `snakethai-media-cleanup` ganha o mesmo gatilho. Campo e valor conferidos no schema oficial (`render.com/schema/render.yaml.json`), que o aceita em serviço web e em cron.
- **Documentação:** README (seção "Como publica" e o passo do Auto-Deploy), `docs/DEPLOY.md` (passos 4 e 5 riscados, como o 8), `docs/BACKEND.md`, `REVIEW.md` (A-2) e P-4/P-5 do `PENDENCIAS.md` sem efeito.
- **`ROADMAP-server.md`:** 1.1 feito, 1.2 e 1.3 atualizados, 4.7 com o #29 no ar e o Registro de 28 e 29/09.

## ⚠️ O que este PR não faz sozinho

Se os serviços não foram criados pelo Blueprint (é o que o comportamento de hoje indica), o `render.yaml` não chega a eles. O dono precisa pôr **Settings → Build & Deploy → Auto-Deploy: After CI Checks Pass** no `snakethai-api` e no `snakethai-media-cleanup`.

**O merge publica:** com o Auto-Deploy por commit de hoje, este commit vai ao ar logo depois do merge. Só muda documentação e CI, sem código da API.

## Conferência depois do merge (item 1.3)

- CI da `main` verde **inteiro**, já sem o job de deploy;
- na lista de deploys do painel, o commit do merge aparece nos dois serviços, publicado só **depois** dos checks.

author: vitali87
body:
## Summary

- `cgr daemon up` used to print `mg_raw_transport_recv: Connection reset by peer` (also `... connection closed by server` and `mg_raw_transport_send: Broken pipe`) once per readiness probe while Memgraph was starting. It no longer does. The same applies to `cgr daemon status` and to the open-access and credential checks around a start.
- **Root cause:** mgclient's C transport reports every failed socket read or write with `perror()`/`fprintf(stderr)`. That writes straight to fd 2, underneath Python's `sys.stderr`, and the probe also gets the same failure back as the `mgclient` exception it already handles. While the container starts, Docker's port proxy accepts each connection on the published port and then drops it, so every attempt in `wait_for_memgraph` printed a line. The issue's other option, checking the TCP port first, would not help, because the proxy accepts the TCP connection.
- **Fix:** the three Memgraph probes in `codebase_rag/stack/health.py` now run with fd 2 pointed at a temporary file. These are `_bolt_reachable` (used by `wait_for_memgraph`), `memgraph_anonymous_access` and `memgraph_rejects_credentials`. fd 2 is restored afterwards, including when the probe raises. A lock guards the swap because fd 2 is shared by the whole process. Whatever the C library wrote is logged at DEBUG (`LOGURU_LEVEL=DEBUG cgr daemon up` shows it). Probe results and every error the stack reports are unchanged. The ingestor's own Memgraph connection is not touched.

## Demo

![cgr daemon up while Memgraph starts](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vitali87/code-graph-rag/claude/confident-johnson-521puc/pr-evidence/2356/daemon-up-quiet-wait.png)

<details><summary>GIF</summary>

![cgr daemon up while Memgraph starts (animated)](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vitali87/code-graph-rag/claude/confident-johnson-521puc/pr-evidence/2356/daemon-up-quiet-wait.gif)

</details>

Real `cgr daemon up` runs against Docker, first on `main` and then on this branch. The compose file in `CGR_HOME` runs Memgraph 3.3.0 with its start delayed 5 s, standing in for the slower memgraph-mage boot. It also runs a stub answering 200 on Qdrant's port, because neither the mage nor the qdrant image is pulled on this machine. On `main`, six mgclient lines are mixed into the wait. On this branch the wait is quiet and the stack reports healthy the same way.

```text
# before (main)
$ cgr daemon up
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:up:595 - Starting cgr stack...
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:_wait_for_services:697 - Waiting for memgraph on localhost:17687...
mg_raw_transport_recv: Connection reset by peer
mg_raw_transport_recv: Connection reset by peer
mg_raw_transport_recv: Connection reset by peer
mg_raw_transport_recv: Connection reset by peer
mg_raw_transport_send: Broken pipe
mg_raw_transport_send: Broken pipe
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:_wait_for_services:716 - Waiting for qdrant on 127.0.0.1:16333...
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:ensure_running:886 - Stack is healthy (localhost:17687, 127.0.0.1:16333).
state:    running

# after (this branch)
$ cgr daemon up
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:up:595 - Starting cgr stack...
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:_wait_for_services:697 - Waiting for memgraph on localhost:17687...
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:_wait_for_services:716 - Waiting for qdrant on 127.0.0.1:16333...
... | INFO | codebase_rag.stack.manager:ensure_running:886 - Stack is healthy (localhost:17687, 127.0.0.1:16333).
state:    running
```

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature
- [ ] Performance improvement
- [ ] Refactoring (no functional changes)
- [ ] Documentation
- [ ] CI/CD or tooling
- [ ] Dependencies

## Related Issues

Fixes #2356

## Test Plan

- [x] Unit tests pass: `pytest -n 2 -m "not integration"` gives 14189 passed, 124 skipped, 2 xfailed. The only failures are the 2 environmental `test_oracle_toolchain_guards.py::TestCsharpGuard` tests (no .NET SDK on this machine). `test_subprocess_encoding` failed on the first run because of this PR's new test, and passes after the fix to that test.
- [x] New tests added in `codebase_rag/tests/test_stack_quiet_wait.py`. The probes run the real mgclient against a local endpoint that accepts and then resets or closes each connection, like Docker's proxy in front of a Memgraph that is still starting. That endpoint runs in a separate process because mgclient holds the GIL while it waits. Output is checked at fd level with `capfd`.
- [ ] Integration tests: not run, because the change needs no database beyond the probes exercised above.
- [x] Manual testing: the real `cgr daemon up` before and after, shown above.

**Red tests.** These fail on `main` because the mgclient lines reach fd 2, and pass here:
- `test_waiting_for_a_starting_memgraph_prints_nothing[reset|close]`
- `test_every_memgraph_probe_is_silent_while_memgraph_starts[reset|close × login-probe|anonymous-access|rejects-credentials]`
- `test_daemon_up_waits_for_a_starting_memgraph_without_noise[reset|close]`: the CLI `up` against a Memgraph that drops probes after `up -d` and then becomes ready.

**Negative tests** (what must not change):
- `test_daemon_up_still_reports_a_memgraph_that_never_starts[reset|close]`: `cgr daemon up` still exits 1 and shows "Stack started but memgraph did not become healthy within …".
- `test_waiting_for_a_memgraph_that_never_starts_still_raises[reset|close]`: `wait_healthy` still raises `StackError`.
- `test_the_c_library_message_is_kept_at_debug_level[reset|close]`: the text is logged once at DEBUG and never at INFO or above.
- `test_stderr_outside_a_probe_still_reaches_the_terminal[reset|close]`: writes to fd 2 before and after a probe still reach the terminal, in order.
- `test_an_unexpected_probe_error_propagates_and_restores_stderr`: a non-mgclient exception is not swallowed, and fd 2 is back afterwards.
- `test_concurrent_probes_leave_stderr_pointing_at_the_terminal`: 8 threads probing at once leave fd 2 restored. This test fails 3/3 with the lock removed.
- `test_a_process_without_stderr_still_probes`: with fd 2 closed, the probe still runs and answers.
- `test_a_refused_login_is_still_told_apart_from_no_answer[...]`: an `Authentication failure` is still `REFUSED` or rejected, and a refused connection is still `NO_ANSWER`.
- `test_a_ready_memgraph_is_still_reachable`

On `main` the file gives 20 failed and 4 passed. The 4 that pass are negative tests that hold on both. On this branch all 24 pass. The existing `test_stack_manager.py`, `test_stack_auth.py`, `test_stack_loopback_bind.py`, `test_health_checker.py` and `test_health_backend_reporting.py` also pass.

- [x] No hardcoded strings in non-config/non-constants files (the log template and the fd number live in `stack/constants.py`)
- [x] No `# type: ignore`, `cast()`, `Any`, or `object` type hints

author: iandballard
body:
Fix Roadmap batch 18 (the register is in Cayenne's `SpecificationDocumentation/FIX_ROADMAP.md`): what batch 4 (#65) narrowed but did not close, in the same files. Each claim was re-checked on `23ef784`, and each fix was written test-first and seen to fail.

## F-108: detection evidence must indicate the system it is offered for
Since #65 a quote had to be whole words with substance, but "2 cups flour" still verified all five systems. The new `_indicates(system, quote, written)` in `refine.py` requires the quote to point to the claimed system, using the refine prompt's own kinds of evidence:

- **A stated size** must match that system:
  - US: 236, 237, 240, 118 or 120 ml, or 8 fl oz;
  - UK, EU and AU: 250 or 125 ml (the metric cup and half cup);
  - AU only: 20 ml;
  - Imperial: 568 or 284 ml, or 20 or 10 fl oz.
- **A statement about the measures:**
  - American or America, and US, U.S. or USA in capitals only;
  - British, Britain, UK, New Zealand or NZ;
  - Europe, European, or EU in capitals;
  - Australia or Australian; "AU" never counts, because of "au gratin";
  - "metric" counts for UK, EU and AU; "British" counts for UK and Imperial.
- **Pre-metric British measures, for Imperial:** gill, teacup, breakfast cup, and stone only after a number, so "1 lb stone fruit" is refused.
- **Ingredient names only one country uses.** These are deliberately closed lists, and each name counts only for its own system:
  - UK: caster sugar, plain flour, self-raising flour, double and single cream, courgette, aubergine, icing sugar, bicarbonate of soda, cornflour, spring onion, demerara sugar, golden syrup;
  - US: all-purpose flour, heavy (whipping) cream, half-and-half, confectioners' and powdered sugar, stick(s) of butter, zucchini, eggplant, cilantro, baking soda, cornstarch, scallion;
  - shared or ambiguous names (coriander, mince) and spellings count for neither.

A genuine name outside the lists costs the detection, never produces a wrong one. The recorded goldens' evidence still verifies: "1 tbsp (20 ml)" for AU and "1 stone potatoes" for Imperial. Three existing tests that offered "1 ounce (about 1/3 packed cup)" as evidence now use genuine evidence, since that quote is exactly the hole being closed. The source-host path is unchanged.

## F-109: Gemini's own retries took no rate-limiter slot
`_call_with_retry` (the 429 and 5xx backoff) and `_generate_and_parse` (parse retries) take an optional `limiter` and take a slot before every request **after the first**. The first request's slot stays with the caller, so nothing is counted twice. The limiter is passed through extraction, baker's-table normalisation and refine, down from `extract()`, `refine()` and the pipeline.

Callers that pass no limiter behave exactly as before: the regen and recategorise workers, categorise, TOC, vision OCR and picture generation. The limiter holds no slot across a wait, so it cannot deadlock.

## F-110: `page_meta_from_html` passed a malformed image address
A new `_is_absolute_http` requires the address to parse, to have an http(s) scheme, and to name a host. `http://[bad/…`, `https://` and `https:///x` now yield no meta image.

## Verification
- Full suite, as CI runs it and offline with every credential variable blanked: **1,372 passed**, against a baseline of 1,353. No golden, snapshot or cassette changed.
- `ruff`: no new violations.

## Found, not fixed
- A source-host quote is not tied to the system: `taste.com.au` offered for US still verifies.
- `get_embeddings` has no retry, so F-109 does not reach it.

Fixes F-108.
Fixes F-109.
Fixes F-110.

body:
HAR-100 round 2: Reef's HAR-94 part-2 audit asked for (C1) lenient unescaped inner quotes and (C2) a cont-1#3 relabel. $0: offline code and replay only; no launches.

## C1: unescaped inner quotes (`src/evallab/mimo_tool_calls.py`)

A Terminus object that fails to decode because a string holds unescaped `"` is now read every way its quotes allow. The object may be bare or the JSON body of an `exec`/`exec_command`/`bash`/`command` call. Each unescaped quote may either end its string or be part of it.
- Only readings with exactly Terminus's keys and field types count.
- The reading that treats the fewest quotes as text wins.
- The turn stays rejected on a tie, when no reading fits, or when the search passes its 4,096-quote budget.
- The winning reading is re-serialized.

The repair runs only after the existing native-call rewrite returns `None` and the object does not decode as written. So valid JSON, prose and every existing shape are untouched.

**Replay** (counterfactual; 5,818 turns in 55 trials, main `13ceb070` → this branch, Harbor 0.21.0 stock parser):

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| HAR-81 pilot, parsed or mapped | 3,384/3,513 (96.33%) | 3,489/3,513 (99.32%) |
| HAR-90 | 2,210/2,305 (95.88%) | 2,210/2,305 (95.88%) |

- **105 decisions change, all from parse error to commands:**
  - a2-arvo-42496599: head 11, 19 and 27-91;
  - candidate-2684: head 21, 24, 26, 35 and 37-69;
  - a2-arvo-42485576: head 32.
- **No other decision changes.** No accepted turn's commands change.
- **Still rejected:** a2-42485576 head 2 (a stray `""]`) and head 23 (`</` with no plan).
- **(b) raw newlines remains a no-op.** 2684 head 35, the one turn that had both raw newlines and inner quotes, is now read.
- **Caveat:** 65 of the recovered turns send the model's literal `… echo 'no git'"; …`, whose quoting is unbalanced in the shell.

## C2: 2684 cont-1#3 is correctly `copied`; only its reason text was wrong

The step is the summarization questions subagent's reply. Its message is byte-identical to step 2 of `trajectory.summarization-1-questions.json`, and Harbor never parses or executes it.
- The keys `job.log` sends after the handoff (lines 248-249) are step 5's `vendor/bandit/bandit/core/…` paths, not step 3's `vendor/bandit/core/…`.
- The same holds for all 13 copied agent steps across the 10 pilot and 3 HAR-90 continuations. Their 4 verbatim key matches in `job.log` are all live steps' recorded sends.
- Relabeling the step as executed would be wrong. This PR corrects only the `copied_layers` reason, which claimed the evidence is in the head segment.

## Pins

`parser_digest` and HAR-81's `normalizer_sha256` change, so the next pilot key must be re-pinned. Completed pilot data is unaffected.

## Checks

- `ruff check .`
- `uvx ty@0.0.71 check src/`
- Focused pytest: mimo_tool_calls, step_layers, terminus2_runtime, trial_treatment, run_report, trial_diagnosis, repomap, docindex.
- The 7 new mimo test cases fail on main and pass here.
- `evallab report run --json` on 2684 is byte-identical before and after.

author: stienswout
body: The review of the first nightly (`0.0.1-nightly.20260929.12`) found four ways it could lose data or leave updates stuck: - A refresh that returned 5 channels, confirmed by a second fetch that returned 0, saved an empty catalogue over 100 cached channels. - Start fresh erased the data before installing Stable. macOS checks an update's signature only while installing, so a refused Stable left the nightly running with its data gone. - Try again after a failed download did nothing, cancelling while the release metadata loaded was missed, and switching to Stable left a downloaded nightly ready to install. - The feed read only the newest 100 releases, so after 100 nightlies the newest stable release disappeared from updates and Start fresh. The fixes: - **Catalogue:** the confirming fetch must also be non-empty. - **Start fresh:** the marker names the Stable version, and Stable erases the data when it first starts, before anything reads it. A refused or interrupted install leaves the nightly running with everything intact. Refused installs, of updates too, are reported, and Settings opens to show why. - **Updates:** Try again downloads again after a failed download or install. Cancelling works at every step, and a download that finishes after a cancel never becomes ready. Switching channels drops a staged or downloading update the new channel doesn't receive. - **Feed:** also reads GitHub's latest release, which is always the newest stable one. Slice 2 is marked complete in its handoff, with its known gaps listed. Tests reproduce each case: the catalogue case after reopening the cache; refused, interrupted and crashed fresh starts; retries; cancels whose download finishes anyway; channel switches; and Stable behind 100 nightlies. The electron-updater adapter is tested with a stand-in updater. Each new test fails without its fix. Native refusal on a real Mac and a failing Windows installer are still untested, pending the nightly-to-nightly upgrade test. author: atteprojects
body:
## Summary

Builds scope row 15 (spec 0008): org owners invite teammates with a link, give them a role (owner, developer, viewer), change it, and remove them, and any member can leave. Orvano can't send email yet, so an invite is a link the owner copies once and shares however they like.

**Server** (`Orvano.Platform`, `Orvano.Auth`)
- New `platform_invitations` table (migration `0004`). The table stores only the SHA-256 of each token. Invitations expire after 7 days, and one expired more than 30 days is removed on the org's next create. An org holds at most 100.
- `consoleInvitations` create, list, revoke, preview (no session needed, rate limited per IP), and accept. Accept and invited sign up both use one conditional `DELETE ... RETURNING` taken after the org lock, so when two accepts race, exactly one wins.
- `consoleMembers` list, update, and remove (which covers leaving). The last owner rule holds under races.
- Every change writes a `platform.invitation.*` or `platform.member.*` event. Payloads carry only IDs, the actor, role values, and reasons.
- Other additions: `ConsoleAccount.isInstallAdmin`, `signupOpen` on `getSetup`, and `ApiKey.createdBy` (resolved in one batch per page).

**Console**
- A Members page with the Invite dialog and a one time link step, Pending invitations (Resend and Revoke), and row actions (Change role, Remove, Leave). Actions are disabled while the org is being deleted.
- A public `/invite` page. It reads the token from the URL fragment and clears it from the address bar.
- `/sign-up` for installs with open sign up, `/install` for install admins, and names in the API keys "Created by" column.

**Contract and SDKs:** `contract/platform/invitations.tsp` and `members.tsp`, plus five new error codes, with SdkGen run again. Every new operation is in the `console` audience, so the public SDKs gain only the new error codes.

## Testing

- Server: `MembersAndInvitationsTests` (22 tests on real Postgres) and the invitation domain rule tests.
- Console: 557 Vitest tests, with axe in both themes, plus the Playwright flow `console/e2e/members.spec.ts`.
- `/check verify` passed against spec 0008 (`docs/specs/0008-console-team-members/verify.md`).

Three spec cases are not automated yet:
- An accept and an invited sign up of one token racing each other.
- A removed member's key authenticating on a provisioned project.
- The invite token being ignored while no install admin exists.

## Docs

- Scope row 15 is `done`, spec 0008 is `Accepted`, and row 3's row 15 slice is ticked.
- The AGENTS.md files are updated by `/sync`.
- One follow up: spec 0007's handoff list still shows the row 15 items as open, which needs `/architect`.

| 节 | 固化内容 |
|---|---|
| §0 | 盘点前必须 `fetch --prune`（用陈旧 origin/main 会把已合分支误判为未合） |
| §2.1 | 分支是否已合入**用 `merge-base --is-ancestor` 判，不用「有没有 PR」**——squash/rebase 或经其他 head 名合入的分支 `gh pr list` 返回空 |
| §2.2 | worktree 回收走「零脏 + 已合入」**双复验**，任一不满足即跳过 |
| §2.3 | **孤儿 worktree 判据**（本轮最大坑）：`.git` 指针的 gitdir 元数据失联后，该目录既不在 `git worktree list` 里、`git worktree remove` 也管不到，只能扫 `.wt/` 与 `/tmp` 发现 |
| §3 | registry 收口**分两步**（`update --all` 只改 `integration` 不改 `lifecycle`），只 finish `integration=MERGED` 的、**绝不手删记录**（§3.4 并行查重依据面，误收口可用 `resume` 退回） |
| §4 | `/tmp` 保护名单：运行中的 AppImage fuse 挂载点、已注册 worktree、活 IPC、当日并行会话文件；凭据**只删不读**；日期盘点用 `ls -lAt`（`find -newermt` 在本环境返回异常） |
| §5 | 容器 unhealthy 真因辨伪：先查 compose `working_dir` 的宿主源目录是否还在，源没了即**僵尸栈**（`exec` 全废、healthcheck 永不可能过），应整体下线；compose workdir 缺失时按 label 用 docker 直接操作 |
| §6 | 仓库文件改动走分支+PR，禁 `git add -A` |

**`.claude/skills/workspace-hygiene/scripts/hygiene-scan.sh`** — 只读盘点脚本，一次跑完四段（分支 / worktree+孤儿检测 / 远端 / registry /tmp / 容器），避免每次盘点重写同一套命令。

## 实跑验证

脚本在本机实跑通过，并**顺带发现一个手工盘点漏掉的活挂载**（`/tmp/.mount_sourceebGlGk`，SourceGit AppImage，63M，正在 fuse 挂载中）——印证了 §4.1 保护名单的必要性。脚本全程只读，无任何修改动作。

## 未做（需 owner 裁决）

**未加 `type: event` 声明**。按 #2785 分型，低频触发的 skill 应声明 `type: event`（HOLLOW 观察窗 60 天 vs persistent 14 天），卫生治理按月触发、14 天窗口会误报 hollow。但 `type: event` 必须在 `tools/dev/check_governance_surface.py` 的 `_SKILL_EVENT_TYPE_REGISTRY` 登记批准依据与复查期（属 owner 裁决范畴），故本 PR 先按默认 `persistent` 合入，登记待 owner 决定后另开 PR 补。

## Verification

- `python3 tools/dev/check_governance_surface.py --check` → 阻塞项全绿（S1–S15、S5x），新 skill 通过 S7 frontmatter 校验（name 与目录一致、description 非空）
- `python3 scripts/run_gates.py check:quick` → 16 gates 全绿
- `bash .claude/skills/workspace-hygiene/scripts/hygiene-scan.sh` → 实跑通过

## 备注

`.agents/skills` 是指向 `.claude/skills` 的符号链接，故本 PR 只在真身目录新增，未提交任何实体拷贝到 `.agents/`。

author: roed-math
body:
This PR computes the torsion of the completed multiplicative module `A(L) = lim_m Lˣ/(Lˣ)^(p^m)` (`TauCeti.padicCompletionUnits`, #9856). It proves that the torsion subgroup is exactly the image of `pPowerRootsOfUnity p L`, that this image has order `q(L)` when the `p`-power roots of unity are finite, and that Mathlib's `Submodule.torsion ℤ_[p]` of `A(L)` is the additive form of that group torsion.

Target: `TauCetiRoadmap/LocalGaloisGroups/README.md`, Layer 7 "Step 2: control of the torsion". This PR proves the first two bullets: `torsion_padicCompletionUnits`, `natCard_torsion_padicCompletionUnits` and `mem_torsion_padicCompletionUnits_iff`. What remains of the milestone after this PR is `padicCompletionUnits_quotient_torsion_linearEquiv`, the `ℤ_p`-linear isomorphism `A(L)/torsion ≃ ℤ_p^{[L:ℚ_p]+1}`. That needs the structure of the principal units through `deepUnitExpLogEquiv`, and it will quotient by exactly the submodule this PR characterises.

Roadmap: LocalGaloisGroups

Main declarations, in the new file `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Padics/MultiplicativeCompletion/Torsion.lean`:
- `padicCompletionUnits_pow_eq_one_iff`: `x ^ p ^ j = 1 ↔ x ∈ (rootsOfUnity (p ^ j) L).map padicCompletionUnitsOf`. At every level, an element killed by `p^j` is the class of a `p^j`-th root of unity. Since there are only finitely many of these, a pigeonhole argument (`Finite.exists_infinite_fiber`) gives one root that works at every level.
- `torsion_padicCompletionUnits`: `CommGroup.torsion A(L) = (pPowerRootsOfUnity p L).map padicCompletionUnitsOf`. This holds for any field `L`, because each level has exponent dividing `p^m`, so there is no prime-to-`p` torsion.
- `injOn_padicCompletionUnitsOf_pPowerRootsOfUnity`, `natCard_torsion_padicCompletionUnits`, `finite_torsion_padicCompletionUnits`: when `Finite (pPowerRootsOfUnity p L)` holds (for `L/ℚ_p` finite this is `finite_pPowerRootsOfUnity`), the roots embed into `A(L)`, and the torsion has order `localRootOfUnityOrder p L h`.
- `mem_torsion_padicCompletionUnits_iff`: `x ∈ Submodule.torsion ℤ_[p] A(L) ↔ x.toMul ∈ CommGroup.torsion A(L)`. The proof divides by the unit part `PadicInt.unitCoeff`.

The statements use the gated `Finite` hypothesis exactly as `localRootOfUnityOrder` does. They are stated for any field, since the proofs never use the local-field structure.

The new file shares the `MultiplicativeCompletion` prefix with the existing file, so this PR also moves that file into a directory (only the module path changes; no declarations are renamed, and nothing in the repository imported the old path):

| old module | new module |
|---|---|
| `TauCeti.NumberTheory.Padics.MultiplicativeCompletion` | `TauCeti.NumberTheory.Padics.MultiplicativeCompletion.Basic` |

The .github hooks are pinned to a commit sha, and detect-secrets'

author: fturleque
body:
## Constat (audit r5, API-3, Moyenne)
`MorpheusVersionsHttpRoutes.java:27-30` : `rejectUnknown(Set.of())` — `?offset`/`?limit` répondaient 400 sur la lignée, que la route sœur `.../versions/{snapshotId}/requirements` accepte. La collection est croissante (`KEEP_ALL_PUBLISHED`), chaque élément coûte deux lectures de store, et `items` était nu alors que `PagedEnvelope` se déclare l'unique vocabulaire de page (ADR-0107).

## Changé
- La route alimente `versions(...)` par le **même** `page(query)` que sa sœur (aucun second extracteur) ; la réponse est `PagedEnvelope.following(projectId, retentionPolicy ; slice(...))`.
- `slice` ne projette que les éléments retenus (`subList(from,to).map(projection)`, lu dans le code) : les deux lectures de store par élément sont bornées par `limit`.
- **Non borné, et écrit dans l'ADR** : la lignée reste parcourue en entier pour `totalMatches` (un `findSnapshot` par prédécesseur — lecture de métadonnées inévitable sans changer le modèle).
- OpenAPI : `Offset`/`Limit` sur `/projects/{projectId}/versions`, même commit. Amendement d'ADR-0107. Façade `MorpheusApiService.versions` alignée.
- Ordre : plus ancien → plus récent, total et append-only : une publication entre deux requêtes s'ajoute en fin et ne décale aucune page déjà lue (garantie entre requêtes successives, pas transactionnelle).

## Alternatives écartées
Borner la lignée côté domaine (la rétention est une décision) ; second extracteur (la copie dérive) ; curseur `?after=` (troisième forme de page).

## Ce que la garde ne couvre pas
`PagedResponseVocabularyArchitectureTest` n'interdit que les littéraux `"totalMatches"`/`"hasMore"` : elle n'aurait pas vu l'ancien `items` nu et ne voit pas une collection non paginée (constaté, non élargi). Le comportement est tenu par `MorpheusApiHistoryContractTest`.

## Doublons
Aucune copie ajoutée. Duplication `PagedEnvelope` api/mcp : nécessaire et gardée (inchangée).

## Preuve
`MorpheusApiHistoryContractTest` : `?offset=0&limit=1` → 1 élément, `totalMatches` 2, `hasMore` true ; `?offset=1&limit=1` → la suite ; `?cursor=1` → 400. Cassé puis remis : retour à `rejectUnknown(Set.of())` → le test tombe (ligne 53). Deux tests d'architecture textuels du routeur/façade mis à jour (plus stricts). `clean verify` vert (un premier run avait révélé la ligne 25 de `HistoryApiServiceArchitectureTest`, périmée — l'agent B l'avait vue avant, corrigée).
Je n'ai pas de test sur une lignée de plus de 50 publications (deux publications dans les fixtures) ; la pagination est prouvée avec `limit=1`.

## Rapport de l'agent B
Verdict « partiellement fermé » sur ce seul défaut (test périmé, corrigé). Annonces vérifiées dans le code : clés et ordre de réponse, « quatre clés de plus », bornes 1..100 défaut 50, ordre oldest-first, 400 sur paramètre inconnu. Aucun autre lecteur de la route (CLI, MCP, scripts, fixtures, manifeste TSV).

## Rupture (silencieuse pour un client qui ne lit pas `hasMore`)
`items` n'est plus la lignée entière mais la page (50 par défaut) : **lire `hasMore` et paginer**. Notes de version 1.2.1.

`NEX-2` non concerné.

author: elias518-alt
body:
Diese Änderung setzt die Garage auf Supabase-Synchronisierung um und reduziert die Belastung in der Lobby deutlich.

Enthalten:
- Fahrzeuge werden aus public.vehicles geladen und kontoweit synchronisiert.
- Bestehende lokale Garage wird beim ersten Start automatisch in Supabase übernommen.
- Freigestellte Fahrzeugbilder werden im Supabase-Storage-Bucket vehicle-images gespeichert.
- Fahrzeugbilder werden als HTTPS-URL an die Lobby übertragen, sodass andere Spieler sie sehen können.
- Aktives Fahrzeug wird in vehicles.is_active und profiles.active_vehicle_id gespeichert.
- Bilder ändern/entfernen synchronisiert ebenfalls mit Supabase.
- Lobby-GPS nutzt nur eine stromsparende Standortabfrage etwa alle 30 Sekunden.
- COUNTDOWN nutzt eine moderate Abfrage.
- HEADSTART/ACTIVE nutzt präziseres GPS etwa alle 6 Sekunden, damit Fund- und Radiuslogik erhalten bleiben.
- Der bisherige zusätzliche parallele High-Accuracy-GPS-Heartbeat entfällt.
- Lobby-Polling wurde von 1s auf 3s reduziert, Ergebnisansicht auf 5s; laufendes Spiel bleibt bei 1s.
- Die Karte wird in der Lobby nur aktualisiert, wenn sie geöffnet ist.
- Serverseitig sind in der Lobby bis 200m GPS-Genauigkeit erlaubt; Fundlogik bleibt bei max. 25m Genauigkeit.
- Supabase-Migration ist im Repository versioniert.

Supabase-Datenbank und Storage wurden bereits eingerichtet.

author: michelbranche
body:
﻿## Summary
- Warm saves were waiting on three things that are not the write: Supabase session mode (port 5432, pool of 15), `revalidatePath("/pms", "layout")` inside the action (Next re-renders the whole PMS tree before the client gets `{ ok }`), and a second `getPlanningAction` after the client already had the new stay.
- The Next.js client now rewrites a Supabase URL to the transaction pooler on port 6543 with `pgbouncer=true` and `connection_limit=1`. Prisma migrations still use the session URL in `DATABASE_URL`. Revalidate runs in `after()`. Notifications run after the response. Cancel/check-in/check-out read only the columns they need. Create does not load the reservation again just to return `id` and `code`. Pricing context is one property read instead of six. Planning inserts or patches the bar from the action result.
- No migration. Hot filters already have `@@index([propertyId, checkIn, checkOut])`, `@@index([propertyId, status])`, and `@@index([roomId, checkIn, checkOut])`.
- PR #11 was not on `main` yet. This branch starts at #10 (`967f2cb`) and includes the deferred revalidate so a layout glitch cannot hold the save.

Vercel env values were not readable from this session. The rewrite applies when `DATABASE_URL` is the Supabase pooler (`*.pooler.supabase.com:5432`) or the direct host (`db.<ref>.supabase.co`). Local `.env` is the session pooler on 5432, which is the shape the README told production to use.

## Where the time went
Measured from this machine to Supabase `eu-west-2`, service functions only (no browser, no RSC). A probe on session port 5432 failed immediately with `EMAXCONNSESSION` (pool_size 15) while `next dev` was already connected.

| Step | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cancel, warm | 1180 ms | 685 ms |
| Create, warm | 2815 ms | 1749 ms |
| `quoteStay` (3 nights) | 892 ms | 508 ms |
| `findById` full include vs slim select | 687 ms vs 264 ms | status path uses the slim select |
| `planningService.get` (14 days) | 713 ms | no longer called after a save that already has the bar |

Before, the user also waited for the layout re-render inside the action and then another planning fetch (~700 ms). That is the 5–8s. Those two are off the response now.

Auth is a JWT cookie (`requirePermission` does not hit Postgres). Audit stays in the transaction. The pricing rules are unchanged; only the load is one query.

## Test plan
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`
- [x] `npx eslint pms-core --max-warnings 0`
- [x] Warm create and cancel timed on the transaction pooler (table above). Probe rows were deleted.
- [ ] On hotel-grauson.vercel.app after deploy: cancel from the planning drawer and create a stay; each warm save should land nearer 1–2s, one success toast, bar updated without a second planning load

author: nsta1
body:
## Summary

Enabling the same tree for replication from two regions under the same merge mode no longer makes its runtime config `Ambiguous`, so receivers keep accepting the tree's data.

Refs #3899

## Root cause

`LatticeReplicationConfigEntry` stores the tree's merge mode in an `MvRegister`. Two regions that each enable the tree before learning of the other's enrolment mint two concurrent dots. `HasAmbiguousMode` was `Mode.Count > 1`, and `TryGetMode` required exactly one live value, so two concurrent dots carrying the SAME mode were reported ambiguous. The compiled snapshot then projected the tree with no mode, `SnapshotLatticeMergeModeResolver` returned `null`, and every receiver's enrollment gate dropped (and acked) the tree's inbound entries.

## Fix

The issue offered two acceptable outcomes. This takes the first - enabling an already-enabled tree from a peer region is idempotent and converges - because it fixes the behaviour rather than documenting a trap, and it needs no protocol change:

- `HasAmbiguousMode` is now true only when the live values decode to more than one DISTINCT mode.
- `TryGetMode` succeeds when every live value agrees on one mode.
- `Modes` returns the distinct live modes.

Divergent concurrent modes are still ambiguous and still fail closed, unchanged. A later `SetMode` after observing the agreeing dots collapses them to one value as before.

## Changes

### Modified API

| Type | Change |
|------|--------|
| `LatticeReplicationConfigEntry.HasAmbiguousMode` | True only for divergent distinct modes; agreeing concurrent values are not ambiguous. |
| `LatticeReplicationConfigEntry.TryGetMode` | Returns the agreed mode when several live values carry the same mode. Now allocation-free (walks `MvRegister.Entries` instead of the copying, sorting `Values()`). |
| `LatticeReplicationConfigEntry.Modes` | Returns distinct modes. |

### Tests (5 new)

- `LatticeReplicationConfigEntryTests`: same-mode concurrent merge is not ambiguous; same-mode pair plus a divergent third is still ambiguous; a later `SetMode` collapses the agreeing values.
- `RuntimeReplicationConfigEndToEndTests.Concurrent_same_mode_enables_from_two_regions_converge_resolvable_and_keep_replicating`: real authority in two regions, cross-delivered, then per region: projection not ambiguous, resolver (the receiver gate's seam) resolves `OrSet`, membership replicates, status not ambiguous, repeat enable is `AlreadyEnabled`, a different mode is still rejected with `CurrentModeAmbiguous = false`.
- `RuntimeReplicationConfigCrossClusterEndToEndTests.Same_mode_enables_authored_on_both_sites_converge_resolvable_on_both` (Integration): the same scenario over two real `TwoSiteClusterFixture` clusters and the real `LatticeReplicationConfigStore`.

### Fail-first evidence

Against the unfixed `LatticeReplicationConfigEntry.cs` (production file stashed, tests in place):

- Unit + in-memory E2E filter: `Failed: 3, Passed: 24, Total: 27` - `MergeFrom_concurrent_same_mode_writes_are_not_ambiguous` (Expected False But was True; Expected OrSet But was LwwRegister), `MergeFrom_same_mode_pair_plus_divergent_mode_is_ambiguous` (`Modes` returned `< OrSet, OrSet, LwwRegister >`), and the E2E test (projection Ambiguous True, resolver null).
- Cross-cluster filter: `Failed: 1, Passed: 1, Total: 2` - `Same_mode_enables_authored_on_both_sites_converge_resolvable_on_both` (Ambiguous True, resolver null).

With the fix: all green.

### Local runs

```
dotnet test test/lattice.replication/Orleans.Lattice.Replication.Tests.csproj -c Release --filter "FullyQualifiedName~LatticeReplicationConfigEntryTests|FullyQualifiedName~RuntimeReplicationConfigEndToEndTests|FullyQualifiedName~LatticeReplicationConfigAuthorityTests|FullyQualifiedName~SnapshotLatticeMergeModeResolverTests|FullyQualifiedName~CompiledReplicationConfigSnapshotMaintainerTests|FullyQualifiedName~SnapshotReplicatedTreeMembershipTests|FullyQualifiedName~CrdtBufferOwnershipContractTests"
  -> Failed: 0, Passed: 83, Total: 83
dotnet test ... --filter "FullyQualifiedName~RuntimeReplicationConfigCrossClusterEndToEndTests|FullyQualifiedName~LatticeReplicationConfigEntryTests|FullyQualifiedName~RuntimeReplicationConfigEndToEndTests"
  -> Failed: 0, Passed: 29, Total: 29
dotnet build src/lattice.replication -c Release -> 0 warnings, 0 errors
```

Repository-wide gates: not run - no metric instrument added or removed.

### Allocation position

Not a hot path (read by the compiled-snapshot rebuild and the authority, not per commit). `HasAmbiguousMode` and `TryGetMode` are now allocation-free; previously `TryGetMode` copied every value through `MvRegister.Values()`. `Modes` allocates one small list, as the array it replaces did. No serialization, alias, or wire-format change.

### Documentation

- `docs/lattice.replication/runtime-config.md` - same-mode concurrent enables converge; ambiguity means distinct divergent modes.
- `docs/lattice.api.replication/architecture.md`, `docs/lattice.api.replication/api.md` - same clarification for the facade and the `Ambiguous` field.

author: lorenzo-22
body:
## Why

`sioff --help` took ~6 s warm and ~22 s on a cold cache. Not dependency checks: `sioff.cli` imported the package, whose `__init__` eagerly pulled `sioff.api` and with it polars, numpy, pyarrow and Biopython; the command modules and `sioff.config` added pyarrow, omegaconf and loguru. Typer only needs the command signatures to render help.

## What

- `sioff/__init__.py`: PEP 562 `__getattr__` resolves the four API functions and `__version__` on first access. `TYPE_CHECKING` imports keep pyrefly and mkdocstrings seeing them (docs build `--strict` passes).
- Command modules, `cli.py`, `_logging.py`: heavy imports moved into the functions that use them.
- CLI wrapper return hints that named polars become `Any`, with a docstring note: Typer evaluates every annotation (`inspect.signature(eval_str=True)` + `get_type_hints`) while building help, so a lazily imported name cannot appear there.
- New `TestCLIStartup` runs each `--help` in a subprocess and asserts the heavy modules are absent from `sys.modules`.

## Known boundary

Subcommand help (`sioff search --help`) still loads loguru (~0.3 s): Click runs the group callback (`setup_logging`) before the subcommand parses its own `--help`, and clears the pending args first, so there is no clean skip signal. Pinned explicitly in the test.

## Numbers (warm cache)

| Command | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `sioff --help` | 6.1 s | 1.6 s |
| `sioff off-targets --help` | ~6 s | 1.9 s |
| `sioff --version` | ~6 s | 1.0 s |

Remaining cost is typer + rich.

## Checks

232 tests pass, ruff check/format clean, pyrefly 0 errors, `zensical build --strict` clean.

author: parthkomalwad
body:
Phase 9 Task 7 (K10). A weekly self-check built only from data Sable already keeps. It makes no model calls and never runs the eval harness.

- `sable/daemon/selfcheck.py`: `summarize(conn, now, days=7)` returns a `Report` covering goals completed; steps, tokens and USD per goal, with and without a matched skill; skills the doctor flags as failing, plus the ones newly failing since the last report ("see /skill doctor"); and the latest `eval_runs` run. `str(report)` is at most 7 lines.
- Skill matches were never recorded per goal. The orchestrator now publishes one `goal_done` event per completed goal with `steps`, `tokens`, `usd` and `skills`, so the numbers start at zero from this release.
- The daemon runs it Sundays at `maintenance_time`, once per week (it reuses the `maintenance` table guard). `sable selfcheck` and `/selfcheck` run it on demand. Each run publishes `selfcheck` on the bus, shows up in `/dash`, and sends one push through `notify.send`, which does nothing when no topic is set.

Sample:
```
sable self-check since 2026-09-20: 3 goals completed
skills matched 1 of 3 goals
with a skill: 3.0 steps, 1200 tokens, $0.0040 per goal
without: 5.5 steps, 2350 tokens, $0.0085 per goal
failing skills: log-rotate
newly failing: log-rotate (see /skill doctor)
latest eval: 22/25 passed (mock, 2026-09-26)
```

Tests: `tests/unit/test_selfcheck.py` (6 tests: numbers from a seeded DB, the no-skill and no-eval case, newly failing, the weekly guard, push only when configured, and `registry.build_backend` never called), plus one orchestrator test for `goal_done`.

Note: `daemon/selfcheck.py` lazily imports `skills.doctor`/`skills.index`, a peer-layer edge like `maintenance.py -> memory`. The layering test is already an xfail for these edges.

author: evabota[bot]
body:
Closes #150. Вторая подзадача эпика #144 (релиз 0.6.0), спека — [docs/groups.md](https://github.com/micromagicman/flotti/blob/develop/docs/groups.md), раздел «Visibility» и Sub-issues п. 2. Ветка от `develop` после #155 (модель групп).

## Какие двери закрыла

Проверка `canReach` стоит на входе каждого пути «агент → агент»; наружу — одна функция супервизора `mayWrite(from, to)`, которая заодно пишет настоящую причину во вкладку отправителя.

| Дверь | Где | Что видит агент | Что видит человек во вкладке отправителя |
|---|---|---|---|
| инструменты `send_message`, `reply`, `forward` | `sendRefusal` — `src/fleet-mcp.ts` | `there is no agent "x" among the agents you can write to; list_agents names them` — те же слова, что для несуществующего агента | `"x" is not in a group with "eva"` |
| `to` инбокса удалённого агента и всё, что пересылает супервизор | `Supervisor.forward` → `forwardRefusal` — `src/supervisor.ts` | ничего (как сегодня при недоставке) | `could not deliver the message to "x": "x" is not in a group with "eva"` |
| задачи — из инструмента `delegate` и из инбокса | `Delegations.delegate` → `REFUSAL_CHECKS` / `sight` — `src/delegations.ts` | задача падает сразу с теми же словами, что для несуществующего агента | строка `"x" is not in a group with "eva"` и карточка failed |
| администраторы — `restart_agent`, `clear_context`, admin-запросы инбокса | `FleetAdmin.refusal` → `sees` — `src/fleet-admin.ts` | `Refused: there is no agent "x" among …` | та же строка |

- Проверяется вход, не выход: ответ в конце хода (`turnAnswer`), исход задачи и возвращённая задача доходят до инициатора, даже если состав группы к тому времени поменялся. `reply` и `send_message` — новый обмен, проверяются заново.
- Сообщение человека (`POST /api/agents/<id>/messages`, broadcast) не проверяется.
- Администраторы связаны группами, как все (open question 4): действуют на пиров и на себя.
- Задача, отклонённая на входе, теперь показывается карточкой только во вкладке давшего: получателю она не уходила, а агент вне поля зрения о ней не узнаёт. Раньше карточка failed ложилась и во вкладку адресата (например, остановленного).

## `list_agents`, `list_groups`, ростер

`list_agents` — только пиры плюс своя запись с `you`; у каждой записи `groups` — общие с вызывающим группы (у своей — все свои). Без пиров — `[]` и фраза, что агент пока ни с кем не в группе.

Новый read-only `list_groups`:

```json
[{ "id": "release", "name": "Release 0.6.0", "topic": "Ship it.", "members": [{ "id": "eva", "name": "Eva" }, { "id": "reviewer", "name": "Reviewer" }] }]
```

`members` — только те, кто есть во флоте (участник «не во флоте» агентам не показывается — писать ему всё равно нельзя).

Ростер удалённого агента (`docs/a2a-fleet.md`) — те же записи с `groups`, рядом с `agents` массив `groups` той же формы, что у `list_groups`; `text` говорит об этом, а без пиров — что писать некому. Ростер уходит заново при смене состава группы (через `announce()` → `fleetChanged`, дебаунс и сравнение ключа как раньше). Старые адаптеры: `groups` игнорируют, `agents` короче.

## Тесты

Юнит (node --test, 476 зелёных): агент вне группы получает отказ на инструментах, в инбоксе, на задаче и у администратора теми же словами, что при отсутствии агента; внутри группы проходит; ответ хода и исход задачи возвращаются после смены состава; `reply` после смены состава отказан; ростер удалённого — только пиры с `groups`, пустой без группы, и заново после `replaceGroup`. Хелпер `fakeFleet` кладёт всех фейков в одну группу `everyone`, тесты групп задают свои. e2e — флоту сценария «агент пишет другому» добавлена группа `team` (64 прошли локально).

## Что намеренно не вошло

- сообщения в группу (`group` на инструментах и в инбоксе, история группы) — #151;
- UI: раздел Groups, вкладка группы, Settings → Groups — #152/#153;
- полный раздел Groups в README — #154; здесь короткий абзац в «The fleet tools», строки таблиц инструментов и администраторов, ростер в `docs/a2a-fleet.md`, запись в CHANGELOG [Unreleased].

Проверки локально: `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:e2e` — все зелёные.

author: miltondavila-ux
body:
## Problema real en producción
Prueba final del PR #253 con la cuenta de Guillermo Martínez: títulos sobre **alquilar** una propiedad (y uno sobre uso de microondas) quedaron archivados en la categoría **"Compra"** (compra de propiedades). Los títulos en sí eran correctos (evidencia real, long tail legítimo) — el problema era 100% la categoría asignada.

## Causa raíz
El PR #253 de esta misma mañana corrigió la regla de asignación de categoría solo en el **texto del prompt**, sin ningún respaldo en código — a diferencia de TODAS las demás reglas obligatorias de este archivo (cita de evidencia, combo de geolocalización, temas excluidos, años recientes), que sí tienen guardarraíl determinista además de la instrucción en el prompt. Sin ese respaldo, el modelo terminó ignorando la regla en producción con datos reales — el mismo patrón que ya se había corregido antes para esas otras reglas.

## Solución
`reasonAboutCategoryFit`: mismo patrón que `reasonAboutAmbiguousCollisions` (canibalización, PR #254 de hoy) — una llamada corta y aparte a OpenAI que recibe el nombre real de la categoría, sus ejemplos ya publicados y los títulos candidatos, y devuelve cuáles pertenecen de verdad. Los que no pasan se rechazan en `applyOpportunityItems` **antes** de aceptarse. No es una lista de palabras prohibidas (eso ya falló antes con `titleFitsCategory`, retirado el 16/9/2026): es razonamiento real.

## Triple auditoría de la propia solución (3 hallazgos corregidos antes de subir)
1. **Fallaba abierta ante un error de red** — aceptaba todo, reproduciendo el mismo bug en silencio. Cambiado a fallar **cerrada**: un título mal archivado es visible para el cliente en su blog; uno perdido por una falla de red se recupera solo en el siguiente lote (cada categoría acumula títulos de todos los lotes).
2. **El prompt solo calibraba con ejemplos de rechazo**, sin un contraejemplo de "mismo tema con otra palabra = sí pertenece" — riesgo real de reintroducir el bug de `titleFitsCategory` disfrazado de razonamiento. Se agregó el contraejemplo explícito.
3. **La llamada se disparaba aunque la categoría ya hubiera llegado a su tope dinámico** (`categoryTitleCap`, PR #255) — se salta ahora por completo en ese caso (eficiencia).

## Qué NO cambia
Evidencia GSC/GA/Bing, `needKey`, cero canibalización (PR #254), tope dinámico por categoría (PR #255), selección de títulos. Solo agrega el respaldo determinista que faltaba para la regla de categoría del PR #253.

## Sin migración
Cambio de código puro.

## Verificación
`tsc --noEmit --strict` limpio (sin errores nuevos, solo los preexistentes de paquetes del monorepo sin compilar). Se valida corriendo "Actualizar análisis" de nuevo en la cuenta de Guillermo Martínez tras fusionar, confirmando que los títulos de alquiler/microondas ya no caen en "Compra".
