author: notactuallytreyanastasio
body:
Chapter 6 of the blog on Blimp. Live at https://bobbby.online/tetris and in the museum at https://bobbby.online/?project=blimp-tetris. Needs notactuallytreyanastasio/blimp#45 (merged).

---

**blimp_site: /tetris, Blimp Tetris played in the browser, and in the museum**

Blimp's Tetris (examples/tetris.blimp, 801 lines of actors) now has a page
on the site, and an exhibit in the Technical Museum that launches it.

    /tetris                 the page, rendered by the Blimp server
    /tetris/tetris.blimp    the game, as source
    /tetris/blimp.wasm      Blimp's interpreter, application/wasm
    /tetris/blimp.js        Blimp's loader
    /tetris/blimp-view.js   Blimp's view host
    /tetris/play.js         30 lines that start the three above

## The one page with scripts on it

Everything else the site serves has no script, and test/pages_test still
says so. This page has three, because a browser starts WebAssembly from
JavaScript and there is no other door. None of them knows anything about
Tetris: the game decides every cell, every key and the drop timer, and
`game <- :view` hands back the whole screen as a value for the host to
draw. The test holds the page to exactly those three external files and
nothing inline.

The host runs in the send mode added in Blimp #45. Through eval, a game
grows the tab by about 7MB per 4,000 moves and ticks; through send it
does not grow.

Played in headless Chrome against the local server: two ArrowLefts move
the piece, a space hard-drops it, the score reads "score 30 lines 0
level 1", and the console is empty.

## One commit of Blimp

static/tetris/sync.sh copies the game, the interpreter and the host from
one Blimp checkout and writes its commit to BLIMP_COMMIT (eab4eaa, main
after #45). The page links that commit. Nothing in static/tetris is edited
by hand.

## The museum

The exhibit is a row in production's museum_projects (id 33, "creative",
sort_order 0, so it lists right after Deciduous) and the snapshot here is
re-exported from it: 33 exhibits. Its icon is a new grid in
lib/blog/museum/icons.ex, a T-piece falling toward a stack with one gap,
which export.sh carried into data/icons.txt. The desktop keeps /tetris on
this site instead of sending it to the Phoenix origin.

deploy.sh now stages static/, and the Caddy snippet adds /tetris,
/tetris/* and /assets/tetris.css to the route. /tetris was a 404 on
Phoenix, so nothing is shadowed.

author: mujrge
body:
## Description

Makes the repository's GitHub Actions gates reproducible and green so that CI can be turned on. The first two commits are ports of the canonical source commits, and their changes are identical. The last two commits fix what the first GitHub-hosted runs on this PR exposed.

## Why is this change needed

Actions was off at launch. When it was turned back on, the Lint workflow would have failed on its first run: `ruff format --check` flagged 3 files, and the workflows installed ruff, cfn-lint and Poetry unpinned, so results drifted with every upstream release.

## Type of Change

- [x] CI/CD changes

## Changes Made

- `style:` `ruff format` with the locked ruff 0.16.9 on `otel_helper/__main__.py`, `tests/e2e/test_contracts.py` and `tests/README.md`. This is formatting only.
- `ci:` pins ruff 0.16.9 and cfn-lint 1.57.0 (the versions in `source/poetry.lock`) and Poetry 2.4.3 (the version that generated the lock). The pins are in `lint.yml`, `pytest-ci.yml`, `integration-tests.yml` and `windows-installer-e2e.yml`.
- `test:` seven `install.sh` manifest tests always packaged a `macos-*` stub, so on Linux the installer exited with "Binary not found for your platform" before reaching the behaviour under test. They now pick the stub the installer selects on the host. This failed on `main` too, on every Linux Python version.
- `ci:` the Windows jobs run on demand only. `windows-latest` is removed from the pytest matrix (27 Windows-specific failures on `main`). `windows-installer-e2e.yml` becomes `workflow_dispatch` only, because on `main` the generated installer fails when Windows PowerShell is started through `cmd.exe` from PowerShell 7: it inherits PowerShell 7's `PSModulePath`, so `Get-FileHash` is not found (PowerShell/PowerShell#27774). Both failures are tracked separately and are not fixed here.

---

## Testing Checklist

### What was tested

- [x] All existing tests pass locally

### Special cases

- [x] This PR only modifies GitHub workflows (auto-exempt from testing validation). It also includes 3 formatting-only source files.

## Testing Evidence

### Test Environment

macOS 15 arm64, Python 3.12.11, Poetry lock as committed. No AWS Region is used; the tests make no AWS calls.

### Test Results

```text
source$ poetry run pytest tests/ -q
3199 passed, 32 skipped, 1 xpassed, 38 warnings in 171.98s

source$ ruff 0.16.9 check .            -> All checks passed!
source$ ruff 0.16.9 format --check .   -> 237 files already formatted
cfn-lint 1.57.0 deployment/infrastructure/*.yaml (pytest-ci.yml ignore list) -> exit 0
```

This PR is also the first GitHub Actions run of the public repository. The workflow results on this PR are the cross-platform evidence.

author: narugo1992
indyjonesnl
body:
Part of #1840. Does **not** close it — see "What this does not show" below.

## The finding

#1840 is a lost update: a ResourceQuota PUT returns `cpu=2`, and a GET 18 ms
later returns `cpu=1`. The issue ruled out five suspects by reading the code,
and concluded "on paper the lost update should be impossible."

It was only impossible *on paper* because **no test could have observed it.**
`MemoryStorage` — the backend nearly every test in the workspace runs on — had
no optimistic concurrency at all. Every write succeeded, whatever
`resourceVersion` it carried. All five suspects are CAS-retry loops, and none
had ever met a conflict under test.

## Storage contract: two rows, four backends

Ported from `RunTestGuaranteedUpdateWithConflict`
(`staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/testing/store_tests.go:3633-3676`),
which requires the second of two overlapping `GuaranteedUpdate`s to lose its
compare-and-swap and re-run. Stated at our CAS primitive: two updates carrying
the same `resourceVersion` must never both succeed.

- `update_with_conflict` — sequential.
- `concurrent_update_is_atomic` — 40 rounds × 4 writers, multi-threaded.

| backend | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| MemoryStorage | **red** — 4 of 4 concurrent writers won; superseded RV accepted | green |
| etcd | green | green |
| kine | green | green |
| rhino/SQLite (new instantiation) | green | green |

## The fix

`MemoryStorage::update` now compares the incoming `resourceVersion` against the
stored one and returns `Error::Conflict` on mismatch — the compare and the
insert under one write guard, as upstream's `OptimisticPut` is one etcd
transaction (`vendor/go.etcd.io/etcd/client/v3/kubernetes/client.go:83-107`).
A value with no `resourceVersion` still writes unconditionally, matching
`RhinoStorage::update`.

Blast radius, every `MemoryStorage` consumer: **four tests** relied on it
never checking — three in api-server, one in controller-manager — each forging
or reusing a stale `resourceVersion`. Each now sends the version it last read,
as a client does. Everything else passes unchanged: api-server 2130 it +
458/457 unit, controller-manager 576 it + 351/348, kubelet, scheduler,
kube-proxy, common, admission-webhook, test-support.

## #1840 regression test, now with teeth

`resourcequota_update_lost_update_test.rs` drives the real handlers through the
upstream e2e's sequence (`resource_quota.go:950-1000` — an **unconditional**
Update, since it re-sends its original local object) against the quota
controller's `/status` write from a pre-update snapshot: as a PUT, as a
merge-patch, and 25 concurrent rounds.

Mutation-checked: with `MemoryStorage`'s CAS disabled, the concurrent case
reproduces #1840's symptom exactly — `spec.hard` reverts to `cpu=1`. That is
the mechanism, confirmed: a status write that re-reads and grafts is safe
**exactly as long as the store's CAS holds**.

## What this does not show

I set out to find the store whose CAS fails. It isn't any of them.

- **My first hypothesis was wrong.** rhino's SQLite `update` looks like a
  TOCTOU — read, compare, then insert in a separate transaction. It isn't: a
  `UNIQUE INDEX ON kine (name, prev_revision)` makes the second of two racing
  inserts fail, which is kine's actual CAS mechanism. 3 × 400 rounds × 16
  writers (19,200 attempts): zero double-wins.
- **The failure has not recurred.** Log-scanned all 30
  `conformance-sig-api-machinery` runs since 2026-09-02: zero hits (detector
  validated on the issue's two cited runs, both of which it flags). Both
  sightings were manual dispatches on 2026-08-31 / 09-01; every clean run
  since has been scheduled.
- **No code change explains the disappearance.** The storage, controller and
  rhino paths are untouched since the failing commit `81f4e8cb`; the handler
  changes to `status.rs` / `resourcequota.rs` all landed 09-08 or later, after
  the failures had already stopped.

So on current main the invariant holds at every layer and is now pinned at
both — and the two sightings remain unexplained. My recommendation is to close
#1840 as not reproducible and reopen on recurrence; the concurrent test here is
what would catch it in-process if a regression reintroduced it.

## Also found (in the queue)

Instantiating the suite for rhino surfaced two pre-existing gaps:

- #2041 — rhino: a delete of a key that never existed returned `Ok`, not
  `NotFound`. **Fixed here** (`RhinoStorage::delete` treats a missing prior kv
  as NotFound, matching upstream `conditionalDelete` → `getState(...,
  ignoreNotFound: false)`); CI's all-features nextest job runs the rhino row.
  Closes #2041.
- #2042 — rhino: a paged list is not a snapshot at the first page's revision.
  The suite now declares `snapshot_paging: false` for rhino, measured.

author: awesomekling
body:
Three places where retained prefix matching state outlived what it was prepared against:

- Compacting prefix states for retention renumbered them in place without giving the arena a new identity, so contexts memoized across flushes read state indices from the old numbering and panicked in `additions_in` (telekom.net, about half of all loads). Compaction now mints a new identity.
- A style update without a document root applied its tree delta without walking the retained prefix relation through the departures, so the relation kept departed nodes live. That flush now drops the retained prefix caches when it moves the tree.
- More generally, where departed nodes are forgotten, a retained relation that still holds one of them as live is now dropped and rebuilt by the next transaction. `--verify-style` caught this on `rootless-style-update-holds-install-feedback` under load.

body:
## Summary

- **Starting items:** gem now reads each player's starting inventory at OpenDota's first once-a-second `@OnTickStart` interval where the hero exists, and times it with OpenDota's tick-start clock (from #240).
  - Pinned `odota/parser` `Parse.java`: `nextInterval`, `isPlayerStartingItemsWritten`.
  - The first dense snapshot is still the fallback when that clock is unavailable.
- **Ward dispensers:** `purchase_log`, `purchase_time` and `first_purchase_time` now leave out `ward_dispenser`, as they already do recipes. `purchase` still counts them.
- **Purchases at 0:00:** `first_purchase_time` now follows OpenDota's `!first_purchase_time[k]` check, so a purchase at exactly 0:00 is replaced by the item's next purchase.
- **Docstrings:** corrected `purchase_log`, `purchase_time` (it is a sum, not the last purchase) and `first_purchase_time`. API reference regenerated.

Refs HY-80 (part of HY-72).

## Rationale

- **Timing:** gem read the starting inventory at the first sample of its own per-second sampler, which falls on a different tick than OpenDota's interval. Starting items were therefore a second early or late (−90/−89, −89/−88, −88/−89).
- **Contents:** at gem's later read, a support's observer and sentry had sometimes already merged into a dispenser.
- **Dispenser entries:** the combat log records a `PURCHASE item_ward_dispenser` on every observer and sentry merge, about 560 entries across the fixtures. `odota/core` `svc/util/compute.ts` (`computeMatchData`, read at 7b4256f) removes them and recipes from `purchase_log` before deriving the time maps. `odota/core` is not one of the pinned parsers; the fixtures' OpenDota JSON confirms the behaviour.

**OpenDota parity** (`scripts/audit_opendota_parity.py --compare` against `main`, 8 fixtures, 80 players):

| Field | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `purchase_log` | 24/80 | 80/80 |
| `purchase_time` | 24/80 | 80/80 |
| `first_purchase_time` | 23/80 | 80/80 |
| `purchase` | 76/80 | 80/80 |
| `purchase_ward_observer` | 46/49 | 49/49 |
| `purchase_ward_sentry` | 39/43 | 43/43 |

Overall 89 of 103 shared fields match, up from 83, and no field got worse.

## Testing

- [x] `uv run ruff check .`
- [x] `uv run ruff format --check .`

- [x] `uv run pytest`: 4,277 passed

- [x] Docs build (`npm run docs:build`)
- [x] New unit tests cover the tick-start interval rule and its catch-up, waiting for PlayerResource, retiming once the game start is known, the dense-snapshot fallback, dispenser filtering in the log and in the aggregates, and the 0:00 rule.

- [x] Generated protobuf files under `src/gem/proto/` were not edited manually.
- [x] Large replay artifacts are not committed unless explicitly required for tests.
- [x] Secrets and local credentials are not included.

author: alex-s-gardner
body:
`NisarRaster` was an `AbstractMatrix` with a hand-written `getindex`
method per combination of scalar and range. It is now a
`DiskArrays.AbstractDiskArray`, so all of those — plus strided and
Cartesian indexing, views, broadcasting and the bounds checks — come
from one `readblock!`.

### Why: `eachchunk`

A filtered chunk is decoded whole however little of it is wanted, so a
window that straddles boundaries pays for chunks it barely touches.
Until now nothing told a caller where the boundaries were. Holding the
sample count fixed on a GSLC band's 512 × 512 chunks and moving only the
offset:

| window | chunks aligned | straddling | aligned | straddling |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1024² | 4 | 9 | 0.0080 s | 0.0108 s |
| 2048² | 16 | 25 | 0.0193 s | 0.0282 s |
| 4096² | 64 | 81 | 0.0693 s | 0.0835 s |

Worth **1.2× to 1.5×**, most at the block sizes closest to the chunk.
Swept blockwise — four 2048² blocks over a 4096² region, which is what a
blocked correlator does — 64 chunk decodes aligned against 100
straddling, and 0.055 s against 0.081 s.

Measured on a NISAR GSLC band (80640 × 161280 `ComplexF32`, shuffle +
deflate 1).

### Two things to know

**`eachchunk` counts in the raster's `(line, sample)` order**, the
reverse of what the creation property list reports. That is the same
transposition `NisarRaster` applies to the dimensions, and a square
chunk would hide a mistake in it — so the test uses a `(5, 8)` chunk on
a 37 × 23 array.

**`readblock!` takes its destination's axes from the destination**
rather than assuming one-based indexing, because `DiskArrays` hands it a
view when batching a request.

### `DiskArrays` becomes a dependency

A hard one, since the supertype has to exist where the type is defined.
It is light — `OffsetArrays` and `Mmap` — and it is where the ecosystem
is going for chunked storage.

### Not in this PR

Nothing yet *uses* `eachchunk` to align its blocks; that is a change in
the consumer, and the numbers above are what it would be worth.

### Tests

The chunk grid is asserted to tile the array exactly and to have the
right orientation; the aligned-versus-straddling chunk counts are
asserted on the fixture (4 against 9); `readblock!` is exercised with a
view destination; and every indexing form `DiskArrays` supplies is
checked against the array it came from, on both a chunked and an
unchunked dataset.

3,119 tests pass, and the docs build clean.

author: lorenzo-22
body:
## Why

polars picks the compat (SSE4-only) runtime over the AVX2 one whenever both are installed. Since a2f35a2 made `polars[rtcompat]` an unconditional dependency, every siOFF install, AVX2 machines included, has been running the slow runtime. Verified in the dev venv: `sys.modules["polars._plr"]` was `_polars_runtime_compat`.

## What

- `polars>=1.43.2` is now a plain dependency (same floor as risearch).
- New extra `sioff[lts-cpu] = ["polars[rtcompat]", "risearch[lts-cpu]"]` for CPUs without AVX2/FMA/BMI2. Same extra name as risearch; pulling risearch's extra keeps the two packages on the same runtime by construction.
- risearch needs no change: its wheel has no `target-cpu`/RUSTFLAGS, is a baseline x86-64 build, and the full siOFF suite passes on the non-AVX2 dev server.
- Development: uv has no default extras, so a default `lts` dependency group keeps plain `uv sync` / `uv run` working on the dev server (Xeon E5-2650, no AVX2). Modern machines: `uv sync --no-group lts`, or `POLARS_PREFER_PKG=32`.
- CI and docs workflows sync with `--no-group lts`, so they test the runtime a default install gets.
- README install notes and CHANGELOG entry.

## Verified

- `uv sync` on the dev server: compat runtime active, 227 tests pass.
- `uv sync --no-group lts` on the dev server: polars warns "Missing required CPU features", proving a default install now gets the AVX2 runtime.
- Built wheel METADATA: `Provides-Extra: lts-cpu` with both requires-dist entries.
- `uv lock --check` clean.

author: bruno-i-a
body:
Dois relatos do uso em produção: um de desenho e um defeito meu.

## 1. Missão devolvida deixava o período fechado

A régua de `syncClosingFromTask` olhava só `completed`. Mas desde a #31 o período também nasce fechado com a missão **entregue aguardando aprovação** — então sair de "entregue" para "devolvida para ajuste" tinha que reabrir, e não reabria: o trabalho voltava a ser feito e o fechamento continuava dizendo que estava pronto.

Agora o período acompanha se o **trabalho** está feito, não se a missão foi aprovada:

- entrar em `completed` ou `awaiting_approval` → fecha;
- sair de qualquer uma delas para `pending`, `in_progress`, `rejected` ou `cancelled` → reabre, procurando antes outra missão do mesmo período que ainda esteja com o trabalho feito.

A regra ganhou nome e casa única — `taskClosesPeriod`, no domínio, com teste. Ela passou a ser usada em dois lugares distantes (ao gerar o período pela missão e ao sincronizá-lo nas transições), e duas cópias da mesma lista é como elas divergem sem ninguém ver. Foi exatamente assim que o bot do Telegram passou a recusar uma conclusão que a web já permitia, mais cedo neste projeto.

## 2. Saldo de caixa e resultado negativos davam erro

O formulário manual passa `allowNegative` nesses dois campos; **eu esqueci no diálogo de gerar fechamento**. Caixa descoberto existe e prejuízo é resultado negativo.

De quebra, eu tinha **invertido** o empréstimo de sócio: `closingFields` (manual) proíbe negativo e o meu schema permitia. Agora os dois usam a mesma régua.

O `UnrecognizedActionError` que aparecia junto no console é aba com JS de build antigo depois do deploy — não tem relação com o valor negativo, e sai com reload.

## Impacto no banco

**Nenhuma migration.** Cinco arquivos, nenhum em `src/db/`.

O período da Marieli, criado antes da #31, continua como está — as correções valem para as próximas transições. Aprovar ou devolver a missão vinculada agora o sincroniza corretamente.

## Verificação

`tsc --noEmit` sem erros · `vitest run` **755 testes**, 0 falhas (+7) · `npm run lint` limpo · `npm run build` completo. Conferido em tela pelo Bruno na homologação.

author: juanikitro
body:
Refs #65. Responde al [comentario del 28/09](https://github.com/Mkdir-arg/SistemaDeSalud/issues/65#issuecomment-5880247825).

## Qué resuelve

**1. Un usuario para el comprador.** `comprador@salud.local`, con la misma clave que el resto (`DEMO_PASSWORD` o `demo1234`). Es para que quien evalúa pruebe solo y sin «Acceso denegado»:

| Dónde | Qué tiene |
|---|---|
| Plataforma | Entra al tablero de instituciones |
| Hospital Central | Los 9 roles, todas las áreas y los 14 equipos: 36 casos sin asignar, 27 pacientes en fila, turnos por confirmar, traslados por responder y 12 notificaciones sin leer |
| Los Aromos | Admin con todos los permisos de finanzas: gastos, pagos y saldos por decidir, un convenio por aceptar |
| Mutual del Valle | Admin del portal, con autorizaciones por responder |
| **Hospital Piloto** | **Su institución, en puesta en marcha:** tiene áreas, personal y asignaciones, pero ni agendas ni flujo. La guía muestra 3 de 6 pasos, y el resto queda para él («que no esté todo ya populado») |

**2. El tablero de instituciones con vida.** Antes tenía 3 filas: una con datos, otra en cero y ninguna alerta. Ahora tiene 8 instituciones y 2 alertas:

| | |
|---|---|
| Hospital Zonal Sur | Lleno: 96 % de camas → alerta de ocupación |
| Clínica San Martín | Ocupación normal |
| CAPS Barrio Norte | Atención primaria, sin camas |
| Villa Real | Ahora con fila de demanda espontánea e internados |
| Lomas del Este | Lleva 45 días en puesta en marcha → alerta |

Cada efector activo tiene 30 días de atenciones de fila, pacientes en sala e internados ahora. Todo se recorre con el **motor real**, con el reloj puesto en cada paso. Por eso las esperas, los tiempos, los tableros por institución y las historias clínicas (firmadas y selladas) salen de la operación, no de números a mano.

## Decisiones (del responsable, 29/09)

- Comprador con **acceso a todo**. Lo que queda por hacer es su **institución propia a medio configurar**.
- **Solo datos**, sin cambios de frontend, a dos días de la demo.
- El «inicio en instituciones» es el tablero de plataforma (`Directorio.jsx`).

## Cambios

- `seed_efectores` (nuevo, en `apps/casos`): los efectores de la red y su operación.
- `seed_comprador` (nuevo, en `apps/demo`): el usuario y Hospital Piloto.
- `seed_entorno_demo`: corre los dos después de `seed_red`.
- `apps/instituciones/puesta_en_marcha.py`: sale de la vista el cálculo de los seis pasos. Lo usan la vista, **sin cambio de comportamiento**, y `trabajo.py`, que ahora cuenta los pasos pendientes como trabajo del admin o configurador de una institución en alta.
- Docs: `docs/entornos/README.md`, `docs/DEMO.md` y la guía comercial.

## Validación

- `apps.demo`: **10 tests OK** (310 s) sobre PostgreSQL 16 en Docker. La carga completa se ancla al 01/10 a las 8 y se mira a las 9, y ahora también verifica:
  - las dos alertas del tablero;
  - atendidos y espera de hoy en cada efector;
  - la cadena de sellos de Zonal Sur;
  - los 9 roles del comprador y sus permisos de finanzas;
  - los 3 pasos pendientes de Piloto;
  - la misma cantidad de datos al cargar dos veces.

  Esa corrida fue anterior al último ajuste de `seed_comprador` (permisos de finanzas en Central y Piloto). El ajuste se validó con la carga completa y el recorrido de abajo.
- `apps.instituciones.tests`: **23 OK**, después del refactor de la vista.
- Carga completa sin ancla, con la imagen reconstruida desde esta rama: **366 s**, antes 293 s (`seed_efectores` suma unos 56 s). Ningún usuario sin trabajo.
- Recorrido con Playwright de 26 rutas × 3 instituciones más el portal, con el comprador: no aparece «Acceso denegado» ni «No tenés permiso». También recorrí las pantallas de `zonal.jefe` y `villa.jefe`.
- **No corrí la suite completa del backend** (la corre la CI). **No probé nada en Railway.**

## Lo que sigue vacío (conocido)

- **Los Aromos no tiene operación clínica** (fila, camas, agenda, formularios). Agregar atenciones en sus áreas cambiaría las cifras de reparto verificadas en `guia-los-aromos.md`, así que en el tablero sigue en «—» y 0.
- **Finanzas y Coberturas de Hospital Central** siguen vacías, como antes: ahora el comprador ve tablas vacías en lugar de «No tenés permiso».
- Los efectores nuevos **no tienen agendas ni turnos**.
- En el portal, **Prepaga y Obra Social Provincial** tienen secciones vacías. El comprador usa Mutual del Valle, que es la completa.
- **Cosmético:** con 9 roles, la barra lateral del comprador lista todos. Queda así porque se decidió no tocar el frontend.

## Riesgo

- Hay que **recargar Railway** con `seed_entorno_demo --noinput --ancla 2026-10-01T08:00` para que esto aparezca. La carga tarda más de un minuto más.
- Con la carga anclada a las 8, «atendidos hoy» de los efectores sale de la madrugada. El comando garantiza al menos 3 por efector.

body:
Five rounds of owner feedback on Chat, all in one PR.

**1. This term only** (2026-09-29): "let's make chats completely a this-semester sort of thing. you shouldn't be able to join one for a future course, that's confusing. your chat tab should just pull from the current semseter."

**2. The list resizes:** "the sidebar on the chat and todo pages should be adjustable just like those on the schedule and plan pages even though the sidebar doesn't have tabs."

**3. Refinements:** "let's refine the names of the chats … no more summary line under it, that should instead display the last message, and we should have some sort of unread message indicator … muted chats should have an extra icon … we don't need the room info thing, just a button in that top bar (with icon and label). instead of search params, the room code can just be an extra path in the url … a small status thing like groupme when someone joins the room … rework the language again on the 'what's allowed' thing. if someone deletes a message, it should say something like *message deleted by author*." And: "make sure that we clean up all the paths that name the rooms."

**4. Review:** "i'd prefer that the messages previews actually work in realtime for chats besides the one that's currently selected. besides that, works well! just double check notifications deliver all good."

**5. Right-click menus:** a context menu in Chat, using the kit's ContextMenu, with long press on touch.

## 1. Chat's term
- **The rule:** `chatTerm(today, listed, calendars)` in `src/core/catalog/term-tag.ts` (tested). Of the terms Testudo lists, it picks the one in session; between terms, the next one to start (any season, winter and summer included).
- **Why not `tags.now ?? tags.next`:** Next is only ever a fall or spring term. In the gap before winter or summer, it would jump past the term that's about to start.
- **Why only listed terms:** rooms come from a term's catalog, so a term with no catalog can't have rooms.
- **Fallback:** if no listed term is in session or still to come, it picks the newest listed term. Real data never reaches this; it keeps the mock working at any real date.
- **No term switcher:** the list, its rooms, auto-join from the main plan and the bar all use Chat's term. The bar shows the term with its tag and doesn't switch it.
- **Schedule:** "Join … chat" in course details shows only for a course in Chat's term (`useChatTerm`). It keeps Chat's icon.
- **Server:** `chat/follow` answers `{status: "other-term"}` for any other term and saves nothing. There's a worker test for this.
- **Earlier memberships in future-term rooms:** follows, main-plan rows and messages are kept, not deleted. They're hidden until that term becomes Chat's term.

## 2. The list resizes
- Chat's list uses the workbenches' `SidebarResizeHandle` and their one shared width (`UiPrefs.sidebarWidth`).
- The width is loaded on demand, so `/chat`'s first load doesn't carry IndexedDB.
- The default goes from a fixed 320px to the shared 360px.
- I built no new shared piece; Todo can reuse the same handle and pref.

## 3. Refinements
- **Names:** rooms are **Everyone**, **Nelson's Sections** (the professor's last name) and **Section 0101**, under the course's code. Where nothing above names the course, they read "CMSC351 · Section 0101". Meeting times and places moved to the room header's second line.
- **One module for names and paths:** `src/core/chat/room-paths.ts`. It has a unit test for the round trip from name to path to room. Everything else now goes through it:
  - Schedule's Join link, Home's chat rows and Todo's chat links
  - notifications, pushes, the digest and the bell's inbox rows
  - admin's "Remove a chat message": a pasted link names no term, so the server uses Chat's term
  - analytics scrubbing (`/chat/:course/:room`) and view transitions (`screenOf`)
- **Paths:** a room is `/chat/<COURSE>/<room>` (`everyone`, a section code, or a professor's slug like `pedram-sadeghian`), with `?thread=` for a thread.
  - These are real TanStack routes: `chat.tsx` is a layout that keeps the list, its scroll and the socket mounted; the children are `chat.index.tsx` and `chat.$course.$room.tsx`. `/chat/CMSC351` redirects to `/chat/CMSC351/everyone`.
  - The redirect routes load the paths module on demand, so Schedule's first load doesn't carry it.
  - Links name no term, since Chat has one. Older `/chat?term&course&room&thread` links redirect to the path. If the older link's term isn't Chat's, it opens the list.
- **List rows:** each row shows the room's name, its newest message ("Alex: anyone get 3b?", "You: …", or "Message deleted by author") and when that came.
  - **Unread mark:** in Chat's blue (`bg-product-chat`): a dot for one message, the count for more. The course heading's total is gone, since each row carries its own.
  - **Muted:** a muted room shows a muted bell at the row's right edge instead of the unread mark.
- **Options instead of room info:** "a button in that top bar" became one labeled button, "Options" with a sliders icon ("Muted" with a muted bell once muted). It opens a menu on desktop and a sheet on a phone with:
  - Mute or Unmute this room
  - Leave CMSC351 chat, for a course you joined. If the course is in your main plan, the item is disabled and says so.
  - What's allowed, which opens the same popover as the link under the composer

  Room info (its side panel and phone sheet) is removed. The header still says how many people are in the room.
- **Joins instead of a people list:** people who joined between two messages on one day share one small line: "Alex, Sam and 3 others joined". Its tooltip has everyone's name and the time. The line comes from the new `chat/joins` endpoint.
  - A join is when a push adds a course to someone's main plan or changes its section (migration `0023_chat_joins.sql` adds `chat_members.joined_at`), or, for Everyone, when they joined it.
  - The members rewrite now leaves unchanged rows alone, so a person keeps their join time.
  - People from before this change show no join.
- **What's allowed, rewritten** (`MODERATION_POLICY.chat`). Draft for review:
  > Everyone in the course can read what you post, with your name on it.
  > **Go ahead:** Questions about the class, deadlines and office hours. · Setting up a study group: your number, email or a place to meet. · Notes, links and code you're stuck on. · Venting about the class.
  > **Think twice:** Answers to graded work. Your name is on them.
  > **Not allowed:** Slurs, threats and harassment. · Sexual content. · Someone else's private details. · Spam, scams, or one message posted in lots of courses.
  > Messages that break these come down. To report one, use its … menu: a person reads every report, and nobody sees who sent it.

  "Posting here" is unchanged.
- **Deleted messages:** a message its author deletes after the room saw it becomes a tombstone, "Message deleted by author", for everyone.
  - Its author and time stay. The object empties the body and sets a new `deleted_at` column (added to existing objects on load), so no text is kept.
  - It takes no edits, reactions or deletes. A thread under it goes on, and it drops out of the digest.
  - A message only its author saw (held, or still being checked) is still deleted entirely.
  - Account deletion (`purgeAuthor`) still deletes an account's messages entirely.
  - Checked against MODERATION.md and the privacy rules: the tombstone carries no text, reviewers never see authors, and nothing new is stored in D1.
  - Chat protocol goes to version 3: a tombstone arrives as a `message` frame with `deleted: true` and empty text, so older clients reload.
- **Other changes in the same spirit:**
  - Rows show when their newest message came.
  - The finder's tooltip reads "Open CMSC351 · Everyone".
  - A link that names Chat's own term drops the `?term=`.
  - Todo's chat link no longer carries a term.
  - A mute set on the page marks its row at once.

## 4. The whole list, live

author: jhnstn
body:
Related to TAGENT-2162, TAGENT-2163

## Proposed changes

* The WoW funnel only takes over the customer's unpaid funnel site for **the run that built it**, meaning the same funnel slug and args, e.g. the same blueprint (`isSameWowFunnelRun()`).
* When a customer enters a **different** run while an unpaid site is in flight, a new `wow-funnel-pending` step asks them:
  * **Continue that site:** re-enters the funnel with that run's own params, so it's resumed as itself (site, site spec and post-checkout destination all agree).
  * **Discard it and start over:** `POST /wpcom/v2/wow-funnel/pending/discard`, then re-enters the run they clicked, which now builds a new site. The server rate-limits this, since each discard tears down an Atomic site. When it refuses (too many recent discards, site still being set up, or a server without the route), the step explains why and keeps "Continue" available.
* `createSiteOrAdoptPending()` no longer adopts a site from another run when `/sites/new` refuses a second one (e.g. a second tab).
* `waitForBlueprintImportComplete()` gives up after 60s with no import record at all, instead of spinning for the full 15 minutes. Every caller queues the import before polling, so no record means nothing is coming. This is what a run adopted onto the wrong site used to sit on.

## Why are these changes being made?

* The server allows one unpaid funnel site per customer. The flow adopted that site for whatever run was being entered, without checking what it was built from:
  * Entering `blueprint=annalee` with an unpaid `punk` site in flight built the punk site but showed Annalee's site spec.
  * Entering a different CTA took over the pending site, and that CTA's own follow-up never ran.
* Tearing the old site down automatically on entry would let anyone reloading a CTA churn Atomic sites, so the customer decides.
* Server half: the `pending/discard` endpoint, Automattic/wpcom#245614. It must deploy first; until it does, the step only offers "Continue".
* Also fixed along the way: resume now recognises a step with a locale after it (`/setup/onboarding/wow-funnel-pending/fr`) and treats a bare locale as no step (`/setup/onboarding/fr`). `getStepFromURL()` matches `/setup/:flow/:step` exactly, so without this a non-English customer on the pending step would be redirected back to it forever.

## Testing instructions

As an Automattician, with `public-api.wordpress.com` pointed at a sandbox that has the wpcom half, on `calypso.localhost:3000` (or calypso.live):

* **Same run resumes as before:** open `/setup/onboarding?wow_funnel=blueprint&blueprint=punk`, leave before checkout, then open the same URL again in a fresh tab. You're taken back to plans/checkout for the same site, with no prompt.
* **Different blueprint asks:** with the punk site still unpaid, open `/setup/onboarding?wow_funnel=blueprint&blueprint=annalee` in a fresh tab. You land on "You have an unfinished site", naming the punk site.
  * **Continue that site:** you're back in the punk run: the URL says `blueprint=punk`, and the site spec after checkout is Punk's.
  * **Discard it and start over:** a new site is built for Annalee, and its site spec is Annalee's. The punk site is reverted server-side shortly after.
  * Doing it again within 10 minutes: the step says you've started over too often, and only "Continue" remains.
* **Different funnel asks too:** with an unpaid `wow_funnel=default` site, open the blueprint funnel. You get the same prompt.

author: jtwebman
body:
**Bug** (found testing directory dependencies on Windows; any OS): two `file:` directories whose packages share a name failed the install. Minimal repro — workspaces `a` and `b`, each with `"dep": "file:dep"`:

```
jpm: workspaces["a/dep"] and workspaces["b/dep"] are both named dep (ELOCK)
```

SvelteKit hits it: each of its adapter test apps has a `server-side-dep` directory of its own.

**Cause**: `lock::validate` required every entry under `workspaces` to have a distinct name, and a `file:` directory is recorded there. Nothing reads those entries by name: each is keyed and linked by path (`name@link:<path>`), and the resolver never links a directory by name. Workspaces proper keep one per name as before (`find_workspaces` warns and installs the first).

**Fix**: drop the name check from `validate`.

**Test**: `installs_file_directories_that_share_a_name` — each app links its own `dep`, each `dep` installs its own `b` version, and the lockfile reads back (up to date, `jpm ci`). On Windows: the repro installs with each workspace resolving its own directory; SvelteKit installs (440 packages, 76 workspaces, nothing missing; repeat 98 ms).

### Motivation
- Introduce a secure server-side API surface with Firebase Admin to handle privileged operations, media signing, product/category management, and user/profile syncing.
- Ensure no secrets are embedded in the repo or browser code and centralize runtime configuration via environment variables and Vercel rewrites.
- Replace legacy single-file endpoints with a modular, lazy-loaded route dispatch pattern to keep Vercel function limits and improve maintainability.
- Add client-side Firebase initialization and secure API helpers to enable authenticated requests from the UI and enforce server-side validation.

### Description
- Added a server API library with `api/_lib/firebase-admin.js`, `api/_lib/http.js`, `api/_lib/phone.js`, and `api/_lib/route-dispatch.js` to initialize Admin SDK, standardize errors/responses, normalize Kenyan phones, and lazily load route modules.
- Implemented granular API routes under `api/_lib/routes/` for admin and catalog operations including `admin-products.js`, `admin-categories.js`, `admin-media.js`, `catalog-products.js`, `firebase-config.js`, `health.js`, and `sync-profile.js`, and wired them to top-level dispatchers `api/admin.js`, `api/catalog.js`, `api/users.js`, `api/payments.js`, and `api/orders.js`.
- Replaced older monolithic endpoints by removing deprecated files like `api/orders/create.js`, `api/payment/initiate.js`, `api/payment/callback.js`, and `api/upload/sign.js` in favor of the new route architecture and Cloudinary signing in `admin-media.js`.
- Added client-side Firebase support with `src/lib/firebase.ts` and an authenticated fetch helper `src/lib/api.ts`, updated `src/context/AppContext.tsx` to track `authReady`, sign-in state, profile syncing, and `logout`, and updated pages (`src/pages/Auth.tsx`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/pages/CustomerDashboard.tsx`, `src/pages/AdminDashboard.tsx`) to use Firebase Auth and enforce `RequireAuth`/`RequireAdmin` guards.
- Updated types (`src/types/index.ts`) to use UPPERCASE roles (`'CUSTOMER'|'ADMIN'|'SUPER_ADMIN'`), added `scripts/grant-admin.mjs` for granting admin roles, and created `AGENTS.md` documenting project rules and data contracts.
- Modified environment and deployment configuration by simplifying `.env.example`, changing `.gitignore` to `env.*` patterns while keeping `!.env.example`, adding Vercel rewrites and headers in `vercel.json` to map friendly API routes to the new dispatch endpoints, and adding `firebase`/`firebase-admin` dependencies and `node` engine in `package.json`/`package-lock.json`.
- Large Firestore rules overhaul in `firebase/firestore.rules` to reflect the server-driven data model, tighten permissions, and define allowed reads/updates for users, products, orders, payments, notifications, and admin-only collections.

### Testing
- Ran TypeScript type checks with `npm run typecheck`, and the static type check completed successfully.

author: gemberkoekje
body:
## Summary

Step 8 of `PLAN-0.8.0.md` (workstream D), as the Bell-Warden's painter decided it in question D. Details are in `NOTES-step8.md`.

Both paintings paid for marks that laid no paint and were never told:
- the Bell-Warden's spark, a 2.9 px dab that moved two pixels;
- twelve passes of its shifted copies, which fell outside the body they were held to;
- Wenna Brask's flour, eight starved bristle strokes.

`easel log` said *NO PAINT LANDED* for every one of them, and neither painter ran it.

- **`dab-blank`**, a new fact said once a dab lands. It fires when a round dab laid by hand, at the default taper, carries under one unit of paint and is under the size its press lands from. That size is in pixels, measured again a quarter of a pixel apart, and is the same on four canvases (400 to 1440 wide) and three surfaces:

  | | one touch | two touches | three touches |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `round_hard` | 6.5 px | 5.5 px | 2.5 px |
  | `round_soft` | 7.5 px | 5.75 px | 2.5 px |

  It is measured on the mark rather than predicted from its size, because some dabs under the cliff do land. It gives the dab's size in pixels and the fix. The spark, rebuilt: *this dab laid no paint -- 0.19 of a pixel's worth: a one-touch round_hard dab lands every time only from about 6.5 px, and this one is 2.9 px (size=0.0028) on this canvas. Press it three times (press=3), which lands from about 2.5 px, or lay it at size=0.0064 or over.*
- **`landed nothing:`**, a new line in the check after any pass that laid such a mark. Hand marks are named by the line that laid them and a mass call's by how many of its passes. Each gets the cause its record shows: half its path or more outside its clip, a round dab under its cliff, an oriented tip under 4 px, or a bristle loaded under `0.5`. It prints the painter's own example word for word: *landed nothing: the dab at p06_finish.py:39 (a round tip under its cliff at press=1)*. It appears in `report()` and `checklist()`, gives records instead of lines when the painting is read in another process, and never prints after a counted pass.
- **`dab()`** now gives all three touches: about a tenth, a fifth and four fifths of the way for a light on a dark passage. It used to say *about a quarter* for one touch and nothing for two.
- **Documents:**
  - `REFERENCE.md`: the code's row, the new line, and a sentence saying a mark that laid nothing is still charged.
  - `PAINTING.md`: the sentence on a missing mark now gives what the corpus measured; it used to blame an opacity of zero or wet paint.
  - `DIAGNOSIS.md`: one extra pointer.
  - `_check_tip_pixels`'s docstring: removed "a round tip has no such cliff".
  - README and `llms.txt`: thirty-two notices.
  - `CALIBRATION.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `SUGGESTIONS.md`, `PLAN-0.8.0.md`: updated to match.

Nothing a mark lays changes, and no saved painting rebuilds differently.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest -q` passes: 1,695 passed, 4 skipped. A docstring reflow landed after that run.
- [x] `ruff check src tests scripts examples mcpb` passes
- [x] No golden image moved
- [ ] `make_brush_sampler.py`: not applicable (no brush, colour or texture change)
- [x] `scripts/check_guide_blocks.py`: 79 blocks ok, 0 failed, no recommended block trips a notice; 22 of 22 demos fail the way they say
- [x] `scripts/check_guide_overlap.py` is clean
- [x] No-nouns grep run over every added guide line, with both paintings' nouns
- [x] `probe_bell_session.py --landed`:
  - The engine's cliff table is the measurement, row for row.
  - Both paintings, rebuilt, print the lines their painters decided on: 3 of 8 passes and 5 of 11, including all eleven of Wenna Brask's marks.
  - Over the corpus the line names **the same 142 marks on the same 50 passes, each with the same count**, as step 2's replay. That is 14.7% of 341 painted passes.
  - `dab-blank` is said 56 times, on 10 passes. That covers every round dab under its cliff that laid nothing. The one round dab it does not tell is centred outside its clip, and the line names it.
  - `dab-blank` fires on no guide block.

## Notes for the reviewer

- **The line is a standing line, not a finding.** The plan left this open. No painter means to lay a mark that lands nothing, and the painter's own `landed nothing: ...` has the shape of a standing line. It also matters for the demo check, which counts findings: step 7's *A silhouette lit from one side* lays three passes of its far copy outside the body (two in its demo). As a finding, the line would have become a fault in a demo whose failure is the cut-out.
- **Two recipes lay a mark that lands nothing, and are F's to fix (step 9):** that far copy, and *A mass built of planes*'s dry-brush stroke (`load=0.35`, which step 2 found). Neither is a notice, so the guide check stays green.
- **Wobble changes one figure, and it was the spark's.** At `tip_wobble=0.7`, three touches of a `round_hard` land only from 2.5 px, not at every size. I caught this reading the grid back before the corpus replay, so each figure in the table is now the worst case over every canvas, surface and wobble.
- **The fact only fires at the default taper.** `pressure="even"` lands from 2.5 px at one touch. A dab with a pressure of its own that laid nothing is still named by the line, without a cause.
- **A stroke that lands nothing stays charged.** The painter asked for these marks to be named, and making them free would hide them from the budget. H4's decline (from step 2) stands; nothing was built for it.

author: saamai591-sudo
body:
## Problem
In forms that show the grand total as a label at the bottom (Purchase Invoice, Sales Invoice, ...), on smaller screens with the sidebar open, the layout broke and the total section extended outside the visible page.

## Root cause
Document forms wrap their content in a `<fieldset>` (it disables the form after approval). A fieldset has the browser default `min-width: min-content`, so it stretched to the width of the widest item inside it: the line-items table (about 1250px). The header, the grid and the bottom totals line all took that width, so in a 550px area beside the sidebar the whole form was more than twice as wide as the page and the totals (at the far end of the footer) ended up off-screen, instead of the table scrolling inside its own box (`.je-lines-scroll` already has `overflow-x: auto`).

## Change (`frontend/src/styles.css`, shared CSS, no per-form changes)
- `fieldset { min-width: 0 }`: fixes the root cause for all ~41 forms that use a fieldset; the row grid now scrolls inside its own container.
- `.je-header-grid` items and their controls may shrink (`min-width: 0`), otherwise the three-column header still spilled to the left at about 800px.
- `.je-lines-totals` no longer forces one line (`nowrap`): the footer already wraps, so the totals move to the next line first and only break their text if there is still not enough room.
- `CLAUDE.md` notes the rule in the shared-behavior section.

## Testing
Local dev server, Playwright, measuring the page content's scroll width against its visible width (sidebar open):
- Before, window 1100px: sales invoice content 850px visible / 1291px wide, totals text 426px outside the left edge. Reproduced on the purchase invoice as well.
- After, 1100 / 900 / 800 / 700px (the sidebar collapses by itself at 700): visible width equals content width, the totals text lies inside the visible area, and only the lines table is wider than the page, scrolling inside its own box.
- Nine document forms at 800px, before: 8 overflowed (sales invoice and purchase invoice by 1291px, service purchase invoice 1251px, deliveries 793px, payments and receipts 730px, quotes and orders 710px); only journal entries fit. After: all nine fit. At 1400px all nine fit, as before.
- Visual check at 800px on the purchase invoice: header fields inside the frame, totals line visible, table scrolls inside its box.
- CSS-only change; no type-check needed. Not tested in Safari or Firefox.

body:
## What changes for the user?

A new page at **`https://shell.online/start/`** to test against the home page with paid traffic. The home page is unchanged.

Paid X traffic (`utm_medium=paid_social`) has been about 6,500 visitors a day, 98–99% on phones. It clicks a CTA about 0.05% of the time, and median time on the page is 1.4–1.6 seconds. `/start/` fits on one phone screen and says only:

- **Use any coding agent from your phone.** Free and open source. No account needed.
- **How it works:**
  1. On your laptop, install shell: `curl -fsSL https://shell.online/install | sh` (with a Windows switch on laptops)
  2. Start your agent through shell: `shell claude`, or tap `shell codex` · `shell hermes` · `shell opencode` · `shell cursor-agent` to swap it in
  3. Scan the QR code it prints with this phone
- On a phone, **Send these steps to my laptop** opens the share sheet with `https://shell.online/start/`. Where there's no share sheet, it copies the link instead. On a laptop the same page shows Copy buttons and no send button.

For the ads, link to `https://shell.online/start/?utm_source=x&utm_medium=paid_social` (plus `twclid` if X adds it).

## Analytics

`/start/` gets exactly what `/` gets, and nothing else does. `shared/landing-paths.ts` has one `isLandingPath()` check, and it's used everywhere `/` was hard-coded:

- Worker CSP: the same Google Analytics, PostHog and X origins as `/`. The test checks that the policy is identical.
- Google Analytics and first-party `page_loaded`, `copy` and `cta_click` events.
- X base pixel. It's attributed to `https://shell.online/start/`, so the two pages can be compared in X Ads.
- PostHog route `start` (`$current_url` `https://shell.online/start/`). Statistics dashboard label: `landing_start`.
- New CTA target `start_share` for the send button.

The page is `noindex` (meta tag plus the Worker's existing `X-Robots-Tag` for non-document paths), so the home page stays the one search engines show.

## Verification

- `npm run typecheck`: passed.
- `npm test`: 66 files, 756 tests passed; installer, Docker entrypoint, deploy guard, landing SEO and mobile-controls checks passed.
- New tests: the X pixel loads on `/start/` with `page_location` `/start/`, and not on `/start`, `/start/extra` or `/start/?password=…`; `/start/` gets the same CSP as `/` plus `noindex`; PostHog route and `$current_url`; statistics label.
- `npm run build` emits `start/index.html` with its own script and stylesheet. Checked in headless Chrome:
  - **iPhone 13 (390×664):** fits on one screen, no sideways scroll.
  - **1440×900:** fits; the agent chips and Windows switch work.
  - **iPhone SE:** the page scrolls slightly, and the install command scrolls inside its box.
- End to end with the current release on macOS: from a fresh `HOME`, the step 1 command installs, step 2 (`shell <command>`) starts a session, and scanning the QR code on a phone opens the terminal with no password to type.

## Access and privacy

No change to sessions, terminal input, encryption or stored content. The new page loads only what the home page loads, under the same opt-out and Global Privacy Control / Do Not Track checks.

- [x] No real share links, credentials, private terminal content or deployment secrets are included.
- [x] The changelog is updated. No user docs change: this is a campaign page, not a feature.

## Rollout

Needs a deploy. **Add `"/start/*"` to `assets.run_worker_first` in `wrangler.production.jsonc`.** Otherwise Cloudflare serves the page straight from assets, without the Worker's CSP or page counting, and `npm run deploy:production` refuses the config anyway, because it routes fewer paths than `wrangler.example.jsonc`.

To measure installs and sessions from the test, the relay also needs `"POSTHOG_ENABLED": "1"` in the same config (see #282). Without it, only page visits and clicks are recorded.

author: srihithg
body:
## Summary

- **Version bump:** this bumps the version to 0.4.0, so installs of 0.3.0 from before the Cowork support landed get replaced.
- **Install:** it makes the Cowork half of the install hard to miss.
- **Skill:** it teaches the skill to tell a Mac that's out of reach from one that was never set up, and what to do when a Mac serves only `search` and `read`.

**Built on albericliu0/starmemory#2**, which is built on albericliu0/starmemory#6. This PR's own commits are the last seven. Merge #6, then #2, then this. It's stacked for two reasons:

- The skill uses #2's server name, `starmemserver`.
- The release in the next section needs #2's fix for the test that fails on macOS.

**Do not merge before release v0.4.0 exists.** Outside Apple Silicon, the first run downloads the addon from the release named after `package.json`'s version.

## Why

- **The old copy can stick.** The Cowork support merged at 0.3.0, the same number as the release before it. Claude Code keys its plugin cache by version, so a machine that installed 0.3.0 earlier can keep that copy, which has no `remember` or `forget`, and the desktop launcher can pick it.
- **Half an install records nothing.** The advertised one-liner sets up only the Mac side. Without the plugin added in Cowork, no Cowork session loads the skill or gets a session key, so nothing is recorded. The skill can't catch that, because it isn't loaded.
- **An asleep Mac looks like a missing install.** The skill read missing tools as "the setup didn't finish" and pushed the install again. People use Cowork away from the Mac, so usually the Mac is just asleep or the app closed.

## Changes

- **The install command upgrades too.** Run on a machine that already has StarMemory, `claude plugin marketplace add` and `claude plugin install` just say "already installed", so the old one-liner ran whatever copy was already there. The command now runs `claude plugin marketplace update starmemory` and `claude plugin update starmemory` as well, and each exits 0 when there's nothing to do. It uses `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME/.claude}` for the path. The README and the skill carry the same command, and a test holds them equal. The skill also recognises an entry under the older name `starmem`, and says that running the command again replaces it.

- **README.** The Cowork install is two numbered steps: the server on the Mac, then the plugin from Cowork's Customize menu. It says what step 2 brings, and that nothing inside Cowork can remind you of it. It also gives the path to use when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is set, and says to restart the app after `claude plugin update`.
- **Skill.**
  - When the tools are missing and something shows the Mac was set up, the skill says in one line that memory isn't reachable right now: the Mac asleep, the app closed, or the session not linked. When nothing shows either way, it offers the setup once, worded for both cases.
  - It recognises its own tools only when they share one prefix. It never searches through another connector's `search` or `read`.
  - A new section covers the case where only `search` and `read` are there. The skill keeps searching and says the session can't be recorded. It gives the update-and-restart fix, and answers "don't record this" with the truth: nothing is being recorded anyway.
- **`npm run package`** now also says to upload the zip in Cowork.
- **Manifests** name Cowork in their descriptions.
- **Tests.** `test/plugin-manifests.test.ts` checks that every version field matches `package.json`. That check caught `package-lock.json` still at 0.2.2, so the lockfile is resynced in its own commit. The tests also check that the skill names every tool `src/mcp-server.ts` registers and the server name `desktop-install` registers, and gives the same install command as the README.
- **Version bump.** It's the last commit, 7 fields across 5 files. The Cargo crate stays at 0.1.0: nothing reads it, and it has never followed the plugin version.

## Release steps before merge

1. Merge albericliu0/starmemory#6 and then #2. #6 is what lets the macOS and Windows CI jobs pass.
2. Tag the bump commit in this repo and push the tag: `git tag v0.4.0 <bump commit> && git push origin v0.4.0`. `DEFAULT_ADDON_BASE_URL` points at this repo, so a fork's release won't be used.
3. `build.yml` runs on the tag and builds and tests on four platforms. The release job runs only if all four pass. It writes `SHA256SUMS` and creates release v0.4.0.
4. Check that the release is published, not a draft. It should have five assets: `starmemory_native.{darwin-arm64,linux-x64,linux-arm64,win32-x64}.node` and `SHA256SUMS`.
5. Merge this PR.

## Testing

`npx vitest run` on macOS arm64, with the real embedding model, on this branch as stacked: 394 of 394 pass. I also ran the command chain against a throwaway `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` and a local marketplace, and it moved a 0.3.0 install to 0.4.0.

## Open questions

1. **Plugin server in a Cowork container.** Once v0.4.0 exists, a Cowork container that starts plugin MCP servers could download the linux addon and serve the tools against a store that's thrown away. `cli/mcp-server.mjs` could exit early when `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT` starts with `remote_cowork`. I haven't checked whether Cowork starts them.
2. **Printing step 2.** Should `desktop-install` print the Cowork plugin step when it finishes? That output is what people see right after installing. I left `cli/desktop-install.mjs` to #2.
3. **The Customize wording.** "This repository or the zip" is carried over from the old README. It hasn't been checked against the real app.
4. **The marketplace description** still says "Prebuilt for darwin-arm64".

author: gfrankliu
body:
## Summary
On NVIDIA Jetson devices without DeepStream installed, `libnvbufsurface` is available under `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/nvidia`, but `nvbufsurface.h` lives in the Jetson Multimedia API (`/usr/src/jetson_multimedia_api/include`) rather than the DeepStream `sources/includes` directory. The build therefore found the library but failed to compile the NVMM buffer factory.

This change falls back to the Jetson Multimedia API include directory when the DeepStream include directory does not provide `nvbufsurface.h`. The check runs independently of the CUDA detection path, so it applies whether CUDA is found via `cuda.pc` or the toolkit fallback. Systems with DeepStream installed keep using the DeepStream headers.

## Testing
On a Jetson without DeepStream:
- `meson setup` + build succeed with NVMM enabled
- `ldd builddir/ext/pylon/libgstpylon.so` resolves `libnvbufsurface.so.1.0.0` from `/usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/nvidia`
- `gst-inspect-1.0 pylonsrc` lists `video/x-raw(memory:NVMM)` caps

## re/02 — gateway registry + shared core modules (G1 gate branch)

  This branch doesn't change behaviour. `powderline.run(recipe, output_dir, engine=...)` works exactly as before, with the same `engine=` names, schema 0.26.0 and outputs. The difference is that dispatch now goes through a plugin registry. The branch also adds the shared core modules that the schema branches (re/03–06) build on. **G1 gate: passed** (independent reviewer session, no blockers); the review's findings are fixed in this branch.

  ### What's in it
  - **Gateway registry** (`powderline.registry`)
    - Discovers gateways lazily from the `powderline.gateways` entry-point group: `ep.load()` runs only when a gateway is first requested.
    - `register_gateway()` escape hatch for tests and development.
    - `GatewayNotInstalledError`, plus a clear "re-install" error when no entry points are found at all.
    - Contract: a frozen `Gateway` dataclass (A54).
  - **Engine-free gateway factories:** `gateways/gsasii/gateway.py`, `topas/gateway.py`, `easydiff/gateway.py`.
    - **Schema layer** (`validate`, `capabilities`): runs with no engine installed.
    - **Runtime layer** (`run`): thin wrappers over today's `kicker.run` / `run_topas_recipe` / `run_easydiffraction_recipe`, importing the engine lazily.
    - **Version check:** a real run checks the installed engine version against `ENGINE_VERSION_SPEC` and fails hard if it's out of range (`EngineVersionError`, A44). Specs: GSAS-II `==5.7.9`, TOPAS `>=7,<8`, easydiffraction `>=0.20.1,<0.21`. There's a test-only bypass, `allow_unsupported_engine_version` (A53).
    - **Missing engine:** raises `EngineNotAvailableError`, which is also an `ImportError`, so existing `except ImportError` code keeps working (A52).
    - **Uniform contract:** every gateway has `validate(recipe, *, verbose=False)` (A50, A59).
  - **Dispatcher** (`powderline.engine.run`) maps the old `engine=` names 1:1 to registry names. Its public signature is unchanged.
  - **`symmetry` promoted** from `topas/` to core `powderline.symmetry`, ending the easydiff → topas import. The move is verbatim except for one thing: the error is created by a lazy `_translation_error()` helper, because a top-level import would be circular. This is a temporary fix; re/03 replaces it with a core error (A56/A57).
  - **New core modules**, created and unit-tested only (gateways start using them in re/04–06):
    - `exceptions.py`: the error types plus the `{code, message, field_path}` warning shape (A60 confirms `RecipeValidationError` subclasses `ValueError`).
    - `fitstats.py`: Rwp and Rexp in percent, GoF and reduced χ² unitless. N counts only in-range points with weight > 0; P is the parameter count reported by the engine (A41, A45, A55).

    - CLAUDE.md notes that `pixi reinstall powderline` is needed after editing entry points.
  - **`known_issues.md` KI-13** (`watch`): every engine, including the default gsasii, now depends on entry-point metadata written at install time. We keep entry points as the only discovery path (A58).

  ### Commits (10 on `ae415c8`)
  | SHA | Subject |
  |---|---|
  | `fe49fd0` | feat(core): add the exceptions module and structured-warning shape |
  | `b9767a7` | refactor(gsasii): move validate + validate_simulation_mode_parameters to an engine-free module (verbatim) |
  | `b3eec02` | refactor(core): promote symmetry out of topas/ into powderline.symmetry |

  | `9c24109` | feat(core): add reports — shared writers for the standardized report files |

  ### Verification
  - **Default env:** 498 passed / 3 skipped at `ae415c8` → **637 passed / 4 skipped** at `a84fd39`.
    - Every baseline test has the same outcome.
    - +139 new tests.
    - The +1 skip is a test that only runs when easydiffraction is installed.
  - **easydiff env:** the pre-existing `test_easydiff_*` give **54 passed**, unchanged. Run with the new registry, gateway, symmetry and fitstats tests: **152 passed / 2 skipped**.
  - **Unchanged outputs:** `run(engine="gsasii")` and `run(engine="topas")` on LaB6 produce **byte-identical** outputs at `ae415c8` and on this branch. GSAS-II also matches the committed references within `regression-tolerance`.

body:
## Summary
- Clears the last two pyright errors in the backend: pyright on `backend/app` now reports **0 errors, 0 warnings**.
- No input behaves differently. W6 final (making pyright a required check) can follow.

## Motivation / Context
Programme item W6, cause C7, approved by Adrian on 2026-09-29 ("Approve as written"). It follows #471 (C4) and #480 (C5). These two findings appear only under the project's `[tool.pyright]` settings.

## Changes
- `backend/app/models.py` `AccessToken.user_id`:
  - fastapi-users-db-sqlalchemy declares the base's `user_id: ID` for type checkers only (inside `if TYPE_CHECKING`, `access_token.py:19-22`; there is no such column at runtime). A mapped column `Mapped[int]` cannot match that declared `int`, because a mutable attribute's type is invariant.
  - Fix: a rule-specific `# pyright: ignore[reportIncompatibleVariableOverride]` with the cause in a comment. This is how #461 settled the same library's typing gaps; the backend has three such FastAPI-Users ignores.
  - Rejected: the library's own UUID-table pattern (declaring `user_id: int` for type checkers). It would mistype a column that code queries, `tests/conftest.py:468` `AccessToken.user_id.in_(ids)`.
- `backend/app/services/aggregate.py` `merge_pdfs`: the `except` branch set the page count to 0 only so the next line skipped the file, and pyright could not see that `reader` is always bound when used. The `except` now `continue`s directly. An unreadable file and a zero-page file are both still skipped.

## Test Plan
- [x] `cd backend && uvx pyright==1.1.414`: `0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 informations`
- [x] `uv run ruff check app tests`, `uv run ruff format --check app tests`: clean
- [ ] CI `backend`: the full suite. Not run locally, because this machine's Docker containers, the test database included, were removed at about 18:35Z by something outside this lane. #480's CI shows the suite green on main just before this.
- OCR / LLM regression: not applicable

## Risk / Rollback
Blast radius: backend. One comment plus a rule-specific ignore on a type declaration, and one equivalent control-flow change. Rollback: revert this PR.

body:
## Summary

`CorrectionLearner.diff` builds a full word-level LCS table even when the pasted text is unchanged — the audit measured 15.5 ms / 17 MB at 1 500 words and 59 ms / 69 MB at 3 000 words, on the main actor, every time the watcher reviews a paste.

`diff` now early-outs on `a == b` — the common case (the user edited nothing), and output-identical since equal arrays can only produce zero blocks.

Deliberately NOT a prefix/suffix strip: an interior word can LCS-match a suffix word, so boundary stripping changes the alignment the original code produces (e.g. a="x A" vs b="y x A": strip → substitution `x→y`, original → pure insertion). Keeping the full table for changed texts preserves every block the learner sees today.

author: kaeawc
body:
On the iPhone Duo (iOS 27.1), `sendKeys` `arrow_left`/`arrow_right` were silent no-ops: `abc`, then ←, then `Z` gave `abcZ`. The runner's `pressKey` used `app.typeKey(.leftArrow, modifierFlags: [])`, and non-destructive keys had no post-condition. The device check found Cmd+arrow works on the Duo, but plain, alt and shift arrows do not.

**Runner:**
- Plain horizontal arrows are sent through the focused element with `typeText(XCUIKeyboardKey.*.rawValue)`, the same route backspace uses.
- A reversible marker probe reads the caret index before and after. The marker is deleted and the value checked against the original, with the existing restore path as backup. The pure `arrowCaretMoved` helper makes the decision.
- If the caret didn't move, `app.typeKey` is tried once. If it still didn't move and the caret wasn't already at the edge, the key fails with "arrow key had no effect".
- If the probe can't run, the result is `verified:false`. Modifier arrows keep app-level delivery and also return `verified:false`.

**Wire and TS:** an optional `verified` field on `press_key_result`, decoded and passed through `InputKey`/`SendKeys`. Runner failures surface as step failures.

**Tests:** Swift `PressKeyTests` (`arrowCaretMoved`, `verified` pass-through). TS tests cover `InputKey`, `SendKeys` and the decoder.

**Not yet run on a device.** Merge is held until the Duo check passes.

Closes [#8169](https://github.com/kaeawc/auto-mobile/issues/8169)

author: fungc-io
body:
## Summary

Makes the browser test run build first and restore a clean dev server afterwards.

## Problem

The Netlify dev emulation reads `dist/_redirects` once, when the dev server starts. The redirect and header tests therefore need two things that nothing enforced:

- a current `dist`
- a server started *after* it was written

Run the suite against a server started before the build and those tests check stale pages, or skip the rules entirely. In practice this meant the prefixed locale pages (`/de`, `/es`, `/ja`, `/fr`) were being asserted against the previous build.

## Changes

- **`pretest`** builds, restarts the dev server so it can see that build, and sets `PUBLIC_GTM_ID`.
- **`posttest`** restores a clean server via `npm run dev`, whose `predev` clears `dist`, so development continues against live-rendered pages. Skipped under CI.
- **`reuseExistingServer`** is now always on. Astro runs `astro dev` as a background daemon, so the foreground process exits immediately and Playwright reports "Process from config.webServer exited early" when it tries to manage the server itself. Letting `pretest` own the server removes that race.

Run the suite with `npm test`, not `playwright test` on its own.

## Validation

- `npm test` → **248/248**, twice in a row
- The GTM smoke test passes now; it was the one persistent local failure, because the server was previously started without the id it expects
- After the run, `dist` is cleared and every locale renders live from the dev server
- `posttest` verified to no-op when `CI` is set

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test` passes and leaves a working dev server
- [ ] `/de/solutions/data-sovereignty/` renders live after a test run, not from the previous build
- [ ] CI is green and does not leave a stray dev server

author: sdl-a1
body:
Tightens what the header path accepts, and gives the node a way to bound a peer's advertised total difficulty before downloading from it.

## Header acceptance

One invariant now holds: **a header is stored only once it has been verified, and verification needs its parent.** A header whose parent is not held is refused rather than stored, and the refusal is reported so the peer is charged.

Nothing is lost by refusing. Header data is the most replaceable thing in the system, and skeleton chunks are drained in order (`PeerChunkTracker::drain_ready`), so an honest peer's headers arrive with their parent already stored. A follow-mode announcement running ahead of its parent is simply re-requested — and that caller ignores the result, so it is not punished for it.

Chunk responses are matched to the skeleton **by hash and contiguity** rather than by block number alone: a chunk is the answer to a specific question, and a matching height does not establish that it is.

## Snapshot sync establishes the checkpoint difficulty

It used to accept the peer's figure and write it as the node's own. The walk already reads every header, so it now sums their difficulty; the claim may exceed that sum by no more than the checkpoint block's own difficulty. A session that fails this charges the peer.

## Cumulative-difficulty checkpoints

A checkpoint states the work from genesis to a height, so nothing may claim more for that height.

Unlike a hash checkpoint this has a **safe failure direction**:

| checkpoint is | hash | cumulative difficulty |
|---|---|---|
| wrong | silent capture | detectable contradiction |
| too generous | no such thing | weak, harmless |
| stale | irrelevant or fatal | merely covers less of the chain |

`audit_own_chain` is what makes shipping one safe: if this node's own validated chain ever carries more work at that height than the checkpoint permits, that is reported rather than silently resolved either way.

The checkpoint is mainnet **#9,020,000**, read from this project's own synced node. A test checks the constants against their decimal values — it caught two transcription errors while this was being written, one a difficulty that silently truncated because 7.39e21 does not fit in a `u64`.

## Bounding the window above it

Request one header every 768 blocks, verify it, and use the retarget rule to bound what the blocks between samples can carry. The rule changes difficulty by a fixed fraction of the parent's per block and nothing a miner controls changes that magnitude — the timestamp and uncle count pick only the sign — so a ceiling follows.

`ChainSampler` computes it; `SamplingGate` drives the requests as a state machine, so it is testable without the service. Three properties are pinned:

- no verdict before the window is covered — otherwise a peer passes by answering the first few samples and going quiet
- silence is rejection, not patience — `Unsubstantiated` rather than pending forever
- honest peers pass — driven end-to-end against a truthful peer over 20,000 blocks

**Live:** the free half. A peer whose claim the checkpoint alone refutes never has its metadata recorded, and `best_peer` selects on recorded metadata, so it is never chosen. No requests at all.

**Not yet invoked:** the sampled half. The gate is built and tested; connecting it needs `GateAction`s issued through the request path and responses routed by request id, which is its own change.

## Tests

710 pass across sync, core, storage and networking. Notable ones:

- a chunk of mutually unlinked headers leaves the store exactly as it found it — **verified to fail against the previous behaviour**
- the sampled bound is never below what a flat chain actually carries — **caught a real bug**, where a strict rise-then-fall model could not express an unchanged difficulty and returned a bound below the truth for short spans
- two existing tests were updated; one had asserted the previous behaviour as intended

author: deepratna-awale
body:
## What

Settings › Assets › **Update from Steam** always downloaded the whole Wallpaper Engine app (431960) with SteamCMD, even when the installed assets were current.

- **Build ID recorded:** the cache's `.owe-assets-info.json` already stored `steamBuildID` from SteamCMD's app manifest (the same field `Scripts/fetch-we-assets.sh` writes, and CI keys its cache on). When the manifest has none, the build found by the check is recorded instead.
- **Check first:** for a complete Steam copy with a known build, the install runs `login <account>`, `app_info_update 1`, `app_info_print 431960` with the cached login (no password prompt, nothing downloaded), and reads the public branch's `buildid` from the app's KeyValues block (`WallpaperEngineAssetsUpdateCheck`, parsed with the existing `ValveKeyValues`).
- **Up to date:** same build and `shaders`/`effects` present → "Wallpaper Engine assets are up to date (build N)." and no download.
- **Update available:** otherwise downloads as before and stores the new build.
- **Re-download:** new button beside Update from Steam; skips the check.
- **Check fails:** no cached login → the existing "Log in" error; any other failure (offline, no build in the output) → "Couldn't check for a Wallpaper Engine update, so nothing was downloaded: … To download anyway, choose Re-download."
- No stored build, a copy from a folder, or a damaged tree (no `shaders`/`effects`) downloads straight away, as before.
- New strings in `Localizable.xcstrings` with all 15 languages; CHANGELOG entry.

The check uses the user's own SteamCMD login rather than an anonymous one, the same as the download, so a lost session is reported before anything runs.

## Verification

**Untested on a Mac with SteamCMD:** SteamCMD wasn't run. The `app_info_print` output in the tests follows SteamCMD's KeyValues format but isn't a captured transcript.

Unit tests (`WallpaperEngineAssetsUpdateCheckTests`, fake SteamCMD runner): parsing the build ID from `app_info_print` output (the last block wins, braces inside strings, other branches ignored), the lookup outcome (build, no login, error), the skip/update decision, and the service: current build → no `app_update`; newer build → download and new build recorded; Re-download → no check; failed check → nothing downloaded. These pass locally, along with `WallpaperEngineAssetsInstallTests`, `WallpaperEngineAssetsAutoInstallTests`, `LocalizationCatalogTests` and `LocalizationLintTests`. The full suite wasn't run.

To check by hand: install the assets from Steam, press Update from Steam again (it should report up to date), then Re-download (it should download).

author: leotsarev
body:
## Симптом

На `/{projectId}/claims/invite-player` при вводе текста в поле ссылки на игрока браузер шлёт
`GET /webapi/characters/GetCharactersByType?projectId=…&listType=…` на **каждое нажатие клавиши**.

## Причина

`CharacterSelector.OnParametersSetAsync` безусловно звал `client.GetCharacters(ProjectId, ListType)`.
`OnParametersSetAsync` вызывается при каждом выставлении параметров, то есть при каждой перерисовке
родителя. Цепочка: ввод символа → `ValuesChanged` из `JoinUserLinkEditor` → обработчик в
`InvitePlayer` → перерисовка → параметры `SingleCharacterSelector`/`CharacterSelector` выставляются
заново → новый HTTP-запрос. Ни кеша, ни сравнения с предыдущими значениями не было.

## Что изменено

- `CharacterSelector`: запоминаем пару `(ProjectId, ListType)`, для которой список уже загружен, и
  ходим в сеть только когда она изменилась. Загруженное и отображаемое разделены: `ExcludeCharacterIds`
  теперь фильтрует локально по уже загруженным данным, а не участвует в запросе.
- `CharacterGroupSelector` и `FieldSelector` — ровно та же конструкция «запрос в `OnParametersSetAsync`
  без условия», починены тем же способом (ключ загрузки — `(ProjectId, IncludeSpecial, ExcludeGroupId)`
  и `ProjectId` соответственно).
- Остальные соседи (`MasterSelector`, `ClaimSelector`, `SingleCharacterSelector`,
  `SingleCharacterGroupSelector`) грузят данные в `OnInitializedAsync` или не грузят вовсе — не тронуты.

## Чем закрыто от регрессии

Новый проект `JoinRpg.Web.ProjectCommon.Test` (bUnit), `CharacterSelectorTest`:
перерисовка с теми же параметрами — один вызов клиента; смена `ListType` или `ProjectId` — повторный;
смена `ExcludeCharacterIds` меняет отображаемый список **без** запроса. Два из четырёх тестов
проверены как красные до правки.

## Отдельно: гипотеза про `selectpicker('refresh')` — не подтвердилась

Проверялась версия, что `TypedSelector.OnAfterRenderAsync` → `refreshBootstrapSelect` →
`selectpicker('refresh')` при `AllowEmpty="false"` выстреливает `change` и замыкает цикл
перерисовок. По вендоренному `bootstrap-select.js`: `refresh()` вызывает
`checkDisabled/setStyle/render/createLi/setWidth/setSize` и триггерит только собственное
`refreshed.bs.select`. Нативный `change` (на который подписан Blazor `@onchange`) диспатчится
лишь из обработчика клика по опции и из `changeAll()` (`selectAll`/`deselectAll`, здесь не
используется). В `render()` при `AllowEmpty="false"` браузер может молча выбрать первую опцию
(`element.selectedIndex = 0`) — но это присваивание без события, запросов оно не порождает.
Побочный эффект тут другой и к этому PR не относится: видимый выбор может расходиться с
`SelectedValues` на стороне Blazor — на это стоит завести отдельную задачу.
