author: masterzorag
isc
body:
## Pourquoi

Le formulaire « Donner un avis » (bouton 💬) enregistrait les messages dans la base du worker, **sans prévenir personne**. Ni Loïc ni Ivan ne les recevaient. En allant les lire le 28/09, on y a trouvé 15 messages jamais lus, dont une demande de Loïc du 6/09 restée sans suite. Ivan veut que Loïc reçoive chaque retour par email.

## Quoi

- **Pour Loïc** : chaque message envoyé depuis le formulaire lui arrive par email, avec le nom indiqué (ou « anonyme »), la date et l'heure de Genève, et le texte. Rien ne change pour les musiciens qui écrivent.
- **Technique** (`worker/src/index.js`) : après l'enregistrement dans le KV, qui reste la trace de référence, le worker envoie l'email via l'API de Resend.
  - Expéditeur : `bemol@arabesque.app` (variable `FEEDBACK_FROM` de `wrangler.toml`), sur le domaine d'Arabesque, déjà vérifié chez Resend.
  - Destinataires : secret `FEEDBACK_TO`, une ou plusieurs adresses séparées par des virgules. Jamais dans le dépôt, qui est public.
  - Clé d'API : secret `RESEND_API_KEY`.
  - Sans configuration, rien ne part, mais le message reste enregistré. Un échec d'envoi ne renvoie jamais d'erreur au musicien.
- **Pas de panne silencieuse** : le verdict de chaque envoi (envoyé, en échec, non envoyé) est compté dans le KV. Le workflow `Diagnostic notifications` l'affiche dans une nouvelle section, qui dit aussi si les deux secrets sont posés. On en tire la leçon des notifications push, restées cassées trois semaines sans que personne le voie. Les journaux étant publics, une adresse citée dans une erreur de Resend y est masquée.
- **CLAUDE.md** documente ce circuit.

## À faire par Ivan (une fois)

1. **Resend** → API Keys → *Create API key* : nom `bemol-worker`, permission **Sending access**, domaine **arabesque.app**.
2. **Cloudflare** → Workers & Pages → `bemol-calendrier` → Settings → Variables and Secrets. Ajouter en type **Secret**, pas *Text*, qu'un déploiement effacerait :
   - `RESEND_API_KEY` : la clé Resend ;
   - `FEEDBACK_TO` : l'adresse de Loïc, suivie de la tienne séparée par une virgule si tu veux une copie.

L'ordre avec le merge n'a pas d'importance : tant que les secrets manquent, les retours sont simplement comptés comme « non envoyés ».

## Comment vérifier

- Tests du worker (`node worker/test.mjs`) : contenu de l'email, envoi vers toutes les adresses de `FEEDBACK_TO`, refus de Resend gardé avec son code et sa raison, aucun appel sans configuration, réponse toujours positive pour le musicien.
- Nouvelle section du Diagnostic testée en local avec de fausses valeurs : secrets manquants, échec avec une adresse masquée, succès.
- **Après merge et pose des secrets** : envoyer un message de test depuis le bouton 💬 de l'app. Loïc doit recevoir l'email, et le Diagnostic doit afficher « 1 envoyé ».

author: mgcronin
body:
Closes #303

## What

Follow-up to #300 (#298). A citation `documentId` of **valid length** (10 to 64 characters) that is not a real document id passed the schema and pointed at nothing. The typical case is `Loan Terms.md#chunk3`, the label `search_knowledge` printed.

1. **Removes the cause.** `search_knowledge` now prints each hit as `[1] spec.md#chunk0 documentId=<real id> chunk=0 (score: …)`. This is the same `documentId=… chunk=…` form the pre-retrieved context block already uses (`agent-runner.ts`).
2. **Repairs what still arrives.** When the project's documents are loaded, a schema-valid, non-`code-graph:` `documentId` that is not one of them is handled in one of two ways:
   - it is resolved by filename/path when it names exactly one document (`document-id-resolved`);
   - otherwise it is dropped. Only the id is removed if the citation is still a valid code citation (`document-id-dropped`); if not, the whole citation is removed (`citation-dropped`).

   Both the orchestrator's main path and salvage do this, and each repair is recorded in the same `REPAIRED:` note #300 uses.
3. **Stays lazy.** `knownDocumentsForRepair` loads the full document list only when needed: an invalid id (#298), or a valid id that a cheap id-scoped check (`findMany where { projectId, deletedAt: null, id: { in } } select { id }`) did not find. An answer whose cited ids are all real never loads the list. The list is still memoized once per run.
4. **The #1314 gate verdict still equals the orchestrator's.** Only a citation that is valid as it stands is touched. Kept, resolved and dropped all leave a valid answer, and the finding always survives. An invalid citation, such as a valid id with no `chunkIndex`, is left for the schema to reject either way. This is pinned by a new agreement table in `findings-repair.test.ts` and by a gate-vs-pipeline test in `agentic-findings-repair-pipeline.test.ts`.
5. **Lookup failure never drops a real citation.** For valid ids, "not loaded" (`undefined`) is now distinct from "loaded, empty" (`[]`). The orchestrator's loader no longer turns a DB error into `[]`; the repair catches it and treats the list as not loaded. Invalid ids are still dropped on failure, as before.

The persisted `REPAIRED:` note no longer says "over-limit field(s)". An unknown-but-valid id is not over-limit, so that wording would now be false.

## Test changes to existing tests (deliberate)
- `agentic-degradation.test.ts`: "a valid id never loads" now holds only once the id check confirms the id. The test passes `findKnownDocumentIds` and adds a label-as-id resolution case.
- `tests/analysis-orchestrator.test.ts`: the `document.findMany` mock now returns `filename`, which is non-null in `prisma/schema.prisma` and read by the repair. The agentic grounding test now cites a document the project actually has; before, it cited `doc-1234567890` while the project held only `doc-1`, which this change correctly drops.

## Coverage (touched files, scoped vitest v8 run)
| File | Stmts before → after | Branch before → after | Lines before → after |
|---|---|---|---|
| `findings-repair.ts` | 98.98 → 99.27 | 96.05 → 96.29 | 100 → 100 |
| `agentic-degradation.ts` | 87.5 → 86.95 | 81.39 → 81.39 | 93.54 → 93.33 |
| `tools/search-knowledge.ts` | 100 → 100 | 94.44 → 94.44 | 100 → 100 |

The uncovered lines in `agentic-degradation.ts` predate this change (the repair-call abort path). Floor: 80% (CLAUDE.md). CI runs no server-wide coverage gate on these files, so this was measured locally.

## Mutations (each applied, suites run, reverted; all went RED)
| # | Mutation | Red test(s) |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | `needsRepair` ignores unknown valid ids | 11 tests, e.g. "drops an unknown valid-length id…" |
| M2 | every valid id treated as known | "drops an unknown valid-length id…", lazy-load test |
| M3 | `repairFinding` with no list uses `[]` (drops real ids) | "repairFinding (salvage) with no document list leaves a valid-length id alone". This mutation **survived** at first, and the test was added for it |
| M4 | otherwise-invalid citations touched too | verdict-agreement "NO chunkIndex" rows, "an otherwise-invalid citation is not touched" |
| M5 | `code-graph:` ids checked | "leaves known ids and code-graph ids alone…" |
| M6 | id pre-check skipped (always load) | pipeline "nothing to repair loads no documents", lazy tests |
| M7 | never load for valid ids | pipeline "both lookups are scoped…", lazy tests |
| M8 | id-check failure falls through to the list load | "a failing lookup never drops a valid-length id" |
| M9 | load failure returns `[]` | same |
| M10 | id check not scoped by `projectId` | "both lookups are scoped to the run's project" |
| M11 | salvage ignores the id check | salvage lazy-load test |
| M12 | orchestrator main path passes no id check | pipeline lazy + scoping tests |
| M13 | tool omits `documentId` | `searchKnowledgeTool` formatted-results test |

## Gate
- `pnpm lint`: exit 0. `pnpm typecheck`: exit 0.
- Server `vitest run`: 1296 files passed, 4 skipped; 20922 tests passed.
- Changelog: `.changes/unreleased/303-valid-length-document-id.md`; `pnpm changelog:verify` passes.

## Security
- The new query is a parameterized Prisma `in` filter scoped by `projectId` and `deletedAt: null`. A model-written id is only ever a bound value, so an id belonging to another project is never matched and is dropped.
- No new dependencies, no shell, no secrets. The repair records still carry only lengths, never model text.
- Note: the id list is deduplicated but not capped before validation. It is bounded in practice by the model's output cap.

author: bilo-io
body: ## What this does Four styling fixes to the Workflows view's react-flow canvas. 1. **Selected node outline.** A selected node now has a 3px ring in `--primary`. Unselected nodes have a 1px ring, and invalid ones a 2px destructive ring. The old `ring-2 ring-primary` never actually showed on an un-run canvas: Tailwind's ring is a `box-shadow`, and `.activity-glow`'s `idle` rule sets `box-shadow: none` with higher specificity. The ring is now an inset shadow on an overlay span, so it doesn't change the card's size and nothing moves when you select. The span is the card's first child, so the port handles still draw on top of it. 2. **Edge visibility.** `edgeAppearance()` in `edge-style.ts` is now the only place an edge's colour, width, dash, animation and opacity get decided. Every opacity it returns goes through `clampEdgeOpacity`, which keeps it between 0.5 and 0.9. Hover is handled in CSS, but CSS only switches between two custom properties (`--wf-edge-opacity` and `--wf-edge-hover-opacity`). Both values are computed and clamped in the same function, so the clamp stays in one place. Edges used to be drawn in `--border` at 1.5px, which was faint even at full opacity. They're now `--muted-foreground` at 2px (2.5px when selected), with no opacity baked into any colour. A vitest checks every variant: 4 kinds × 3 run states (pending, taken, dead) × running × selected, both at rest and on hover. 3. **Collapsible inspector.** The right panel collapses to zero width. Its collapsed state is stored in ui-store as `workflowInspectorCollapsed`, next to the palette's existing `workflowPaletteCollapsed`. 4. **Toggles in the canvas toolbar.** The palette toggle is now the first control in the canvas toolbar and the inspector toggle is the last. Both use `LuPanelLeft/RightClose|Open` (checked that all four exist), with a tooltip from `IconButton` plus `aria-label` and `aria-expanded`. A collapsed panel is 0px wide and `inert`, with no rail, border or gutter left behind. The palette keeps its existing store flag and collapse logic. Only the toggle moved, and the old 36px rail and header button are gone. ## Decisions (made unattended, recorded here) - **When the inspector opens and closes.** It opens whenever it has something to show: a selected node, or the run history or a run pushed onto the panel stack. Otherwise it collapses: on load, after a click on empty canvas, after Escape, and after deleting the selected node. - **Manual toggle.** A manual collapse or expand stays until the selection (the set of selected ids, order ignored) or the panel entry changes. Re-selecting the same node doesn't count as a change. Multi-select counts as "something selected", so shift-clicking a second node doesn't slam the panel shut. - **Persistence.** The state is persisted because the palette's already is. But the auto rule runs again on mount (in a layout effect, so the first paint already has the right width). That means a persisted value only matters until the first selection change after launch. - **Escape.** It now goes through the shared dismissal stack (`useDismiss`, `inline` layer, passive), replacing the canvas's own `onKeyDown`. That means open menus and popovers take Escape first, and that includes the ones #603's `useDismissable` registers on the same stack, which this branch is rebased onto. It also stands down while focus is in something you type into (a new `useEditableFocus` hook: input, textarea, select, contenteditable), which covers inspector fields, the terminal's xterm textarea and Monaco. Escape in run mode deselects but leaves the run detail panel open. - **Deleting the selected node** now sends an empty selection. Before, a `remove` change never reached `onSelectionChange`. - **Viewport when a panel opens or closes.** The graph stays where it is on screen instead of re-fitting. A re-fit would zoom and pan on every node click, because selecting a node opens the inspector. React Flow's viewport is anchored to the container's left edge, so a right-panel resize needs nothing. For a left-panel resize, a `ResizeObserver` shifts `viewport.x` by however far the container's left edge moved. One exception: if opening the inspector would cover the selected node, the canvas pans just far enough to keep it visible (24px margin). - **Dead edges** now sit at the 50% floor instead of the phase doc's 35%. They still read as dead because they lose their colour and their marching dashes. ## Tests - vitest: `edge-style.test.ts` (clamp across all 48 variants, resting and hovered; no opacity baked into any stroke colour), `use-inspector-collapse.test.tsx` (the auto rule and when a manual toggle stays), `canvas/inspector-escape.test.tsx` (Escape deselects; stands down while an input has focus; an open menu takes it first; deleting the node clears the selection), `workflow-panel-toggles.test.tsx` (toggle placement and ARIA, 0px and `inert`), `use-editable-focus.test.tsx`, and `workflow-node-view.test.tsx` (ring widths and colour). - e2e: one new `workflows.spec.ts` case checks that a node's on-screen x doesn't move while the palette's width animates to 0 and back. It needs a real browser because it depends on layout and `getBoundingClientRect()`, which are all zeros under jsdom. `MAX_DECLARED_E2E` goes from 457 to 458, with that reason recorded. The existing "deselecting every node closes the inspector" case now asserts the collapse instead. - `moon run :typecheck :lint :test` passes. ## Screenshots Before (left) and after (right). Shot by `e2e/adhoc-workflow-canvas-shots.spec.ts`. **Selected node, dark** **Selected node, light** **Edges, dark** **Edges, light** **Both panels open** **Both panels collapsed.** Before, only the palette could collapse, and it left a 36px rail. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

Jules session `13478740581429121516` completed a full Gates 1–9 refactor of `skills/bioinformatics` with no remote branch/PR. Local takeover from `origin/main` applied the Jules patch, then independent Ani hardening (related-skills JSON string shape, drop unsupported `displayName`, portable example paths).

## File Changes

- `setup.md` / `formats.md` / `rnaseq.md` / `tools.md` / `variants.md` → `references/`

- `assets/memory-template.md` — portable example paths

## Semantic-Preservation Inventory

| Original item | Source | Disposition | Destination or replacement | Evidence / rationale |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Core Rules (QC, reference, resources, traps) | `SKILL.md#Core Rules` | move | `references/core-rules.md` | Same operational constraints, progressive disclosure |
| Essential Commands block | `SKILL.md` | remove | covered by `references/tools.md` / pipelines | Duplicate of tools docs |
| Absolute Clawic paths | package-wide | replace | `<state_root>/bioinformatics/` | Gate 3 portability |
| "Do not infer preferences" | `setup.md` | replace | positive Freud wording | Gate 9 white-bear |
| Tool command recipes (bwa/samtools/bcftools/bedtools/fastqc/fastp) | `tools.md` | retain | `references/tools.md` | Unchanged recipes; cross-checked against official docs |

## Research Sources and Knowledge Updates

Verified 2026-09-30 (HTTP 200) against official docs; command recipes retained where consistent:

- **BWA** — `bwa mem` paired-end / RG patterns via https://bio-bwa.sourceforge.net/bwa.shtml
- **samtools** — view/sort/index/flagstat via https://www.htslib.org/doc/samtools.html
- **bcftools** — filter/index via https://samtools.github.io/bcftools/bcftools.html
- **FastQC** — pre-analysis QC via https://www.bioinformatics.babraham.ac.uk/projects/fastqc/

## Best-Practices and Description Optimization

- Imperative, trigger-focused description
- Required reading index for progressive disclosure

**Provisional local score: 88/100** (threshold 80). Jules claimed 95; independent review treats Gate 8 `test-prompts.json` `actual` fields as author-supplied fixtures (structure consistent: id/expected/actual/pass), not live multi-model runs in this takeover environment.

body:
El árbol del rival llegaba a la jugada 8 (16 medias jugadas): el plan no veía sus líneas largas y «Juega contra él» salía siempre de su libro ahí. Ahora:

- El árbol llega a **30 medias jugadas** (`MAX_JUGADAS_ARBOL`), el plan principal a **16** (antes 10) y el libro guarda **1500 posiciones** por color (antes 1000).
- **Sin que explote la memoria**: `armarArbol()` abre todo hasta la media jugada 16, como antes; más allá, una secuencia que vio una sola partida no se abre (el nodo guarda la partida en `solo`) hasta que llega una segunda por el mismo camino. Con 6000 partidas de prueba de 40 medias jugadas: hoy 1,95 s y 107 MB; abriendo todo, 3,74 s y 356 MB; así, 1,94 s y 122 MB.
- Lo que se pierde: dos partidas que llegan a la misma posición profunda por caminos distintos, una por camino, no se juntan. Con dos o más por un camino, la transposición se junta como siempre.
- `lineasDeSuRepertorio()` (explorador de maestros) y el cruce con el alumno siguen con su tope.

Verificador `preparacion-rivales` («El árbol más hondo»): una Española cerrada de 24 medias jugadas 6 veces y una que se aparta: el libro llega a la jugada 11, el plan pasa de la jugada 5, la que se apartó no se abre, con una segunda se abre y se junta por transposición, y una Berlinesa que vio una sola entra entera hasta la media jugada 16. author: maxghenis
body:
## What

`Supervisor._collect` decides whether a finished scenario "timed out", and `_record` steps concurrency down when more than 30% of the last 8 did. It used to match `"Timeout" in text or "timed out" in text` against the worker log, and it read the log only after finding the scenario CSV. Both halves were wrong, in opposite directions:

- **False positives.** Every worker's `import litellm` fetches the remote model-cost map (httpx, 5 s timeout) and on failure logs `LiteLLM: Failed to fetch remote model cost map from <url>: timed out. Falling back to local backup.` (or `Server error '504 Gateway Timeout'`). A completed worker then counted as timed out. Under network pressure that has nothing to do with any provider request, a healthy run throttled to `MIN_WORKERS`.
- **False negatives.** When a request really times out, `run_no_tools_eval` calls `_save_checkpoint(output_path, [], …)`, which deletes the scenario CSV, and then re-raises. `_collect` returned on the missing CSV before reading the log. Timeouts that failed a scenario never counted, so a timeout storm stepped concurrency **up** to `max_workers`.

This PR:

- Reads the log before the CSV check.
- Matches only what a request timeout actually prints (`eval_no_tools.log_shows_request_timeout`, defined beside the code that emits those messages):
  - `litellm.Timeout: `: the start of its `str` and `repr`, so it survives the 60-character `Retry` line. litellm raises it for a client timeout and for a provider's HTTP 408 or 504.
  - `RequestWallTimeoutError`: the class name.
  - The wall-timeout message, now the constant `WALL_TIMEOUT_MESSAGE`. SIGALRM fires inside httpcore's socket read, where the error is re-raised as `httpcore.ReadTimeout` and then `litellm.Timeout`, and only the message survives in the traceback.

## Evidence from real workers

Sixteen real `python -m policybench.cli eval-no-tools` subprocesses were spawned with the supervisor's own `_spawn` against a local mock provider (litellm 1.88.1, no provider API calls). The old `_collect` was wrong on 8 of 16. The new `_collect`, run on the same run directories, is right on all 16:

| case | truth | old | new |
|---|---|---|---|
| cost-map fetch stalled / 504, request OK (2) | no timeout | **timed out** | not |
| request stalled, Responses and chat paths (2) | timeout, CSV deleted | **not** | timed out |
| response trickled past the wall timeout (2) | timeout, CSV deleted | **not** | timed out |
| provider HTTP 504 / 408 → `litellm.Timeout` (2) | timeout, CSV deleted | **not** | timed out |
| stall, then OK on retry (2) | timeout, CSV kept | timed out | timed out |
| clean (2), HTTP 500 (2), HTTP 401, cost-map refused | no timeout | not | not |

The new tests use lines captured from these logs, with the cost-map failures as negative cases. Against the old `_collect`:
- a clean run with cost-map noise drops concurrency from 4 to 1;
- a run where every request times out raises it from 4 to 6.

## Invariants (tested)

Seeded, deterministic generators; Hypothesis is not a dependency here, see below.

- **Exactness (differential):** a log counts as timed out if and only if one of its lines is a labelled request-timeout line (400 random logs built from the labelled real lines).
- **Cost-map noise invariance:** inserting any number of cost-map fetch-failure lines, with random URLs and error strings including `timed out`, `504 Gateway Timeout`, `408 Request Timeout` and `ReadTimeout`, never changes the verdict.
- **Monotonicity:** adding log lines never undoes a timeout.
- **Concurrency bounds:** for random result streams, `MIN_WORKERS <= workers <= max_workers`; a step down only follows a timed-out result in the window; and with no timeouts, workers never decrease.
- **Drift guards:** a real `litellm.Timeout` and a real `RequestWallTimeoutError` (raised by `_run_request_with_wall_timeout`) match in every form the worker prints them: the Retry line, the ERROR line, the traceback, and the httpcore re-raise.

## `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True` for supervised workers: not flipped, queued for Max

Setting it would remove the per-worker network call and the cross-worker pricing nondeterminism. I compared the bundled 1.88.1 map (2,754 entries) with the current remote map (4,410 entries) for every `MODELS` entry, using policybench's own `_reconstruct_token_cost` after its import-time registrations. Only four models differ, and all four are on the published board:

| model | local-only | remote (today, when the fetch succeeds) |
|---|---|---|
| claude-opus-5 | **routing fails** (`BadRequestError: LLM Provider NOT provided`), cost None | anthropic, estimated cost |
| claude-sonnet-5 | **routing fails** (its price override keeps cost unaffected) | anthropic |
| grok-4.5 | cost None | estimated cost |
| grok-4.6 | cost None | estimated cost |

Flipping it as-is would break two models' runs and leave two unpriced. `analysis._sum_or_nan` drops unpriced rows, so a board total would be understated rather than fail. Making it safe means adding list-price overrides and local registrations for claude-opus-5, grok-4.5 and grok-4.6. That changes where published costs come from (a PolicyBench override instead of litellm's estimate), so it is queued as a decision rather than done here.

The same analysis shows the status quo already has this failure mode: any worker whose fetch fails silently falls back to the bundled map, and for these four models it then fails to route or loses its cost rows.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- The wall timeout is retried even though `RequestWallTimeoutError` is in `NON_RETRYABLE_ERRORS`, because it reaches `_should_retry` as `litellm.Timeout` (observed in the trickle cases).
- `uv lock` can no longer re-resolve: `policyengine-us==1.723.0`, pinned by `policyengine[us]==4.16.1`, now returns 404 on PyPI. `uv sync --locked` still installs, but any dependency change fails to lock. That is why the property tests are seeded plain-pytest generators rather than Hypothesis.

## Overlap

PR #181 edits the neighbouring lines of `_collect` (its `provenance_recomputed` read of the same log). Whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

axiom: n/a: infra (supervisor scheduling), no policy change

Evidence: `~/reviews/policybench-timeout-costmap-2026-09-29/` (worker logs, harness, cost-map audit).

## What Problem This Solves

Equivalent operations across core, packages, scripts, and plugins had separate implementations or forwarding functions with no policy of their own. This sweep consolidates those operations at their existing owners.

## User Impact

The refactors preserve accepted values, error text, callback and evaluation order, chunking, persisted state, wire formats, and the public plugin SDK. No intended user-visible behavior change.

## Simplifications

- Reuse canonical map eviction, numeric/string normalization, record/JSON coercion, hashing, and first-wins deduplication; retain different malformed-input and fallback contracts.
- Share literal-schema merging for MCP and provider tools, the parenthesis-aware breakpoint scanner, and the Responses web-search predicate; preserve consumer-specific policies.
- Reuse the Gateway client's WebSocket transport and remove superseded per-consumer worker transforms.
- Reuse installed dependency-name parsing and listener lifecycle helpers.
- Remove the internal frontmatter-list, Anthropic cache-control, CLI drain, decoding, and normalization forwarders while migrating their callers.
- Share approval span selection between Gateway and UI, preserving UI sparse-array materialization and identical rendering.
- Consolidate media-provider lookup, failover-probe status mapping, TTS persona projection and reserved keys under their existing runtime owners.
- Consolidate no-output service writers and equivalent Gateway/CLI response and help construction; preserve service admission and restart ordering.
- Reuse documented SDK text-result construction across tools and channels, preserving compact JSON where required, details references, property order and error flags.
- Consolidate Discord private media-operation forwarding, channel-entry checks and skipped-reply diagnostics; share Slack delivery-hook construction and equivalent MS Teams error responses.
- Share release diagnostic sub-schemas, artifact-validation primitives, argument parsing and phase projection in existing script owners.

Production measurement: **927 net production lines removed**.

Retained differences include promise-observer timing, mutable schema identity, bootstrap/deployment closures, and case-distinct channel-ID normalization. Plugins use existing documented SDK seams; no public SDK export is added. Protected audit, cron, PR-tooling and wrapper-closure paths are unchanged.

## Scope reductions during validation

Overlapping build-fence, channel-status, Diffs-tool, and transport changes were dropped when rebasing onto newer main behavior. The new SQLite scope/cache helper extractions and optional Discord spelling fix were dropped under the maintainer's quick-validation limit. The earlier PR-caused declaration-fixture gap no longer applies because its new build-fence dependency was dropped too.

## Evidence

The maintainer's final shipping policy uses hosted CI on the exact PR head as the test gate.

- Focused retained tests: **111 passed across five files** (provider-tools, command-explainer formatting, tool results, agent display, and approval-card rendering).
- Earlier broader local selections stalled in compiled-worker preparation. They produced no assertion failure. Unvalidated SQLite helper changes and the optional Discord diagnostic change were dropped; the retained passing suites are recorded above.
- Hosted exact-head CI: [run 36665590030](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/36665590030) failed in main-owned preflight before the test/check lanes. Pinned squash auto-merge is enabled; the PR is ready and mergeable.

Optional Blacksmith validation was stopped under the revised maintainer policy. Every confirmed owned lease is stopped, including `tbx_01m3qq95eg6knq0mgzz3hx9d9g`; no fresh remote pass is claimed for this head.

Independent Codex review covered the combined candidate at P2 severity. Two reported findings were rejected against complete source and the actual index: Discord event creation still falls through to the identical `channelId` reader, and both WebSocket consumers were already committed on the shared transport. No accepted actionable findings remained. Subsequent changes kept newer main behavior and removed clone groups rather than adding scope.

Detector discovery on the earlier `0f6e8d0` candidate measured 2,360 to 2,240 duplicated production lines (12-line/80-token scan). That is historical discovery evidence, not a final-head measurement after subsequent overlap removals.

author: tannevaled
body:
The Fugue row added in #130 said **9.6×**. It was measured by running
`bench.js fugue`, then `bench.js yjs`, then the Go benchmark: each arm
its own command, each its own stretch of wall-clock time. The machine was busy,
the text said so, and it excused itself on the reasoning that whatever the
machine was doing landed on all three alike.

**It does not land on all three alike**, and that is worth more than the row it
corrects.

### Corrected

Twenty interleaved rounds with spare cores, median of the per-round ratios:

| Implementation | Replay (median) | × ours | published |
|---|---|---|---|
| **go-crdt/crdt** | **20.9 ms** | 1.0× | 21.6 ms |
| list-positions 2.0.0 (Fugue) | **177.2 ms** | **8.4×** | 9.6× |
| yjs 13.6.33 | 3 170 ms | **152×** | 173× |

Two more runs put Fugue at 8.6× (two arms, 25 rounds) and 8.1× (the block
control, 15 rounds).

### What contention actually does

| | ours | Fugue | Fugue ÷ ours |
|---|---|---|---|
| spare cores | 20.9 ms | 177 ms | **8.4×** |
| twelve busy loops | 42.5 ms (**×2.04**) | 227 ms (×1.28) | **5.4×** |

The penalty falls hardest on the fastest arm and least on the slowest — ours
×2.04, Fugue ×1.28, Yjs ×1.23. **A busy machine flatters whatever you are slower
than**, so a comparison run on a loaded workstation understates whoever is
winning, and the error has a direction rather than being noise.

**Most of that is the length of the timed window, not the language.** A 21 ms
measurement loses a whole scheduling quantum where a 180 ms one absorbs it, and
the fastest implementation necessarily has the shortest window. Timing eight
consecutive replays under one clock — so our sample lasts 168 ms like Fugue's —
takes our inflation from ×2.04 to **×1.42** and the ratio from 5.4× back to 7.6×.
More than half the gap, and not all of it: at equal window length we still lose
somewhat more.

**The minimum estimator recovers some of the rest, and the literature says why it
cannot recover all.** Chen and Revels model the environment as adding delay and
never removing it (*Robust benchmarking in noisy environments*, IEEE HPEC 2016 —
the strategy in Julia's `BenchmarkTools`): if every error term is positive, the
smallest sample carries the least error, which is why they estimate with the
minimum rather than the mean or the median. Here it pulls the contended ratio
from 5.4× back to **7.4×** with no change to how the arms are driven. Their
equation (9) is why it stops there — repetition removes a delay that *sometimes*
fires, not one that fires on every execution, and a starved CPU is the second
kind.

**A load average cannot label a measurement.** It lags about a minute in both
directions: the first round of the contended run read `load1` **10.69**, a value
the uncontended control had spent its whole run inside, while every arm was
already 20–30% slow.

### The same defect, the other way

While checking whether anything else in the document rested on the same
assumption, one thing did — and it fell *our* way. The paragraph under the
throughput table said the current code is "level with diamond-types on this
trace", from our 18.4 ms against the 18.4 ms in that table. **Those two numbers
were taken in different sessions and never met the same machine.**

Paired, 25 interleaved rounds:

| | median | × ours |
|---|---|---|
| **go-crdt/crdt** | 20.9 ms | 1.0× |
| diamond-types 1.0.2 | **18.8 ms** | **0.90×** |

Every round but the first puts the ratio between 0.87 and 1.00; the first is its
native module warming up at 32.5 ms, and neither series drifts. **Diamond-types
is faster by about a tenth**, and saying we were level with it was not true.

### What is added

- **`docs/comparison/paired.js`** — asks each arm for one replay in rotation,
  rotating the order each round, each process staying warm. `--block` is the
  control: the same processes doing the same work as consecutive blocks. On a
  steady machine the two agree to within the spread (8.1× against 8.4×), which is
  the useful thing to know — **a block is not wrong, it is unprotected**, and
  nothing in its output says which of the two it was.
- **`bench.js --serve`** — one replay per line on stdin, one JSON line back.
- **`TestServeTraceReplays`** — our arm, gated on `CRDT_SERVE`. A test rather
  than a program of its own, so the loader and the replay are the ones the
  benchmark and the correctness test already use: a second copy could drift, and
  a comparison whose two sides are timed differently measures the harness.
- **A repeat count on the request line**, which is how one arm's sample is made
  to last as long as another's — with one clock around the repeats rather than
  one per replay, because summing short windows averages a delay, it does not
  remove it.

The throughput table further up predates `paired.js` and was taken as blocks; it
says so now, and has not been re-run.

Verification is unchanged and still outside the clock: every replay, in every
mode, is compared against the trace's recorded `endContent` before any time is
reported.

author: robertdkirkby
body:
Checked Lean 4 / Mathlib formalisations of all ten chapters of Obstfeld and Rogoff (1996), *Foundations of International Macroeconomics*, including the chapter appendices, the Supplements (to Chapters 2, 5 and 8), and the provable exercises.

Each chapter is an independent Lake project with its own `proof-manifest.json`, `scripts/verify.py`, `docs/source-map.md` (book equation/page → Lean name) and `docs/corrections.md` (where the printed text is false or imprecise, or relies on an unstated hypothesis). Shared lemmas are copied, not imported across projects. Every project pins Lean and Mathlib `v4.34.0`.

| Project | Chapter | Theorems |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| IntertemporalTrade | 1. Intertemporal Trade and the Current Account Balance | 272 |
| SmallOpenEconomyDynamics | 2. Dynamics of Small Open Economies (+ Supplements A–C) | 379 |
| LifeCycleFiscalPolicy | 3. The Life Cycle, Tax Policy, and the Current Account | 288 |
| RealExchangeRate | 4. The Real Exchange Rate and the Terms of Trade | 281 |
| InternationalFinancialMarkets | 5. Uncertainty and International Financial Markets (+ Supplement) | 503 |
| CapitalMarketImperfections | 6. Imperfections in International Capital Markets | 738 |
| GlobalGrowth | 7. Global Linkages and Economic Growth | 927 |
| MoneyExchangeRates | 8. Money and Exchange Rates under Flexible Prices (+ Supplement) | 820 |
| NominalRigidities | 9. Nominal Price Rigidities | 567 |
| StickyPriceModels | 10. Sticky-Price Models of Output, the Exchange Rate, and the Current Account | 597 |
| **Total** | | **5,372** |

**Standard.**
- **Infinite horizons are genuine infinite horizons.** Values are `tsum`s and limits. Transversality, no-Ponzi and no-bubble conditions are derived from primitives wherever possible.
- **First-order conditions** are proved both necessary and sufficient.
- **Existence and uniqueness** are proved wherever the book claims them.
- **Uncertainty** lives on finite state spaces, event trees or Markov chains. Where the book uses normals, genuine Gaussians via Mathlib are used where needed.
- **Diagrams and "it can be shown"** are replaced by precise theorems. Log-linearised results are proved as exact derivatives, and often as exact nonlinear statements.

**Verification.** For each project, `python scripts/verify.py` does three things:
1. Builds the library.
2. Freshly recompiles every proof.
3. Audits every named declaration's axioms. Only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound` are allowed, and warnings fail.

All ten projects pass. `.github/workflows/check.yml` runs them as a matrix.

**Selected corrections to the book** (full lists in each `docs/corrections.md`):
- **Ch1:** Ex 8(b) needs an extra hypothesis.
- **Ch2:** (2.65) has an index typo, Ex 1(b) fails for large ξ, and Ex 5's iff needs a no-bubble condition.
- **Ch3:** Ex 2(b) is false, and §3.6 omits a debt threshold.
- **Ch4:** the Balassa–Samuelson signs on pp. 208/212 need non-negative productivity growth, and p. 251 has the right sign but the wrong mechanism.
- **Ch5:**
  - "Efficiency only when S ≤ N+1" (p. 304) is neither necessary nor sufficient.
  - Lucas's welfare cost is exactly exp(ρV/2) − 1.
  - No-arbitrage also needs p ≥ 0.
- **Ch6:**
  - Both incentive constraints bind iff the contract is null (p. 405).
  - Capital inflows can rise with income (p. 412), and the "perverse flow" (p. 415) is impossible.
  - The Table 6.1 Venezuela entry is finite.
  - The concave Laffer curve as drawn is inconsistent.
- **Ch7:**
  - The boundedness condition on p. 440 must be strict.
  - The output figure on p. 506 is about 0.1%, not below 0.04%.
  - The Romer model is missing a finiteness condition and does not jump to its balanced path.
  - The Grossman–Helpman example needs correcting.
- **Ch8:**
  - (77) drops the exchange rate.
  - The μ = 0 attack formula divides by zero.
  - The Appendix 8A budget constraint has a sign error.
  - Transversality rules out deflations iff Σv′(m) = ∞, with verified counterexamples.
  - The Supplement's transversality condition needs a no-Ponzi condition.
- **Ch9:**
  - There are sign errors on p. 632 and in Ex 3(d).
  - Some feedback rules have sunspot equilibria.
  - The half-life on p. 624 is 4.265 years.
- **Ch10:**
  - Country size does enter the current account (p. 688).
  - "χ not too large" has an exact threshold and a counterexample.
  - The small-shock bound is exact: a money ratio of at most √(θ/(θ−1)).

Items not fully formalised are listed in each project's `docs/corrections.md`.

The book is cited by equation and page and is not reproduced; see each project's `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

## Why
- **Client's latest instruction:** "if there is a voicemail it should leave VM after a beep as per VM script". This replaces the earlier "just detect and drop" (#135).
- **CDR call details and Campaigns were slow.** Production HTTP logs show every endpoint slowing at once (up to 49s) for several minutes right after a container took over the worker lease. Backend CPU stayed under 8%, so the time went to the database. At takeover, the voice-catalog rewrite (~1,000 voices) and the historical call-end repair (sequential Vapi lookups) both started immediately, on top of live campaign calls.

## What
- **Voicemail:**
  - Campaign calls send `voicemailMessage` again: Vapi waits for the beep (up to 20s), speaks the campaign's voicemail script, then hangs up. Without a script it hangs up on detection. Detection stays on for every campaign call.
  - The transcript backup check leaves the same script 1.5s after the greeting (time for the beep), then hangs up. It skips if Vapi is already leaving it.
  - AI guidance: stay silent on a voicemail greeting.
- **Startup load:** the voice-catalog sync starts after 5 min and the call-end repair after 2 min, instead of at takeover.
- **Dashboard:** the warmer only reads and fills the process's own cache, so it runs in every container again. A container waiting for the lease was building the dashboard from scratch on the first request after login.
- **CDR detail:** the call row, transcript, recording, summary and segments (looked up by the indexed `call_id`) are now fetched in parallel instead of one after another.

Backend suite: 539 passed. Lint and typecheck are clean.

author: au-re
body:
## Summary

Add bundled extension-authoring guidance for native table/kanban toolbar actions and command-backed parameter choices. Also fix the CI scope gap that let this PR pass its own checks but fail in the merge queue.

## Why

PS-307 needs agent-facing guidance for the APIs introduced in #844. Repository policy requires SDK and extension changes in separate PRs.

The merge queue kept rejecting this PR. `core-extension-catalog.test.ts` in `pstdio-api` installs `pstdio-skills` from source and lists its skill files, so the new reference broke it. Pull request CI never ran that test: `pstdio-api` did not declare the core extensions its tests install, so `lerna --since` treated a `pstdio-skills` change as unrelated to `pstdio-api`. The merge queue runs every test, so the failure only showed up there.

## What

- Add the native-actions skill reference and link it from the authoring skill.
- Document dependent choices, custom values, CLI behavior, and forms requiring fixed options.
- Check that the new reference is included in packaged skills and add a pstdio-skills patch changeset.
- Declare `extension-lab`, `pstdio-planner`, and `pstdio-skills` as `pstdio-api` dev dependencies, record them in the boundary map and the package boundaries reference, and list the new reference in the core catalog test.

## How

Keep one short bundled reference and link central API documentation for full examples. The dependency fix follows the existing `e2e` pattern: declare what the tests install without importing it, so the package graph marks `pstdio-api` as affected when one of those extensions changes. It also keeps Nx from reusing a cached `pstdio-api` test result after an extension changes.

Validation: `lerna ls --since` now lists `pstdio-api` for a skills change; the core catalog and notification tests pass; `verify:boundaries`, `verify:lockfile`, `bun install --frozen-lockfile`, and `format:check` pass. Rebased onto main 520819487.

Change: `people-register-prefill` (archived as `2026-09-29-people-register-prefill`, new spec `openspec/specs/register-prefill/spec.md`).
Rows moved to built: `dm-plate-lookup`, `ppl-brp-lookup` (humaniq matrix).

Base: development 92a16456 (#571 merged in).

## What the user can now do
HR presses Fill from RDW on a company car and gets its make, model, first admission date, catalogue value and fuel type from the RDW vehicle register; HR at an employer that records a legal basis for the BRP presses Fill from BRP on an employee and gets the name, date of birth and address. Only empty fields are filled; every field where the register differs is listed in the answer with both values and kept. Both calls go through integriq (sources in app config `prefill_rdw_source` and `prefill_brp_source`, declared in `lib/Settings/connections.json`); the BSN goes in a POST body with `persistLog: false`, so no CallLog keeps it. Register 0.36.0 (Asset make, model, firstAdmissionDate; hrAdministration brpGrondslag).

## Scenarios and tests
- REQ-RPF-001 "A new lease car is filled from its plate", "A stored catalogue value is not overwritten": `tests/Unit/Service/RegisterPrefillServiceTest.php` against a recorded RDW open data answer for GZS78Z (29 Sep 2026), the filled payload validated against the real Asset schema; `tests/Unit/Controller/RegisterPrefillControllerTest.php`.
- REQ-RPF-002 "A municipality fills a new employee's address", "No basis, no lookup": RegisterPrefillServiceTest (Haal Centraal BRP Personen v2 answer), RegisterPrefillControllerTest (no basis: 403 `no-legal-basis`, nothing sent; the BRP action offered only on a basis).
- Red first: RegisterPrefillServiceTest 7 errors, RegisterPrefillControllerTest 6 errors; green after.

## Design changes (in the archived design.md)
- The integriq source per register is app config; `connections.json` lists the connections for integriq's registry page.
- OpenRegister's save replaces an object, so the controller merges the stored record with the filled fields before saving.
- Fill from BRP is shown through `GET /api/prefill/brp-available` (HR, and the active administration records a basis): the manifest schema has no "not empty" operator.
- A filled field that a change-approval rule covers is refused by the existing guard and the endpoint answers 409 with that rule's message.
- The api-call toast cannot list the differences; they are in the JSON answer.

## Checks (head 5a9c81ef, development merged in)
- `composer check:strict` exit 0 (phpcs, phpmd on a cold pdepend cache, psalm, phpstan, PHPUnit 1984 tests, 1 skipped).
- `npm run lint`, `check:l10n-js`, `check:schema-l10n`, `check:l10n`, `check:manifest`, `check:manifest-parity`, `check:widget-keys`, `check:seed-refs`: exit 0.
- Hydra gates `--scope-to-diff` exit 0; hydra gates at full scope from ConductionNL/.github main (the version CI runs) exit 0, 81 of 81 applicable.
- Inherited, not fixed here: `TravelController::routeDistance` saves three fields of a CommuteArrangement through a full-replace save; the other fields would be nulled. Needs its own PR.

## Live check
1. `occ app:update humaniq` (register 0.36.0).
2. With integriq and a source in `prefill_rdw_source`: open a vehicle asset with only plate GZS78Z, choose Fill from RDW: make, model, first admission date, catalogue value, fuel type are filled; a stored catalogue value stays and is listed as different.
3. Without `brpGrondslag` on the administration the Fill from BRP action is absent and `POST /apps/humaniq/api/prefill/brp` answers 403 `no-legal-basis`.

author: cameronsjo
body:
Closes cameronsjo/cadence-hooks#930
Closes cameronsjo/cadence-hooks#793

This PR is a stack of five branches. Each passed an independent regression verification against its base before merge.

1. **`old-redact-sep29`:**
   - **#930:** guard-body-budget measures `gh api` bodies, using the new `core::gh_bodies::parse_gh_api`.
   - **#793:** warn-going-public reads the `redaction.toml` identity terms through the shared scanner. The env ignore list can't relieve those matches.
   - **Perf:** terms are compiled once per run. The 6,250-segment flood drops from 1.9–3.5 s to 0.1 s. That was already slow on main, from per-segment regex compiles.
   - **Tests:** redact tests are hermetic against a HOME `redaction.toml`.
2. **`identity-titles-api`:**
   - **Wider scan.** The blocking identity tier now scans titles, `--subject`, release notes, gist and repo descriptions, `git commit --file`/`-am` bundles, every `gh api` write field, and `--input` JSON.
   - **Shared gate.** `is_external_post` covers `gh api` writes, graphql mutations, `gh pr merge` and `gh repo create/edit`.
   - **Fail-open fixed.** Caching the term regex also fixes a 3.1 s deadline fail-open that exists on main.
3. **`identity-unescape`:** word-valued texts are also scanned after bash's backslash removal, so `--body zorbl\axcorp` now blocks.
4. **`flagname-locale-quote`:**
   - **Escaped flag names.** Flag names are matched as bash passes them (`--bo\dy`, `-\m`).
   - **Locale quoting.** `walk_words` reads `$"…"` like bash. This was an estate-wide bypass: `git co$""mmit`, `cat $".envrc"` and `gh pr $"create"`.
5. **`ansi-dollar-desync`:**
   - **Phantom quote.** `\$'…'` and `$$'…'` no longer open a phantom ANSI-C quote in any tokenizer, segmenter or scanner. Before, a phantom quote could hide `; cat .env`.
   - **body-budget.** It reads an escaped noun or verb (`gh pr c\omment`).

**Verification.** Each branch was diffed against its base across all Bash guards. Every BLOCK→ALLOW row has a twin that is ALLOW on both binaries, with identical bash argv (checked with a `printf` canary). There are no other relaxations. 200 KB floods run in ≤0.28 s. The merge with main (#1167, #1168) is CHANGELOG-only, and `make ci` exits 0 against a fresh cadence checkout.

**Accepted over-blocks.** A backslash that bash keeps inside an identity term (`'zorbl\axcorp'`) now blocks. warn-overshare also nudges on `gh api` writes, `gh pr merge` and `gh repo create/edit`.

author: ad-repo
body:
## Summary

**Play after stopping a cast was silent.** Starting a cast calls `stopLocalForCasting()`, whose `playerNode.stop()` discards everything scheduled on the node. `stopCastPlayback` only set `state = .stopped`, so Play found `audioFile` still set, skipped the reload, and started an empty node: the clock advanced and the output device ran, but nothing was heard. Stopping a cast now leaves local playback where Stop leaves it: stopped at 0:00 with the file queued again.
- It stops the node before re-queueing. A Stop pressed during the cast has already queued the file, and a second copy would play it twice.
- A track picked during the cast replaces only the selection, never the open file. When the open file is not the current track's, it is dropped, and Play loads the track on screen.

**Cue tracks keep their place.** Stop, Stop Casting and the graph rebuild after an output-device change re-queued a cue track from the start of the shared file (or at its in-track position counted from the file's start). Every local schedule — load, seek, Stop, Stop Casting, graph rebuild — now goes through one helper, `scheduleLocalFile(_:fromTrackPosition:generation:)`, which adds the cue offset itself. None of them can miss it again.

**Play Now while the post-cast graph rebuild is held** (the follow-up CodeRabbit raised on #455). `loadTrack` held the request as `.loadTrack(index:)`, which replays as a load only. If a track was loaded before the cast, the following `play()` replaced that intent with `.play`, so recovery resumed the old track. Play Now is now held as its own `.playNow(PlayNowRequest)` intent and replays through `startPlayNowLocally`, keeping Play Now's rules:
- a bad file is skipped no further than the inserted tracks;
- if none of them opens, they are taken back out and the failure is reported, instead of the next queued track starting.

If the playlist was edited while the request was held, it plays the chosen track as a plain Play. `playbackUsesLocalAudioGraph` is now false for video, which plays in its own window, so neither Play Now nor `playTrack(at:)` holds a video.

**Cleanup.**
- Stop and Stop Casting share `resetStoppedTransportToStart()`.
- `stopCastPlayback` loses its `resumeLocally` parameter; its only caller always passed `false`.
- Position 0 still schedules the whole file. A later start uses a segment whose frame count is now clamped, so seeking in a file over about 24 h no longer traps.

**Quieter logs.** The periodic discovery refresh (`CastManager` refresh/boost/idle lines, Chromecast browser start/ready/cancel/stop) is gated behind `NULLPLAYER_CAST_DISCOVERY_LOG`. It and `NULLPLAYER_UPNP_LOG` now share `EnvGatedLog`.

Docs: `audio-system`, `sonos-casting` (Stop Casting section, logging switches) and `chromecast-casting` skills; CHANGELOG. Tests share a new `TestAudioFile` WAV fixture instead of hand-written copies.

## Verification

- **Live, Sonos (Dining Room), debug build of the final commit:** play a local file → cast → Stop Casting → Play plays, and the reporter hears it. Before the fix, a temporary state dump showed the player "playing" with an advancing sample time and a spectrum level of 0.0.
- **`AudioEngineCastHandoffTests`:**
  - `testPlayAfterCastStopsPlaysTheLocalFile` times out without the fix.
  - `testStopDuringCastThenStopCastingPlaysTheFileOnce` covers the double queue.
  - `testPlayAfterCastPlaysTheTrackPickedDuringTheCast` covers the picked track.
- **`AudioEngineGraphRecoveryTests`:**
  - `testPlayNowHeldForGraphRecoveryPlaysTheRequestedTrack` asserts the `.playNow` hold and that the requested track plays after recovery.
  - `testHeldPlayNowOfAnUnreadableFileTakesItBackOutAfterRecovery` fails when the held request replays through `playTrack(at:)`: it plays the pre-existing queued track, leaves the inserted row in the playlist, and ends with `currentIndex` 2. It passes with the fix.
  - `testReplacementReschedulesCueTrackAtItsOffset` covers the cue offset after a graph rebuild.
- The live window for a held Play Now (session still open after Stop Casting) lasts about 50 ms on Sonos, too short to hit by hand, so the unit tests (real AVAudioEngine, injected rebuild failure) are the evidence for that path.
- `swift test`: 2858 tests, 0 failures.

author: hawkixs
body:
PR 3 of ADR 27 lot C (plan tasks T3.1 to T3.3, plus T3.4 added by the operator): a read-only production fact, `claims_verification_last_night`, that says the next morning whether the nightly claim verification ran and what it wrote. No schema change, no migration, no new index.

## What changes

- **T3.1 — benchmark gate** (`tests/integration/db/bench_claim_nightly.py`, not collected by pytest). Seeds a disposable database at the projected size (10 000 claims over 10 projects, 1 000 000 verdicts, 2 000 `dream_runs` rows), then prints `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` and five warm timings for the run query, `eligible_now` and the nightly selection. It exits 1 if the gate fails.
- **T3.2 — the probe** (`facts/probes/claims_verification_last_night.py`, `read_last_wet_verify_run` in `repositories/pg_claim_nightly.py`). Definition v1, target `production`, TTL 60 s, timeout 3 s, in the briefing, appended last to the catalogue. One REPEATABLE READ read-only snapshot reads:
  - the latest wet `verify` run (`run_date DESC, id ASC`);
  - the `holds`/`falsified`/`unreadable` verdicts that run wrote under its own issuer and key;
  - `eligible_now`, the selection predicate at the transaction clock.

  With no wet run, the fact is unreadable, never zero. A wet run with no claims reads as zeroes.
- **T3.3 — briefing line and docs.** One French line for every status. `partial`, `timeout` and `fail` come first. Any unknown status, including the initial row left by a dead process, renders as `ÉCHEC`. MCP_TOOLS, OPERATIONS and the living-state table of CLAUDE.md name the fact without copying a value.
- **T3.4 — self-referential skip.** The step inserts its own wet row before it verifies anything, so a claim on this new fact would measure the run in progress. The nightly step now skips such claims, as it already skipped `dream_last_night` claims (`skipped_self_referential`). The skip set is now one constant, and a test ties it to the catalogue.

## Deviation from the approved spec (operator decision, 2026-09-30)

The spec §7.2 SQL failed the benchmark gate as written. With a plain `LEFT JOIN knowledge_claim_verdicts v ON v.claim_id = c.id AND ...`, the planner chose a hash join over a **sequential scan of the whole verdict ledger**: about 150 ms on the seed, growing with every verdict ever written. It never probed `uq_knowledge_claim_verdicts_idempotency`.

The shipped query uses `LEFT JOIN LATERAL (... LIMIT 1) v ON true` instead:
- `LIMIT 1` stops the planner from pulling the lateral up, so each claim gets one unique-index probe. The cost is O(claims × log verdicts), as the spec intended.
- `LIMIT 1` drops nothing: `(claim_id, issuer_identity, idempotency_key)` is unique, so each claim matches at most one verdict either way.
- A plain `LATERAL` is pulled up into the same sequential-scan plan.

The bench imports the shipped statement, so the gate cannot drift from production. It also still measures the spec's text as ungated evidence.

## Evidence

Benchmark on PostgreSQL 16.14, on the shipped statement:

| Query | Median of 5 warm | Worst | Seq Scan on verdicts | Unique index | Gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| (1) run query, shipped | 25.5 ms | 29.7 ms | no | yes, 10 000 probes | pass |
| (2) `eligible_now` | 33.3 ms | 33.6 ms | no | n/a | pass |
| (3) selection at cap 200 | 35.7 ms | 36.2 ms | no | n/a | evidence |
| (4) spec text, verbatim | 154.5 ms | 154.9 ms | **yes** | no | evidence (would fail) |

Tests run on the host, at the head of this branch:
- Real PostgreSQL, on disposable databases (`brain_claimfact_*`, `brain_claimnight_*`): 27 passed across `test_claims_verification_fact.py`, `test_claim_nightly_run.py` (now with the self-referential case for both facts, wet and dry) and `test_claim_nightly_selection.py`.
- `pytest tests/unit` with a dummy DSN: 13907 passed, 123 skipped. The skipped count is unchanged from `main`.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `mypy src/` and `scripts/check_module_layering.py` all pass.
- The GitNexus index is stale (it was built at `98d9a53`), so the blast radius was measured by hand. `_catalogue`, `render_fact_line` and the skip set reach two callers: the MCP server's startup composition and the nightly CLI `maintenance/claim_verify.py`.

## Not in this PR

- No release. A merge on `main` is live only after the next immutable release. That release must also drop the retired `brain-v42-model-liveness` unit from the release tooling.
- Dream stays paused, and the verify step stays disabled and dry by default.

body:
## 根因（t449）

负责人令牌的权限判定 `peekBody`（`internal/org/leaders/guard.go`）为了取请求体里的 `org` 先读一遍请求体，但只读前 1MB（`io.LimitReader`）就 `json.Unmarshal`。资料内容是 base64，报告连图片一次加时超过 1MB，被截断成半截 JSON，于是报「请求体不合法：unexpected end of JSON input」。逐个文件加时每次都不到 1MB，所以正常。用户令牌不走这个判定，不受影响。

## 加了什么、删了什么

| | 内容 |
|---|---|
| 改 | `peekBody` 按所有接口里最大的上限（资料上传的 `org.MaxMaterialBody`）读全请求体再放回；超了报「请求体超过上限」，不再截断后当成 JSON 不合法。各接口自己的上限仍由处理函数 `DecodeMax` 卡 |
| 加 | `org.MaxMaterialBody` 常量，资料接口的 `DecodeMax` 和 `peekBody` 共用（原来是写在调用处的表达式） |
| 加 | `material add --help` 的 Detail：传目录时标题是相对路径（`report.md`、`images/arch.png`）；目录要只放这次要加的东西，里面有克隆的仓库等无关内容就先把报告和图片放进单独的目录。没加新参数 |
| 改 | 目录里文件超过 50 个时的报错提示改成「目录里只放这次要加的文件，或分几次加」 |
| 加 | 负责人唤醒说明「收尾」一节加一句：原地干（`--dir`）的报告、调研类交付，收尾时 `material add` 进部门资料。没加检查或自动入库 |
| 加 | 测试：`TestLeaderGuard` 两条（负责人加过 1MB 的资料到本部门放行、到别处拒绝）——修之前两条都得到 `usage`；`TestReadLocalMaterialsDir` 钉住传目录的标题是相对路径、跳过隐藏项 |
| 删 | `io.LimitReader(q.Body, 1<<20)` 这个隐含上限 |

## 端到端验证

隔离实例（临时 `ATRIUM_DATA`、端口 43858，用完 `stop`；只在隔离环境）：

```
$ atrium org add 研究部
已建部门 o1 研究部
# 目录 t446/：report.md、images/arch.png（1.5MB 随机字节）、.git/HEAD
$ atrium material add o1 <t446 目录> --note "t446 调研报告"
已加 m1  细节  images/arch.png  1.4 MB  第 1 版  —— t446 调研报告
已加 m2  细节  report.md  26 字  第 1 版  —— t446 调研报告
$ atrium material add --help
…传目录：加目录里全部文件（跳过点开头的隐藏项），标题是相对这个目录的路径，如 report.md、images/arch.png；…
```

隔离实例里拿不到负责人令牌（只在唤醒时签发），负责人这条路径由 `TestLeaderGuard` 验证：它走真实路由、真实权限判定和真实资料接口，经 HTTP 发 1MB 以上的请求体。

跑过：`go vet ./internal/org/...`、`go build ./...`、`go test ./internal/org/... ./internal/api/`，全部通过。

## 碰到哪些已有能力

- 负责人权限判定（`leaders.guard`）：所有需要读请求体的写接口都经 `peekBody`；原有的 `TestLeaderGuard` 用例全部通过，越权仍然被拒。
- 资料上传（`POST /api/materials`）：上限数值没变，只是抽成常量共用。
- 负责人提示词（`leaders.Prompt`）：收尾编号从 1–3 变成 1–4，`TestPrompt` 已覆盖新句子。

## 发现

- **同名报告会互相覆盖**：资料按「部门 + 标题」认同一份，两次调研都叫 `report.md`、图片都叫 `images/arch.png` 时，后一次会变成前一次的新版本。网页按相对路径找图也会串。这次没改；要避免，可以让交付的报告目录带上任务号（如传 `t446/` 的上一级，标题变成 `t446/report.md`），或者由负责人设计别的办法。挡住的是「自己找事」：产出进了资料却覆盖了旧的。
- **判定层偷偷截断请求体**：`peekBody` 的 1MB 上限和接口自己的上限对不上，截断后报的错看起来像调用方写错了 JSON，查起来容易往错的方向走。以后判定层读请求体都应该按接口上限读，不能自己另设更小的上限。

## Human comments

## What was wrong

Sidebar shortcut collection excluded overflow-menu rows but did not check CSS visibility. Hidden rows consumed numbered shortcuts and remained in previous/next navigation, including hidden windowed placeholders.

## What changed

Section disclosure buttons now stop only Enter/Space activation keys, allowing numbered shortcuts and previous/next navigation while the disclosure remains focused.

Modifier-hint tracking now listens during capture, so collapse controls that stop event propagation no longer hide modifier holds. Revealed hints stay visible through thread jumps until Cmd/Ctrl is released or the window loses focus. Quick shortcut chords still cancel the pending 700 ms hint delay.

Filter sidebar shortcut and navigation candidates with `checkVisibility({ visibilityProperty: true })` before assigning numbers or expanding windowed placeholders. Offscreen windowed rows remain navigable. Add a regression test for invisible rows and placeholders.

A separate test-only commit fixes two packages-CI timing failures: await the invalid-lock watcher warning/delivery instead of assuming filesystem work finishes within 20 ms; give the real-pnpm install integration test a 30-second enclosing deadline matching its existing subprocess deadlines. Assertions and production behavior are unchanged.

## How you verified

- Regression test fails on the original collector and passes after the fix.
- Initial visibility-fix validation, `pnpm exec turbo run test lint typecheck --filter=@bb/app`: 5,233 tests passed, 6 skipped; lint and typecheck passed.
- Chromium verified CSS-hidden groups and visibility-hidden rows are excluded while offscreen placeholders remain navigable; actual app keyboard handlers skipped a hidden fixture group.
- Exact PR head `9734c2dd29f57d71596754b94c5eb27952070266` built with `pnpm start:worktree`; the served index matches the built artifact. [Live seeded QA route](https://ymichael--21512.getbb.app/projects/proj_qa4430/threads/thr_qa4430_parent).
- The original CSS fixture had 20 CSS-hidden mounted rows, 20 CSS-hidden placeholders, and 120 visible threads. Hold Ctrl for 700 ms: visible rows show 1–9. Ctrl+1/2 opens Visible 001/002. Ctrl+Shift+[ wraps from Visible 001 to the offscreen Visible 120; Ctrl+Shift+] returns to Visible 001. Click the blank conversation area after each route settles so input focus does not consume shortcuts.
- Comparing original and fixed collectors on the same browser DOM: 160 versus 120 navigation targets; numbered shortcuts change from hidden rows to visible rows.
- Browser QA is Chromium on macOS; native desktop, Safari, and mobile were not exercised. Screenshots, runnable QA/reset scripts, and provenance are in the BB thread handoff, outside git.

- Modifier follow-up: both regressions fail on the original provider and pass after the fix (58 focused tests passed); lint/typecheck passed. Live Chromium confirms Cmd/Ctrl hints from the focused collapse button and continuous hints across Ctrl+1 → Ctrl+2 → Ctrl+1, clearing on release. Final-head CI is green: 17 checks passed, 3 skipped; PR remains unmerged.
- Focused-toggle regression fails before the repair; all 465 thread-list plugin tests, lint and typecheck pass after it. Live QA clicks expanded/collapsed section and parent toggles, then uses numbered shortcuts and previous/next without refocusing; Enter/Space still activate the toggle.
- Final live-server reconfirmation: same PR head, clean worktree, healthy server/daemon, and served index/JavaScript bytes match the build.

- Repeated QA with normal UI collapse controls and no custom CSS: a Backlog section with two threads, plus a Release checklist parent with two children and two peer threads. Collapsing the section and parent reduced badges from seven to three; numbered jumps and previous/next skipped collapsed rows. Expanding restored ordering; collapse persisted after reload. This smaller fixture is now the live route; the prior CSS fixture is archived. Ordinary collapse unmounts rows, so this is regression coverage alongside the original CSS-defect reproduction.

Fixes #4430

## **User description** GitHub Pages vroeg geen certificaat aan voor boekhoudenvoorniks.nl: de domeincontrole van GitHub bleef een oude proxy-stand zien. De site was daardoor alleen via http bereikbaar, terwijl Mollie en de app https nodig hebben. ## Wat - **`workers/site`:** een Worker met static assets die `site/` serveert op `boekhoudenvoorniks.nl` en `www.boekhoudenvoorniks.nl` (custom domains, certificaat van Cloudflare). - http en www gaan met een 301 naar `https://boekhoudenvoorniks.nl`; - `.html`-adressen worden rechtstreeks geserveerd, zonder doorverwijzing; - `/` wordt `index.html`. - **`.github/workflows/site.yml` vervangt `pages.yml`.** De site wordt bij elke wijziging met wrangler gedeployd. Daarvoor zijn de repository-secrets `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN` en `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID` nodig; zonder die secrets slaat de job over en deploy je met de hand. - **CI:** een dry-run van de site-Worker. - **Opgeruimd:** `site/CNAME` is weg, de privacyverklaring noemt de hosting bij Cloudflare, en het domein is uit de GitHub Pages-instellingen gehaald. ## Al gedeployd en gecontroleerd - https geeft 200, met een geldig certificaat (Google Trust Services) voor beide domeinen. - http en www geven een 301 naar https. - Alle pagina's, het voorbeeldpakket, `llms.txt`, de sitemap en de favicons geven 200. ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Host the website on Cloudflare with HTTPS and canonical redirects ### What Changed - The website is now served through Cloudflare on `boekhoudenvoorniks.nl` and `www.boekhoudenvoorniks.nl` - HTTP requests and `www` URLs permanently redirect to `https://boekhoudenvoorniks.nl` - Directory URLs load their `index.html`, while direct `.html` links remain accessible - Website changes can be deployed automatically through the Cloudflare workflow; deployments are skipped when credentials are unavailable - The privacy notice now identifies Cloudflare as the website host, and GitHub Pages hosting has been removed ### Impact `✅ HTTPS website access` `✅ One canonical website address` `✅ Automatic website publishing`

author: spy4x
body:
## In short

The site now imports five pieces from Anton's `ts-libs` instead of keeping local copies. Pages render the same HTML apart from build hashes. The audit of everything else (kept, or moving to the `preact-*` components in part 2) is on #195: https://github.com/spy4x/antonshubin.com/issues/195#issuecomment-5901209697

## Why it matters

Fewer local copies of generic code, and the tools pages can say the site runs on the libraries. Part 2 (components) waits until the library's theme tokens are more than a day old.

## What I suggest (what this PR replaces)

Five pieces, one row each:

| Local code removed | Library module |
| --- | --- |
| `breadcrumbFromCanonical()` in `lib/head.ts` | `@spy4x/platform/universal/seo` `breadcrumbListJsonLd`, used by `components/SEOHead.tsx` |
| clipboard code in `islands/CopyButton.tsx`, `islands/BlogImageEnhancer.tsx` | `@spy4x/platform/browser/clipboard` `copyToClipboard` |
| retry sleep in `lib/subscribers.ts` | `@spy4x/platform/universal/async` `sleep` |
| hour and week arithmetic in `lib/tools-live.ts`, `islands/GhStars.tsx`, `scripts/weekly-numbers.ts` | `@spy4x/platform/universal/time-constants` |
| `MONTH_YEAR`, `DAY_MONTH_YEAR` in `lib/blog.ts`; unused `prettyDate` in `lib/data.ts` | `@spy4x/time/locale` `monthLabel`, `dayLabel` (new pin `@spy4x/time@1.14.0`) |

Not touched, as briefed: `lib/rate-limit.ts` (#310), `assets/styles.css` tokens, page layout and copy.

Refs #195 (part 2 remains).

## Decisions

- `toJsonLd` stays: `jsonLdText` escapes only `<`. Needs a ts-libs change first; recorded on #195, no library edited.
- The lead form's honeypot stays: the library rejects a whitespace-only value, the site accepts it.
- Intended behaviour changes, all pinned by `test/copy.browser.test.ts`: the /pay copy button says "Copy failed" (for 3 seconds) instead of "Copied!" or nothing when the copy fails, matching the blog code button, and the blog code button gains the textarea fallback.
- `@spy4x/time@1.14.0` was published 2026-09-29T20:20Z, under 24 hours ago, like the four packages already pinned at 1.14.0 on main. This is no risk: main's `deno.lock` already resolved `@spy4x/time@1.14.0` through another package, a frozen `deno install` in `denoland/deno:2.9.0` accepts it, and Woodpecker passed.

## Done when

- [x] Audit table posted on #195.
- [x] The ts-libs rows are replaced, pinned exactly (`deno.json`).
- [x] `deno task check` passes twice (below).
- [x] Browser tests pass unchanged; `test/copy.browser.test.ts` added.

<details><summary>Evidence</summary>

Checks after rebasing onto main 35d1c74: `deno task check` exit 0 and `CI=true DENO_DIR=$(mktemp -d) deno task check` exit 0.

HTML compared against `origin/main` 7fa4639, both built, served on two ports: `/`, `/work`, `/blog`, `/contact-me`, `/blog/building-mcp-servers-with-deno`, `/pay`, `/tools`, `/tools/oko`. Every page differs only in `/assets/*` content hashes (the client entry and the CopyButton, GhStars, BlogImageEnhancer, LeadForm, NavMore, SWUpdater island chunks) and the `__frsh_c` build id. With those replaced, all eight are byte-identical, so the BreadcrumbList JSON-LD and the blog dates did not change.

LCP on `/`, `deno task lcp --ab <main> <this> --n 15`:

| mode | main median | this PR median | range main | range this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| cpu | 176 ms | 184 ms | 164-196 | 164-192 |
| network | 1064 ms | 1060 ms | 1048-1092 | 1044-1092 |

The cpu medians differ by 8 ms with fully overlapping ranges (one sample step is 4 ms); network is 4 ms better.

Mutation: components/SEOHead.tsx `getBreadcrumb(...)` → `.slice(1)` → the BreadcrumbList items are absolute addresses that end on the page's own canonical address → AssertionError: Values are not equal.
Mutation: lib/head.ts `getBreadcrumb` Home `href: "/"` → `"/home"` → the BreadcrumbList items are absolute addresses that end on the page's own canonical address → AssertionError: Values are not equal.
Mutation: islands/BlogImageEnhancer.tsx `copied ? "Copied!" : "Copy failed"` → always "Copied!" → a post's code Copy button reads Copied! on success and Copy failed when nothing could be copied → TimeoutError: page.waitForFunction: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
Mutation: islands/CopyButton.tsx `copyToClipboard(txt)` → `navigator.clipboard.writeText(txt)` only → the /pay copy button still copies through the textarea fallback when the clipboard API rejects → TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
Mutation: lib/blog.ts `dayLabel(iso, "en-GB")` → `"en-US"` → a post date reads as day, month name and year → AssertionError: Values are not equal.
Mutation: lib/blog.ts `monthLabel(..., "en-US")` → `"fr-FR"` → an archived post's note names the month and year it was written → AssertionError: Values are not equal.

Mutation: islands/BlogImageEnhancer.tsx old `try { await navigator.clipboard.writeText(...) } catch` restored → a post's code Copy button reads Copied! when the clipboard API rejects and the textarea fallback works → TimeoutError: page.waitForFunction: Timeout 30000ms exceeded.
Mutation: islands/CopyButton.tsx `failed.value = true` → `false` → the /pay copy button says Copy failed, not Copied!, when nothing could be copied → TimeoutError: locator.waitFor: Timeout 5000ms exceeded.
Mutation: lib/blog.ts `postDate` formats without `timeZone: "UTC"` → a post date does not move to the previous day west of UTC (runs `postDate` in a `deno eval` subprocess with `TZ=America/Los_Angeles`) → AssertionError: Values are not equal.

The earlier "never says Copied!" /pay test was replaced by the "Copy failed" one, and its mutation line went with it.

</details>




**Added by the lead after the second review.** A failed copy on `/pay` read "Copy failed" in Sage, the success colour. It now uses Brick, the error colour (6.27:1 on Paper), with one colour class at a time.

Mutation: islands/CopyButton.tsx, the failed state's `text-brick hover:text-brick` → `text-sage hover:text-sage` → "the /pay copy button says Copy failed, not Copied!, when nothing could be copied" → `AssertionError: Copy failed is not in the error colour`. The same test now selects the named "Copy EVM address" button again.

author: tomerh2001
body:
Next episode could reuse the previous episode’s media source and track indices, producing rejected playback requests that the native pipeline swallowed and retried indefinitely. Keep selection options scoped to their episode, propagate preparation failures, and enforce bounded retries during reconnects.

Report Activity viewers as remote so automatic quality uses measured throughput without the gateway’s 140 Mbps LAN floor. Bound fatal HLS restarts, deliver errors after playback has started, and preserve signed-in clients through temporary initial snapshot failures. Pause/resume from a buffering or lagging viewer now preserves the party’s current position instead of rewinding everyone to a stale frame.

Validation: 576 tests pass, including regressions executed against the pinned native playback and HLS implementations. Native and application builds, type checks, lint, and isolated health/authorization smoke checks pass. The compiled client recovered from two initial snapshot failures without another native launch, advanced to the next episode with its own media source, and paused/resumed successfully. HLS playback retried an injected 503 and continued through a 13-second delayed response without stalling. Browser checks use synthetic Discord RPC and local fixture APIs; real Discord desktop/mobile playback remains a separate verification boundary.

author: huiq777
body:
## 做了什么

以前在桌面上改小伙伴的大小，只能右键进「调整大小」，自定义窗口里拖滑块时小伙伴会一闪一闪。这个 PR 让大小可以直接在小伙伴身上调，并且调整过程稳定、不闪：

- **双指捏合调大小**：鼠标停在小伙伴身上双指捏合，它实时变大变小；按住 ⌃ 滚动鼠标滚轮效果相同。
  - 手指停下约 0.4 秒后自动保存。
  - 经过 100% 时会轻轻吸附，气泡显示「刚刚好」；到上下限时显示「已经最大啦 / 已经最小啦」。
- **自定义面板用同一套机制**：右键「调整大小 → 自定义…」拖动滑块时，实时效果与捏合完全一致。
  - 按「就这么大」保存，数值按输入保存，不做吸附。
  - 按「先这样」或关闭面板，恢复原来的大小和位置。
  - 面板打开时如果开始捏合，面板会关闭，由捏合接手。
- **位置固定**：竖直方向脚底不动；水平方向从离屏幕边更近的一侧往外长，锚点按小伙伴在屏幕上的位置按比例决定。所以缩回去会回到完全相同的位置，在角落里也不会被推开。
  - 靠近屏幕顶部时，最大尺寸受脚底上方空间限制。
  - 右键三档也改用同一规则。
- **拖动时的提示**：前三次拖动时，小伙伴在气泡里说「想换个大小？在我身上双指捏一捏，或者右键我～」，之后不再出现。这时点它，它会照常回应，提示随即消失。

## 为什么会闪，以及怎么解决的

原来的做法是每一帧都改原生窗口的尺寸，一次捏合大约要改 16 次。页面拿到新缩放比例要晚一帧，所以每改一次，小伙伴都会先按旧比例画一帧。

现在的做法：

- 每次调整开始时，把窗口按固定点一次性撑到这次能达到的最大尺寸。
- 过程中只用 CSS 缩放小伙伴本身。
- 结束时把窗口收回到最终尺寸。

每次调整只改两次原生窗口。

排查中还发现：`setBounds` 之后，页面先拿到新尺寸，下一帧才拿到新的 `screenX/screenY`，而位置变化不会触发任何事件。如果按 `screenX` 排版，窗口刚撑大的那一帧会把小伙伴画在旧位置。所以现在的流程是：主进程先把计划的窗口位置交给页面，页面确认后才撑大窗口；页面按计划坐标排版，并以自身宽度判断撑大是否已生效。

## 主要改动

- `desktop/layout.mjs`：
  - 捏合步长换算：单步限幅，因为没焦点时 Chromium 会给出很大的单步值；
  - 100% 吸附；
  - 固定点计算：`resizeAnchor`、`anchoredPetBounds`、`pinchRoom`；
  - `resizedPetBounds` 改用固定点。
- `desktop/resize-hint.mjs`：提示次数的规则和存储，写入 `userData/resize-hint.json`。
- `desktop/main.mjs`：
  - 调整手势的状态和上下限；
  - `pet:resize-begin / expand / commit / cancel`；
  - 自定义面板的预览、保存、取消转交给小伙伴页面处理；
  - 删除原来逐次改窗口的 `previewScale`。
- `desktop/renderer.tsx`：处理捏合和面板请求，按计划坐标排版，显示提示和气泡文字。
- `desktop/preload.cjs`、`desktop/bridge.d.ts`：新增对应接口。
- `package.json`：`build.files` 加入 `desktop/resize-hint.mjs`。

## 测试

- `npm test`：44 个全部通过，其中本 PR 新增 16 个：
  - `pinch-resize.test.mjs`：捏合换算、吸附、上下限、固定点、缩回原位、脚底上方空间；
  - `resize-hint.test.mjs`：提示规则、损坏文件的处理、跨重启保留；
  - `packaging.test.mjs`：主进程加载的每个模块都必须在 `build.files` 里。开发中真的漏过一次，打包后的 App 一启动就报错。
- `tests/pinch-resize.desktop.mjs`：用 Playwright 驱动**打包后的** App，手动运行，命令见 README。测试使用独立的数据目录，并用一只接近 8 MB 上限的照片小伙伴，让保存耗时接近真实情况。覆盖：
  - 每次调整只改两次原生窗口；
  - 捏合、停下、再捏合时，逐帧检查固定点都没有移动；
  - 自定义面板的预览、保存、取消；
  - 捏合时面板正在打开；
  - 捏合后立刻点它，不会被粘在光标上；
  - 真实拖动路径上的提示，以及点它打断提示；
  - 保存失败时恢复原样；
  - 面板预览时从右键选档位：结束后小伙伴仍画在窗口内、可以拖动；
  - 保存进行中开始拖动：等保存落定后再移动，不会跳到撑大窗口的位置；
  - 保存期间继续捏合：第二次捏合从刚保存的大小接着变化，不会突然变回旧大小；
  - 头部在菜单栏下方时：调整结束的每一帧也不跳（macOS 会把窗口压在菜单栏下方）。

  为了稳定复现，测试会临时让保存变慢；另外让小伙伴保持清醒，因为系统空闲 10 分钟后它会睡着，不说话。

  在 macOS 15.6（Apple Silicon）上多次运行通过。另有一次运行在等待保存时超时，之后没能复现。
- 手动验收：在真实触控板上逐轮试用，并按反馈修正了位置、闪烁、提示和面板。

## 需要你注意

- **需要重新打包发布**，用户拿到的安装包才会有这些改动。
- **行为变化**：
  - 右键三档和自定义面板都改为固定点规则。
  - 面板预览期间，`getView().scale` 会保持已保存的大小（小伙伴用 CSS 缩放），直到保存为止。`tests/accessory-size.desktop.mjs` 里对预览期间 `view.scale` 的断言需要相应更新。
- **顺带发现**：Playwright 1.63 的 `waitForFunction` 不会等待返回的 Promise。`accessory-size.desktop.mjs` 里 `getConfig().then(...)` 这类等待其实会立刻通过；本 PR 的新测试改为在测试进程里轮询。
- **与 #1 相互独立**。在 VS Code 等编辑器的终端里用 `npm run desktop` 启动开发版时，需要先去掉 `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`，这个修复在 #1 里。

## 目前的状况和已知限制

- 窗口没有焦点时，第一下捏合收到的事件很粗；单步已限幅，不会跳，只是第一下变化会慢一些。
- 自定义面板预览期间不能拖动小伙伴。
- VoiceOver 会读出捏合过程中的每一个百分比；按住 ⌃ 横向滚动也会触发一次保存。
- 透明窗口空白区域的点击穿透仍在 Roadmap 上，本 PR 未涉及。
- 如有后续修正，会追加到本 PR。

body:
## Summary

Stacked on #185 (CSAT fix) — base it there and merge in order (#185 first, then this).

Reconciling the shipped Attention Centre against the full spec in `PRODUCT-ROADMAP.md` surfaced three drifts, all fixed here:

1. **Missing data source** — the spec lists "cases approaching their escalation deadline" as one of the things that feeds Attention Centre, distinct from a case already overdue by its own `dueDate`. The engine had nothing for a case still on time but about to breach its escalation SLA and get auto-bumped a level by the existing cron. Adds `escalation_deadline_approaching` as a new `AttentionKind`, resolving each business's effective `escalationSlaHours` in bulk (one query per org referenced, not one per case) using the same inheritance rule (`ragThresholds`/`escalationLevels`) already established elsewhere.
2. **Sort order drift** — the spec names "unassigned high-severity cases" as its own priority tier, not just whichever high-severity case happens to be oldest. The sort now breaks ties within a severity band by unassigned-before-assigned, before falling back to age.
3. **Missing visual treatment** — the spec says "Unassigned" should be flagged in red; the frontend rendered it as plain text. Now renders in `var(--red)`, bold.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `npm test` (vitest) — 29/29 passing
- [x] `npm run build` — clean, no errors
- [ ] Manual: reseed, confirm an account with a case near its escalation SLA shows the new item; confirm Unassigned renders red on both `/business/attention-centre` and `/group/attention-centre`.

body:
## O que foi feito
- Painel inicial em `/painel` (OF11, OF12, OF13), seguindo o protótipo da documentação (seção 6.2):
  - cartões de **Saldo atual**, **Entradas do mês** e **Saídas do mês**;
  - barra de **faturamento acumulado no ano** em relação ao limite do MEI, com percentual e margem restante;
  - alerta por faixa (RN02): atenção (80%), crítica (90%) e excedida (100%). Na faixa excedida, mostra o valor excedente e orienta procurar o contador;
  - aviso quando o limite é proporcional aos meses de atividade (RN01).
- O percentual é arredondado para baixo, para 89,99% nunca aparecer como "90%" dentro da faixa de atenção.
- Se o faturamento falhar, a tela não mostra números parciais (caso de uso "Acompanhar faturamento", 4a), exibe um erro amigável e oferece "Tentar novamente". O saldo e o faturamento carregam de forma independente.
- Resposta 401 encerra a sessão e leva de volta ao login.
- Botões "+ Nova receita" e "+ Nova despesa" levam para `/lancamentos` (ajustar quando a rota do formulário do Murilo existir).
- Layout validado em 360 px e em telas largas, sem rolagem horizontal.

## Contrato proposto para o backend (a combinar com Henrique e Hiury)
Os endpoints ainda não existem. Esta é a proposta, e a tela se ajusta se o formato final for diferente:
