author: mtrifilo
body:
## Summary

Three leftovers from the MTC-65 review (PR #53, 2026-09-22), each tracked on MTC-72, plus the runbook.

### 1. Progress rows past the budget: no longer shown, even for a moment

**What was wrong.** `withProgress` in `lib/chat/handler.ts` predicted the read and activity caps from finished calls only. In `ai` 7.0.99 a step's tools run only at `model-call-end`, after every call in the step has arrived. So a step that asked for more than the budget listed every call it made until the refusals came back, and a visitor who stopped the run in that window kept all those rows.

**How the prediction counts now.** Calls still in flight count too, each the way its session counts it:

- **Reads count per call.** The read budget charges a repeat like any other read.
- **Checks count per repository.** The activity session coalesces a repeat into the fetch already running, and spends its call whatever the fetch returns, so a failed fetch counts too.

The prediction lives in a new `fitsPrediction`. `toStep` now only builds the step. The prediction was not left in `toStep`, as the ticket's wording put it, because a held-back call needs its step later.

**Two guards keep the list honest.**

- **A call held back but served anyway gets its row late.** A call the prediction holds back may still be served, because a call ahead of it was refused for its size, which the prediction cannot see. Its row goes up when its success arrives, so no read that happened goes unlisted.
- **No row goes past its kind's cap.** This applies however a row got there. A late success that finds no room waits for the place a withdrawal frees.

**"Distinct in-flight ids" is read per session.** The ticket asked for distinct in-flight ids. Here that means distinct repositories for checks, but calls for reads. Counting reads by distinct document would still show `projects` for a moment in `resume, resume, faq, projects`: the budget charges the repeat, so `projects` is refused on count.

**Stopped-run part bound** (characters of JSON, every field at its cap; `lib/chat/validate.test.ts`):

| | Before | After |
|---|---:|---:|
| Part left by a run stopped mid-step | 62,059 at 34 index entries (the ticket's figure); 65,651 on today's main (36 entries) | **6,374**, pinned; no longer depends on the corpus |
| Part left by a finished run | 6,383 | 6,383 (unchanged, pinned) |
| Longest conversation the input budget accepts, the largest part on every answer | 824,089 on today's main (796,481 on 2026-09-22) | **349,945** (about 1.05 MB at three bytes a character, against Vercel's 4.5 MB) |
| Stopped part, real corpus (three heaviest documents plus three checks) | 10,943 (every entry plus every repository) | 1,773 |

The conversation test now carries the finished part, which is the larger of the two. A new test asserts that the stopped part is no larger than the finished one.

**New tests in `lib/chat/handler.test.ts`.** Each was written first and failed on the base:

- A step of four reads never shows the fourth row in any part.
- A repeated read takes a place in the prediction.
- A read held back behind a too-large document still gets its row, and there are never more than three rows.
- A success that finds no room waits for a withdrawal. This test feeds the stage directly, because the handler cannot produce that ordering.
- A repository whose fetch failed has spent its call, so a later repeat past the cap never reappears.

**Test-only changes.** `readsAll` in the test file now gives each call its own id, as `checksAll` already did. Before, two calls for one document shared an id, so a repeat test would not have tested a repeat. `withProgress` is exported for the stage tests.

### 2. The vendored memos: removed (Matt's call to confirm, below)

`ChainOfThought`, `ChainOfThoughtHeader` and `ChainOfThoughtContent` in `components/ai-elements/chain-of-thought.tsx` are now plain components. The file header says why: their one caller builds fresh elements on every render (the header `icon`, and `children` for the root and the content), so a shallow comparison never matched.

- **Measured under Happy DOM.** A scratch test wrapped the Collapsible parts in render counters, rendered `AssistantProgress`, then re-rendered it 10 times with an identical view and clock. Finished panel: root, trigger and content each rendered 10 of 10 times, with the memos and without them. Running panel (no header): root and content rendered 10 of 10 both ways. Render counts are the same, so nothing re-renders more than before.
- **Not committed.** The measurement test used `mock.module`, which leaks across files in a Bun run, so it was not committed.
- **Formatting.** The registry formatting is kept. The file was not prettier-clean on main either, per PR #53.

### 3. Over-long headings: caught by name

**What was wrong.** `lib/knowledge/knowledge.test.ts` checked the headings `documentHeadings` kept, and the build had already skipped any heading over 120 characters.

**What changed.** Extraction is split in two:

- `sectionTitles` in `lib/knowledge/build.ts` returns every non-empty `##` title of the text the tool hands the model. Fenced code and dropped faq questions are still excluded.
- `documentHeadings` applies the caps on top of that.

The corpus test now checks the caps on `sectionTitles` and fails naming the document and the heading. The thresholds are the ones the old test used: 12 sections, or a heading of 120 characters. A fixture test builds a document with a 123-character heading and shows that the build drops it while the check reports it.

**Comments corrected.**

- The stale `documentHeadings` comment in `build.ts`.
- The matching sentence in `lib/progress-caps.ts`, which said the test could not see such a heading.

**Byte identity.** On today's main (36 documents), the base `build.ts` and the branch's produce byte-identical corpus JSON with `builtAt` blanked (`cmp`). Before the rebase, the same check on 34 documents also matched, apart from the timestamp.

### 4. Runbook

In `docs/career-assistant-operations.md`:

- **"The progress view (MTC-42, MTC-50)":** how calls in flight are counted, the late row, and the new figures. The "each new corpus document adds 43 KB" note is gone, because the corpus no longer grows the part.
- **"Updating the knowledge base":** the heading length and count rule, and what fails when it is broken.
- **The MTC-63 paragraph under "Recent GitHub activity":** now describes the new activity prediction. The Completeness lens flagged it.

### Research

`~/docs/research/INDEX.md` was read on 2026-09-28. No research document bears on this ticket beyond the runbook's progress-view section, because nothing here changes what a visitor reads.

## Verification

Run at head `7707992`, rebased on `origin/main` `2585521`:

- `bun run typecheck`: exit 0.
- `bun run lint`: exit 0.
- `TZ=America/Phoenix bun test`: 1,515 pass, 0 fail (61 files).
- `bun test`: 1,515 pass, 0 fail.
- `bunx prettier --check` on every touched non-Markdown file except the vendored `chain-of-thought.tsx` (registry formatting): clean.
- `bun run knowledge:check`: 101 pass, 0 fail; 36 documents, index about 2,714 tokens. Both are unchanged, since the built corpus is byte-identical to the base's.
- `bun.lock`: untouched.

**Smoke run** (`GCP_PROJECT_ID=matttrifilo-com VERTEX_PROJECT_ID=matttrifilo-com bun run evals:smoke`, ADC, 2026-09-29T00:02Z, 38 s). The eval provider runs the real `createChatHandler`, and its read ledger (`evals/read-ledger.ts`) counts a read as proven only from the final progress part. So a green run shows the parts still parse. Every answer that used a document carried its Sources: trailer, and no test needed a retry.

| Suite | Passed | Total |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| golden | 3 | 3 |
| groundedness | 3 | 3 |
| injection | 3 | 3 |
| refusals | 3 | 3 |
| **total** | **12** | **12** |

**The full suite is the orchestrator's.** This PR changes `lib/chat`, so the full suite runs before merge; that run belongs

## Summary
**Build on modern Java.** `development` didn't compile on JDK 17+, because Lombok 1.16.10 crashes on newer compilers.
- Lombok 1.16.10 → 1.18.48.
- maven-compiler-plugin 3.3 → 3.16.0, compiling with `--release 8`. The WAR still contains Java 8 bytecode and uses only Java 8 APIs, including the JAX-WS classes.
- Surefire 2.19.1 → 3.5.6 and maven-war-plugin 2.6 → 3.5.1, since both old versions fail on current JDKs.
- The WAR is still named `HealthBody-WebClient.war`, now set through `finalName` because `warName` is read-only in war plugin 3.
- Test-only dependencies: Mockito, spring-test (4.3.1, matching Spring), Hamcrest, and the JAX-WS APIs that JDK 11+ no longer ships. None of them go into the WAR.

**Real TestNG tests.** The empty `AppTest` stub is replaced by 45 tests. `testng.xml` now runs every test package. No web service, database or network is needed:
- **All 11 controllers,** through Spring MVC's MockMvc with a mocked SOAP client:
  - pagination and clamping of page numbers
  - admin and user competition lists
  - join and leave flows, including the Google Fit step count
  - competition create and edit, with validation errors
  - profile editing
  - group pages, join and edit
  - the main page's weather parsing
  - the user cabinet
  - login, logout and time-on-app statistics
- **SOAP-response handling:**
  - the XSL transform of the sample `CompetitionsTest.xml` into an HTML table
  - the JSON competitions servlet

**Bug fix found by the tests:** `SOAPHandler.getAllRequestEntityFromWS` always threw `ClassCastException` because it cast a W3C DOM node to a dom4j `Element`. It now uses `getTextContent()`, the line that was left commented out next to it.

**CI:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `mvn verify` on JDK 21 for pull requests and for pushes to `development`. Dependabot now also updates the workflow's actions. The Maven entry stays security-only.

author: clintval
body:
Brings record validation in line with the BED spec.

- A feature may start where it ends (`start == end`), as insertions do. The start and end errors now say what is actually wrong.
- `OverlapDetector` finds a zero-length feature by the bases on either side of it, whether it is stored or used as the query.
- Records refuse an empty `refname`, a `name` outside 1 to 255 characters, and a `score` outside 0 to 1000.
- `Bed12` refuses thick bounds outside the feature (or out of order) and blocks that overlap or are out of order, which also rules out blocks running past the end.


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

* **Bug Fixes**
  * BED interval records now reject empty reference names, negative starts, and end coordinates before start coordinates, while allowing zero-length features.
  * Optional names and scores are checked against BED length and range limits. BED12 records also enforce valid thick-region bounds and ordered, non-overlapping blocks.
  * Zero-length features now overlap features containing either adjacent base, with positions clamped at the start of the reference.

* **Documentation**
  * Quickstart documentation now describes BED validation and zero-length overlap behavior.

author: frankbria
body:
## Summary
Implements #249: Portal signup, login and email verification (BetterAuth).

- **Shared policy in `createAuth()`** (`src/auth/config.ts`), spread over the caller's `emailAndPassword` / `emailVerification` / `rateLimit` so neither portal nor API can relax it:
  - verified email required
  - verification mail on sign-up, **and again on every correct-password sign-in of an unverified account** (BetterAuth only logs a failed send, so this is the recovery path for a lost, expired or failed link)
  - no sign-in on verification (login CSRF)
  - sessions revoked on password reset
  - rate limits in every environment
- **Portal**:
  - `/api/auth/[...all]`, `/signup`, `/login`, `/forgot-password`, `/reset-password`, and a session-gated `/dashboard` with log out
  - imports `../../../src/auth/config` directly (Turbopack workspace root); no workspace package needed
  - `getAuth()` is lazy, so `next build` needs no secrets
- **Mail**: SMTP via nodemailer (`SMTP_URL`, `SMTP_FROM`), pinned to 10.0.10 (the latest release was a day old). The user chose this over a vendor SDK.
- **Security fix found while testing:** before hydration, a native form submit is a GET with the **password in the query string**. Submit buttons now stay disabled until hydration, which also blocks Enter.
- **Infra**: Mailpit in `docker-compose.dev.yml` and as a CI service. CI runs the portal E2E after `next build`.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] BetterAuth email+password with verification email and password reset
- [x] Session cookies secure/httpOnly/sameSite, pinned by a probe test (Secure iff https `baseURL`) and by the E2E (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax)
- [~] Rate-limited auth endpoints. Built-in rules are on (sign-in/up 3 per 10s, reset/verify mail 3 per 60s), and the E2E asserts the 429. **Bypassable until #347**: see Known Limitations.
- [x] E2E test: sign up, verify, log in, log out

## Test Plan
- [x] TDD: the policy probe was red before the implementation; the E2E was red before the pages existed; the no-JS password-leak test was red before the hydration gate.
- [x] Portal E2E (Playwright, production build, real Postgres + Mailpit), 5 tests:
  - sign up → login refused, fresh link mailed → verify (no auto sign-in) → log in → cookie attributes → log out → replayed cookie rejected
  - wrong password
  - forgot/reset password
  - 429 on a sign-in burst
  - no-JS form can't leak a password

  25/25 and 15/15 across repeat runs.
- [x] Root suite: 1607 passed, 1 skipped, 93.9% statements / 84% branches. The one local failure is the known WSL-only #382 test; this branch does not touch that code.
- [x] Diff coverage: the new root code is `src/auth/config.ts`, which runs in spawned Node processes that Jest coverage cannot see. Each policy line is covered by a mutation check instead. Portal code is covered by the E2E.
- [x] Lint, typecheck and prettier are clean at the root and in the portal.
- [x] Internal code review (advisory): M1, S2–S5 and N1 fixed; M3 (docs) done; S1 handled by narrowing the documented claim; M2 deferred (below).
- [x] Cross-family review: **opencode (GLM)**, verdict REQUEST_CHANGES on the XFF bypass (deferred with rationale below). Its auto-sign-in finding was already fixed at HEAD; the CI Playwright pin and the verify-redirect assertion are fixed.
- [x] Mutation check (7d): flipping each of the 5 policy settings fails the probe test.

## Known Limitations / Intentionally Deferred
- **Rate limits are keyed on a client-chosen `X-Forwarded-For`.**
  - BetterAuth trusts a single-value header, and `next start` passes the client's through unchanged. The GLM reviewer showed 8 requests with rotating values never getting a 429.
  - No app-layer fix exists without a proxy: there is no socket IP to fall back to, and disabling IP tracking would put every client in one bucket (3 bad logins would lock everyone out).
  - The fix belongs with the TLS ingress in **#347**: the proxy overwrites the header, `createAuth()` pins `advanced.ipAddress` to match, and a two-hop regression test goes with it. That is filed on #347.
  - The portal is not deployable before then: no image, and `.dockerignore` excludes `apps/`.
- In-memory rate-limit counters: correct for one portal process. `storage: 'database'` is needed once there are several (#316).
- The SMTP connection is not checked at startup; a bad `SMTP_URL` shows only in logs. Mitigation: a user can always get a fresh link by signing in again.
- No unit tests for `components/auth-forms.tsx`; the E2E covers every branch except the 429 message and the generic fallback.

## Implementation Notes
- The E2E global setup runs `src/db/migrate.ts` as a child process, as a deploy does. Playwright's loader cannot link Kysely's ESM `kysely/migration`.
- Each test sends a random `X-Forwarded-For` to get its own rate-limit counter. A counter would reset when Playwright restarts a worker after a failure.
- Local WSL runs spend about 2 minutes up front: a closed 127.0.0.1 port blackholes instead of refusing (the same cause as #382). CI is unaffected.

Closes #249

author: jgueniche
body:
Session 22 of `docs/PLAN-SOCIAL-2026.md` (« Créatrices »), with the plan Jeremy approved as is. ADR-035.

**Stacked on #10**: merge #10 first. GitHub then retargets this PR to `master`.

## What changes
- **Imports tied to their creator**: TikTok/YouTube by the link (or oEmbed `author_url`), Instagram by the typed @ (new « @ de la créatrice » field), a site by its domain.
  - If she withdrew the post or refuses imports: polite refusal with « Voir l'original ».
  - If she published her official version: « Enregistrer la version officielle » (book + À cuisiner) instead of a copy.
  - `saveRecipe` enforces the same gate server-side. The verified creator can always import her own posts.
  - An import's credit can no longer be edited. Forks and vegetarian variants of a withdrawn copy stay private and marked.
- **Credit**: « D'après une vidéo de @X » / « une publication de @X » / « le site X ». @X links to her page, with a verified badge.
  - « Voir l'original » goes through `/api/sortie/[id]`. It counts the click with no member id and keeps the referrer origin. Visitors of public pages are redirected, uncounted.
  - The official player (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube nocookie) loads only on a tap.
- **Creator page** `/createrices/[plateforme]/[pseudo]` (members only, not indexed): totals (posts, saved, cooked), link to her account, her recipes and the public versions crediting her, « C'est moi », « Demander un retrait ».
- **Claims**: a `copine-xxxxxxxx` code in her bio (checked by the team) or on her site's home page (checked by the server).
  - Site approval goes through `approve_site_claim`, which only the service role can execute. Without the key, the claim waits for the team.
  - « Tu es créatrice ? » card in Moi.
- **Her space**: per-post saved · cooked · clicks, never naming a member. Withdraw (copies go private and marked, new imports refused) and restore. Refuse or allow imports. « Publier ma version ».
- **Team queue** `/admin/createrices`: pending claims (validate, or refuse with a reason shown to the requester) and removal requests with the post they concern, even behind a private copy. The moderation page keeps posts and comments.
- **Badge** « Créatrice vérifiée » on her page, her posts and her member profile, linked both ways, only while her Copine profile is public.
- **Privacy**
  - Who claimed a profile is not a readable column: members get `verified`, and `creator_links` reveals the member only for public profiles, herself or the team.
  - The account link is computed in SQL from the platform and the handle, never from the caller.
- **Fix**: imported recipes shared to the community were indexed. `/r/[slug]` of an import is now `noindex` and left out of the sitemap and pre-rendering. `robots.txt` and the middleware now cover `/createrices` and `/notifications`.
- **GDPR**: export (claims, verified profiles, withdrawn posts). Self-service deletion removes claims and unclaims profiles; withdrawals stay, without her name.

## Database
- `202609291500_creators.sql` is additive:
  - creators, claims, withdrawals, anonymous outbound clicks;
  - `recipes.creator_id` / `source_key` (generated) / `withdrawn_at`, with guard triggers (members can't touch creator fields; any new copy of a withdrawn post is marked, even when written straight through the API);
  - reports extended to recipes and creators;
  - backfill of existing imports.
- Replayed on a local Postgres 16 in both orders around `202609291210`. The RLS test script covers backfill, resolution, the hidden column, claims, team decisions, stats, official version, withdraw/restore, the direct-API copy, `mine`, the removal queue, service-role-only site approval and GDPR forget. The S21 RLS script still passes.
- **Already applied in production on 29/09 with Jeremy's approval**: one transaction, recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`, history checked (`…1200` to `…1500`). Prod had no imported recipes yet, so the backfill tied nothing. `master` reads none of the new objects.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test` (150 tests, 13 new), `pnpm build`
- [x] RLS scripts on local Postgres (both orders)
- [x] App on `@supabase/lite` with four test accounts, 45 end-to-end checks:
  - credit and on-tap player, counted redirect, noindex and sitemap;
  - TikTok claim validated by the admin, her space, withdraw then refuse imports, locked copy, polite import refusal, restore;
  - official version published then offered to another member;
  - removal request handled, site check, refusal with reason, badges, export.
  - Two refusal checks first failed on a test click during a refresh; they pass rerun one by one. A final pass after the SQL hardening also passes.
- [ ] Real TikTok/Instagram/YouTube players on a device (no outbound access to the platforms here)

author: codyw912
body:
## Summary

Route Cargo through [mbx](https://mr-boxington.jdx.dev), a shared Cargo build cache, on hosts that provide it. The agent hosts export `MBX_CARGO_SHIM_DIR`; devenv puts its own `cargo` first on `PATH`, so `enterShell` prepends the shim when that variable is set.

The same block unsets `CARGO_TARGET_X86_64_UNKNOWN_LINUX_GNU_LINKER`. devenv's Rust module links through a clang/lld driver by passing `-C linker` to every rustc call, and mbx 1.21 bypasses any call carrying it (`mbx explain --last` reported `unknown-codegen-option`). Linking falls back to the default `cc` only while mbx is active.

On machines without `MBX_CARGO_SHIM_DIR` (contributors, CI, laptops) nothing changes.

## Verification

On agent-workstation with yach's devenv shell (`cargo build --release -p yach`), a second clone at a different path restored 269 of 275 compilations and built in 1m17s instead of 2m58s; the resulting binary runs.

author: itismyfield
body:
## Summary
#5340 stage 2 P5-0: a dormant, typed and host-aware session liveness contract next to the existing `SessionProbe`. Existing callers keep their current behaviour; wiring consumers onto the typed API is P5-C.

- **Moved:** the legacy `SessionProbe` body moves from `provider.rs` into `provider/session_probe.rs` byte for byte. Both ranges hash to md5 `7ecf6eb4…`. `crate::services::provider::SessionProbe` is re-exported, and the seven constructor call sites are unchanged.
- **New typed contract:**
  - `SessionLiveness { Alive, Missing, Unknown, ProbeFailed }` and `SessionObservation`.
  - `legacy_tmux_alive()` returns `Some` only for tmux Alive or Missing.
  - `SessionProbeTarget::from_resolution` and `observe_session_liveness` read through the session-host registry. Herdr and Unknown return Unknown without probing.
  - `SessionProbe::for_target` builds a bool probe only for tmux or process targets. Herdr and Unknown are refused as `Unobservable`, and Qwen accepts only tmux.
  - A Herdr or Unknown result therefore never collapses to a bool `false`.
- **Test override:** `tmux_diagnostics` pane-liveness overrides now live in a `#[cfg(test)]` `session_host::test_support` store keyed by (host kind, name). The legacy test API and guard keep their signatures.
- `provider/output_reader.rs` is untouched. Only legacy or `for_target` bool probes reach the poll loop.

## Evidence
- New tests: 4 pass. The related regression run (provider, tmux_diagnostics, session_host, claude, codex, qwen, restore_inflight, claude_idle_tail, session_backend, session_resume, platform::tmux; PG via throwaway cluster) has 627 pass and 1 known flake. Merge-touched tests pass: 24 after the first main merge and 19 after the second.
- Mutants: 7/7 killed with the expected assertion.
  - Unknown mapped to `Some(false)`, and a tmux ProbeError mapped to Missing.
  - Herdr routed to a tmux target, the override skipped, and Herdr accepted in the common API.
  - The Herdr/Unknown refusal removed, and the Qwen gate removed.
- Production caller 0 for the typed API. The dormant caller guard registers the new file with at most 2 name-only mentions.
- `pr_cap_prod.py`: prod 5 files +341/−148, CAP PASS.
- PREPUSH_OK (`--skip-windows`; CI checks Windows).

## Known flake (please watch CI)
`codex_tui::input::tests::rollout_composer_ready_signal_beats_dead_pane_capture` fails when `services::codex` and `services::claude::` run together in parallel. It failed 9/9 on this head and 4/7 on main `e5867d30b`. It passes alone and in `services::codex_tui` runs. The failing path (`tmux_session_has_live_pane`, global `prompt_ready_notify`, capture) is not changed here, but this PR does move the pane-liveness override store, and the higher reproduction rate on this head is recorded.

Refs #5340

## Summary
Implements automatic step advancement on mobile devices for the onboarding guide. On phones, the guide is simplified to show only the progress bar, and steps advance automatically once their requirements are met, eliminating the need for Back/Next buttons.

## Key Changes
- **Mobile detection**: Added `matchMedia` listener to detect phone breakpoint (≤820px) and set `isMobile` state
- **Auto-advance logic**: Implemented `useEffect` hook that automatically advances to the next step or completes onboarding when `ready` becomes true on mobile
- **UI simplification**: Hidden step list, title, hint text, and action buttons on mobile via CSS (`display: none`)
- **Test coverage**: Added comprehensive test for mobile auto-advance behavior, including step navigation and final completion flow
- **Cleanup**: Added `afterEach` hook in tests to prevent global stubs from leaking between test cases

## Implementation Details
- Used `useCallback` for `handleFinish` to include it in dependency arrays safely
- Used `useRef` to guard against multiple `handleFinish` calls on the final step
- Page reloads on step navigation to keep server as source of truth for onboarding order
- Guarded `matchMedia` usage for SSR and jsdom compatibility
- Mobile layout maintains the eyebrow header and progress bar while removing interactive elements

author: info1837
body:
## Le changement

| | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| **Titre** | Des Fêtes éclatantes, sans monter dans l'échelle | **Votre maison, illuminée par des professionnels.** |
| **Sous-titre** | On s'occupe de tout — résidentiel et commercial | **Conception, installation, entretien et retrait. Un nombre limité de propriétés chaque saison.** |
| **Bouton** | Réserver ma date | idem, avec la **ligne de rareté** dessous |

« Sans monter dans l'échelle » vendait le **confort** : l'argument d'un service qu'on achète pour s'éviter une corvée. Le positionnement change — ce n'est plus une corvée déléguée, c'est un résultat confié à des professionnels.

## La ligne de rareté est vraie, ou absente

Elle disait « les dates de novembre partent en premier » — une affirmation qu'on ne pouvait ni prouver ni démentir. Elle porte maintenant **le chiffre du CRM**, et elle **disparaît** quand le CRM se tait.

Le hero est `"use client"` à cause de son formulaire : il ne peut pas lire le CRM lui-même, et le CORS du CRM refuserait le navigateur de toute façon. La **page** lit, le hero affiche. Vérifié dans les deux états.

## 🚨 Ma passe de vocabulaire avait cassé du français en production

La substitution mécanique de [#28](https://github.com/info1837/lumiere-de-noel-site/pull/28) a remplacé « soumission gratuite. » partout — **y compris à l'intérieur de phrases** où c'était un groupe nominal. Résultat, dans une réponse de FAQ **visible par les clients** :

> « On évalue la faisabilité lors de **la un nombre limité de propriétés chaque saison**. »

Et un commentaire de `Hero.jsx` tordu de la même façon. Les deux sont réparées.

Le harnais balaie maintenant **tout le dépôt** : sa première version listait quatre fichiers choisis à la main, et aucun n'était celui qui contenait le pire cas.

## Mon assertion visait trop large

« plus d'échelle » échouait sur *« On fournit l'échelle, le matériel et la main-d'œuvre »* — une description de service parfaitement légitime. Elle exigeait une purge que personne n'a demandée. Elle porte maintenant sur le **titre** et le **hero**, ce qui était la demande.

## Preuve

| | |
|---|---|

author: samhatoum
body:
Replaces the auto-agent plugin with the iteration-zero foundation for auto-brain: a Node server runtime, packaged as one container image that runs on Cloudflare Containers (the public offering) and on-prem.

The plugin's last state is preserved in `BeOnAuto/auto-agent-backup` at `e50f420`.

## Layout

| Path | Package | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| `apps/server` | `@beonauto/server` | Node HTTP server: `GET /health`, graceful shutdown on SIGTERM |
| `apps/cloudflare` | `@beonauto/cloudflare` | Worker + Durable Object that fronts the server container (`@cloudflare/containers`) |
| `packages/config` | `@beonauto/config` | Reads `HOST`/`PORT` from the environment |

## Toolchain

- **Node 26.10**, running `.ts` directly (native type stripping). No build step for the server or internal packages; workspace packages export `src/index.ts`.
- **TypeScript 7.0.2** for type-checking: strict, plus `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and `erasableSyntaxOnly`.
- **Oxlint 1.86** with type-aware rules. Covers every rule from the old ESLint config, and adds:
  - no `as` assertions or `any`
  - no disable directives
  - no coverage-ignore comments
- **Oxfmt** for formatting.
- **Vitest 5**, with 100% coverage enforced per file. Tests run on Node's native loader, so they execute exactly what production runs. `main.ts` is covered by spawning the real process.
- **Turborepo 2.11** for caching. A transit-node task makes a dependency's source change re-run its dependents' lint, type-check and tests. This is verified by hash comparison.
- **pnpm 12**, with catalogs, a 24-hour minimum release age, `trustPolicy: no-downgrade`, and an explicit `allowBuilds` list.
- **Guardrails:**
  - lefthook runs Oxfmt and Oxlint on staged files, commitlint on commit messages, and the affected gate on push.
  - Commit scopes come from workspace names; `czg` provides the guided prompt (`pnpm commit`).
  - knip and sherif check for unused code and dependency consistency.

## Container

- One Dockerfile, multi-arch (amd64 + arm64). It runs as the non-root `node` user, contains no test files, and is 249 MB.
- Dependencies resolve in a build-platform stage, so the arm64 build needs no emulation.
- It exits 0 on SIGTERM, which is how Cloudflare stops instances.

## CI/CD

- **`ci.yml`** runs on PRs, the merge queue and `main`. It contains:
  - `pnpm check`
  - a container build plus smoke test
  - a commitlint check on the PR title
  - a zizmor audit of the workflow files

  All of these sit behind one required check, `ci-ok`. Every action is pinned by SHA, and the repo now enforces that.
- **`release.yml`**: release-please maintains a release PR using a short-lived BeOnAutoBot token. Merging it tags `vX.Y.Z` and then:
  - publishes the multi-arch image to `ghcr.io/beonauto/auto-brain`, with provenance and an SBOM, and also to Docker Hub once it is configured;
  - copies the amd64 manifest byte for byte into Cloudflare's registry. Cloudflare can't pull from GHCR;
  - deploys the Worker pinned to that digest.

  Both the Docker Hub and the Cloudflare steps stay off until their credentials exist.
- **Renovate** handles dependency updates, grouped for non-major bumps and held back by a one-day minimum release age.

## Verified locally

- `pnpm check`: all 13 tasks green, about 0.5 s cold.
- `docker build` plus a smoke test: health returns 200, the process runs as `node`, and it exits 0 on stop.
- `wrangler deploy --dry-run` builds the Worker bundle and the image.
- zizmor reports no findings.
- Save-to-signal timings:
  - `pnpm dev` reload: 288 ms
  - root Vitest run: 191 ms
  - TypeScript 7 full type-check: 0.6 s

body:
## What this changes

Rebuilds the visitor → trial → paid path around **live research from the database**, not illustrations. Positioning: *one football research terminal for the game, the market, and the players. Research, not picks.* No model or decision rule changed. Full write-up: `docs/funnel-upgrade.md`.

### Landing page (`index.html`, new `/methodology/`)
- Hero: **"Find where the model and the market disagree."** CTAs are "Explore today's board" and "Start free trial". Live stats (games analyzed, research-grade opportunities, props tracked, sportsbook quotes, updated X ago); each one is hidden when the data doesn't have it.
- Live research preview (2–4 RESEARCH/WATCH items), **Today on EdgeDesk** board, game + player-markets workflow, player-prop table (Player · Prop · Market · EdgeDesk · Difference · Best odds · EdgeDesk EV · Status).
- The long explanations (walkthrough, EV demo, model, statuses, uncertainty, record) moved to `/methodology/`.
- **Performance:** two small parallel reads replace ~7 MB of artifact downloads on load: `public_home_board()` (60 s server cache) and `football/home/board.json` (~28 KB). Each read has a 7 s deadline and a 90 s session cache. The record lazy-loads.

### Honesty rules (`lib/edgedesk_home.js`, shared by the page, the first run and the emails)
- **Missing data:** a missing value gets no number. A zero headline is hidden.
- **Staleness is judged at view time:**
  - a game market older than 3 h becomes DATA INCOMPLETE;
  - a prop price older than 30 min drops from RESEARCH to WATCH;
  - a prop price older than 90 min is DATA INCOMPLETE and shows no EV.
- **Headline counts follow those downgrades.** A board with nothing refreshed in 3 h drops "Live" and shows "Last update X ago".
- **NFL consensus markets are labelled** "consensus reference, not a captured quote".
- **The four public words** are RESEARCH, WATCH, PASS and DATA INCOMPLETE. `ed_public_status` (SQL) and `EDHome.publicStatus` (JS) are tested equal over 1,920 combinations.

### Trial first run (`lib/edgedesk_first_run.js`)
- New accounts (under 14 days) see **"Here's what EdgeDesk found today."** It lists:
  - the largest disagreements;
  - research-grade games and props;
  - incomplete games, with reasons;
  - changed markets.
- Five-step progress, plus optional preferences: sports, focus, books, favorite teams.
- The older six-step onboarding modal no longer asks a second time.

### Analytics (`supabase/funnel.sql`, `lib/edgedesk_track.js`, `/admin/funnel/`)
- **Storage:** `user_events` has the requested columns, a per-event dedupe rule and a unique key.
- **Writes:** `ed_track()` is the only client write. It accepts at most 25 events per call and 600 per hour per reader, and takes the user from the token.
- **Server events:** triggers record accounts, trials, payments and cancellations. Day-1/3/7 returns are derived.
- **Privacy:** the client dedupes per page load, batches events, and never sends emails, tokens, query strings or full referrer URLs.
- **Operator dashboard** (`/admin/funnel/`):
  - the twelve requested rates;
  - a three-section funnel with the biggest drop marked;
  - where trials stopped;
  - cohorts (signup week, source, NFL/CFB, stated focus, what they opened).
- **Signup rate** counts only landing visitors linked to an account, so it can't exceed 100%.

### Trial emails (`supabase/lifecycle_email.sql`, `tools/lifecycle/`, `lifecycle-email.yml`)
- Four emails: welcome ("Your EdgeDesk terminal is live"), day 1, day 3 (what's new since the last visit), and a renewal reminder with the exact charge date and the amount on the reader's own Stripe item. A subscriber on the earlier $79.99 price is reminded of $79.99.
- Built from the live board at send time; stale prices are never quoted.
- A copy rule refuses tout wording.
- Sent hourly through Resend with idempotency keys, and a re-run can't double-send.
- One-click opt-out for the tips.
- **Sending is off until an operator switches it on** in `/admin/funnel/`.

### Pricing: follows dsrackler17/EdgeDeskSports#427
Merged with `main`'s **$49.99/month EdgeDesk Full Access** decision, with no founding-rate copy.
- `lib/edgedesk_pricing.js` is `main`'s module. This PR adds only derived helpers there: `money()`, `TRIAL_LABEL`, `FIRST_CHARGE_DAY`, `renewalLine()`, and the `trial` and `day8` placeholders.
- The landing page uses #427's offer: JSON-LD, the plan card with `FEATURES`, the cost FAQ, the v7 renewal terms, and `checkoutLink()` with its stop-before-consent guard.
- **Checkout stays closed until the $49.99 Stripe links are pasted into `lib/edgedesk_pricing.js`**, exactly as #427 intended.

## Bugs found and fixed along the way
- A regex lookbehind would have been a parse error on iOS Safari < 16.4 and taken down the whole live board.
- `pricing_view` could never fire on phones: the 30% threshold is unreachable for a section taller than the screen. `EDTrack.seen` had the same problem.
- The onboarding modal re-opened after the reader had already saved or skipped preferences inline.

## Deploying
1. Apply SQL in this order: `supabase/funnel.sql` → `supabase/home_board.sql` → `supabase/lifecycle_email.sql`. Each runs twice safely, and every report row should say `ok`.
2. Merge. The page and the terminal degrade honestly if step 1 hasn't run yet.
3. Checkout: create the $49.99 Price and Payment Links in Stripe, paste them into `lib/edgedesk_pricing.js`, then run `node tools/billing/verify_stripe_offer.js`. This step is from #427.
4. Emails: check `lifecycle_settings` (sender, reply-to, address). Run `lifecycle-email.yml` once with `dry_run`, then switch sending on in `/admin/funnel/`. The `SB_SERVICE_ROLE` and `RESEND_API_KEY` secrets already exist.

## Tests (on the tree merged with `main`)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `tools/home/home.test.js` | 77/77 |
| `tools/home/home_sql.test.js` (real PostgreSQL) | 37/37 |
| `tools/funnel/funnel_sql.test.js` (real PostgreSQL) | 104/104 |
| `tools/lifecycle/lifecycle.test.js` | 65/65 |
| `tools/home/landing.e2e.js` (375/390/430/768/1280; live, stale, down) | 119/119 |
| `tools/funnel/first_run.e2e.js` | 47/47 |
| `tools/funnel/admin_funnel.e2e.js` | 31/31 |
| #427's `tools/billing/checkout_flow.e2e.js` against the new landing page | 38/38 |
| #427's subscriber lifecycle, comp entitlement, verify-stripe-offer suites | pass |
| Every other offline `*.test.js` in `tools/` (183) | pass |
| Existing browser suites: personal_ui, props_ui | pass |

New CI: `.github/workflows/funnel-tests.yml`. The pre-existing `tools/bettor/decision_ui.e2e.js` failures (3) also occur on `main` and are unrelated.

## Not done
- Checkout is closed until the $49.99 Stripe links exist (from #427), so the funnel's checkout and trial steps stay at zero until then.
- Landing and terminal events start when `funnel.sql` is applied. Accounts, trials and payments are backfilled.
- There is no stored NFL game-line EV, so game EV is shown for college games only.
- Real sign-in, Stripe checkout and email delivery against production were not exercised from the sandbox.

author: felipeorellanacaro
body:
Sale de revisar Mxtsi7/integra-lll#33. Es deuda mía del #29 y la arreglo acá para que la paginación de Victor pueda entrar sin romper el panel.

## El problema

`getSuscripciones()` pedía una página y devolvía `results` sin mirar si había más:

```ts
const pagina = await pedir<Paginado<SuscripcionDeApi>>('/suscripciones/');
return pagina.results.map(desdeLaApi);
```

Con el `PAGE_SIZE: 50` actual, un hogar con 51 suscripciones ve **50**, y el gasto proyectado suma **$50.000 en vez de $51.000**. Sin ningún aviso: el número simplemente sale más chico.

Está latente hoy porque nadie tiene 51 servicios. Pero el #33 propone bajar el tope a 10, y ahí lo pega cualquier hogar con 11 — lo probé y el panel mostraba $10.000 de $12.000 reales.

## Lo que encontré al arreglarlo

Mi primera idea fue seguir el `next` que manda la API. **No sirve.** Esto es lo que le llega al navegador:

```
GET http://localhost:8000/api/suscripciones/

  count: 51
  results: 50
  next: http://subscriptions:8002/api/suscripciones/?page=2
```

Ese `http://subscriptions:8002` es el **hostname interno de Docker**: el navegador no puede alcanzarlo. Django arma esa URL con la petición que le llegó *del gateway*, no con la que hizo el navegador.

Así que la solución construye la URL de cada página y usa `next` solo como señal de que queda otra:

```ts
for (let pagina = 1; pagina <= MAX_PAGINAS; pagina += 1) {
  const respuesta = await pedir<Paginado<SuscripcionDeApi>>(`/suscripciones/?page=${pagina}`);
  todas.push(...respuesta.results);
  if (!respuesta.next) break;
}
```

El tope de 20 páginas está para que un `next` mal formado no deje el navegador girando para siempre. Con el PAGE_SIZE actual son 1.000 suscripciones, muy por encima de lo que un hogar puede tener.

## Probado

Cargué 51 suscripciones de $1.000 y abrí el Home:

```
Total mensual   $51.000 /mes
Paginación      1–5 de 51
```

Antes habría dicho $50.000 y «1–5 de 50».

Y en la pestaña de red se ve el recorrido, sin tocar nunca el host interno:

```
GET /api/suscripciones/?page=1 → 200
GET /api/suscripciones/?page=2 → 200
```

3 pruebas nuevas; **dos fallan si se quita el recorrido**:

```
→ expected [ 'A', 'B' ] to deeply equal [ 'A', 'B', 'C' ]
→ expected 'http://api.test/api/suscripciones/' to contain '/suscripciones/?page=1'
```

Una de ellas verifica explícitamente que **nunca** se le pegue a `subscriptions:8002`.

Typecheck limpio, **18 pruebas**, `✓ built in 11.73s`.

## Aparte: el `next` filtra la topología interna

Que `next` y `previous` salgan como `http://subscriptions:8002/...` tiene dos costos más allá de este arreglo:

- **son inútiles para cualquier cliente**, no solo para el nuestro;
- **le cuentan al navegador el nombre y el puerto interno del servicio.**

Se arregla en el gateway, reenviando `X-Forwarded-Host` y `X-Forwarded-Proto` y activando `USE_X_FORWARDED_HOST` en los servicios. No lo hago acá porque toca infraestructura compartida y prefiero conversarlo antes — lo llevo a la reunión.

author: mcm
body: ## Summary Loading a `.litematic` file whose region has a negative `Size` failed with "Failed to project Litematic schematic: Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView". Litematica writes a negative size on any axis where the selection's second corner is on the negative side of the first. The packed `BlockStates` are still laid out by absolute dimensions. `LitematicRegion.getBlockMatrix` looped over the absolute dimensions but computed the storage index from the signed ones. For a region sized `{x: -90, y: 79, z: -90}`, that pushed the index past the end of the `LongArray`. The index now uses absolute dimensions. This only fixes reading. Regions are still placed at the origin whatever their `Position` is, so multi-region files overlap. That's tracked separately in SCHEM-52. ## Test plan - [x] New `src/lib/schemlib/__tests__/litematic.test.ts` builds regions in code with negative sizes on different axes and checks they read the same blocks as the positive-size region. Without the fix it fails with the original `RangeError`. - [x] The user schematic that reported the error now parses (435 palette entries) and converts to Sponge v3 and Litematic, and both outputs parse again. It isn't committed as a fixture. - [x] `pnpm test` (551 passed, 16 skipped), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, prettier check on `src/lib/schemlib` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes loading `.litematic` regions with negative sizes, which previously threw "Offset is outside the bounds of the DataView". - Computes the packed block-state index from absolute dimensions; Litematica writes signed sizes when the selection's second corner is negative relative to the first, but block storage is laid out by absolute dimensions. - Adds tests covering negative sizes on different axes and a test pinning block order to a hard-coded layout, including values straddling long boundaries. - Regions are still placed at the origin regardless of their `Position`; multi-region files overlap (tracked in SCHEM-52). Written for commit eaca5e7d35441b4e0fef99b2b7d2603bdbadcc96. Summary will update on new commits.

author: closer-claudio
body:
Part of converging xz on limen's lint-go baseline, one linter per PR. The baseline is a proposal; where a rule is wrong for this fork, we change the baseline or the overlay, not work around it.

## intrange: 7 findings (4 production, 3 test), all fixed

- **Five counted loops now range over their bound:** the hash roller's warm-up, the properties code sweep in a test, and the three tree-codec bit loops.
- **Two benchmark `b.N` loops now use `b.Loop()`,** as the repo's other benchmarks already do. That also keeps the temporary file's setup out of the timing.

Two of the tree-codec loops are decoders on the path PERF.md measures, so I checked instead of assuming:
- **Generated code:** the loop bodies are identical. The range form reads `tc.bits` once before the loop, where the old loop reloaded it from memory on every iteration.
- **BenchmarkReader:** a sequential run showed +1.5% on Reader, but also +1.2% on Writer, which these loops don't touch, so that was drift. An interleaved run, 10 each with both binaries built up front, shows no significant difference (p=0.089).

## Assessment

intrange is useful and cheap: all mechanical, and the result reads better. The only care it needs is on measured hot paths, and there the change is neutral.

`just lint` and `just test` are green locally, except the links lane, which my sandbox cannot reach.

The bean also records what was measured on main today: which downstream tools fail invisibly, and which staleness machinery exists but doesn't cover them.

body:
## Descrição

Cria a página `/cart` (FE-US021-2, RN-46) e corrige o `cartService`, que tratava a resposta do back num formato que ele não manda. Sem essa correção, com `VITE_USE_MOCKS=false` o carrinho ficava sempre em erro e peça vendida aparecia como disponível.

## O que foi feito

**`cartService`: o contrato real** (`app/schemas/cart_schema.py`, `cart_routes.py`, `develop` de 29/09)
- As três rotas devolvem `Page[CartStoreResponse]`: o service passa a ler `data.items` do envelope `{ items, page, page_size, total }` em vez de fazer `.map` num objeto.
- Item plano (`product_id`, `name`, `price`, `cover_image_url`, `status`, `available`), com a loja só no grupo; `available: false` vira `unavailable: true`.
- `addedAt` virou opcional no tipo, porque o back não manda `added_at`. `pix_key` segue opcional (ver Observações).
- Testes com o envelope de verdade: as três chamadas, peça vendida marcada como indisponível, `pix_key` presente/ausente.

**Página `/cart`** (deixa de ser o último `RoutePlaceholder` de rota)
- Recarrega o carrinho ao abrir, porque a disponibilidade muda sem o comprador fazer nada.
- **Um carrinho por loja:** seção por brechó com `CartItemRow`s e subtotal próprio, sem total somando lojas (RN-18/19).
- Remover chama `useCart().remove`, e a lista e o subtotal atualizam; falha vira `Toast` de erro.
- **Peça vendida:** `Toast` "X foi vendida e saiu do seu carrinho", a peça é removida e fica visível marcada como "Vendido" até sair da tela; o subtotal não conta com ela. O aviso não repete quando o carrinho recarrega.
- `EmptyState` "Seu carrinho está vazio" com "Explorar o catálogo"; skeleton no carregamento; `ErrorState` com retry.
- "Finalizar compra" desabilitado, com a nota "Em breve" (checkout é S3).
- A rota já era protegida por `RequireAuth` (#205); o teste de rotas foi ajustado para o título real.

Inclui o mesmo commit `chore(deps)` do #288 (`undici` 7.30.0, só `package-lock.json`).

## Tipo de mudança

- [x] Feature
- [ ] Bugfix
- [ ] Hotfix
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Chore

## Uso de IA

Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) conferiu o contrato no back-end, corrigiu o `cartService`, implementou a página, escreveu os testes e redigiu este PR, a pedido de um membro do time.

## Checklist

- [x] Rodei `npm run lint` localmente e não há erros
- [x] Rodei `npm run format:check` localmente e não há problemas de formatação
- [x] Rodei `npm run build` localmente e o projeto builda sem erros
- [x] Rodei `npm run test` localmente (quando aplicável)
- [ ] Adicionei prints caso envolva mudança visual

## Prints

Pendente.

## Observações

Closes #226

**Decisão sobre o `pix_key`:** a tela desta tarefa não mostra a chave Pix, porque o pagamento é S3. O subtotal por loja fecha sem ela. O service lê `store.pix_key` do grupo quando ele vier, e isso foi pedido ao back na issue. A alternativa (buscar `GET /stores/{id}` por grupo) foi descartada porque o retrato público da loja não deveria expor a chave.

body:
Phase 0 of `buck2 repl`: the frozen interfaces and a working end-to-end
stub.

- daemon.proto: `ReplRequest`/`ReplMessage`/`ReplResponse` and their
  messages, `StreamingRequest.repl` plus `build_opts` (read from the
  context message), `PartialResult.repl_message`,
  `CommandResult.repl_response` and `rpc Repl`. data.proto:
  `ReplCommandStart`/`ReplCommandEnd` (id 44).
- buck2_cli_proto: conversions; `HasBuildOptions for StreamingRequest`
  returns the context message's build options.
- buck2_client_ctx: `FlushingBuckdClient::repl`, which also sends the
  session's build options; `StreamingCommand::handles_sigint`.
- buck2_server/buck2_server_ctx: `Repl` RPC dispatched through
  `BxlServerCommands::repl`, with `ReplCommandOptions` (does not hold off
  background cleanup).
- buck2_bxl: `repl` module stub that answers `Open` with `Ready`, echoes
  each `Eval` input as a string value and answers `Complete` with no
  candidates.
- New `buck2_repl_syntax` crate (pure, depends only on shlex): tolerant
  Starlark lexer, input completeness (the line editor's validator), the
  line-by-line chunker for piped input, dedent/precheck/string-literal/
  capping helpers, and the full meta-command table and parser.

author: creativalcance
body:
The previous matcher rewarded missing information, matched misleading substrings and treated ambitions/AI keywords as skill evidence. It omitted manually declared profile skills, while an independent frontend family classifier could hide server results.

This change extracts a versioned evidence-v2 engine, includes declared skills, compares complete phrases/explicit aliases, excludes unknown criteria from scoring and reports coverage separately. Automatic recommendation requires sufficient information, mandatory skill evidence and required language presence; uncertain or transferable cases remain for human review. Displays use an index out of 100 and explain that it is not hiring probability. Existing weights/thresholds are provisional.

Validation: 15 matching tests (including 512 optional-field combinations), 12 security tests, TypeScript, targeted lint and synthetic production build passed. Full lint remains 32 existing errors and 38 warnings. The evaluation CLI reports aggregate precision/recall only when independent human labels are supplied.

A subsequent read-only shadow pilot evaluated 60 current pairs from 5 candidates and 12 active vacancies; 50 had stored baseline scores. Results: 0 automatic recommendations, 9 possible, 24 low compatibility/insufficient evidence and 27 not relevant. Four stored recommendations moved to possible because mandatory evidence was unmatched. Review found vocabulary ambiguities, a misspelt requirement and unconfirmed budgeting evidence. These are potential missed suitable matches, not established false negatives. No recruiter labels exist, so accuracy cannot be measured. docs/matching-shadow-pilot.md contains aggregate results; scripts/shadow-matching.ts reproduces diagnostics without record writes or external AI calls. No private snapshot is committed.

Integration into main authorized by the platform owner on 2026-09-30. No production recalculation or new database migration is included. Recruiters still need to assess relevant pairs independently, separate truly mandatory/preferred requirements and validate aliases on a separate sample. Regulated qualifications, language fluency, remote geographic restrictions and salary units still need structured validation. Existing stored matches remain unchanged until explicit recalculation after adoption.

author: pondorasti
body:
> **Stacked on #128.** #128 fixes the Linux Service e2e failures (systemd's start limit, caused by #124 and unrelated to this change), and its commit is the first one on this branch. Merge #128 first; this PR then contains only its own commit.
>
> **Rebased onto #123.** The overlapping-runs scenario now uses #123's `Start-Watcher`/`Stop-Watcher` and its process-tree checks. `Assert-NoWindow` includes `Assert-WatcherSawRun`, and a new check requires that the watcher saw all three `wscript` launchers as roots. This version of the scenario hasn't run on Windows yet; CI's Windows Service jobs are its first run. The VM results below are from before #123.

## Problem

In the 0.7.0 Windows battle test (scenario 5f), three concurrent runs of the scheduled-task wrapper gave one sync, which is correct because the lock works. The other two exited 0 without running or logging anything.

The cause: `cmd` opens a `>>` target without write sharing and holds it for the whole command, so the running wrapper holds `service.log` while it syncs. When an overlapping wrapper tried `>> "%TOKENMAXXING_LOG%"`, it hit a sharing violation. cmd then skips the command without changing `ERRORLEVEL`, so neither the header nor the runner ran and the wrapper exited 0.

Separately, a scheduled run that found the lock held (`service run --scheduled`) printed nothing at all, so even with a writable log it left no trace.

## Fix

- **Windows wrapper (template 8).** The body runs as a `:sync` subroutine under a single redirect, `(call :sync >> "%TOKENMAXXING_LOG%" 2>&1) 2>nul`. `:sync` sets a marker as its first step, so the wrapper can tell a run that never started from one that failed.
  - A run whose log is held moves on to `service-overlap-1.log`, then `-2` … `-4`.
  - If all of them are held, it runs with its console.
  - The runner's exit code still passes through.
  - The redirect-in-subroutine form was chosen over the other options (the CLI opening the log itself, or the launcher checking the lock) because it needs no new CLI flag, so a new wrapper can't break against an older runner. The launcher is unchanged, so the hidden-window guarantee is unchanged.
- **Rotation** is now a `:rotate_log` subroutine that works on whichever log the run opens. It moves the log aside first. Before, a held oversized log shifted `.1→.2→.3` and deleted `.3`, then failed the final move, losing a generation on every overlapping run.
- **CLI.** A scheduled locked skip now logs a `service_run` line on every platform:
  `{"event":"service_run","message":"Sync skipped; service run is already in progress (since …, pid …)","reason":"locked","status":"skipped",…}`
- **Template bump 7 → 8**, so installed services rewrite the wrapper once through the existing reload-required repair. On macOS/Linux the POSIX wrapper bytes don't change, so only `service.json` is rewritten.

## Can Task Scheduler overlap runs itself?

No. I measured this on the Windows 11 VM with a probe task that uses the same XML settings, and documented it in `service.ts`:

- `MultipleInstancesPolicy` `IgnoreNew` ignores a trigger or `schtasks /Run` while an instance is running ("INFO: … is currently running").
- Re-registering the task with `/Create /F` (what a repair does) while it runs keeps tracking the running instance. The next `/Run` is still ignored.
- The instance Task Scheduler tracks is `wscript.exe`. `schtasks /End`, End in Task Scheduler, and presumably `StopIfGoingOnBatteries` stop only the launcher. The `cmd` and runner keep going, the task reads Ready, and the next `/Run` starts a second instance that overlaps them.

So overlaps come only from ending the task mid-run, or from running the wrapper or launcher by hand, which is what 5f did.

## Tests

- **Unit** (`service.test.ts`): the rendered wrapper's fallback chain, the marker ordering, the rotation subroutine, and that no label is fallen into.
- **`argv.test.ts`**: a scheduled run against a held lock prints the skipped/locked line and writes no state.
- **Windows e2e** (`service-e2e.ps1`): a new `overlapping runs` scenario, with a README row.
  1. Another process holds an oversized `service.log`. The run logs to `service-overlap-1.log`, still syncs, and the held log and its rotations are untouched.
  2. Three runs start at once: the task, a second `schtasks /Run` while it runs, and two launcher runs by hand. The second `/Run` starts nothing; there are 3 log entries, exactly 1 sync and 2 locked skips; nothing opens a window; the lock is released; `doctor` exits 0 with no WARN or FAIL.
  - `Invoke-TaskRun`'s watcher and log-reading code moved into small helpers so the new scenario can reuse them.
- **Fixtures.** `bun run check` and `bun run test` pass. Template-version literals in the tests and the `current/usage.checkIn.json` fixture moved 7 → 8, as in #115.

## Verified on the local Windows 11 ARM VM

- Ran `service-e2e.ps1` twice against a windows-arm64 build of this branch and the API sandbox on the host (`10.0.2.2:8811`), in a limited interactive session.
- The second run was on the final wrapper. It passed 161 of 162 checks: core, overlapping runs, and all four path cases (`Zoë O'Neil (Work) & Co 100%` included). The one failure is "legacy release available", because I didn't stage the legacy release; CI covers that scenario.
- A session-wide window watcher saw no new windows and no focus changes across the whole run.
- Separately, a standalone copy of the wrapper under `Zoë (Work) & Co 100%` rotated an unheld 5 MB log (`log→.1`, `.1→.2`, `.2→.3`, old `.3` dropped), passed a nonzero runner exit code through, and fell back to the console with all five logs held.

body:
## Why

Agent Proof already has strong evaluation, regression, critical-failure and economics evidence. The commercial gap is making sure an **Agent Trust Audit** cannot be sold from a happy-path-only eval pack.

## What this adds

- audit-readiness validator
- minimum 30-case default
- five mandatory starter dimensions:
  - correctness
  - boundary
  - injection
  - recovery
  - approval
- `agentproof audit-check` CLI with non-zero exit when coverage is incomplete
- deterministic unit tests
- bounded commercial offer and evidence/claim limits

## Important boundary

`audit-ready` means the **pack has minimum structural risk coverage**. It does not certify the agent, prove representativeness, or replace domain/legal/security review.

## Commercial hypothesis

Starter Agent Trust Audit: €2k–€10k depending on case preparation, integrations and domain complexity. This is explicitly a hypothesis until paid demand validates it.

author: browens5
body: The reload that stops the -6662 abort was running on the same thread as the game. Every few seconds the picture froze while MediaPipe loaded again, and when the hands came back the two pterodactyls could trade players. The Mac tracker now lives in its own process. A spare process loads beside it and takes over about every 15 seconds, before the graphics cache fills. The game keeps drawing on the live tracker, so the frame does not stop and the flyers are not reassigned from left to right. If that process does run out of graphics memory, it exits on its own and Live Play starts another instead of aborting. Linux still runs the model in-process on the CPU and does not recycle it. ```bash caffeinate -d python -m liveplay ```

scx_nitosis is a fork of scx_mitosis and follows mitosis commit by commit. This adds CONVERSION.md, which records how nitosis differs from mitosis at the fork point and the procedure for syncing, and then ports the mitosis commits landed since the fork that nitosis lacks. Each port is a cherry-pick of the mitosis commit with notes on what the conversion changed.

Commits, with the mitosis origin of each port:

- scx_nitosis: Add CONVERSION.md
- scx_nitosis: Always use tracepoints for cgroup tracking (929f6c3708d8)
- scx_nitosis: Raise the BPF clang-format column limit to 120 (1318596ef024)
- scx_nitosis: Keep a task's vtime across refreshes that do not move it (9b957314d77b)
- scx_nitosis: Charge the CPU's subcell for pinned placements (ab712b421576)
- scx_nitosis: Cap the vtime debt a task may carry at enqueue (df929233bf74)
- scx_nitosis: Bound how long the per-CPU DSQ goes unserved (0dda6e2cb2a6)

Every draft except the core opened with a `# Status:` section: a generated block of catalog facts, plus, in 23 drafts, hand-written applicability prose. The section:

- moved draft bytes the conformance ledger pins on every manifest edit, forcing re-pins (#856 removed the worst of it);

author: buluoray
body:
## Problem / Motivation

**Goal:** Typing in the dashboard's inline file editor keeps focus and the caret where the user is typing.

Since #12818, every keystroke in the inline editor (for example a Markdown file opened in the side panel and switched to Edit) drops focus and moves the caret to the top of the file. Continuous typing is impossible: the user has to click back after each character.

## Why it matters

The inline editor is the dashboard's only way to edit a file in place, and today it cannot be used for more than one character at a time. Every host of `PierreEditorImpl` is affected (side-panel file viewer, `CodeEditor`, Papyrus).

## Not a goal

- Changing Pierre (`@pierre/diffs`) itself or its version.
- Changing how `CodeEditor` / `PapyrusEditor` seed or key their sessions.
- Live-diff decoration behaviour while typing.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

Symptom: focus lost and caret reset to line 1 on every keystroke.

Root cause: the host echoes each edit Pierre emits back into `file.contents`, and since #12818 `PierreEditorImpl` derived Pierre's `cacheKey` from those live contents. Pierre's editor treats a changed `cacheKey` as a different file (`editor.js`, `shouldRebuildDocument` compares `fileInfo.cacheKey`): it builds a new `TextDocument`, calls `#resetState()` and restores the initial selections. So each keystroke rebuilt the document.

#12818 was fixing the opposite half of the same problem: new contents under an unchanged key re-render against a stale line cache, and Return threw "Line doesnt exist" (#12349). Both come from handing Pierre the live buffer while Pierre's own document already owns the text.

Change, in `PierreEditorImpl` only:
- A prop equal to the contents Pierre last emitted is treated as the host's echo and leaves Pierre's `file` input untouched (same object, same key, same contents), so neither the rebuild nor the stale-cache render happens.
- A prop that differs (disk read, Cancel, Refresh) reseeds the session with a content-derived key. When it restores exactly the seed text (Cancel after an edit), the key gets a reseed suffix so Pierre still drops the edited document.
- The worker-recovery remount path is unchanged: it still seeds from the remount draft.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: the component's props and callbacks are unchanged; only which `file` object reaches Pierre while typing changes.

## Tests

`website/src/test/PierreEditorImpl.test.tsx`:
- echoing an in-line edit, and a Return that grows the buffer, leaves the `file` handed to Pierre identical (`toBe`) to the one before the edit;
- an external change after an edit that restores the seed text reseeds with a different key and the restored contents.

All three fail against the pre-fix implementation and pass with the fix. The existing contract tests (external grown buffer / in-line change get a content-tracking key, caller's frozen session key is never handed to Pierre) and the recovery test still pass. All 100 test files that touch the editor's callers pass (1848 tests), and `tsc --noEmit` is clean.

## Manual verification

Done in headless Chromium against real `@pierre/diffs` (no doubles), at `8985016e52`. A throwaway Vite page (not committed) mounts `CodeEditor` with a host that echoes each edit back as `content`, the way the side panel does, plus a Cancel button that restores the saved text. The probe clicks the end of `beta line`, types `XY`, presses Return, types `Z`, then clicks Cancel.

- This PR: buffer after typing is `beta lineXY\nZ` (every key lands at the caret, Return adds the line), no page or console errors, and after Cancel the editor shows `beta line` again (no `beta lineXY` left on screen).
- Same probe with `origin/main`'s `PierreEditorImpl.tsx`: buffer is `beta lineX`. Only the first keystroke lands, then focus and caret are lost. That is the reported bug.

Not covered: the full dashboard side panel (Edit button, file load from disk) was not driven. The harness uses the same `CodeEditor` → `PierreEditor` path the side panel renders.

## Screenshots / video

<!-- no-visual-delta -->
Why no screenshot: no layout or styling changes; the fix is keystroke-level caret and focus behaviour, which a still image cannot show. The browser check above covers it.

## Related Issues

Regression from #12818 (the fix for #12349).

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: a controlled wrapper around an editor that owns its own document must not feed the editor's own emitted value back as a new input identity (key or contents); only external changes reseed.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|style|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [ ] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

## Contribution License Agreement

body:
## Upstream

Translate `edcf7d9d0c6042b8882311733e5103992c3d4d84`, one upstream commit only.

- Preserve reflected UBO minimum sizes in 18-byte binding-map rows, accepting legacy 14-byte rows with no minimum. Include the field in stage merging, layout IDs, layout construction and cross-stage checks.
- Reject short/out-of-bounds UBO ranges before native creation in Metal, Vulkan, WebGPU and WebGL2, and before deferred recording. Zero-size ranges use bytes remaining after the offset.
- Carry the field through the Rust host shader decoder and layout adapter too.
- Translate all five new binding-map cases, the round-trip changes, and the deferred rejection case.
- Wasm guest GPU proxy/factory traps and locale import remain deferred under UNIV-3728. Unsupported D3D backends are not introduced.

## Reviews and validation

Mechanical translation, independent source-equivalence pass, then separate Rust-integration pass. Both clean. Validation found only stale embedded-source byte/line counts; those corrections received both narrow rereviews. No runtime behavior or behavioral assertions were weakened to pass validation.

- ORE library: 165 passed; live Metal binding witness: 1 passed, Metal API/GPU validation enabled and live resources required.
- Renderer library (Metal/Vulkan/WebGL2/tools): 695 passed, 11 existing ignored (hidden corpus/measurement, expected-red Bezier cases, configured Vulkan-host cases). This is not a claim of all-platform device execution.
- Scripting library: 310 passed, 1 existing scripted C++ oracle ignored; shader resolution/GPU input/async shader integration: 31 passed.
- Manifest generator: 23 passed; generated manifest current. Structural correspondence: 1,036 mirrored owners, not behavioral proof.
- wasm32-unknown-unknown scripting and WebGPU/WebGL2 renderer compilation passed; this is not browser device execution.

The three embedded backend C++ snapshots receive this commit's hunks; they are not claimed to be full byte-identical current upstream snapshots (unrelated historical snapshot drift remains).

Accounted checkpoint: 75 commits since the September restart, 99 remaining against the recorded target. Merge without waiting for CI per user direction.

## Ringkasan
Dua laporan dari pemilik yang diuji di HP Android.

### 1. Bug: slider warna menggulir halaman balik ke kolom nama
Setelah mengetik Nama Kursus lalu menyentuh slider warna, halaman menggulir kembali ke kolom nama, sehingga warna tidak bisa dipilih. Penyebabnya, kolom teks masih fokus: keyboard menutup, lalu Chrome menggulir ke kolom yang fokus itu.

author: mfittko
body:
## Objective

Prove the agent-platform architecture from the epic with a runnable prototype, so the design can graduate into phased plans on evidence.

Closes #233. Part of the epic https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/229.

## What this is

A working prototype of the agent platform. Agents only advise. Nothing is traded and the paper ledger is not touched. The engine still runs from SQLite. The new code lives under `platform/`, plus a small opt-in hook and a few engine routes in `scripts/`.

## In scope

- Go control plane on Postgres: durable run queue with leases, fencing tokens, cancel, retry and timed follow-ups. Idempotent event intake with frozen decision snapshots.
- Separate Go worker with allowlisted read tools scoped to one instrument, an OpenAI-compatible runtime with a bounded tool loop, and a deterministic mock.
- Advisory position monitor: stops, targets, trailing, time stop and kill switch run on each new one-minute bar with no model call. Tripwires wake the agent, which may hold, close, tighten the stop or replace its tripwires, and never widen the stop. The monitor simulates advisory shadow fills for these positions only; the non-goal on portfolio and fills covers the real paper ledger.
- Next.js console: Desk, instrument page with live chart, Portfolio, Strategies (versioning, wizard, guided and automatic grill with a backtest), Runs, Alerts, Settings, and a chat panel that streams from the engine. A grill proposal fills the strategy editor and an Undo control restores the earlier text. The console proxy refuses writes to the paper bot settings and to executable-path settings.
- SQLite importer into Postgres. It refuses to commit unless cash reconciles with realized profit. Re-runs insert nothing new.
- Engine changes: routes for indicators, news and decision context (the indicators route fetches upstream candles and saves them to SQLite, like the chart route); running and done tool events on the chat stream for every provider; an opt-in snapshot hook that is off unless `MS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` is set; and the `claude-code` LLM provider, which the engine uses for filter, recheck, bot and chat calls only when the `provider` or `llmFallbackProvider` setting selects it.
- Scripts: `dev.sh` (with run and db subcommands), `smoke.sh`, `backup.sh`, and `switch-launchd.sh` (opt-in via `MS_ALLOW_LIVE_SWITCH=1`), which also installs the console stack launchd jobs. A `consoleUrl` engine setting makes alert links open the new console, and the instrument page reads the `granularity` query parameter.

## Explicit non-goals

- No order execution. Agents advise and the paper ledger is not touched. The console cannot change paper bot settings.
- No cutover of the live engine to Postgres. The migration plan is documented, not executed.
- No Pi runtime and no Go port of portfolio and fills.
- No merge of this PR as the final architecture. It graduates into phased plans.
- No new test coverage work in this PR, for example the importer refusal-branch tests. The owner decided coverage is added when the new engine replaces the old one. Coverage findings are deferred to that follow-up.
- No change to make the dev-loops validation record resolvable. `resolve-validation` cannot classify this repo's scripts (no Bun pin, Node scripts). CI on the current head and the results in "How it was tested" are the validation evidence.

## Validation command

```
(cd platform && MS_REQUIRE_DB=1 MS_TEST_DATABASE_URL=<test database url> go test -p 1 -race -count=1 ./...)
npm test
(cd platform/web && pnpm typecheck)
```

## How it was tested

Head 5649679dcab700fb20723eb2349d1dbadbfbfca9.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Go tests, race detector, real Postgres | all 9 packages with tests pass, 135 tests |
| Node tests | 714 of 714 pass |
| Console type check | clean |
| Browser review, 13 URLs x desktop/phone x dark/light, isolated stack with a fake engine, at 5649679dcab700fb20723eb2349d1dbadbfbfca9 | no horizontal overflow, no console or page errors; a new engine signal appears on the instrument page 2.3 s after it is recorded and a new headline 3.7 s after, without a reload; another instrument's page stays quiet; the watcher stops after the last browser leaves; clearing Chart indicators sends null; the research run form re-selects a visible agent; the watcher toggle (instrument page and Settings) merges into freshly read settings; an instrument without candles shows the empty chart state; a late strategy or coach reply is ignored after a switch; every settings form re-reads settings and saves only its changed keys, and clearing a field sends null; late replies cannot overwrite a newer instrument, granularity, chat thread or run selection |

Performance: the Desk candle summary query went from 74 ms to 5 ms, and a warm Desk answers in about 5 ms.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All Go packages pass with the race detector in CI.
- [ ] All Node tests pass and the console type check is clean.
- [ ] Every console page renders without console errors or horizontal overflow, at desktop and phone width, in dark and light.
- [ ] The engine hook is off unless `MS_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` is set, and its failures never affect the engine.
- [ ] The importer refuses to commit unless cash reconciles, and a re-run inserts nothing new.
- [ ] A stale worker, a duplicate claim and a forbidden tool call are rejected.

## Definition of done

- [ ] CI is green on the current head.
- [ ] Every confirmed high and medium review finding is fixed with a regression test.
- [ ] The status and adapted plan note is in the repository.
- [ ] Follow-up issues exist for the open work, and the epic links to them.
- [ ] A human approves the pull request. Merge stays with the owner.

## Risks

- Go statement coverage is below the 90% target and the console has no unit tests. Coverage is added when the new engine replaces the old one.
- The live engine currently runs from this temporary worktree. `switch-launchd.sh up` stops and disables the old supertrend watcher LaunchAgent. Roll back with `platform/scripts/switch-launchd.sh rollback` after merge; add `--with-watcher` to bring the watcher back.
- The importer refuses to commit while the source has open paper positions.

## Follow-ups

- Raise Go coverage to 90% and add web tests when the new engine replaces the old one.
- Follow-up issues for the adapted plan: https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/234 to https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/243.
- Plan for moving the engine fully to Postgres: `platform/docs/postgres-migration.md`.
- Reconcile with https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/123 and https://github.com/mfittko/market-signals/issues/36.
- Deferred review findings: the lease duration setting is ignored; the engine hook and operator snapshots use two shapes; a slow indicators callback can drop the shadow snapshot; the engine alert filter can block up to 90 s on the `claude-code` path; news text can steer the model through tool results.

author: frankaloia
body:
## Summary

- **Fix CWE-459 (disk exhaustion)**: `parseSendgridWebhookContent` now collects all temp file paths written by formidable during multipart parsing and deletes those not returned as email attachments in a `finally` block. The caller (`webhook.ts` IIFE) deletes the returned attachment temp files after all processing is complete.
- **Fix CWE-770 (body buffered before size check)**: The webhook trigger route now applies the shared `bodyLimit` middleware before the handler function, so oversized requests are rejected before the body is buffered into memory.

## Findings

| File | Line | Finding | Source |
|------|------|---------|--------|
| `front/lib/api/assistant/email/webhook_helpers.ts` | ~356 | formidable writes every file attachment to `os.tmpdir()` and temp files are never deleted → disk exhaustion (CWE-459) | Row 13 |
| `front-api/routes/v1/w/[wId]/triggers/hooks/[webhookSourceId]/[webhookSourceUrlSecret]/index.ts` | ~89 | `ctx.req.arrayBuffer()` buffers entire body before size check → memory exhaustion on large payloads (CWE-770) | Row 14 |

## Changes

**`front/lib/api/assistant/email/webhook_helpers.ts`**
- Added `import fs from "node:fs"`
- After `form.parse(req)`, collects all temp file paths into `allTempPaths`
- Tracks which paths become `attachmentPaths` (those returned in `InboundEmail.attachments`)
- `finally` block unlinks all non-attachment temp files (rejected due to unsupported content-type, zero-size, or parse errors)
- Added `@cc [owner:flvndvd,label:security] temp-file-cleanup` contract

**`front-api/routes/email/webhook.ts`**
- Added `import fs from "node:fs"`
- Collects `attachmentPaths` from `email.attachments` before the IIFE
- Added `finally` block in the IIFE that unlinks all attachment temp files after use

**`front-api/routes/v1/w/[wId]/triggers/hooks/[webhookSourceId]/[webhookSourceUrlSecret]/index.ts`**
- Imported `bodyLimit` from `@front-api/middlewares/body_limit` (the shared wrapper that returns a proper `{ error }` envelope)
- Applied `bodyLimit(WEBHOOK_REQUEST_MAX_SIZE_BYTES)` as a middleware before the handler
- Removed the manual post-buffer `byteLength` check (now redundant)
- Added `@cc [owner:flvndvd,label:security;performance] body-limit-before-buffer` contract

## Testing Plan

- [ ] Send an inbound email with an attachment whose MIME type is not supported — verify no temp file remains in `os.tmpdir()` after processing
- [ ] Send an inbound email with a valid attachment — verify the temp file is removed after the IIFE completes
- [ ] POST to `/api/v1/w/:wId/triggers/hooks/:webhookSourceId/:webhookSourceUrlSecret` with a payload > 2 MB — verify the response is HTTP 413 with `{ error: { type: "content_too_large" } }` without the handler body being read
- [ ] POST with a valid ≤ 2 MB payload — verify normal processing continues

## Risk

Low. The temp-file cleanup is fire-and-forget (`unlinkSync` errors are swallowed); attachment reading happens before the `finally`. The `bodyLimit` middleware is already used on other routes in this codebase (`mcp/results`) with the same wrapper.

author: noah-emp
body:
Ports snap to bend 2.0.34.

## What broke
- **`String.eq.fin` is gone (2.0.33).** `String.eq` is now `Cmp.is_eq(String.order(a, b))`. `check/LAWS.bend` defines `eq.of(rr) = Cmp.is_eq(Pair.snd(String & String, Cmp, rr))` and the laws that named `String.eq.fin` (`eq_fin_rec`, `eq_head.cmp`, `eq_tail.cmp`, and the `string_eq_self` proof) use it. No law was weakened.
- **The verdict fails any file whose imports hold foreign code (2.0.32).** `LAWS.bend`/`PROOF.bend` imported `main.bend`, which reaches `snaprun.exec/start/par`, so `PROOF.bend` printed `SOME PROOFS FAIL` even with every law proved. The laws now state SNAP-ANS-1..3 over `src/answer.bend` and the `cmd`/`line` round trips over `src/argv.bend`. `main.bend`'s `code`, `text`, `ok`, `cmd` and `line` return those unchanged, and SPEC.md records that as the new trust row **SNAP-TRUST-5**. `main.bend` marks those five one-line delegates `# noqa: L001` for bolt's coverage rule. The change is comments only, and the entry behaves the same.
- `bend main.bend --check-only` prints `SOME PROOFS FAIL` by design, because the entry reaches snap's foreign effects. The proof gate is the PROOF.bend files, and SPEC.md now says so.

## Build
- The flake pins bendlang/bend at `777ee0b` (packages 2.0.34). ez's own bend is pinned at `af569d4` (2.0.31) instead of followed. `checks.proofs` runs every PROOF.bend on this flake's bend and requires `ALL PROOFS CHECK` (in place of `ez.mkProofs`).
- CI `readme` job: bend 2.0.34 with the new sha256, and the gate string is now `ALL PROOFS CHECK`.
- Nothing reads `IO.args`, so the demo is unchanged. It runs compiled, interpreted, and as `.js` on bun, so the JS twins of the effects still register.

## Verdicts (bend 2.0.34)
- `PROOF.bend`: ALL PROOFS CHECK
- `check/PROOF.bend`: ALL PROOFS CHECK
- `nix flake check -L`: passes (demo, proofs, lint clean)
